papers.abstract_en: As a critical tumor suppressor gene, mutations in p53 often contribute to the initiation and progression of cancer. Anti-p53 autoantibody (p53-AAb), produced by the immune system in response to mutated p53 protein, can be detected in the blood during early stages of tumor development. As a non-invasive biomarker, p53-AAb demonstrates potential for early screening, auxiliary diagnosis, prognosis evaluation, and treatment monitoring across various cancer types. Based on current literature and evidence-based medical data, this Review Article provides an overview of the scientific rationale, technical aspects, and clinical applications of p53-AAb testing. It summarizes practical considerations to guide scientific research and clinical practice, with the aim of promoting standardized utilization of this biomarker.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To investigate genetically supported molecular factors associated with uveitis and to evaluate the clinical, transcriptomic, and retinal relevance of intercellular adhesion molecule 5 (ICAM-5) across major immune-mediated non-infectious uveitis subtypes. METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was conducted using eQTLGen eQTL data and two independent pQTL resources (Icelandic SomaScan and FinnGen R10), with uveitis GWAS summary statistics as the outcome. ICAM5 was evaluated using complementary MR estimators, sensitivity analyses, reverse MR, and Bayesian colocalization. Plasma ICAM-5 concentrations were measured by ELISA in 90 patients with active non-infectious uveitis (30 each with Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease, Behçet's disease-associated uveitis, and HLA-B27-associated acute anterior uveitis) and 40 healthy controls using age- and sex-adjusted models. ICAM5 expression was further examined in the peripheral-blood transcriptomic dataset GSE194060, whereas retinal Icam5 expression and cellular distribution were evaluated using experimental autoimmune uveitis retinal single-cell RNA-sequencing data and GSE132229. RESULTS: Genetically predicted higher ICAM5 expression and ICAM-5 protein levels were associated with increased uveitis susceptibility in the eQTLGen dataset (OR = 2.46, 95% CI 1.48-4.11, P = 5.69 × 10-4; nSNP =8), the Icelandic SomaScan cis-pQTL analysis (OR = 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.46, P = 5.30 × 10-4; nSNP =89), and the FinnGen R10 cis-pQTL analysis (OR = 1.21, 95% CI 1.07-1.38, P = 3.13 × 10-³; nSNP =4). Sensitivity analyses showed no significant heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy, and reverse MR provided no evidence of an association from uveitis liability to ICAM-5 levels. Plasma ICAM-5 concentrations were higher in all three uveitis subgroups than in healthy controls and remained elevated after age and sex adjustment, with the greatest increase in Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease. In the GSE194060 peripheral-blood transcriptomic dataset, ICAM5 expression was higher in the uveitis group. Analysis of the retinal single-cell RNA-sequencing data showed that Icam5 was predominantly detected in neuronal populations. CONCLUSION: Multi-omics MR, clinical protein quantification, transcriptomic analysis, and retinal single-cell profiling provide convergent evidence linking ICAM-5 to immune-mediated non-infectious uveitis. These findings support ICAM-5 as a genetically supported candidate mediator and circulating biomarker.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Osimertinib and cisplatin are widely used as standard treatments for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, their effects on tumor microenvironment remodeling remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether TREM2-positive tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) promote immune evasion through the CCL5/CCL22-CCR5/CCR4-Treg axis under anticancer treatment. METHODS: The spatial and quantitative correlations between TREM2+ and FOXP3+ cells were assessed using NSCLC patient-derived single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets, human lung adenocarcinoma tissue microarrays, and cisplatin-treated mouse lung cancer models. Mediators linking TREM2+ and FOXP3+ cells were identified by cell-cell communication analysis using CellChat and gene expression profiling of THP-1-derived macrophages treated with osimertinib or cisplatin, with validation in bone marrow-derived macrophages. RESULTS: scRNA-seq dataset analysis showed significantly enriched TREM2+ and FOXP3+ cells in lung adenocarcinoma tissues compared with adjacent normal lung, with a significant positive correlation at the aggregated single-cell level (Spearman's rho = 0.7323, P < 0.001). CCL5 and CCL22 were identified as key mediators linking TREM2+ TAMs and FOXP3+ Tregs and were markedly induced by treatment but suppressed by TREM2 knockdown or pharmacologic inhibition. TREM2 overexpression further enhanced their induction. Mechanistically, CCL22 induction was broadly dependent on SYK, Src, AKT, NF-κB, or STAT3 signaling pathways, whereas CCL5 upregulation depended on Src, NF-κB, and STAT3, with SYK involvement varying by cell type. In the orthotopic Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) model, Trem2 inhibition reduced Treg infiltration and mitigated chemotherapy-associated immune evasion. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that TREM2+ TAMs drive CCL5/CCL22-mediated Treg recruitment and support targeting TREM2 to enhance therapeutic efficacy of standard NSCLC treatments.

papers.abstract_en: Patterns of gene and sequence preservation across species provide insight into gene essentiality under natural selection. Here we developed two interspecies constraint metrics across 462 mammalian species: Gene Identity Score of Mammalian Orthologs (GISMO), which quantifies gene loss weighted by evolutionary distance to humans, and GISMO-mis, which measures missense constraint using the ratio of missense to synonymous variation across mammals. Both metrics are strongly correlated with human loss of function, missense and dosage constraint derived from large-scale sequencing studies, yet are largely independent of coding sequence length. GISMO and GISMO-mis identify essential genes missed by existing human-only metrics, particularly short genes. Genes in the most constrained deciles are enriched for rare variant associations in disorders linked to reduced fecundity, including schizophrenia, autism and neurodevelopmental disorders, and show strong enrichment for common variant heritability. These deciles also exhibit reduced copy number variation, consistent with dosage sensitivity. In addition, GISMO improves prioritization of recessive disease genes and captures signatures of homozygous selection across the mammalian tree. Taken together, GISMO and GISMO-mis leverage deep mammalian evolution to provide complementary, length-robust measures of gene essentiality that strengthen disease-gene prioritization and illuminate the selective forces shaping human biology.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Intermediate-dose spillage is central to normal-brain sparing in stereotactic radiosurgery, yet fixed adverse-event and relative indices do not define achievable plan quality for single-target linear accelerator treatments. The aim was to derive a volume-dependent absolute benchmark for the 50% prescription isodose volume (V50%; equivalent to V10 Gy for 20 Gy plans) for brain metastases. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In total, 276 single-isocenter single-target plans were analyzed: 178 idealized model plans and 98 clinical plans. Power-law regression in log-log space modeled spillage against planning target volume (PTV, cm3). The volume-scaling exponents were 0.83 for the ideal references and 0.75 for the simplified clinical threshold. The clinical upper threshold was derived using q = 0.90 quantile regression. Threshold-exceeding plans were reviewed for anatomical or technical justification. RESULTS: In the model cohort V50% value correlated strongly with PTV (r = 0.994, p < 0.001). The ideal mean model was V50% = 3.71 × PTV0.83, the conservative ideal-planning reference was V50% = 4.10 × PTV0.83, and the clinical upper threshold was V50% = 5.00 × PTV0.75. Ten of 98 clinical plans (10%) exceeded the threshold. Seven lacked anatomical justification and were replanned, reducing V50% by a median of 14% (range 7-29%) without compromising target coverage. CONCLUSIONS: A volume-based V50% benchmark provided a complementary quality-assurance reference for single-target linear accelerator radiosurgery for brain metastases. It flagged plans that warranted structured review alongside target coverage, organs of interest, conformity, and gradient metrics.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: As radiotherapy techniques become increasingly complex, patient-specific quality assurance (PSQA) must evolve to detect a broad spectrum of potential failure modes across the treatment chain. This study presents a extensive evaluation of a multi-modal PSQA program by assessing its ability to detect clinically relevant failure modes and quantifying its efficacy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A five-year retrospective analysis was conducted of an integrated PSQA program implemented at Maastro, combining secondary dose calculations, log-file based verification, and Electronic Portal Dosimetry (EPD) in both pretreatment and in vivo workflows. The efficacy of individual QA methods and the overall program was quantified using positive predictive values (PPVs). PSQA outcomes were linked to potential improvements in treatment planning strategies and delivery techniques. RESULTS: A total of 18,558 treatment plans were analyzed in the pretreatment workflow and 1817 treatment plans in the in vivo workflow. Nearly all high-priority failure modes could be detected except machine output miscalibration. Combining PSQA methods substantially improved PPVs across failure categories. The in vivo workflow flagged the most failure modes and additionally gives insight into possible improvements in planning strategies or treatment techniques. CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective analysis demonstrated that a comprehensive framework incorporating independent, purpose-specific PSQA methods is essential to detect a wide range of treatment deviations. Combining complementary methods improves the reliability and interpretability of results. The clinical impact of a PSQA program can be further enhanced by adopting more clinically meaningful evaluation metrics and using the results to guide the optimization of new treatment strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose To develop and evaluate TRAM-AI, a consensus-based checklist for verifying whether medical imaging datasets described as publicly accessible are functionally usable for AI development. Materials and Methods A modified Delphi study was conducted. A steering committee generated candidate checklist items through a targeted literature review. An international expert panel (n = 33) rated items on criticality and feasibility across two Delphi rounds. Consensus was defined as ≥ 75% agreement on both dimensions. The checklist was pilot-validated in 10 publicly available datasets. An advisory group of four experts from Latin America and sub-Saharan Africa evaluated cross-regional applicability. Results Of 16 candidate items, 14 were retained in the final checklist; one item was removed because of feasibility concerns, and another was merged with an existing item because of conceptual redundancy. All 14 final items achieved consensus for both criticality and feasibility. The final TRAM-AI checklist comprises 14 items across four domains: Dataset Access and Persistence (3 items), Technical Interoperability (4 items), Metadata and Reproducibility (4 items), and Ethical, Legal, and Maintenance considerations (3 items). In pilot validation, all items were applicable to all 10 datasets, compliance was 90% for trusted repository, de-dentification, and subject-level mapping, 10% for archive validation, and 30% for partition keys. All four advisory group members endorsed the checklist. Conclusion TRAM-AI provides a practical framework for verifying the functional accessibility of medical imaging datasets, complementing existing methodological reporting standards. Further evaluation and broader validation across diverse geographic settings are warranted. ©RSNA, 2026.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Obesity is a chronic inflammatory and metabolic condition implicated in the pathogenesis of several fibrotic diseases. However, population-based evidence regarding the association between obesity and the risk of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains limited. METHODS: This is a nationwide population-based cohort study using the National Health Information Database of South Korea. Adults aged ≥20 years who participated in the National Health Screening Program in 2012 were included. Individuals with prevalent IPF or those diagnosed within 1 year after baseline were excluded. Obesity was assessed using body mass index (BMI ≥25 kg/m² by Asian criteria) and waist circumference (WC). Incident IPF was defined by insurance claims with the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code J84.1 in conjunction with registration in the Rare Intractable Diseases programme. RESULTS: Among 4 788 202 participants followed for a mean of 10.15 years, 1 591 830 (33.2%) were classified as obese. Higher BMI was associated with an increased risk of IPF in a dose–response manner after multivariable adjustment. Compared with participants with BMI 18.5–22.9 kg/m², adjusted HRs for IPF were 1.25 (95% CI 1.16 to 1.35) for BMI 23–24.9 kg/m², 1.55 (95% CI 1.45 to 1.66) for BMI 25–29.9 kg/m² and 1.66 (95% CI 1.42 to 1.94) for BMI ≥30 kg/m². In contrast, underweight individuals (BMI <18.5 kg/m²) had a lower risk of IPF. WC demonstrated a similar trend, with higher values independently associated with increased IPF risk. CONCLUSIONS: In this large nationwide cohort, both general and abdominal obesity were independently associated with an increased risk of incident IPF. These findings provide population-based evidence supporting a potential role of increased adiposity in IPF pathogenesis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Identifying progression in fibrotic interstitial lung disease (f-ILD) is essential for treatment decisions and prognostication. Quantitative CT (qCT) may improve detection of progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). We evaluated whether routine qCT enhances identification of disease progression. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients presenting to an ILD service over 2 years. Patients with f-ILD who underwent two CT scans within 24 months prior to ILD multidisciplinary team (ILD-MDT) review were included. CTs were initially reported by a mixed pool of radiologists and subsequently reviewed by an expert thoracic radiologist at ILD-MDT. The contextflow ADVANCE Chest CT was used to quantify lung abnormalities. The cohort was divided 70:30 into derivation and validation sets, stratified by ILD-MDT-defined progression. In the derivation cohort, optimal qCT thresholds were defined using Youden’s index and applied to the validation cohort to assess detection of previously unreported progression. RESULTS: 127/502 patients met inclusion criteria and were stratified into derivation (n=89) and validation (n=38) cohorts. In the derivation cohort, a 0.39% increase in combined honeycombing and reticulation yielded an AUC of 0.64 for identifying progression. In the validation cohort, this threshold achieved sensitivity and specificity of 0.71 for PPF detection. Although 27/38 (71.1%) patients were initially reported as stable or without comment on progression, 12/27 (44.4%) were later classified as having radiological progression at ILD-MDT. Of these discordant cases, qCT correctly identified progression in 10/12 (83.3%). DISCUSSION: This study demonstrates that qCT may assist the non-specialist radiologist in identifying fibrotic disease progression enabling earlier access to appropriate treatment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The global burden of liver cancer has been increasing over recent decades, whereas the incidence in Switzerland has remained relatively stable. This study assessed long-term trends in incidence, mortality, and 1- and 5-year relative survival of primary liver cancer in the Swiss canton of Zurich from 1980 to 2022, stratified by sex and age. METHODS: This population-based retrospective analysis included all primary liver cancer cases diagnosed in the canton of Zurich and registered in the Cancer Registry of the cantons of Zurich, Zug, Schaffhausen and Schwyz between 1980 and 2022. Mortality data were obtained from the Federal Statistical Office. Cases were classified according to ICD-O-3 topography and morphology and, from 2003 onward, TNM stage. Age-standardised incidence and mortality rates were calculated using the 1976 European standard population. Temporal trends were analysed using Joinpoint regression and reported as Average Annual Percentage Changes (AAPCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Relative survival was estimated using the Ederer II method and standardised according to international standards. RESULTS: Among 3866 incident cases, 71.3% were hepatocellular carcinomas and 70.7% occurred in men. Overall age-standardised incidence remained stable in both men (AAPC -0.1%, 95% CI -0.6 to 0.3%) and women (-0.2%, -0.9% to 0.4%). However, incidence increased significantly among individuals younger than 65 years, particularly in women (AAPC 2.3%, 1.3%-3.3%) and men (1.2%, 0.6%-1.9%). Mortality remained broadly stable in men and increased modestly in women. One- and five-year relative survival improved substantially, from 13.8% and 3.5% in 1980-1999 to 53.9% and 25.8% in 2016-2022, respectively. Improvements were greater in men than women. CONCLUSION: These findings reflect major advances in liver cancer diagnosis and treatment over the past four decades. Continued prevention, targeted screening of high-risk groups, and epidemiological monitoring remain important.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a major public health priority, with survival shaped by clinical, behavioral, socioeconomic, and organizational factors. Socioeconomic disadvantage may affect risk exposure, diagnosis, treatment access, continuity of care, and data completeness. OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between area-level socioeconomic deprivation and cause-specific survival in lung cancer and apply the M.A.S.T.E.R. (Methodological Approach for Strategic Transformation, Evaluation, and Redesign) framework to translate epidemiological evidence into organizational design and implementation planning. METHODS: A retrospective population-based registry cohort study within ASL Napoli 1 Centro included incident malignant tumors of the trachea, lung, and bronchi recorded between 2010 and 2023. Cancer Registry data were integrated with the 2021 Socioeconomic Disadvantage Index (IDISE), Hospital Discharge Records, and progressi delle Aziende Sanitarie per la Salute in Italia (PASSI) 2022-2024 contextual smoking prevalence by sex and Primary Health Care District (DSB). Cause-specific survival was analyzed using multivariable Cox regression with district-clustered robust variance; Fine-Gray competing-risk regression was used as sensitivity analysis. M.A.S.T.E.R. comprised six phases: Mapping and contextualization, analysis and diagnosis, strategic design, testing and adaptive execution, embedding and sustainability, and resilience and renewal. RESULTS: Of 11,162 cases, 10,039 were included in the main analysis, totaling 207,600 person-months. There were 8,514 deaths, including 6,990 cause-specific deaths. In the primary model without contextual smoking prevalence, adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) increased across deprivation quintiles (Q5 vs. Q1: HR 1.11; 95% CI: 1.05-1.18; p < 0.001). Adding PASSI smoking prevalence attenuated the estimates (Q5 vs. Q1: HR 1.09; 95% CI: 0.99-1.19; p = 0.069); smoking prevalence was not statistically associated with mortality. M.A.S.T.E.R. outputs included a qualitative failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), a plan, do, study, act (PDSA) protocol with control plan, a completeness dashboard, and plans for updates, audits, and strategic review. CONCLUSIONS: Greater area-level socioeconomic deprivation was associated with higher cause-specific mortality in the primary model; the association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adding contextual PASSI smoking prevalence. M.A.S.T.E.R. clarified the transition from epidemiological analysis to candidate interventions for prevention, smoking cessation, early diagnosis, patient navigation, and information integration. Outputs from the final four phases are design-oriented and require prospective implementation and validation.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To examine whether Medicare's 2018 National Coverage Determination (NCD) for next-generation sequencing (NGS) was associated with changes in the use of targeted oral anticancer therapies among older adults with lung cancer. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate the probability of initiating an oral targeted therapy within 12 months of diagnosis. Key exposures were (1) diagnosis before versus after the NCD and (2) residence in a region with versus without pre-NCD NGS. Data were drawn from the SEER-Medicare linked data with Part D claims, including diagnosis years 2016-2019 with follow-up through 2020. The analytic sample included Medicare fee-for-service Part D beneficiaries aged 65 years or older with newly diagnosed lung cancer. RESULTS: Among 30,855 Medicare fee-for-service Part D beneficiaries with lung cancer, 7.1% used targeted oral anticancer therapies. The NCD was not associated with a significant overall change in targeted therapy use (0.4 Percentage Point; 95% CI, -1.6 to 2.4; p = 0.71). Before NCD implementation, targeted therapy use was 1.0 PP higher in regions with pre-NCD NGS coverage than in regions without such coverage (95% CI, 0.2-1.9; p = 0.015). In stage-stratified analyses, the additional post-NCD change was significant among patients with distant-stage disease (3.2 PPs; 95% CI, 2.6-4.0; p < 0.001) but not among those with regional-stage disease (p = 0.29). CONCLUSIONS: Medicare's NCD for NGS was not associated with a significant overall increase in targeted oral anticancer therapy use but was associated with increased use among patients with distant-stage disease. Targeted therapy use remained higher in regions with preexisting NGS coverage.

papers.abstract_en: The clinical translation of RNA interference (RNAi) for lung cancer treatment remains hampered by the lack of delivery vectors that concurrently optimize cellular uptake, target specificity, and in vivo stability. This work reports an intrinsically chiral gold nanoparticle (Au NP) platform with precisely controlled morphology for targeted siRNA delivery. Through a full 2 × 2 factorial design (2 chiralities × 2 morphologies), the work decouples the individual and combined contributions of these two parameters. It is found that right-handed chiral nanoparticles (D-NPs) show significantly faster cellular internalization and higher gene silencing potency than left-handed (L-NPs) and achiral (DL-NPs) counterparts. Beyond chirality, nanoparticle morphology serves as an equally critical parameter: the rhombicuboctahedral (RCO) architecture yields markedly higher silencing efficacy than cubic counterparts with D-chirality. Furthermore, proteomic analysis revealed that Au RCO nanoparticles with different chirality displayed distinct functional enrichment profiles. By D-RCO combination with minimal surface modification, siRNA targeting PD-L1 achieves potent knockdown and robust inhibition of H460 lung cancer proliferation both in vitro and in vivo. This work establishes chirality and morphology as co-designable parameters for gene delivery and provides a mechanistic blueprint for translating chiral nanomaterials into solid tumor therapy.

papers.abstract_en: The disease course in patients with advanced lung cancer with malignant serous effusions (ALC-MSE) is complex, and treatment outcomes are difficult to predict; systematic studies on the tumor stem cell-like characteristics and regulatory mechanisms of this condition are still lacking. Based on single-cell transcriptomic data and the TCGA-LUAD cohort, this study systematically analyzed the functional characteristics and key regulatory networks of malignant epithelial cells in severe lung cancer. Key findings include: epithelial cells in severe lung cancer exhibit significantly attenuated inflammation- and immunity-related signaling pathways (including NF-κB, TNF, and JAK-STAT signaling pathways), enhanced stem cell-like properties, and metabolic reprogramming; we identified a highly stem-like malignant epithelial cell subpopulation, represented by Cluster 3, which is enriched in stem-like pathways such as Notch, Hippo, TGF-β, and FoxO, and is accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial metabolism and stress adaptability; STMN1 is a key molecule regulating this stem-like state, showing a significant positive correlation with stemness scores and mRNAi; cells with high STMN1 expression gain a survival advantage and may maintain their stemness by attenuating CAF/ECM signaling with other cells (COL1A1-CD44), inhibiting complement activation and antigen presentation signaling (such as C3, ANXA1, and MHC-II-related molecules), and enhancing stemness niche signaling (MIF-CD74/CD44). Furthermore, NELFE, MYBL2, FOXN3, POLR2A, and RAD21 were identified as potential upstream regulators of STMN1. In vitro experiments confirmed that, following induction of stem cell-like properties, STMN1 was significantly overexpressed in lung adenocarcinoma cells, accompanied by upregulation of related stem cell markers (SOX2, NANOG, OCT4, and CD44). In summary, this study reveals a significantly enhanced stemness state in malignant epithelial cells in advanced lung cancer, accompanied by suppressed inflammatory signaling and enhanced metabolic adaptation, and identifies STMN1 as a key molecule driving stemness maintenance and disease progression.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate classification of lung tumors in cytology specimens and small biopsies remains a diagnostic challenge because of limited cellularity, preanalytical variables, and significant morphologic overlap among entities. This review summarizes key cytomorphologic characteristics and practical immunocytochemical strategies, and common diagnostic pitfalls encountered in the evaluation of non-small cell lung carcinoma, small cell lung carcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors, secondary pulmonary neoplasms, and uncommon thoracic entities in endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration and fine-needle aspiration samples. Particular emphasis is placed on the appropriate use of limited immunohistochemical panels to optimize tumor subtyping while preserving material for molecular testing. Diagnostic challenges such as crush artifact, necrosis, reactive mimics, overlapping morphologic patterns, and the risk of misclassification of rare tumors are addressed with practical guidance for differential diagnosis. By integrating morphologic assessment with ancillary testing, cytopathologists can achieve accurate tumor subtyping, distinguish mimics, and provide precise diagnoses that guide clinical management and selection of targeted therapies.

papers.abstract_en: While lysine acetyltransferase 6A (KAT6A; MOZ/MYST3) and 6B (KAT6B; MORF/MYST4) function as context-dependent oncogenic drivers-with KAT6B also displaying tissue-specific tumor-suppressive roles-their pharmacological targeting holds promise as a therapeutic avenue. This conceptual and translational review synthesizes evidence from genetic depletion models, pharmacological catalytic inhibitors, and emerging proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) degraders, introducing the "Dual-Compartment Hypothesis" as a conceptual interpretive framework to organize current evidence and generate testable hypotheses regarding their putative impacts on the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Under this framework, KAT6A/B blockade within the primary tumor compartment is proposed to indirectly foster regional antitumor immunity via preclinically implicated pathways, including tumor cell ferroptosis, cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) activation, and interleukin-6 (IL-6) suppression, alongside putative downstream influences on immune checkpoints. In contrast, systemic drug exposure in the secondary compartment may directly alter hematopoiesis and lymphocyte development, creating a tension between local immune activation and systemic constraints. Importantly, immune cells within the tumor microenvironment may also be directly suppressed by KAT6A/B inhibition-an alternative outcome that remains to be systematically investigated. Resolving these divergent outcomes necessitates distinguishing genetic knockout/knockdown (KO/KD) from pharmacological inhibition or degradation-a distinction that is critical because much of the mechanistic evidence derives from genetic models, while accounting for KAT6A versus KAT6B isoform selectivity. Finally, we outline testable translational frameworks, such as intermittent dosing schedules and rational immunotherapeutic combinations, to direct subsequent experimental and clinical validation, while acknowledging that current early-phase clinical observations (objective response rate [ORR]/clinical benefit rate [CBR]) reflect composite therapeutic responses and require further paired biomarker validation to definitively isolate immune-mediated effects.

papers.abstract_en: Ras-related protein Rab7a participates in fundamental cancer cell processes; however, its role in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to define Rab7a's oncogenic functions in ESCC and its involvement in the Hippo signaling pathway. Rab7a expression was assessed using ESCC datasets and validated by immunohistochemical analysis of ESCC tissues. We examined functional effects using small interfering RNA knockdown and Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1) overexpression rescue experiments, primarily by evaluating proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis in ESCC TE-1 cells. We also established a xenograft model for in vivo validation. Regarding its mechanism(s) of action, we analyzed the effects of Rab7a on Hippo core kinases (LATS1/2 and MOB1) and further assessed YAP nuclear localization in ESCC cells. Rab7a was overexpressed in ESCC tissues, and elevated expression correlated with aggressive clinicopathological features, including advanced tumor, node, metastasis stage, positive lymph node metastasis, deep tumor invasion, and poor differentiation. Rab7a knockdown suppressed cellular proliferation, migration, and invasion and induced apoptosis in vitro while inhibiting tumor growth and decreasing Ki-67 expression in vivo. Mechanistically, Rab7a silencing downregulated YAP1, p-YAP1, CTGF, and survivin without affecting MST1. Furthermore, Rab7a knockdown significantly increased p-LATS1/2 levels without altering total LATS1/2 or MOB1 expression and decreased YAP nuclear accumulation. Importantly, YAP1 overexpression effectively reversed the suppressive effects of Rab7a knockdown on malignant phenotypes at both the functional and molecular levels, and restored the expression of downstream targets. Rab7a depletion also reversed an epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-like phenotype, as evidenced by upregulated E-cadherin and downregulated vimentin and Snail. This effect was rescued by YAP1 overexpression. Our findings demonstrate that Rab7a promotes ESCC progression by regulating the Hippo pathway effector YAP, thus inducing an EMT-like phenotype. Rab7a may serve as a promising prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in ESCC that functions upstream of LATS1/2 to modulate YAP-mediated tumor progression.

papers.abstract_en: BRAF-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comprises three functional classes (I-III) with distinct driving mechanisms, yet effective therapies for classes II and III remain limited. To address this, we developed a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model that mechanistically recapitulates signaling networks and drug responses across all three classes, integrating multiscale preclinical-to-clinical datasets. The model enabled high-throughput prediction of clinical efficacy for monotherapies and combination therapies across diverse dosing regimens, and we identified that combining MEK and ERK inhibition represents a novel strategy for class II/III mutants, validated by original in vivo MiniPDX data using NSCLC patient tumors. Simulations further revealed that only triple blockade of EGFR, IGF1R, and FGFR pathway initiation can potently reduce tumor growth and overcome resistance in these classes. Our work is the first multiscale QSP platform mechanistically addressing class I-III BRAF mutations at the systems level for disease-centric translational combination therapy discovery and precision medicine design.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces lung cancer-specific mortality in high-risk populations, yet screening rates remain low nationwide. Electronic health record (EHR) health maintenance tracking may support guideline-concordant screening, but implementation varies across outpatient settings. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between manually adding the LCS health maintenance topic in the EHR and completion of LDCT screening in a resident-run outpatient clinic. METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated adult patients at a resident-run Federally Qualified Health Center Look-Alike clinic who met age and smoking history criteria for LCS in October 2024. Patients were categorized based on whether the LCS health maintenance topic was manually added within the Epic EHR and whether LDCT screening had been completed. Screening completion rates were compared using a chi-square test. RESULTS: Among 305 eligible patients, 130 (43%) completed LDCT screening. Of screened patients, 96 (74%) had the LCS health maintenance topic added, compared with 86 (49%) of 175 (57%) unscreened patients. Adding the LCS health maintenance topic was significantly associated with LDCT screening completion (p<0.001). CONCLUSION: Having the LCS health maintenance topic activated in the EHR was associated with higher rates of LDCT screening completion in a resident-run clinic compared with not having the LCS health maintenance topic activated. These findings support the role of having the LCS health maintenance topic added in the EHR as a practical strategy to reinforce preventive care delivery in outpatient practice.

papers.abstract_en: The intratumor microbiome, one of the hallmarks of cancer, plays a crucial role in cancer progression through its interaction with the host. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, six publicly available single-cell transcriptomic lung cancer datasets (comprising 178 samples) from multiple centers (Shanghai, New York, Seoul) were integrated to investigate the heterogeneity of host-microbiome interactions at the single-cell level using single-cell analysis of host-microbiome interactions (SAHMI). The results indicate that primary tumor tissues have a high proportion of fungi-associated cells, whereas metastatic brain tissues predominantly contain bacteria-associated cells. There are also distinct microbial distributions across cell types. Notably, the presence of specific bacteria significantly influences the transcriptome of resident host cells, including T cells and macrophages, by modulating pathways related to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) processing, cellular responses to stress and stimuli, and RNA and protein metabolism. Finally, specific cell-associated bacteria are significantly correlated with clinical features, such as lung cancer stages and smoking frequency. These single-cell insights into microbiome-host interactions improve current understanding about lung cancer development and progression and offer potential micro-ecological and diagnostic insights.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) is an uncommon mesenchymal spindle cell neoplasm (incidence ~1.4 per million). Although most SFT occur in the thoracic cavity, they can also arise in the retroperitoneum, pelvis, head, and neck. While the majority exhibit benign behavior, approximately 5% are associated with paraneoplastic syndromes, most notably Doege-Potter syndrome (DPS). DPS is characterized by non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia (NICTH) resulting from tumor hypersecretion of high-molecular-weight insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF2), which saturates insulin and IGF receptors causing refractory, life-threatening hypoglycemia. Due to nonspecific presentation and low incidence, DPS secondary to pelvic SFT is frequently misdiagnosed, underscoring the need for heightened clinical awareness. CASE REPORT: A 56-year-old man presented to the neurology department with acute loss of consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence. He had a 3-year history of hypertension but no diabetes mellitus. Initial laboratory tests showed a blood glucose of 4.76 mmol/L; however, during hospitalization, he developed recurrent severe hypoglycemia, with a nadir glucose of 1.6 mmol/L. Further biochemical evaluation during fasting hypoglycemia revealed undetectable insulin (<0.2 mIU/L) and low C-peptide (0.14 ng/mL). Contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT demonstrated a 17.8 cm heterogeneously enhancing pelvic mass causing bladder compression and left ureteral displacement. The patient declined preoperative biopsy. Preoperative euglycemia was maintained with continuous intravenous dextrose infusion, and open en bloc surgical resection was performed. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry (positive for STAT6, CD34, and CD99; Ki-67 8%) confirmed an atypical solitary fibrous tumor. Postoperatively, hypoglycemic symptoms resolved completely, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 6 without further hypoglycemic episodes. CONCLUSION: Pelvic SFT with DPS frequently presents with recurrent hypoglycemia or altered consciousness rather than local compressive symptoms. Early recognition of non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia (NICTH) and prompt cross-sectional imaging are essential for accurate diagnosis. Complete surgical resection is definitive and results in full resolution of hypoglycemia. Given the unpredictable biological behavior of SFT, long-term follow-up is essential. Heightened clinical awareness may improve diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed-large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space-Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset (n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are distinctive toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and have been reported to correlate with clinical outcomes in several cancers. However, whether this association also exists in patients with esophageal cancer (EC) receiving ICIs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between irAEs and clinical outcomes in this population. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated the association between irAEs and progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), or disease control rate (DCR). Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for PFS and OS, whereas odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were pooled for ORR and DCR using random-effects models. Between-study heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), sensitivity analyses, publication bias, prespecified subgroup analyses, and immortal-time bias were also assessed. RESULTS: 14 studies involving 1, 546 patients were included. The occurrence of irAEs was associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.31-0.63), OS (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.46-0.64), ORR (OR, 4.00; 95% CI, 1.58-10.12), and DCR (OR, 3.85; 95% CI, 2.40-6.20). The 95% PIs were 0.16-1.24, 0.44-0.66, 0.19-82.57, and 1.42-10.44 for PFS, OS, ORR, and DCR, respectively, crossing the null value for PFS and ORR. Subgroup estimates were generally similar in direction but remained exploratory. No eligible survival estimates using landmark or time-varying approaches were available for the comparison between patients with and without irAEs. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with EC receiving ICIs, the occurrence of irAEs may be a prognostic marker of favorable outcomes. However, wide PIs for PFS and ORR indicate that these associations may vary across future studies and immortal time bias may overestimate survival associations. This observational evidence derives mainly from East Asian patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and is primarily applicable to these patients. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and require prospective validation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261346294.

papers.abstract_en: Conditional and joint (COJO) analysis of genome-wide association study (GWAS) data is a standard post-GWAS analysis for identifying statistically independent associations. Although GWAS meta-analyses are increasingly conducted across multiple ancestry groups, the optimal strategy for multiancestry COJO analysis remains unclear. Here we introduce Manc-COJO, a method for multiancestry COJO analysis. Simulations and real-data analyses show that Manc-COJO improves detection of independent association signals while reducing false positives compared with single-ancestry COJO implemented in genome-wide complex trait analysis (GCTA) and its ad-hoc multiancestry adaptations. We also introduce Manc-COJO:FIX, a follow-up algorithm to identify ancestry-specific independent associations. The C++ implementation of Manc-COJO is over 120-fold faster than GCTA-COJO and supports linkage disequilibrium references derived from either individual-level genotype data or pre-computed matrices, facilitating analyses when data sharing is limited.

papers.abstract_en: Treatment-related cavitary transformation in lung cancer may complicate radiological response assessment. We report a man in his 70s with stage IVA invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma treated with atezolizumab, bevacizumab, carboplatin and paclitaxel. After two cycles, CT showed enlargement of cavitary components despite regression of solid tumour components, making response assessment difficult. After two additional cycles, the pulmonary lesions showed little change, whereas progression of the Th4 bone metastasis led to an overall assessment of progressive disease and a change to docetaxel plus ramucirumab. Thereafter, the cavities further enlarged while the cavity walls progressively thinned and the solid components appeared to regress. This case illustrates that marked multifocal cavitary transformation may produce discordant morphological changes, limiting response assessment based on imaging alone. Serum CEA and SLX levels remained within the normal ranges at diagnosis and throughout treatment.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) is yet to be considered an oncologic clinical condition characterized by a dismal prognosis. However, about 5 years ago, the introduction of immunotherapy in the first-line regimens, combined with platin-based chemotherapy, has produced an improvement of survival outcomes for this patient population. AREAS COVERED: In the last year, two innovative approaches have further improved efficacy outcomes for ES-SCLC patients. The addition of lurbinectedin to the immunotherapeutic drug atezolizumab in the maintenance phase of first-line treatment, and the introduction of the bispecific T-cell engager antibody tarlatamab as second-line treatment, have established two new standards of care for the treatment of ES-SCLC. Moreover, ongoing phase III trials are testing the possibility to introduce tarlatamab in the first-line setting, as induction or as maintenance. Simultaneosusly, phase II trials have reported very promising antitumor activity for ifinitamab deruxtecan and sacituzumab govitecan, two antibody drug conjugates in the second-line setting, and phase III trials are ongoing. EXPERT OPINION: As never in the past, the prognosis of ES-SCLC patients seems characterized by a new light, with innovative drugs that used combined or sequentially, have the potential of a substantial change of the natural history of this aggressive disease.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Although pleural tissue debris is occasionally encountered in the drainage systems of patients undergoing catheter or chest tube drainage, its clinical utility has not been reported. Here, we report two cases in which pleural tissue debris retrieved during catheter drainage enabled a definitive diagnosis of malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and molecularly guided treatment decisions. CASE PRESENTATION: The first case involved a 67-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease who developed a right pleural effusion suggestive of lung cancer with pleural metastasis. Invasive procedures for tissue acquisition were required; however, biopsy was withheld because of the high risk of pneumothorax and acute exacerbation of the underlying lung disease. Tissue debris was incidentally found in the drainage system. The tissue was adequate for pathological examination and revealed lung squamous cell carcinoma without genomic alterations. Chemoimmunotherapy was initiated without further invasive procedures. The second case involved a 78-year-old woman who presented with a left pleural effusion and a brain lesion, highly suggestive of lung cancer with brain metastasis. She declined invasive diagnostic procedures; however, tissue debris was incidentally collected from the drainage bottle and diagnosed as lung adenocarcinoma. Molecular testing revealed that the tumor harbored an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) L858R mutation, allowing first-line targeted therapy to be initiated without further invasive testing. CONCLUSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first case report to describe the clinical utility of pleural tissue debris for the diagnosis of MPE and its suitability for molecular profiling. Our report highlights that this previously overlooked byproduct of routine pleural drainage can provide adequate material for histopathological diagnosis, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing in patients with MPE, particularly those for whom conventional biopsy is contraindicated or declined.

papers.abstract_en: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE) is an ultra-rare vascular neoplasm with variable biologic behavior. Mediastinal EHE is particularly uncommon and may mimic more prevalent prevascular mediastinal tumors. We report a 52-year-old man with a 10.5 × 8.9 × 9.6 cm mixed-density left upper anterior mediastinal mass containing macroscopic fat, soft-tissue components, and coarse calcification. FDG PET/CT demonstrated mild-to-moderate uptake (SUVmax 4.8) without nodal or distant metastatic disease, and the imaging appearance favored mature teratoma. Resection demonstrated a 9.5 cm conventional EHE intimately associated with a myelolipomatous component containing extensive extramedullary hematopoiesis and metaplastic ossification. The neoplastic cells expressed endothelial markers, and RNA fusion analysis detected WWTR1::CAMTA1. Surgical margins were negative, early postoperative and abdominopelvic imaging showed no residual or metastatic disease, and multidisciplinary review recommended surveillance without adjuvant therapy. Although similar EHE-myelolipoma/extramedullary hematopoiesis associations have been reported, this case emphasizes the multimodality imaging mimic of mature teratoma and provides direct radiologic-pathologic correlation of the fat-containing, solid, and ossified components.

papers.abstract_en: Gastric and esophageal cancers pose major global health challenges due to high incidence, frequent late-stage diagnosis, and poor survival outcomes. This review synthesized current evidence on emerging technologies and innovative approaches shaping research and practice. We included studies that evaluated diagnostic imaging, endoscopic and surgical treatments, molecular biomarkers, staging, screening, and innovative therapeutic approaches in gastric and esophageal cancers. The review revealed notable demographic and geographic disparities in disease incidence and outcomes. Recent advancements in endoscopic techniques, imaging modalities, and staging systems have enhanced early detection and prognostic stratification. Intriguing findings include significant improvements in survival with HER2-targeted and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapies, the ability of liquid biopsy to detect resistance mutations and monitor treatment efficacy in real time, and the use of patient-derived organoids to predict individualized responses. Additionally, artificial intelligence (AI) applications have reduced diagnostic variability, thereby refining therapeutic decision-making. Despite promising innovations, further validation of these emerging technologies is required. Integrating advanced imaging, biomarker-based treatments, and AI-driven tools into clinical practice holds the potential to optimize treatment strategies and improve survival outcomes in gastroesophageal cancers.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To provide a software resource that enables medical researchers and practitioners to develop and apply reproducible, out-of-the-box, AI-based analysis workflows for radiological and radiotherapy data. DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION METHODS: The framework comprises two main components: the Python-native computational environment for radiological research (pyCERR) for radiological image processing, and the cancer genomics cloud (CGC), a National Cancer Institute-funded resource that supports cloud-hosted collaborative projects, with tools for managing collaborators and compute-hardware from providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud Platform. pyCERR is open-source (GNU GPL) and distributed at https://github.com/cerr/pycerr; it provides user-friendly data structures, simplified access to metadata across radiological imaging modalities, and tools for data transformation, AI-based image segmentation, radiomics, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI analysis, radiotherapy dose-volume histogram (DVH) feature extraction, and normal-tissue complication and tumor-control models. Radiomics features comply with the Image biomarker standardization initiative (IBSI) standards and are validated against published reference values. Unit tests covering data input/output, radiomics, DVH features, and visualization run on every code update. Workflows are containerized for reproducible, identical execution on the CGC and on local hardware. The CGC enables AI inference from radiological images to be combined with other data types such as genomics and proteomics. Our public CGC project (https://cgc.sbgenomics.com/u/sevenbridges/pycerr-radiological-radiotherapy-imageanalysis), accessible with free registration, currently includes apps for organ-at-risk (OAR) and lung-nodule segmentation based on published models trained in-house and clinically validated. These apps can be run interactively from a web browser or programmatically via a REST API with client support for multiple programming languages. Notebooks demonstrating the CGC API and pyCERR capabilities are provided at https://github.com/cerr/pycerr-notebooks. POTENTIAL APPLICATIONS: The framework facilitates end-to-end radiological image analysis and reproducible research, including data access from public and private repositories, training and inference with AI models, and utilities for data management, visualization, and simplified access to image metadata.

papers.abstract_en: Advances in spatial omics are shifting the study of lung macrophages from the characterization of isolated transcriptional states toward an understanding of their function in the context of cellular origin, anatomical location, neighboring cells, and tissue architecture. Here, we distinguish the macrophage niche in the strict sense-the local microenvironment that sustains tissue-resident macrophage survival and identity-from the broader cellular niche, in which macrophages are spatially organized with multiple interacting cell populations, and integrate recent insights into lung repair and chronic remodeling. Following injury, remodeling of the resident macrophage compartment, recruitment of monocyte-derived macrophages, and the emergence of regenerative epithelial intermediates and stromal responses generate transient multicellular environments that normally resolve as tissue homeostasis is restored. Spatial analyses, however, indicate that in at least some lung diseases, these repair-associated states fail to resolve and instead become organized into pathological cellular niches characterized by recurrent proximity among aberrant epithelial cells, inflammatory and profibrotic macrophages, activated stromal cells, and extracellular matrix. We further propose a spatial framework in which shared immune-epithelial-stromal interactions can give rise to distinct fibrotic architectures depending on whether they are anchored within alveolar-interstitial regions or around small airways. Finally, we discuss how pathological cellular niches identified by spatial approaches can be functionally validated and translated into therapeutically actionable intercellular circuits.

papers.abstract_en: Miliary intrapulmonary carcinomatosis (MIPC) is a rare metastatic pattern of lung cancer that closely mimics disseminated tuberculosis (TB), posing a significant diagnostic challenge. We present a 53-year-old Filipino woman, a lifelong nonsmoker with prior latent TB, who presented with progressive cough and a diffuse bilateral miliary nodular pattern on chest imaging. An extensive infectious workup was unrevealing, and bronchoscopic biopsy revealed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (TTF-1+) harboring an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. Staging demonstrated brain, osseous, and pleural metastases (stage IVB NSCLC). The patient was initiated on osimertinib 80 mg daily with palliative radiation and zoledronic acid, achieving no evidence of active disease at 2.5 years on serial PET-CT and brain MRI. This case underscores the importance of tissue diagnosis in unresolved miliary patterns, early molecular profiling in lung adenocarcinoma, and the potential for durable exceptional responses with osimertinib in EGFR-mutated NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) continues to present therapeutic challenges because of pathway redundancy and treatment resistance, underscoring the need for multi-target and systems-level strategies. Baicalein (BA), a flavonoid metabolite from Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, shows antitumor potential, yet integrative and immune-related evaluations of BA in LUAD remain limited. METHODS: We integrated network analyses with TCGA-LUAD transcriptomics, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), network topology, GO/KEGG enrichment, bulk RNA-seq-based immune-infiltration estimation (CIBERSORT), molecular docking, and clinical association analysis (GEPIA2/HPA). Cell viability was assessed in A549 cells​ using the CCK-8 assay, and AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression were further examined experimentally by western blot analysis. RESULTS: A total of 117 candidate BA-LUAD overlapping targets were identified, and six candidate hub genes (EGFR, AKT1, TP53, BCL2, HIF1A, and ESR1) were prioritized. Enrichment analyses suggested that the candidate network was associated with oncogenic signaling and stress-response programs, particularly PI3K-AKT/MAPK signaling, ROS-related processes, apoptosis, and p53 signaling. CCK-8 assays showed that BA reduced A549 cell viability in vitro, with IC50 values of 54.93 μM at 24 h and 22.83 μM at 48 h. Among the prioritized candidates, AKT1 and BCL2 were selected for focused experimental assessment in A549 cells. BA treatment reduced AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression in A549 cells, whereas total AKT1 remained largely unchanged. HIF1A expression showed broad associations with computationally estimated immune-cell fractions and poorer overall survival. CONCLUSION: These findings prioritize a BA-associated candidate network in LUAD involving kinase signaling, apoptosis-related regulation, oxidative-stress responses, and immune-microenvironment associations. The CCK-8 results support an inhibitory effect of BA on A549 cell viability in vitro, and the observed changes in AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression provide focused experimental support for selected components of the candidate network; further in vitro and in vivo studies are required to validate biological relevance and translational potential.

papers.abstract_en: γδ T cells are a unique lymphocyte lineage that bridges innate and adaptive immunity through MHC-unrestricted recognition of phosphoantigens, lipids, and stress-induced proteins. Their tissue-resident subsets, shaped by Vγ/Vδ chain usage, play essential roles in barrier surveillance, tissue homeostasis, and host defense.This review synthesizes recent advances that fundamentally reshape our understanding of γδ T cell biology. We highlight two conceptual frameworks: (1) dual recognition modalities of γδ TCRs, distinguishing structurally resolved ligand interactions from functionally supported recognition; and (2) a developmental wave model in which TCR signal strength and transcriptional networks program effector fates. Mouse and human studies are presented in dedicated species-specific sections and tables, with explicit attention to species-specific nomenclature and evidence levels.We cover γδ T cell development, tissue-resident programs, antigen recognition mechanisms (including butyrophilin-mediated phosphoantigen sensing, antibody-like foreign antigen recognition, and intracellular self-protein recognition), and the dual roles of γδ T cells in infection, cancer, and chronic inflammation. Therapeutic applications-adoptive transfer, CAR-engineered cells, and extracellular-vesicle vaccines-are critically appraised against current clinical evidence.Finally, we identify major unanswered questions: the complete γδ TCR ligand repertoire, the mechanisms maintaining tissue residency, and the translational gaps between mouse models and human disease. This review provides a structured framework for understanding γδ T cells as pivotal connectors of innate and adaptive immunity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Primary pericardial mesothelioma (PPM) is an exceedingly rare, highly invasive cardiac neoplasm with insidious onset and non-specific clinical symptoms. Due to the lack of typical early manifestations and effective routine diagnostic methods, PPM is often misdiagnosed and missed, resulting in delayed treatment and poor prognosis. CASE PRESENTATION: A 42-year-old male presented with 6 months of recurrent chest tightness and pain, worsening over 2 months, and two prior admissions for unexplained pericardial effusion. On admission, he had tachycardia, distant heart sounds, bilateral lower extremity edema, and a 3×2 cm hard, fixed left supraclavicular lymph node. Imaging confirmed pericardial effusion with abnormal pericardial lesions. Ultrasound-guided pericardiocentesis yielded only a small amount of red jelly-like material, with cytology suggesting epithelioid neoplastic cells. Supraclavicular lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic malignant mesothelioma. Nivolumab immunotherapy showed no improvement. Pericardial tumor resection revealed diffuse, fish-flesh-like tumor invading the myocardium and great vessels. Final pathology confirmed epithelioid-type PPM. CONCLUSION: Patients with recurrent unexplained pericardial effusion and atypical sonographic features, such as flocculent echoes and irregular pericardial thickening, should raise suspicion for PPM. Early recognition of these signs and timely pathological confirmation are critical to avoid diagnostic delays and may improve outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: G protein-coupled receptor 183 (GPR183), also known as EBI2, is a chemoattractant receptor whose principal endogenous ligand is 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC). Its expression varies dynamically across immune-cell subsets and activation states. By sensing local 7α,25-OHC gradients, GPR183 converts tissue metabolic cues into spatial information, thereby regulating immune-cell migration, tissue distribution, and function. Dynamic receptor expression, ligand synthesis and degradation, responding cell type, and the tissue microenvironment collectively shape the direction of pathway activity, whereas intervention studies in animals and longitudinal observations establish disease stage as a temporal coordinate for interpreting divergent effects. Genetic, pharmacological, and cell-engineering studies provide functional evidence that GPR183 contributes to lymphoid-tissue compartmentalization, host defense, inflammatory responses, tissue repair, and tumor-immune remodeling. Analyses of patient tissues and clinical cohorts extend this mechanistic framework to associations with disease activity, treatment response, and prognosis. Three intervention strategies have emerged: receptor agonism, pharmacological inhibition, and immune-cell engineering. The oral antagonist IPG11406 has entered early clinical evaluation, whereas preclinical assessment of other candidate strategies has focused on ligand stability, tissue selectivity, and long-term immune safety. This review integrates current evidence across four dimensions - immune-cell type, the 7α,25-OHC gradient, tissue microenvironment, and disease stage - and organizes the disease-related actions of GPR183 and potential stratified interventions around pathogenic recruitment, protective recruitment, tissue repair, tumor-immune remodeling, and biomarker applications.

papers.abstract_en: This anatomical study of the upper eyelid is based on detailed analysis of 74 consecutive primary upper blepharoplasty procedures (148 eyelids) performed under the operating microscope. There were 54 Asian and 20 Caucasian patients. Visualization under the miscroscope provided a unique operative perspective on the structural anatomy and relationships of the upper eyelid. The anatomy of the orbital septum and its relationships to the retro-orbicularis oculi fat (ROOF), levator aponeurosis, and retroseptal fat pads are presented in detail. The lower-positioned transverse ligament, its relationship to the anterior fascial sheath of the levator aponeurosis and the bilaminar nature of the levator aponeurosis, consisting of anterior and posterior layers, were clearly demonstrated. The lower-positioned transverse ligament was identified in 94% of eyelids. The mean length of the levator aponeurosis was 17.6 mm (range, 14-21 mm), and the mean length of its fused proximal portion was 5.4 mm (range, 4.0-8.0 mm). The clinical relevance of these anatomical findings in upper blepharoplasty is discussed. An anterior approach to the Müller muscle and its dissection is also presented. Finally, danger zones for bleeding are detailed with videographic demonstration. This paper provides a clearer surgical roadmap, offering practical anatomical guidance for various cosmetic and reconstructive upper eyelid procedures.

papers.abstract_en: The eye is increasingly recognized as a tissue shaped by systemic immune and metabolic states rather than an isolated immune-privileged organ. Translocator protein (TSPO), an 18-kDa outer mitochondrial membrane protein enriched in myeloid and glial cells, links mitochondrial homeostasis, redox signaling, lipid metabolism, and immune polarization. This review synthesizes evidence for TSPO involvement in systemic-ocular immunometabolic crosstalk and organizes it into a three-stage working model: peripheral immunometabolic priming, blood-retinal barrier vulnerability, and intraocular glial amplification. We review evidence from systemic autoimmune diseases with ocular manifestations, metabolic diseases with ocular complications, and primary ocular diseases with systemic contributions. We then assess the potential of TSPO as an imaging or fluid biomarker and as a therapeutic target. Current evidence suggests that TSPO is a promising immunometabolic node and underscores the need for cross-organ disease models, cell-specific TSPO manipulation, spatial multi-omics, and local ocular delivery strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as important regulators of innate immunity, acting across multiple molecular layers to shape antiviral and inflammatory responses. Among their diverse functions, protein-centered regulation provides a particularly versatile means of controlling immune signaling by altering the functional state, interactions, localization, or turnover of proteins without necessarily changing their transcription. In this review, we synthesize current evidence for lncRNA-mediated protein regulation in innate immunity and propose a protein-centered framework that connects molecular regulatory mechanisms with their functional and immunological consequences. At the mechanistic level, lncRNA-protein interactions can modulate post-translational modifications, alter protein conformations, and facilitate or disrupt protein-protein interactions. These regulatory modes, in turn, affect four major properties of immune proteins: protein stability, subcellular localization, molecular activity, and protein-protein interaction-dependent signal transmission, ultimately reshaping innate immune responses. Across these mechanisms, several recurrent principles emerge, including preferential regulation of functionally important signaling nodes, integration of multiple regulatory mechanisms, and strong dependence on cellular and immunological context. Emerging evidence further suggests that some lncRNAs may act on defined protein states or regulatory interfaces without altering total protein abundance, although the generality of such functional selectivity remains to be established. Together, these findings support a hierarchical model in which lncRNAs translate specific molecular interactions into changes in protein function and, ultimately, innate immune states. This framework provides a basis for understanding how lncRNA-protein interactions contribute to the fine-tuning of innate immunity and for evaluating their potential as targets for selective immune modulation.

papers.title_zh: 综述：TGF-β在慢性肾脏病中的作用争议——从全局通路抑制转向细胞来源、时空与转录辅因子依赖的信号重编程

papers.authors: Wang H, Tian J, Zheng G, Zhou Y

papers.authors_conclusion: 未来TGF-β靶向治疗应超越全局通路抑制，转向空间、时间与分子层面信息指导的信号重编程，并以生物标志物引导的患者分层及新兴单细胞与空间技术为支撑；这种精准调控有望在抑制病理性纤维化的同时保留免疫稳态与再生能力。

papers.reason: 该文讨论的是CKD肾纤维化中TGF-β的细胞来源与时空依赖性调控，对胸部肿瘤围手术期、肺结节评估、手术决策或胸部肿瘤药物治疗均无可直接转化的证据；仅在TGF-β通路生物学层面（如纤维化与免疫稳态平衡的通路重编程思路）对胸部肿瘤相关转化研究设计有间接参考价值。
papers.abstract_en: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is characterized by persistent inflammation, maladaptive repair and progressive renal fibrosis, yet therapeutic strategies capable of effectively targeting these interconnected processes remain limited. Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) is a central mediator of renal fibrosis but also exerts essential immunoregulatory and tissue-protective functions, creating a fundamental therapeutic paradox. Emerging evidence indicates that these divergent effects are determined not simply by TGF-β1 abundance, but by its cellular source and target, spatial and temporal context, interactions with other signaling pathways, and the transcriptional cofactors that determine downstream gene expression. This context dependence may partly explain why systemic TGF-β neutralization has shown limited clinical efficacy despite compelling preclinical evidence. In this Review, we discuss the cell-specific and stage-dependent functions of TGF-β1 in CKD, controversies surrounding the cellular origins of renal myofibroblasts, and the integration of TGF-β signaling with some signaling pathways. We further examine lessons from clinical trials and emerging therapeutic approaches designed to selectively modulate pathological TGF-β signaling, including regulation of latent TGF-β activation, receptor and Smad signaling, transcriptional cofactors, tissue-targeted delivery, and gene- and cell-based strategies. Particular attention is given to transcriptional partner selection as a mechanism of signal reprogramming. The β-catenin-TCF/FOXO1 axis provides a proof of concept whereby redirecting β-catenin from profibrotic TCF-dependent transcription toward FOXO1-associated anti-inflammatory and reparative programs may preserve beneficial TGF-β functions while limiting fibrosis. We propose that future TGF-β-targeted therapy should move beyond global pathway inhibition toward spatially, temporally and molecularly informed signal reprogramming, supported by biomarker-guided patient stratification and emerging single-cell and spatial technologies. Such precision modulation may provide a more rational strategy to suppress pathological fibrosis while preserving immune homeostasis and regenerative capacity in CKD.

papers.abstract_en: The genetic architecture of inborn errors of immunity continues to grow in complexity, exposing the limitations of variant-centric concepts that have long shaped the field. While complete loss-of-function genotypes have been instrumental in defining essential gene functions in human immunity and inflammation, they have also entrenched binary interpretations of causality that fail to account for pleiotropy, variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance-especially in monoallelic disease. Monoallelic variants often perturb signaling rather than abolishing it. The integration of these perturbations into molecular and cellular systems, and eventually immune circuits, governs phenotypic expression. Here, we revisit and extend classic concepts of genetic dominance and genetic pleiotropy and suggest that these are not sole properties of alleles but emerge from the complex and dynamic behavior of molecular, cellular and immune systems to buffer genetic variance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Since the publication of the ESMO Scale for Clinical Actionability of Molecular Targets (ESCAT) in 2018, precision oncology has evolved substantially. Tumour-agnostic therapy approvals, expanding real-world evidence datasets, and the clinical recognition of genomic resistance biomarkers have created the need to revise the original framework. METHODS: The ESMO Precision Oncology and Taxonomy Committee convened an international expert panel to revise the ESCAT classification. Through iterative review of the evolving evidence-base, structured feedback rounds, and consensus discussions, the panel developed an updated actionability scale and a novel resistance scale. The revision followed three principles: explicit grading of uncertainty within actionable tiers, formal inclusion of tumour-agnostic eligibility criteria, and systematic classification of resistance biomarkers to complement sensitivity designations. RESULTS: ESCAT version 2 (ESCAT v2) introduces several substantive changes. Tier I is restructured into three categories, proven, inferred, and extrapolated, that carry the same clinical directive but differ in the level of certainty within the supporting evidence. The guideline introduces formal tumour-agnostic gating criteria, the ESMO Tumour-Agnostic Classifier and Screener (ETAC-S). Tier II is refined into three sub-tiers graded by prospective interventional evidence, high-quality real-world or non-prospective evidence, and replicated case-level evidence. Tier X is subdivided into alterations that are tested and found not to be predictive (X-A) and biomarker-therapy matches in which the therapy lacks meaningful activity in the biomarker-defined population (X-B). A parallel four-level resistance scale ranges from clinically validated resistance (contraindication) to preclinical or computational evidence (research use only). CONCLUSIONS: ESCAT v2 provides a comprehensive, evidence-graded framework for interpreting actionability and resistance biomarkers in cancer, enabling more nuanced communication among clinicians, patients, regulators, and researchers while preserving a clear directive to act when evidence supports patient benefit.

papers.abstract_en: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. RESULTS: All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03164473.
