papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) is used for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but its effect on postoperative recurrence patterns remains uncertain. We compared overall, locoregional, and distant recurrence after NCIT versus neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT). METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 01 May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with resectable or potentially resectable locally advanced ESCC who received NCIT or NCRT followed by radical esophagectomy. Recurrence outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs), and disease-free survival or recurrence-free survival (DFS/RFS) and overall survival (OS) as hazard ratios (HRs), using random-effects models. Post hoc sensitivity analyses excluded studies with marked between-group follow-up imbalance. RESULTS: Twenty comparative studies, all conducted in China, were included; 19 were retrospective observational studies and one was a randomized phase 2 trial. Five studies contributed to the overall-recurrence analysis, and six studies contributed to each of the locoregional- and distant-recurrence analyses. NCIT was associated with lower overall recurrence (RR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.03) and distant recurrence/metastasis (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.43-0.89; P = 0.009), whereas locoregional recurrence did not differ significantly (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.67-1.55; P = 0.92). In post hoc analyses excluding studies with marked follow-up imbalance, the locoregional estimate remained nonsignificant (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.66-1.15), and the distant-recurrence/metastasis estimate was attenuated and no longer significant (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.36-1.17). Ten studies contributed to OS, which favored NCIT (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93; P = 0.02; I² = 77%), whereas eight contributed to DFS/RFS, which did not differ significantly (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.59-1.13; P = 0.21; I² = 74%). CONCLUSIONS: Compared with NCRT, NCIT was associated with fewer overall recurrences after radical esophagectomy for locally advanced ESCC. The primary distant-recurrence signal was not robust after excluding studies with marked follow-up imbalance, and no locoregional advantage was demonstrated. These findings do not establish therapeutic superiority and should be interpreted cautiously given the predominance of retrospective evidence, risk of bias, and substantial heterogeneity in survival analyses.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Long-term survival after lung transplant is limited by chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD). Oscillometry is a novel pulmonary function technique that complements spirometry. We hypothesise that oscillometry and spirometry at 3 months post-transplant are associated with CLAD. METHODS: Double lung transplant recipients (n=280) were enrolled from 2017 to 2020 for oscillometry at the first post-transplant spirometry. We excluded re-transplantation and patients missing 3-month oscillometry-spirometry data. Patients who died within 3 years where a CLAD diagnosis was ascertained were included. We used Mann-Whitney U and Pearson’s χ2 tests for group comparisons, logistic regression to assess the associations of spirometry and oscillometry with CLAD, and receiver operating characteristic curves to identify the threshold values for CLAD. RESULTS: At 3 years post-transplant, 129 were alive and CLAD-free while 75 patients had CLAD. Preoperative and perioperative characteristics were similar except for higher body mass index in the CLAD group. At 3 months, CLAD patients had lower forced expiratory volume in 1 s (%FEV1) and FEV1/FVC (forced vital capacity), and worst lung mechanics with high R5 (resistance at 5 Hz), low X5 (reactance at 5 Hz) and high AX (area of reactance). %FEV1, FEV1/FVC, R5 and R5−19 (difference in resistance from 5 to 19 Hz), X5, X5 z-score and AX were independently associated with CLAD. A composite metric of %FEV1, FEV1/FVC, R5 z-score, R5−19 and AX provided the strongest association with CLAD. CONCLUSIONS: The 3-month composite spirometry-oscillometry score post-transplant provides risk stratification of CLAD. Patients at risk can be monitored closely, to enable earlier interventions and minimise progression to CLAD.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: The aim of the study is to evaluate real-world clinical outcomes of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) for central (C) and ultracentral (UC) lung tumors, with a focus on toxicity, tumor control, and overall survival (OS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective analysis included 133 patients with C or UC lung tumors treated with SBRT across multiple participating centers. Patient characteristics, treatment parameters, toxicity outcomes, tumor control, and OS were analyzed retrospectively. RESULTS: Grade 2 toxicity occurred in 30.1% (n = 31/103) of patients with C tumors and 26.7% (n = 8/30) with UC tumors, while grade 3 toxicity was observed in 8.7% and 16.7% of patients, respectively. Median OS was 24 months. Favorable outcomes were observed in patients with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant disease and smaller planning target volumes (PTVs). Delivery of SBRT in conjunction with systemic therapies was feasible and associated with manageable toxicity profiles. CONCLUSION: In this multicenter real-world cohort, SBRT for C and UC lung tumors was associated with acceptable toxicity and clinically meaningful outcomes when delivered using contemporary techniques and cautious fractionation. Observations in selected subgroups, including patients with EGFR-mutant disease and smaller PTVs, should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and support individualized clinical decision-making in anatomically high-risk settings.

papers.abstract_en: University students with cancer in Italy face major barriers in maintaining their academic pathways despite existing disability legislation. This brief communication combines an overview of the Italian legal and institutional context with findings from a community-led qualitative descriptive needs-assessment. Following a national social media call, the analysis included semi-structured interviews with 69 eligible participants. Interviews were documented through contemporaneous written notes and analyzed manually using descriptive content analysis, combining domains from the interview guide with recurrent categories identified in open-ended responses. Participants described administrative burdens, inconsistent recognition of cancer-related needs, limited access to remote learning and flexible examinations, marked variability in university support, emotional distress, and social isolation. These findings provide preliminary real-world evidence of how existing arrangements are experienced by Italian university students affected by cancer. Although specific interventions were not evaluated, the findings may inform the development and prospective assessment of more consistent academic accommodations, accessible information, individualized support, and integrated psychosocial services.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: The use of evidence in clinical practice is essential for the provision of best practice care in psychosocial oncology. However, research demonstrates gaps in the implementation of evidence-based interventions and important resource barriers for clinicians. Clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) are designed to translate the latest evidence into recommendations applicable within various clinical domains. A recent study identified 23 English-language, up-to-date psychosocial oncology CPGs. The present study sought to systematically assess the quality of these tools. METHODS: CPGs were independently evaluated by four trained appraisers using the AGREE II tool, consisting of 23 items across six domains. Quality was determined using aggregate and consensus domain scores (0%-100%), with an acceptability cut-off score of 60%. RESULTS: Findings revealed that 20 of the 23 CPGs (87%) met the acceptability threshold (M = 76.45, SD = 12.35). The highest average domain scores were observed for Clarity of Presentation (M = 96.26, SD = 6.25) and Scope and Purpose (M = 87.38, SD = 19.55) while Applicability received the lowest score (M = 33.83, SD = 10.72). Rigor of Development scores (M = 71.17, SD = 17.46) demonstrated substantial variations across CPGs. CONCLUSIONS: Findings indicate that psychosocial oncology CPGs are specific and clear but may benefit from more transparency in reporting procedures and greater consideration of applicability and implementation strategies. These findings may help illuminate guideline developers on gaps in current tools and serve to inform clinicians on the strengths and shortcomings of these tools prior to selecting which ones to integrate within their clinical practice.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To explore the specific mechanism by which Siwuyin (SWY) inhibits esophageal cancer metastasis, verification focused on whether its effect is mediated by the fumarate-prolyl hydroxylase domain (PHD)-hypoxia-inducible factor-1 (HIF1α) signaling axis. METHODS: Network toxicology was employed to predict potential targets for exploring the pathways through which fumarate promotes esophageal cancer metastasis. In vitro, KYSE150 and Eca109 cells were treated with monomethyl fumarate (MMF, 50 or 100 µmol/mL) or SWY (150 µg/mL) for 24 h. Scratch and Transwell assays were used to detect cell migration and invasion abilities. Western blot was performed to examine the protein expression of prolyl hydroxylase (PHDs) family members, HIF1α, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers E-cadherin and vimentin. For in-vivo experiments, C57BL/6 mice were allocated into 5 groups. Esophageal carcinogenesis was induced by 4NQO in drinking water during weeks 1-16. The MMF-treated groups received intragastric administration of MMF at a dose of 30 mg/kg daily druing weeks 17-18. The SWY-treated groups were given 20% SWY solution at a dose of 400 mg/kg daily via drinking water druing weeks 17-24, and the remaining groups received plain drinking water. Western blot, immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry were applied to detect PHDs and HIF1α expression in mouse esophageal tissues, and HE staining was used to verify tumor metastasis. RESULTS: Network toxicology analysis suggestd that fumarate promoted esophageal cancer development by acting on the HIF1α signaling pathway. Fumarate accumulation promoted esophageal cancer cell migration and invasion. The underlying mechanism involved the downregulation of PHD2 and PHD3 by fumarate accumulation (P<0.01), leading to the stabilization and increased expression of HIF1α (P<0.01). This, in turn, facilitated a decrease in E-cadherin protein expression and an increase in vimentin protein expression, thereby promoting esophageal cancer cell metastasis (P<0.05 or P<0.01). SWY effectively suppressed the promotion of esophageal cancer cell migration and invasion by fumarate accumulation and acted on the PHD2/3-HIF1α signaling pathway (P<0.05 or P<0.01). CONCLUSION: Fumarate accumulation promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) metastasis, and SWY could inhibit ESCC cell metastasis by regulating the fumarate accumulation-mediated PHD2/3-HIF1α signaling pathway.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to describe the pricing, availability, and affordability of antineoplastics approved by the Food and Drug Administration from 2016 to 2021 and those on the 2021 World Health Organization Essential Medicine List (WHO EML) in 5 upper-middle-income South American countries (availability data only for Peru). METHODS: We collected publicly available data from Peru, Colombia, Brazil, Argentina, and Paraguay. Prices were converted to US dollars (USD) using purchasing power parities and reported per defined daily dose (DDD). Availability data were only available in Peru and were determined by the number of pharmacies stocking each drug. Affordability was measured as the number of days a minimum-wage worker would need to work to afford 1 DDD. RESULTS: Forty-one medications were included: 18 WHO EML and 23 non-EML drugs. Median prices were 230.42 USD/DDD and 761.25 USD/DDD for WHO EML and non-EML drugs, respectively. In Peru, >99% of cancer drugs were exclusively sold in privately owned pharmacies; only 13 non-EML drugs were available. Median affordability was 10.36 days and 27.55 days for the WHO EML and non-EML drugs, respectively. WHO EML drugs were most affordable for breast cancer (0.26 days) and least affordable for melanoma (37.68 days), whereas non-EML drugs were most affordable for prostate cancer (15.5 days) and least affordable for lung cancer (31.76 days). CONCLUSION: Prices are variable in upper-middle-income South American countries; newer therapies are more expensive and unaffordable, requiring more than 25 days of minimum wage work to afford 1 DDD of most non-EML drugs. Limited availability was evident in Peru. This highlights the need for policies to improve access to treatment in the region.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pneumonia, influenza, asthma, tuberculosis, lung cancer, and COVID-19 are all prevalent in Africa, where they cause a very large burden on the population's health, but are managed by health systems with a limited capacity for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. They are also underlaid by substantial inequities in outcomes, with the poorest who have no access to care being affected the most. An interdisciplinary group of academics, policymakers, representatives of non-governmental organisations (NGOs), patients, and civil society are implementing a programme to address key respiratory diseases (RD) in five African countries where morbidity and mortality from RD is very large: Nigeria, Kenya, Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire, and South Africa. The aim is to build capacity, conduct quality research and an intervention trial, and engage communities and policymakers in order to achieve demonstrable and equitable reductions in morbidity and mortality from RD through evidence-based improvements in prevention, diagnosis, treatment, interventions, and policies. The EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project will map the landscape of respiratory medicine in partner countries through rapid reviews of the available literature and data; engage relevant in-country stakeholders; study patients' and providers' preferences and needs; identify research priorities using the Child Health and Nutrition Research Initiative method; and conduct summer schools for capacity building in data science and machine learning/artificial intelligence, in community engagement, and in advocacy for and the use of the Equitable Impact Sensitive Tool (EQUIST) and Pathways to Survival (PATHS) tool. The project will also assess national health system preparedness for emerging infections, identify bottlenecks for early response, assess oxygen capacity and security, study adherence to international guidelines, and conduct qualitative studies to understand barriers to seeking care. It will also explore the feasibility of delivering a pulmonary rehabilitation programme through a randomised controlled trial. Ultimately, the programme will link evidence with policy using the EQUIST and PATHS tools to improve equity in outcomes and identify bottlenecks that lead to morbidity and mortality from respiratory causes. Through high-level meetings, it will prioritise the implementation of equitable interventions that are appropriate to each African context and tailored to patients' needs. A team of social scientists and NGOs, joined by a team of researchers of diverse backgrounds, will engage communities, stakeholders and policymakers to build capacity through summer schools, and disseminate the results through a dedicated project website, the Journal of Global Health, the Journal of the Pan-African Thoracic Society, collaborating NGOs, and mainstream and social media.

papers.abstract_en: Nile Blue (NB) is a red-emitting phenoxazine dye with affinity for DNA G-quadruplexes (G4s), yet its low fluorescence quantum yield in aqueous media and limited selectivity restrict biological applications. We synthesized three NB derivatives bearing hydroxy (5a), amino (5b), or carboxyl (5c) substituents. These derivatives exhibit blue-shifted absorption/emission maxima (approximately 40 nm) relative to NB, enhanced quantum yields (19-27% vs. 3% in aqueous buffer), and up to a 4-fold increase in brightness. Their interactions with parallel, hybrid, and antiparallel DNA G4s and a DNA hairpin were systematically investigated. The neutral 5a and positively charged 5b bound G4s presumably via stacking, resulting in hypochromism, red-shifted absorbance maxima, and fluorescence quenching. In turn, the negatively charged 5c showed negligible binding. Circular dichroism melting experiments revealed that 5a stabilizes only parallel G4s, whereas 5b stabilizes all G4 topologies, with neither compound affecting the DNA hairpin. Microscale thermophoresis demonstrated that 5b binds parallel G4s with submicromolar affinity, exhibiting up to 100- and 1000-fold selectivity over other G4 topologies and the DNA hairpin, respectively. Leveraging the efficient quenching of 5b by G4s, we suggested a red-fluorescent Nile Blue Displacement Assay (NBDA) for profiling G4 ligands, which provided dissociation constants comparable to those obtained in the standard thiazole orange-based displacement assay but with the advantage of monitoring emission enhancement in the red region. In cytotoxicity tests, 5b inhibited the proliferation of lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells with an IC50 value comparable to that of the G4 ligand pyridostatin and a superior selectivity index vs. non-cancerous HEK293T cells. Due to its enhanced photophysical properties and selective cytotoxicity, 5b is a promising lead for further studies as an antitumor and/or theranostic agent.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Type A thymoma is generally considered a low-risk thymoma subtype with an excellent prognosis and low rates of distant metastasis. Atypical type A thymoma is a recently established entity characterized by more aggressive biological behavior despite retaining the morphology of conventional type A thymoma. Patients with primary conventional type A thymoma who subsequently develop recurrence with atypical histological features are extremely rare. CASE PRESENTATION: A 79-year-old man was referred to our hospital due to gradual enlargement of bilateral pulmonary nodules. Seven years earlier, he had undergone complete resection of an anterior mediastinal tumor, which had been diagnosed as conventional type A thymoma. Retrospective review of preoperative computed tomography images revealed that small pulmonary nodules had already been present at the time of the initial surgery but had yet to be identified. The nodules enlarged slowly from 3 mm to 10 mm and from 3 mm to 7 mm over the 7-year period. Positron emission tomography showed no abnormal fluorodeoxyglucose uptake. After thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left lower lobe lesion, histopathological examination demonstrated pulmonary metastasis of type A thymoma with focal hypercellularity and increased mitotic activity, consistent with atypical type A thymoma. No necrosis was identified. The Ki-67 labeling indices of the primary and metastatic lesions were 7% and 20%, respectively. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that even apparently low-risk type A thymoma may exhibit indolent but metastatic behavior and may develop atypical histological features during a prolonged clinical course. Careful long-term surveillance and detailed pathological evaluation, including assessment of the Ki-67 labeling index, may be important in patients with type A thymoma.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The aim of the study was to report a case of severe vision-threatening intraocular inflammation with exudative retinal detachment presenting as a masquerade syndrome in a patient receiving dupilumab therapy for severe bronchial asthma. CASE PRESENTATION: A 51-year-old male with severe bronchial asthma developed sudden-onset no light perception (NLP) vision, iris rubeosis, pupillary seclusion, and total exudative retinal detachment in the right eye during his second cycle of dupilumab treatment. The clinical presentation raised strong suspicion for intraocular malignancy. Comprehensive evaluation including fluorescein and indocyanine green angiography, B-scan ultrasonography, magnetic resonance imaging, and positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) was performed. PET-CT demonstrated intense metabolic activity in the right eye (SUV max 19.6) and a pulmonary nodule (SUV max 3.5). Lung biopsy revealed inflammatory changes only, and vitreous sampling excluded malignancy. Dupilumab was discontinued, and systemic and topical corticosteroids were administered. Despite treatment, the eye remained NLP. The course was further complicated by sinusitis and orbital cellulitis, requiring hospitalization. Over more than 12 months of follow-up, the right eye progressed to chronic hypotony and gradual phthisis bulbi. Application of the Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale yielded a score of 6, classifying the association as probable. CONCLUSION: This case represents a severe dupilumab-associated ocular complication. Clinicians prescribing dupilumab should be vigilant for severe ocular adverse events beyond the commonly recognized conjunctivitis.

papers.abstract_en: Poly-(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) is highly expressed in various malignancies and represents an important therapeutic target. Noninvasive evaluation of PARP expression is therefore of potential clinical significance for patient stratification. In this study, we developed and evaluated [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827, a structurally modified PARP-targeted radiotracer derived from niraparib, featuring a two-carbon linker between the DOTA chelator and the pharmacophore. [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827 demonstrated high uptake in MDA-MB-231 and OE-19 tumors with elevated PARP-1 expression, which was significantly reduced by blocking, supporting a PARP-related component of tumor accumulation. The tracer exhibited favorable pharmacokinetics, including high hydrophilicity and predominantly renal clearance, resulting in low abdominal background activity. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging enabled clear tumor visualization with good contrast, supported by biodistribution findings. Preliminary clinical imaging further showed notable uptake in an esophageal cancer lesion, with immunohistochemical confirmation of PARP-1 expression in the biopsied tissue. These results suggest that [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827 has potential as a PARP-targeted PET tracer for tumor imaging and merits further investigation in larger clinical cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: The present case report describes the development of polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) in a 73-year-old male patient following lung cancer resection in the absence of prior exposure to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Following a left upper lobectomy, the patient presented with a persistent fever and diffuse myalgia and arthralgia, which was unresponsive to antibiotic therapy. Subsequently, the patient was treated with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory therapy, which led to rapid clinical improvement and complete resolution of PMR-associated symptoms during the 6-month follow-up. Unlike the well-recognized ICI-associated PMR, the present case highlights a distinct postoperative presentation, suggesting that tumor-associated inflammation and surgical stress may act as independent triggers. Through a literature review, the present study further explores the potential mechanistic links between lung cancer and PMR, including the role of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6. These findings provide additional insight into PMR pathogenesis beyond immunotherapy-related mechanisms and may aid in the differential diagnosis of an unexplained fever and musculoskeletal symptoms in postoperative patients with cancer.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy of intrapleural anti-PD-1 therapy in elderly patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) complicated by malignant pleural effusion (MPE), and to assess its impact on T-cell subset dynamics. METHODS: A total of 152 elderly patients (≥65 years) with advanced NSCLC and MPE were enrolled. All patients received a single intrapleural injection of anti-PD-1 antibody (Sintilimab, 100 mg) after thoracentesis and drainage. Clinical outcomes, adverse events, and quality-of-life measures were evaluated at baseline, 5 weeks, and 10 weeks after treatment. Concurrently, peripheral blood and pleural effusion T-cell subsets, as well as pleural effusion levels of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) were also measured. RESULTS: The pleural atresia rates at 5 and 10 weeks were 75.7% and 64.5%, respectively. The objective response rate (ORR) increased from 29.0% at 5 weeks to 38.2% at 10 weeks, and disease control rate (DCR) from 59.9% to 76.4%. Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score improved significantly from baseline (57.3 ± 9.6) to 5 weeks (66.5 ± 9.2) and 10 weeks (74.5 ± 8.3), Borg scores decreased from (6.1 ± 1.3) to (3.8 ± 0.9) and (3.1 ± 0.7), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores decreased from (4.5 ± 1.1) to (2.8 ± 0.5) and (2.2 ± 0.6) (all P<0.01). At 5 weeks, peripheral blood CD3+, CD4+, and CD8+ T cells increased from baseline (53.3 ± 8.6%, 28.25 ± 5.64%, 20.5 ± 4.6%) to (60.5 ± 9.5%, 32.5 ± 7.2%, and 25.2 ± 6.3%), while the CD4+/CD8+ ratio decreased from (1.38 ± 0.11) to (1.29 ± 0.12) (all P<0.01); in pleural effusion, corresponding values rose to (69.5 ± 4.3%, 34.5 ± 6.4%, and 28.8 ± 7.7%), with the ratio falling to (1.19 ± 0.04) (P<0.01). By 10 weeks, peripheral values further increased to (68.7 ± 8.4%, 36.2 ± 6.9%, and 30.5 ± 5.2%), and the ratio dropped to (1.19 ± 0.06) (P<0.01); pleural effusion values reached 74.5 ± 7.4% (CD3+), 37.1 ± 6.2% (CD4+), and 32.9 ± 7.3% (CD8+), with a ratio of 1.13 ± 0.05 (P<0.001). Pleural effusion levels of LDH, TNF-α, and IL-6 all declined from baseline (856.6 ± 130.2 U/L, 48.4 ± 2.3 pg/mL, 74.81 ± 9.17 pg/mL) to 5 weeks (512.5 ± 95.7 U/L, 32.3 ± 3.8 pg/mL, 52.8 ± 7.1 pg/mL) and 10 weeks (385.6 ± 74.8 U/L, 24.9 ± 2.6 pg/mL, 36.6 ± 5.4 pg/mL) (all P<0.01). Multivariable logistic regression identified that a higher baseline KPS score (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.05-1.32, P<0.01) and a lower baseline pleural effusion LDH level (OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.58-0.89, P<0.01) were independent protective factors, while a higher baseline peripheral blood CD4+/CD8+ ratio (OR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.48-0.88, P<0.01) was an independent negative predictor for 10-week DCR. CONCLUSION: Intrapleural administration of anti-PD-1 antibody is relatively safe and demonstrates effective control of MPE in elderly patients with advanced NSCLC. It improves performance status and quality of life, enhances both systemic and local T-cell immune responses, and reduces inflammatory cytokines and LDH levels in pleural effusion.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Late-stage cancer incidence is being considered as an earlier endpoint in cancer-screening trials, but its trial-level association with cancer-specific mortality may depend on evidence selection and endpoint harmonization. We evaluated the robustness of this association to source-verified additions. METHODS: We reconstructed the PubMed corpus underlying a 41-comparison review. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview was used only to prioritize reports for blinded human reassessment. Reviewers determined eligibility, linked reports from the same trial, harmonized endpoints, and verified comparison-level data. We recalculated unweighted Pearson correlations overall and by cancer type after adding earliest-compatible trial comparisons. RESULTS: Among 1209 candidate records, 996 PDFs were assessed. Thirty-three reports absent from the source review were prioritized; 26 were eligible, representing 18 trials, and 8 provided compatible comparisons. Adding these comparisons increased the dataset from 41 to 49 and attenuated the overall correlation from 0.73 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.55 to 0.85) to 0.59 (95% CI = 0.37 to 0.75). Updated correlations were 0.49 (95% CI = -0.26 to 0.87) for breast, - 0.23 (95% CI = -0.71 to 0.40) for colorectal, and 0.83 (95% CI = 0.54 to 0.95) for lung cancer. One sparse-event comparison influenced the colorectal estimate. CONCLUSIONS: The overall association was sensitive to evidence composition, and cancer-specific stability varied. Late-stage incidence should be evaluated by cancer type and with prespecified sensitivity analyses for evidence selection and endpoint definitions. Model-assisted prioritization cannot replace human eligibility review, trial reconciliation, and source verification.

papers.abstract_en: Predicting disease risk from prior diagnoses is fundamental to clinical decision-making, particularly during health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic, when individuals with long-term conditions may be disproportionately vulnerable to adverse outcomes. Despite intense interest in developing models to predict disease risk from prior diagnoses 1-3 , most prediction models do not estimate effects of each prior diagnosis on disease risk conditional on other diagnoses, limiting interpretability and clinical utility. We developed the Comorbidity Risk Score (CRS), trained on 13 million individuals (age 40-69) from linked electronic health record (EHR) datasets of the entire population of England, to predict COVID-19 hospitalisation and 87 other disease outcomes. CRS was trained at close to saturated sample size and precisely estimated the effects of 212 prior diagnoses on the 88 disease outcomes, conditional on all other prior diagnoses. Correlations of CRS effect sizes across outcomes (e.g. 0.76 for myocardial infarction vs. hyperlipidaemia) matched the corresponding genetic correlations (e.g. 0.79 for myocardial infarction vs. hyperlipidaemia), confirming that comorbidity architectures capture disease aetiology. On average, CRS identified 5% of the population with 3.4-fold higher disease risk, including myocardial infarction (4.4-fold), lung cancer (6.5-fold), and COVID-19 hospitalisation (6.3-fold). Using prior diagnoses alone, CRS outperformed state-of-the-art clinical COVID-19 models 4 . Furthermore, CRS ( N =13 million) substantially outperformed state-of-the-art AI 1 ( N =0.5 million) and linear 3 ( N =0.5 million) models in predicting disease risk, suggesting that training sample size outweighs model complexity. CRS attained near-perfect transferability across self-reported ethnicities (e.g., Black vs. White: AUROC ratio = 97.3%). Finally, CRS distinguished independently predictive comorbidities from indirect associations, e.g., lipid metabolism disorder was a strong predictor of myocardial infarction risk but not ischaemic stroke, after conditioning on other prior diagnoses. In conclusion, CRS provides a comprehensive resource for understanding the impact of comorbidities on COVID-19 and other future diseases, revealing disease aetiology while enabling powerful prediction of disease risk.

Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed to compare groups, as well as multivariate logistic regression, identifying, at the municipal level, factors associated with the outcomes. Adjusted odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were obtained. RESULTS: A total of 206,703 deaths and 89,265 cases (43% coverage) were analyzed. Approximately 85.7% of patients were diagnosed at a late stage, and half of the cases with initial staging did not receive adequate treatment. In Model 1, a lack of RHC coverage was associated with municipalities in the Central-West region compared to those in the North [OR 3.9; 95%CI 2.7; 5.7] and with those having a Gross Domestic Product below the national average [OR 1.3; 95%CI 1.1; 1.7]. In Model 2, municipalities in the South [OR 9.1; 95% CI 6.8; 12.2], small-sized municipalities [OR 7.1; 95%CI 4.0; 12.3], and those with below-average travel distances for treatment [OR 4.2; 95%CI 2.3; 7.7] had increased odds of a high registration rate. CONCLUSION: Localities with better infrastructure were more likely to register cases and have greater coverage of registries, while areas with poorer infrastructure were more likely not to register cases, despite presenting deaths due to lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: Unmeasured confounding threatens causal inference and replicability in observational multi-omic studies across variable environments. Genetic instrumental variables (Mendelian randomization) and negative-control calibration each address complementary sources of unmeasured confounding, yet no existing framework unifies them for omics-scale mediation analysis. We introduce ICONIC, an R package that embeds genetic instruments and negative controls within a proximal causal inference framework for total-effect and mediation analysis. ICONIC implements eight estimators spanning five confounding-control strategies, supports continuous, binary, and time-to-event outcomes, and provides extensive diagnostics including sensitivity analyses that map estimator performance across plausible assumptions. Ground-truth benchmarks are calibrated to real-omics covariance structures via a hybrid generative model (GAN + feature-level Gaussian copula) rather than parametric simulation, and a companion planning tool predicts performance gains from collecting additional omic data. We demonstrate ICONIC in two case studies: screening for placental transcriptomic mediators of gestational diabetes on birth weight (n = 164), and tumor-expression mediators of smoking intensity on lung cancer survival (n = 494). Notably, ICONIC's diagnostics recommended different estimation strategies across the two scenarios, reflecting differences in the likely influence of unmeasured confounding. ICONIC is freely available at https://github.com/sbresnahan/iconic/ .

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening reduces lung cancer mortality but is limited by low uptake and associated with high rates of false-positives and indeterminate-nodules. Breath volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis is a non-invasive candidate biomarker approach that could complement LDCT, but prior work has relied on laboratory-based high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), limiting point-of-care deployment. METHODS: In this pilot study, breath samples were collected from 40 patients with treatment-naïve, pathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 25 lung-cancer-screening-eligible healthy controls. Paired samples were analyzed via a compact point-of-care GC-MS platform (CLARION) and a laboratory HRMS reference. Diagnostic classification models were built independently for each platform using elastic net logistic regression with leave-one-out cross-validation, and performance was evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: CLARION identified 103 VOCs across breath specimens, compared to over 900 identified by HRMS. Despite this difference in panel size, CLARION achieved diagnostic performance nearly identical to HRMS for distinguishing NSCLC cases from controls (AUC 0.864 vs. 0.863). Compared to controls, performance statistics were similar for early-stage NSCLC (AUC 0.854 vs. 0.841) and adenocarcinoma (AUC 0.770 vs. 0.787). VOCs of interest include p-cymene, phenol, propylbenzene, tetradecane, β-ocimene, 2,3-dihydro-indole, and 1-methylthio-(Z)-1-propene. CONCLUSION: A compact, point-of-care breath GC-MS platform achieved diagnostic performance for NSCLC detection comparable to a laboratory HRMS reference despite a substantially smaller detected VOC panel. These findings support continued development of point-of-care breath VOC testing as a non-invasive, field-deployable complement to LDCT-based lung cancer screening.

papers.abstract_en: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) enables spatially resolved metabolomics in intact tissue sections, but analysis remains challenging at scale. Existing MSI workflows often require users to combine multiple software tools, while others rely on proprietary vendor software that limits interoperability and reproducibility. To address these challenges, we developed spatialMET, an open-source framework that provides an end-to-end workflow for MSI analysis. spatialMET provides a unified platform for preprocessing, spatial domain detection, and visualization. Downstream analyses include differential abundance testing, spatial autocorrelation and gradient analysis, dimensionality reduction, and correlation network analysis. Spatial domain detection uses hcdist, a C-based hierarchical clustering implementation that substantially reduces runtime and memory use relative to existing R-based approaches. spatialMET can be run through an interactive R Shiny application or as a standalone command-line workflow for larger datasets or high-performance computing environments. Applied to mouse small cell lung cancer MALDI-MSI data containing 284,673 pixels, spatialMET identified tumor-associated, stromal, and adjacent lung spatial domains that aligned with matched histology. Differential abundance analysis identified 117 m/z features that differed between tumor and stromal regions, while spatial autocorrelation analyses revealed spatially structured abundance patterns. Applying spatialMET to mouse lung adenocarcinoma data from an entire lung lobe containing 338,477 pixels further demonstrated scalability and captured spatial heterogeneity across tumor and surrounding lung tissue. In summary, spatialMET provides a scalable, open-source framework for end-to-end spatial metabolomics analysis, and it is distributed as a Docker container for reproducible deployment. Source code and installation instructions are available at https://github.com/biodatalab/spatialMET .

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) patients have an ∼8% 5-year survival; new therapies are urgently needed. Approximately 15% of SCLC patients have naturally-occurring low-titer antibodies against neuronal ELAVL proteins, associated with improved response to therapy and significantly improved survival. We previously determined that the anti-ELAVL4 response is triggered by isoaspartylation in the unstructured ELAVL4 N-terminal region. METHODS: We used a Tp53 fl/fl ; Rb1 fl/fl inducible SCLC mouse model to test whether 1) immunization with isoaspartylated Elavl4 (isoAsp-Elavl4) prior to SCLC induction improves survival in the absence of any other treatment, and 2) immunization with isoAsp-Elavl4 following completion of 3 rounds of cisplatin+etoposide therapy improves survival. Immunizations contained incomplete Freund's adjuvant with either a recombinant N-terminal fragment of Elavl4 (amino acids 1-117), incubated under isoaspartyl-inducing conditions, or phosphate-buffered saline (used as the negative control, since Elavl4 spontaneously isoaspartylates). Mice were monitored by blinded assessors until euthanasia was indicated. RESULTS: IsoAsp-Elavl4-immunized animals all became immune responsive, and spontaneous anti-isoAsp-Elavl4 antibodies were observed in 7% of the control animals. Kaplan-Meier analyses revealed that pre-SCLC immunization with isoAsp-ELAVL4 in the absence of other treatments did not affect survival. In contrast, immunization of SCLC mice following chemotherapy significantly improved survival. CONCLUSIONS: An anti-isoAsp-ELAVL4 response can be actively induced in mice and significantly increases SCLC survival when given following chemotherapy. This indicates that the anti-isoAsp-ELAVL4 immune response can be leveraged to develop new therapies for SCLC patients.

papers.abstract_en: Three-dimensional (3D) chromosome reconstruction from Hi-C contact maps remains challenging because genome organization is hierarchical and fine-resolution models must reconcile local structure with chromosome-scale constraints. Here we present HiC-LEGO, a domain-aware hierarchical framework integrating ensemble chromatin domains with graph-based structural learning and progressive chromosome assembly. By combining ensemble domain selection with hierarchical reconstruction, HiC-LEGO reduces dependence on individual domain definitions while maintaining local organization during chromosome-scale assembly. Across five human cell lines at 5-kb resolution, HiC-LEGO achieves higher reconstruction concordance than evaluated state-of-the-art methods while better preserving domain organization. At 1-kb resolution, HiC-LEGO reconstructs complete GM12878 chromosome 8 and recovers close spatial proximity between an epigenomically supported distal MYC enhancer and its promoter. Reconstructions from 5-kb Micro-C data show that 249 experimentally defined RCMC microcompartment interactions at the Ppm1g locus occupy compact 3D configurations. In the breast cancer dataset, HiC-LEGO reconstructs structures that maintain stable TAD organization across healthy breast, primary tumors, and liver metastases, while revealing greater inter-patient structural heterogeneity in malignant pleural effusion samples. Pore-C validation shows that experimentally observed multi-way contacts spanning 1-5 Mb are enriched in compact reconstructed configurations across all 23 chromosomes. Thus, HiC-LEGO preserves regulatory interactions, disease-associated chromatin organization and higher-order spatial relationships beyond pairwise contact-map concordance.

papers.abstract_en: People with lung cancer commonly experience stigma, however, the temporal impacts are poorly understood. This study investigated changes (using linear mixed modelling) and trajectories (using latent growth modelling) of stigma over a 6-month period in people newly diagnosed with lung cancer, who were participants of a larger trial of supportive care interventions (ACTRN12615000932561). Participants (n = 192) completed surveys which included the Cataldo Lung Cancer Stigma Scale. Lung cancer stigma did not vary significantly over time, with mean scores of 53.2 ± 15.6 and 54.0 ± 16.7 reported at recruitment and 6 months respectively (range 31-124, higher scores indicate greater stigma). Two main trajectory patterns were identified: (1) 'Relatively lower stigma trajectory'; and (2) 'Relatively higher stigma trajectory'. Relatively higher stigma trajectories were associated with younger age and a history of smoking. Further research is warranted to identify strategies to reduce lung cancer stigma and explore differences across sub-groups and stages of the lung cancer continuum.

papers.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based technologies have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy while reducing tissue loss in small biopsies. In non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), small biopsies often limit ancillary testing. We aimed to develop a deep learning-based framework for automated histopathological classification of NSCLC subtypes. Archived hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images from 341 NSCLC and benign specimens were digitized and annotated by two expert pathologists. A two-stage Dense Net121-based cascade was employed: Stage 1 differentiated not otherwise specified (NOS) from not-NOS specimens; Stage 2 classified not-NOS into adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or non-cancerous tissue. Patient-level predictions were derived via majority voting. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. In Stage 1, NOS versus not-NOS classification achieved 0.92 patient-level accuracy. In Stage 2, accuracy for adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and non-cancer was 0.94, with perfect classification of non-cancer patients (precision, recall, and F1 = 1.00). In the final step, the combined analysis demonstrated an overall accuracy of 0.88, with recall rates of 1.00 for adenocarcinoma and non-cancer, 0.83 for squamous cell carcinoma, and 0.67 for NOS. The proposed two-stage model demonstrated strong performance across NSCLC subtypes, including the diagnostically challenging NOS group. This approach may reduce reliance on ancillary tests, accelerate diagnosis, and optimize tissue preservation.

papers.abstract_en: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are rare cancer-derived cells in peripheral blood, carrying vital information about tumor heterogeneity and progression. Their reliable detection remains challenging due to extreme rarity and high background interference. Herein, we report an electrochemical biosensor that integrates a DNA-based AND logic gate with cascaded signal amplification for the specific and sensitive determination of CTCs. The system requires the co-recognition of EpCAM and MUC1 on the cell surface via corresponding aptamers, which initiates an amplification cascade comprising hybridization chain reaction, DNAzyme-mediated cleavage, and entropy-driven assembly. This cascade ultimately results in the in situ formation of a DNA network on the electrode, enabling the capture of platinum-coated gold nanoparticles (Au@PtNPs) via biotin-streptavidin interaction, thereby significantly enhancing the electrocatalytic signal. The biosensor exhibits a linear response from 50 to 2.5 × 105 cells mL-1 with a detection limit down to 14 cells mL-1. It also exhibits high selectivity against nontarget cells, isolated proteins, and cellular debris, and displays excellent stability in serum and whole blood. Thus, this work may provide a reliable and clinically translatable strategy for CTC-based liquid biopsy, highlighting its potential for personalized lung cancer management.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is a dynamically evolving disease characterized by marked temporal heterogeneity across tumor progression, treatment response, resistance development, and clinical outcomes. Nevertheless, the majority of existing artificial intelligence (AI) systems continue to rely predominantly on single time-point imaging, imposing inherent constraints on their capacity to characterize disease evolution and capture continuously shifting risk states. The growing availability of longitudinal imaging data, combined with ongoing advances in temporal deep learning, is driving a transition in lung cancer AI from static image interpretation toward dynamic risk prediction. In this narrative review, relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from database inception to September 2026, using terms related to lung cancer, longitudinal imaging, temporal deep learning, and dynamic risk prediction, with representative studies selected according to their methodological relevance, clinical applications, and implications for clinical translation. Longitudinal imaging tracks disease trajectories over time and offers distinct opportunities to characterize tumor growth dynamics, treatment-induced changes, and evolving recurrence risk. Temporal deep learning, in turn, enables the modelling of complex time-dependent relationships that conventional static approaches are poorly suited to represent. The field has progressed from early dual time-point analyses to long-range temporal modelling, multimodal temporal fusion, and continuous risk updating, with encouraging applications spanning pulmonary nodule management, treatment response assessment, recurrence surveillance, survival prediction, and individualized disease management. Nonetheless, substantial obstacles persist, including the scarcity of large-scale longitudinal datasets, irregular temporal sampling, limited model generalizability, insufficient causal interpretability, and a lack of robust evidence supporting real-world clinical deployment. Addressing these challenges will require coordinated efforts toward standardized longitudinal data infrastructure, continuous-time modelling frameworks, multimodal integration strategies, and closer alignment of AI systems with clinical workflows. Taken together, longitudinal imaging and temporal deep learning are steering lung cancer AI away from static image analysis and toward dynamic disease management, with the potential to support continuous risk assessment and potentially inform adaptive clinical decision-making throughout the full spectrum of lung cancer care.

papers.abstract_en: Epigenetic age, influenced by environmental factors like smoking, predicts mortality in general populations but remains under-explored in early-stage lung cancer. We analyzed blood DNA methylation from 75 Boston Lung Cancer Study participants with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), of whom 63 died during follow-up. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was estimated using Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, and GrimAge2 clocks and assessed using Cox models and random survival forests (RSFs). Across clocks, EAA significantly predicted survival in early-stage NSCLC. GrimAge2 EAA achieved the highest predictive accuracy (C index = 0.73±0.04) and emerged as the dominant predictor of survival among RSF models (variable importance = 5.7%), surpassing smoking and age. GrimAge2 EAA showed a non-linear association with mortality in which current smokers had >10% higher predicted mortality risk than former or never smokers at equivalent EAA, a pattern confirmed in Kaplan-Meier analyses. GrimAge2 EAA is a promising biomarker for personalizing risk stratification alongside traditional clinical factors.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Garsorasib (D-1553) is an orally administered selective KRAS G12C inhibitor. We report results from group 1 of the phase 1b D1553-101 study assessing garsorasib plus pembrolizumab and platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC. METHODS: Eligible participants had locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with KRAS G12C mutation and were candidates for pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy. Participants received garsorasib 600 mg once daily or twice daily combined with pembrolizumab 200 mg once every 3 weeks plus 4 to 6 cycles of cisplatin or carboplatin and pemetrexed (nonsquamous histology) or carboplatin and paclitaxel (squamous histology). The primary end points were safety and the incidence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs). RESULTS: As of February 24, 2024, 17 participants received garsorasib 600 mg once daily (n = 10) or twice daily (n = 7) combined with pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy. Overall, 94% of participants experienced grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs), and 88% had a dose reduction or interruption due to treatment-related AEs. One participant in the twice-daily group experienced a DLT of grade 2 diarrhea; no other DLTs occurred. Among all participants, the objective response rate was 59%, and the median progression-free survival was 7.4 months. CONCLUSION: In participants with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, despite an encouraging signal of efficacy, the incidence of treatment-related AEs with garsorasib plus pembrolizumab and platinum-based chemotherapy was high, and participants frequently had dose modifications or interruptions due to treatment-related AEs. Based on these findings, the study did not proceed to phase 2. CLINICALTRIALSGOV IDENTIFIER: NCT04585035.

This narrative review examines the metabolic and immune conditions under which ferroptosis may enhance ICI responsiveness or resensitize selected ICI-refractory tumors. Radiotherapy (RT) increases oxidizable phospholipids and can repress SLC7A11, the light-chain component of system xc-. ICI-activated CD8+ T cells provide convergent interferon-γ signaling. Tumors can resist this pressure through GPX4, FSP1-CoQ10, mitochondrial DHODH, NRF2-dependent programs, and iron-export pathways. Recent preclinical studies have tested RT with ferroptosis-directed interventions and ICIs. These studies include functional evidence of ferroptosis dependence in radioresistant lung cancer and resensitization of LKB1-deficient, primarily ICI-refractory tumors. The findings support a preclinical rationale for combination therapy, although their causal strength varies. Reversal of clinically defined acquired ICI resistance remains unestablished, and the clinical RT-ICI studies reviewed here did not measure ferroptosis in patients. The immune effects also vary by cell type. Tumor-cell ferroptosis may support immunity, whereas lipid peroxidation in CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, or polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells can impair antitumor responses. Translation will require functional validation, cell-resolved biomarkers, achievable drug exposures, and evaluation of RT dose, fractionation, and sequence alongside normal-tissue and immune-cell safety.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved dramatically over the past decade with the advent of widespread genetic testing, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies. Treatments directed against epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and other driver mutations have reduced toxicity and improved efficacy for selected patients. CASE PRESENTATION: We present a 59-year-old man with metastatic NSCLC harboring coexisting EGFR, BRCA1, and RNA-binding motif protein 10 (RBM10) mutations and high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. A BRCA2 mutation was later detected on peripheral blood testing. The patient presented with a debilitating stroke that included dysphagia and hemiparesis. During his course of care, he received osimertinib, after which EGFR and RBM10 variant allele frequencies (VAFs) increased on peripheral blood testing. He also received immunotherapy and olaparib. Despite high response rates reported in the literature, he did not respond to these agents. He had a response to chemotherapy but tolerated it poorly. Ultimately, given the lack of durable response and his inability to tolerate chemotherapy, the patient opted for palliative care. DISCUSSION: Patients with actionable targets such as EGFR, BRCA1/2, or elevated PD-L1 generally have superior outcomes with targeted and combination therapy compared with patients who lack targetable options. However, coexisting mutations can interact and provide escape mechanisms. The lack of response in our patient is consistent with studies showing reduced efficacy of EGFR-directed therapy in the presence of RBM10 loss-of-function (LOF) alterations. Further research in patients with multiple concurrent mutations is needed to improve treatment options for this group.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Oncogenic KRAS mutations drive 25-30% of western lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cases, however the mechanisms that restrain tumor progression remain poorly defined. N-Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (N-WASP) regulates actin cytoskeleton dynamics and epithelial architecture, but its role in KRAS-driven lung tumorigenesis is unclear. METHODS: We generated a conditional N-WASP knockout in KRASG12D-driven lung adenocarcinoma mice (N-WASPLKO/KRASG12D) using Sftpc-CreERT2, and assessed N-WASP knockdown A549 cells (A549KD) in 3D culture for tumor burden, ERK signaling, transcriptomic changes, and E-cadherin expression. RESULTS: Conditional deletion of N-WASP in type II alveolar cells (N-WASPLKO) markedly increased tumor number and size in KRASG12D mice. The tumors isolated from these mice retained strong pro-surfactant protein C expression, confirming alveolar epithelial origin and predominantly adopted a solid growth pattern, indicative of disrupted epithelial organization. Mechanistically, N-WASP loss enhanced KRAS-driven ERK1/2 activation in lung tissue, consistent with increased mitogenic signaling. In A549 cells, N-WASP deficiency disrupted cytoskeletal architecture, promoted proliferation, and impaired cell-cell adhesion, recapitulating in vivo tumor phenotypes. A kinase inhibitor screen identified Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) activity as a driver of this hyperproliferative phenotype, with ROCK inhibition normalizing proliferation in N-WASP-deficient cells, linking elevated Rho/ROCK signaling to the increased ERK1/2 activation observed upon N-WASP loss. Transcriptomic profiling of N-WASP-deficient lungs revealed coordinated upregulation of genes regulating proliferation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and tumor-promoting pathways, alongside downregulation of epithelial differentiation and adhesion programs. CONCLUSION: These results establish N-WASP as a critical suppressor of KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma, linking cytoskeletal integrity to oncogenic signaling and transcriptional regulation. Our findings highlight the interplay between actin dynamics, epithelial architecture, and KRAS signaling, suggesting that targeting N-WASP dependent pathways could modulate lung cancer aggressiveness and offer novel therapeutic opportunities.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Cisplatin has been a standard chemotherapeutic agent for advanced non-small cell lung cancer for decades. Conventionally administered intravenously, it undergoes systemic distribution, exposing both tumour and healthy tissues to the drug. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle injection of cisplatin is emerging as a potential intratumoural drug delivery (ITDD) strategy. However, rigorous preclinical research is needed before ITDD can be more widely adopted. METHODS: We used our experimentally induced ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA) model, generated by Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV) infection, to evaluate transthoracic and transbronchial ITDD techniques. We compared systemic platinum exposure following intravenous cisplatin delivery with that following intratumoural cisplatin administration. Both non-recovery and recovery studies were conducted in a total of eight sheep. RESULTS: ITDD techniques were successfully developed and performed in three tumour bearing sheep during non-recovery procedures. To provide a reference for systemic platinum exposure, intravenous cisplatin was administered to three JSRV-infected sheep that did not develop OPA. Intravenous administration produced a rapid plasma platinum peak followed by a rapid decline. ITDD resulted in preferential platinum deposition within targeted lung tumours while producing substantially lower systemic platinum exposure compared with intravenous administration. Intratumoural cisplatin delivery was also evaluated in a recovery procedure using a single sheep, comparing single-site and fractionated administration over a 28-day period, with tumour biopsies confirming lesion presence before treatment. Following ITDD, tumour volumes were observed to decrease over the study period. The recovery experiments demonstrated the feasibility of repeated tumour biopsies, intratumoural injections, longitudinal CT monitoring and recovery anaesthesia using the OPA model. DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first report of direct intratumoural cisplatin administration into ovine lung tumours. This study also provides proof-of-concept that this clinically relevant large animal lung cancer model can serve as a translational platform for evaluating intratumoural therapeutic delivery strategies relevant to human lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) are standard first-line therapy for psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Observational studies suggest earlier initiation is associated with superior minimal disease activity (MDA) attainment, yet the economic and health implications of treatment timing remain uncertain. This cost-utility analysis evaluated the cost-effectiveness of early versus delayed DMARD initiation in DMARD-naive adults with PsA from a U.S. payer perspective. METHODS: We built a cohort state-transition (Markov) model (monthly cycles, 15-year horizon) from published data (2000-2025). Patients initiated a DMARD under two strategies: early (≤1 year post-diagnosis) and delayed initiation (>1 year). Patients remained in the pre-treatment state for six months prior to response assignment, then transitioned among complete response (sustained MDA), partial response (non-sustained MDA), non-response, no treatment, and death. Primary outcomes included the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) and incremental net monetary benefit (INMB). Uncertainty intervals (UIs) were derived from probabilistic sensitivity analyses. FINDINGS: Early DMARD initiation provided an additional 0.56 (95% UI, 0.32-0.83) QALYs at an incremental cost of -US$43,902.94 (95% UI, -US$147,096.29 to US$61,615.86) per patient relative to delayed initiation, yielding a favourable ICER (-US$78,398.11/QALY). At a willingness-to-pay threshold of US$50,000/QALY, mean INMB was US$71,902.94 (95% UI, -US$36,663.51 to US$176,658.91), with early initiation preferred in 90.6% of simulations. INTERPRETATION: Early DMARD initiation was associated with improved long-term health outcomes at reduced costs, suggesting timely DMARD initiation may represent a high-value strategy. Given the observational basis of the key treatment-timing input, findings support disease-duration stratified analyses of existing phase III trials and further characterization of access delays. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: This study elucidates the distinct roles of Wrap53 isoforms (1α/1β) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) radiosensitivity through integrated bioinformatics and functional analyses. Bioinformatics revealed Wrap53-associated enrichment in DNA repair and p53 pathways, with TCGA data linking its expression to prognosis and chemotherapy response. Functional studies demonstrated isoform- and p53 context-dependent effects: In p53-wild type A549 cells, Wrap53-1α silencing upregulated p53, enhanced radiosensitivity through Bax/Bcl-2-mediated apoptosis, and impaired DNA repair through RAD51 recombinase (RAD51)/Breast cancer susceptibility gene 1 (BRCA1) regulation. Conversely, in p53-mutant H1975 cells, silencing either Wrap53-1α or Wrap53-1β individually increased colony formation. Wrap53-1α was found to modulate post-radiation G2/M arrest through cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1) regulation, with effects contingent on p53 status. Importantly, Wrap53 expression correlated with differential chemosensitivity. High Wrap53 tumors showed increased cisplatin sensitivity but resistance to docetaxel, while low-expressing tumors were resistant to paclitaxel and vinca alkaloids. Our findings reveal a previously unappreciated inverse correlation between Wrap53-1α and p53 in LUAD cells and establish a molecular network where Wrap53 isoforms and p53 status collectively determine LUAD radiosensitivity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Previous studies on diet and cancer have mainly examined individual dietary indices in relation to specific cancer outcomes, limiting direct comparison across dietary patterns. A unified population with consistent adjustment and standardized dietary-index scales is needed to explore whether different dietary patterns show different statistical associations with each specific cancer outcome. METHODS: We included 118,056 cancer-free UK Biobank participants with at least two valid 24-h dietary assessments. Six predefined dietary indices were evaluated: DRLCD, aMED, AHEI-2010, DASH, CDAI, and E-DII. All indices were standardized to enable direct comparison. Progressively adjusted Cox regression models and 1-, 3-, and 5-year lagged sensitivity analyses were used as the primary analysis to identify the most stable diet-cancer outcome pairs. In the exploratory analysis, after excluding potential non-linear associations, standardized dietary indices were compared for colorectal, kidney, and lung cancers in the overall population and high genetic risk group to compare the direction and magnitude of associations across dietary patterns for each cancer outcome. RESULTS: Eleven robust diet-cancer associations were identified. AHEI-2010 and DASH were inversely associated with colorectal cancer; AHEI-2010, aMED, CDAI, DASH, and reversed E-DII were inversely associated with kidney cancer; AHEI-2010, aMED, and reversed E-DII were inversely associated with lung cancer; and reversed E-DII was associated with lower overall cancer risk. DRLCD showed no robust association. In cross-index comparisons, the lowest HRs in the overall population were for DASH (colorectal cancer), reversed E-DII (kidney cancer), and AHEI-2010 (lung cancer); in the higher PRS group, they were for DASH (colorectal cancer), AHEI-2010 (kidney cancer), and reversed E-DII (lung cancer). However, bootstrap pairwise comparisons were not statistically significant, suggesting directional trends, not evidence of superiority. CONCLUSION: We identified significant and stable diet-cancer risk associations and observed differences in the direction or magnitude of associations across dietary indices. Because bootstrap pairwise comparisons were not statistically significant, these findings should be interpreted as directional trends and hypothesis-generating, not as evidence of a definitively optimal dietary strategy or dietary superiority.

papers.abstract_en: ObjectiveTo review the mechanism of action, clinical efficacy, safety considerations and future development of bispecific T-cell engagers (BTCEs) in solid tumors.Data sourcesA literature search was conducted using PubMed for clinical trials leading to FDA approvals and major oncology conference proceedings through February 2026. Major ongoing clinical trials were identified through a search of clinicaltrials.gov. Search terms included "bispecific T-cell engager," "BiTE," "solid tumors," "tarlatamab," and "tebentafusp." Prescribing information was also evaluated.Data summaryBTCEs are antibodies designed to redirect cytotoxic T-cells toward tumor cells through binding of CD3 and tumor-associated antigens. FDA approvals of tebentafusp for HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic uveal melanoma and tarlatamab for extensive stage small cell lung cancer have established utility of BTCE therapy in solid malignancies, with improved outcomes over conventional chemotherapy and immunotherapy. BTCEs have unique toxicities, such as cytokine release syndrome, that must be monitored and treated appropriately. Ongoing investigations are evaluating novel targets, optimized molecular constructs to overcome development challenges, including toxicity and tumor microenvironment barriers, as well as combination treatment strategies to improve the efficacy of BTCEs in solid tumors.ConclusionsTebentafusp and tarlatamab have established proof of concept for BTCE therapy in solid tumors, bridging the gap from hematologic malignancies. This class of therapy represents a promising platform for expanding applications across tumor types. Continued advances in target selection and strategies to overcome the tumor microenvironment and T-cell evasion barriers are expected to further expand the role of BTCEs in solid tumors.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Mediastinal epidermoid cysts are exceptionally rare benign lesions, particularly in the anterior mediastinum. Their nonspecific clinical and radiological features may resemble other anterior mediastinal masses, including thymic lesions and mature cystic teratomas, making preoperative diagnosis challenging. CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old man with no relevant medical or surgical history presented with a 2-month history of retrosternal chest pain. Clinical examination and cardiac evaluation were unremarkable. Chest radiography demonstrated mediastinal widening, while contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a well-defined anterior mediastinal mass measuring approximately 7 × 5 × 3 cm. CT-guided biopsy and fluid aspiration initially suggested a mature cystic teratoma without immature or malignant elements. The patient underwent complete excision using a three-port video-assisted thoracoscopic approach. Intraoperatively, the cyst was densely adherent to the pericardium and contained thick purulent material. Hair-like material and firm cartilage-like areas were observed grossly but were not confirmed histologically. Culture of the cyst contents yielded Staphylococcus aureus. Histopathological examination demonstrated a squamous epithelial lining with chronic inflammation, granulation tissue, and fibrosis, confirming an infected mediastinal epidermoid cyst. The discrepancy between the initial cytological impression and the final histopathological diagnosis highlights the limitations of imaging and needle biopsy in evaluating rare cystic mediastinal lesions. CONCLUSION: Complete surgical excision provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment. Epidermoid cysts should be considered in the differential diagnosis of cystic anterior mediastinal masses. Video-assisted thoracoscopic excision may be feasible in carefully selected patients, even in the presence of dense pericardial adhesions.

papers.abstract_en: ALK rearrangements are uncommon in lung squamous cell carcinoma, and neoadjuvant ALK inhibition remains investigational. We report a 52-year-old never-smoking female with stage IIIB ALK-positive squamous cell carcinoma treated with neoadjuvant lorlatinib for 12 weeks. Serial imaging demonstrated a 61% reduction in tumor size with nodal regression. The patient subsequently underwent a uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic (uVATS) lobectomy, and final pathology revealed a complete pathological response (pCR) of the primary tumor. This case highlights the feasibility and safety of minimally invasive anatomical lung resection following neoadjuvant lorlatinib despite treatment-related hilar fibrosis and vascular-bronchial adhesions.

papers.abstract_en: Thymic cysts are uncommon benign lesions of the anterior mediastinum and are frequently detected incidentally on imaging studies. Microscopic thymoma and microthymoma are extremely rare microscopic thymic epithelial proliferations that are usually identified only by histopathological examination. Their relationship to thymic cysts and to each other remains poorly understood. A 54-year-old woman was referred to our institution after an anterior mediastinal lesion was incidentally detected on routine chest computed tomography (CT). Magnetic resonance imaging and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT findings were consistent with a thymic cyst. Robot-assisted thoracoscopic resection of the cyst with the adjacent thymic tissue was performed for definitive diagnosis and treatment. Histopathological examination revealed a unilocular thymic cyst accompanied by two incidental microscopic thymic epithelial lesions within the adjacent thymic tissue: a 0.6-mm microscopic thymoma and a 2.0-mm Type A microthymoma. Based on their characteristic size and histological features, both lesions were diagnosed without additional immunohistochemical analysis. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remains free of recurrence 18 months after surgery. To our knowledge, the coexistence of microscopic thymoma and Type A microthymoma adjacent to a thymic cyst is exceptionally rare. The close proximity and similar histological features of these lesions suggest that they may represent different stages within a continuous morphological spectrum of microscopic thymic epithelial proliferations rather than entirely distinct entities. Furthermore, this case highlights the potential value of careful pathological examination of thymic tissue adjacent to resected thymic cysts for detecting occult microscopic epithelial lesions and improving pathological assessment.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a recently recognized, rare, and highly aggressive malignancy. No standard treatment has been established for unresectable disease, and the prognosis is generally poor. These tumors often grow rapidly, and bulky masses can cause clinically significant symptoms. CASE PRESENTATION: A 52-year-old man with a history of heavy smoking presented with chest and back pain. Imaging revealed a large mediastinal mass. A CT-guided biopsy demonstrated an undifferentiated neoplasm with complete loss of BRG1 (SMARCA4) expression, a high proliferative index (Ki-67 labeling index, 80%), and no evidence of specific lineage differentiation, findings consistent with SMARCA4-UT. Subsequent comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a SMARCA4 nonsense mutation and a high tumor mutational burden. The tumor was clinically unresectable and showed rapid progression, resulting in severe dyspnea and syncope due to marked extrinsic airway compression. Because a high-grade sarcoma was initially suspected before the final diagnosis of SMARCA4-UT was established, first-line doxorubicin plus ifosfamide (AI) therapy was administered, resulting in rapid symptomatic relief and a partial response. However, after three cycles of AI therapy, the disease progressed clinically with a left adrenal metastasis. Subsequent treatment with the immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) atezolizumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel showed no objective response, and the patient died 6 months after the initiation of systemic therapy. CONCLUSION: This case suggests that doxorubicin plus ifosfamide may provide rapid but transient tumor shrinkage and symptomatic improvement in thoracic SMARCA4-UT with airway obstruction. This regimen may be considered when urgent tumor reduction is required to relieve impending airway compromise. However, early diagnosis may also be important because first-line ICI-containing regimens have been associated with improved clinical outcomes in thoracic SMARCA4-UT.

papers.title_zh: 人工智能在医学影像中的应用综述：印度视角下的放射诊断现状、AI素养缺口与本地化验证需求
papers.title_en: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: A Review of Radiodiagnosis in Indian Perspectives.
papers.authors: Das E, Mondal R, Dhor A, Basu T
papers.affiliation_highlight: Maulana Azad Medical CollegeNew DelhiIndia.
papers.authors_conclusion: AI literacy is no longer optional: the radiologist's role is not threatened by AI but transformed by it—from film reader to AI-augmented clinical imaging physician capable of extending world-class diagnostic care to underserved populations across India and globally.
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，摘要未见系统检索策略、纳入排除标准、文献筛选流程或偏倚风险评估，无法判断证据覆盖是否完整、是否存在选择性引用。摘要核心为立场性论述与背景统计（950件FDA清关器械、约75%属放射领域、<30%放射科医师能批判性评价AI研究、<20%接受过正式AI培训、放射科医师与人口比1:50,000对比WHO建议1:10,000、印度占全球TB负担26%），这些数字均未标注来源与年份，属背景引用而非研究结果，不宜作为证据引用。表述上“validated-and in controlled settings superior-performance”将外部验证与受控条件下的优越性并置，易被读作临床效能已确立；对肺结节检测等应用的落地限制、假阳性/工作流影响与前瞻性对照证据未在摘要中交代。摘要亦未说明利益冲突与本综述的方法学质量，需回到全文核实检索时限与引用结构。

papers.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become the most transformative development in radiology since digital imaging, with deep learning algorithms demonstrating validated-and in controlled settings superior-performance across pulmonary nodule detection, breast cancer screening, tuberculosis (TB) triage, acute stroke identification, and glioma segmentation. Over 950 AI/machine learning-enabled medical devices have received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as of 2024, ∼75% within radiology, yet a consequential knowledge gap persists: fewer than 30% of practising radiologists can critically evaluate an AI study and fewer than 20% have received formal AI training. This review addresses that gap by providing a clinically accessible account of core AI concepts, major neural network architectures-including convolutional neural networks, U-Net, generative adversarial networks, vision transformers, and foundation models-the complete model development and validation workflow, and validated clinical applications across all major imaging modalities. We give dedicated attention to the Indian context, where an acute radiologist deficit of 1:50,000 against the World Health Organization-recommended ratio of 1:10,000, a 26% share of the global TB burden, and heterogeneous imaging infrastructure make AI both urgently necessary and uniquely demanding of local validation; we discuss the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, federated learning, and the domestic ecosystem of Qure.ai, Niramai, and Sigtuple as structural enablers, as well as algorithmic bias, explainability, and regulatory frameworks. We conclude that AI literacy is no longer optional: the radiologist's role is not threatened by AI but transformed by it-from film reader to AI-augmented clinical imaging physician capable of extending world-class diagnostic care to underserved populations across India and globally.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive malignant tumor which suffers from poor prognosis and limited therapeutic remedies. As a physiologically-oriented radiotherapy and highly tumor-specific modality, boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) shows great potential for the treatment of ESCC. Since efficacy of BNCT is critically restricted to boron drugs, novel boron agents with satisfactory boron load and intracellular uptake are highly demanded. Herein, we developed a novel albumin/BSH-conjugated nanoparticle (BSH@Alb) as a safe and effective boron agent. It resulted BSH@Alb displayed uniform particle size, high encapsulation efficiency (93.1 ± 0.39%), loading capacity (15.52 ± 0.41%) and good stability in different solution (water, PBS and plasma). Collectively, BSH@Alb significantly enhanced intracellular boron accumulation and showed acceptable cytocompatibility in comparison with prototype BSH, supporting its potential value for BNCT therapy as a promising boron-delivery candidate.

papers.abstract_en: Breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are most prevalent forms of malignancies worldwide and are associated with BRCA2 variants. While BRCA2 pathogenic variants are well established in breast cancer, their transcriptional consequences in lung adenocarcinoma remain poorly characterized, and no study has directly compared the shared differentially expressed gene (DEG) signature between BRCA2-variant metastatic breast cancer and BRCA2-variant LUAD. In this study, we used an integrative bioinformatics approach to identify and characterize this shared transcriptomic profile using publicly available TCGA and GEO datasets accessed via cBioPortal. Top dysregulated genes were subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis using STRING and Cytoscape (CytoHubba, MCC algorithm), functional enrichment through Metascape and survival analysis through UALCAN, with disease associations validated against the DISEASES database. SERPINA1, PIGR, FGG and FCGBP were identified as candidate hub genes, common in both types of malignancies. The breast cancer gene set was associated with impaired BRCA2-RAD51-mediated homologous recombination, and the lung dataset had strong signatures of alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells and signatures specific to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). SERPINA1 and PIGR were significant markers in breast cancer and FGG was significant marker in LUAD. The findings identify a partially overlapping epithelial transcriptional profile associated with BRCA2-variant breast and lung tumor datasets. However, these observations represent associations within BRCA2-altered cohorts and do not establish that BRCA2 dysfunction directly drives the identified transcriptional changes. SERPINA1, PIGR, FGG, and FCGBP therefore represent candidate tissue-dependent biomarkers requiring independent validation.
