papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Choroidal metastases may cause substantial visual impairment in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although local ocular treatments are frequently considered, targeted systemic therapy may provide effective control in tumors harboring actionable mutations. We report the rapid regression of a choroidal metastasis following first-line osimertinib therapy in a patient with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated NSCLC. CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man with metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC presented with progressive visual decline in the left eye. Ophthalmic examination revealed a peripapillary choroidal lesion associated with serous retinal detachment. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated subretinal fluid, consistent with a choroidal metastasis. First-line osimertinib therapy had been initiated 12 days before presentation at our clinic. An early reduction in subretinal fluid was observed during follow-up, followed by complete resolution at the 2-month follow-up. This was accompanied by regression of the choroidal lesion and improvement in visual function. No local ocular treatment was required. CONCLUSION: First-line osimertinib may induce rapid regression of choroidal metastases in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. In selected cases, an early response to systemic targeted therapy may allow local ocular treatment to be avoided.

papers.abstract_en: The individual incidences of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease in the elderly population mean that there is a strong likelihood of both occurring simultaneously. Common practice for severe aortic stenosis (AS) would be surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR), unless deemed high-risk for this surgical procedure. Age and lung cancer both increase a patient's surgical risk; hence, the less invasive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to manage valve disease ahead of lung resection for lung cancer is an acceptable alternative after assessing other factors such as procedural risk, comorbidities, and prognosis. We present the case of an 82-year-old female patient who underwent a TAVI seven months before lung resection for an incidental diagnosis of lung cancer with staging T1b N0 M0. Postoperatively, she was treated for atrial fibrillation and lung collapse, then discharged after resolution of these complications on the eighth day after surgery, and remained well at follow-up three months later. This case report explores a situation when this sequence of interventions was appropriate due to increased surgical risk in the elderly population.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening emergency classically associated with Beck's triad of hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous pressure; however, incomplete or atypical presentations may delay diagnosis. We report the case of a previously healthy 28-year-old woman who presented with progressive dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, orthopnoea, peripheral oedema, fever, and fatigue. Examination revealed mild tachycardia, soft heart sounds, reduced basal air entry, and ankle oedema, while the patient remained normotensive. Initial investigations demonstrated cardiomegaly with pleural effusions on chest radiograph, low-voltage QRS complexes on electrocardiogram, and markedly raised inflammatory markers. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography identified a large anterior mediastinal mass encasing the great vessels, a significant pericardial effusion with features of cardiac tamponade, and bilateral pleural effusions. Emergency pericardiocentesis resulted in immediate clinical improvement. Histopathological analysis confirmed high-grade B-cell lymphoma, most consistent with primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma. The patient was treated with immunochemotherapy, achieving complete metabolic remission on end-of-treatment PET-CT. This case highlights the importance of recognising atypical presentations of cardiac tamponade and considering mediastinal malignancy in young patients presenting with unexplained cardiorespiratory symptoms.

papers.abstract_en: Endothelial dysfunction-induced platelet activation contributes to thrombosis in major cardiovascular diseases. Endothelial cells sense hemodynamic shear stress via the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1, which determines their physiological functions. However, the downstream transcriptional pathways of Piezo1 linking mechanical force to endothelial function remain incompletely defined. Here, nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1 (NR4A1) is identified as an endothelial mechanosensitive transcription factor induced by Piezo1 that modulates platelet activation and thrombosis. Mechanistically, shear stress is shown to activate Piezo1, resulting in calcium influx and the subsequent activation of protein kinase C δ (PKCδ), which activates extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) to induce NR4A1 transcription. NR4A1 then upregulates prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2) expression, leading to the increased production of prostacyclin and inhibition of platelet activation and thrombosis. In vivo, mice with endothelial cell-specific deletion of Nr4a1 exhibit greater thrombus weights and faster occlusion. These data establish the Piezo1/Ca2+/PKCδ/ERK/NR4A1/PTGS2 signaling cascade as a critical endothelial mechanotransduction pathway that senses physiological shear force to transcriptionally promote an antithrombotic state.

papers.abstract_en: This study investigated the biochemical mechanisms by which rosmarinic acid (RA), a natural polyphenol, sensitizes A549 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells to mild hyperthermia (43°C). A549 cells were treated with RA (100 or 200 μM) and exposed to mild hyperthermia (43°C, 30 min), after which we performed a comprehensive analysis of cell viability, clonogenic potential, and migratory recovery. The molecular underpinnings were explored through flow cytometry for reactive oxygen species (ROS) and cell cycle progression, together with western blotting for MAPK signaling (JNK, ERK), apoptosis-related proteins (Bcl-xL, survivin, caspases), and the heat-shock response (HSP27, 70, 90, and HSF1). Our results show that the combination of RA and hyperthermia impaired cell proliferation and migration while promoting S-phase accumulation and apoptosis. At the biochemical level, combined RA and hyperthermia increased intracellular ROS beyond the level produced by either treatment alone. This rise in ROS occurred alongside an altered p-JNK/total JNK profile and caspase activation-associated apoptosis. Importantly, RA suppressed the canonical heat-shock response, lowering the p-HSF1/total HSF1 ratio and reducing the expression of the molecular chaperones HSP27, 70, and 90. Pretreatment with N-acetylcysteine (NAC) attenuated the observed ROS, Annexin V, and immunoblot changes, consistent with a contribution of redox imbalance to this sensitization process. In conclusion, RA enhanced hyperthermia-induced oxidative stress and suppressed the HSF1-HSP axis in A549 cells, providing a rationale for its further preclinical evaluation as a biochemical adjuvant in hyperthermic lung cancer therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Therapeutic mRNA vaccines are a clinically validated cancer immunotherapy platform using in vitro transcribed mRNA encoding tumor antigens to induce durable anti-tumor immunity. Advances in mRNA engineering, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery, and immunomodulatory combinations have propelled this approach from preclinical models to randomized trials with survival benefit. This review systematically examines vaccine efficacy through an antigen-delivery-immunomodulation tripartite framework. We trace the evolution from shared tumor-associated antigens to personalized neoantigens identified by computational pipelines, discuss ionizable lipid chemistry and LNP formulation for controlled tissue tropism and transfection, and analyze the bidirectional crosstalk between vaccine components and innate immune sensing that shapes adaptive T cell responses. Clinical evidence across melanoma, pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and other solid tumors is critically evaluated, alongside combination strategies-checkpoint blockade, oncolytic virotherapy, and adoptive cell therapy to overcome TME resistance. Persistent challenges include optimal neoantigen selection, standardized immune monitoring, and predictive biomarkers. We conclude that future research should prioritize systematic optimization of the tripartite design through multi-antigen targeting, tissue-specific delivery engineering, and rational combination immunotherapy, aiming to establish mRNA cancer vaccines as a standard-of-care modality.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Superficial pharyngeal cancers are frequently missed during routine endoscopy and remain challenging to diagnose, even with image advances such as digital chromoendoscopy. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has emerged as a minimally invasive, organ-preserving, therapeutic option. Pharyngeal ESD, however, requires awareness of specific anatomical and technical considerations, including narrower working space, thinner pharyngeal wall, proximity to vascular and neural structures, and the risk of airway impairment during the procedure. METHODS: A 71-year-old male patient had previously undergone subtotal esophagectomy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). On follow-up endoscopy, after examination of the oral cavity and pharynx, a subtle flat lesion with minimal erythema was identified on the posterior wall of the oropharynx, extending distally to the hypopharynx and right piriform sinus, mildly brownish on virtual chromoendoscopy with preserved loop-like vessels. Biopsy confirmed high-grade dysplasia, and ESD was performed. RESULTS: Histopathology confirmed in situ SCC with free margins. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged after 2 days. Endoscopic follow-up revealed cicatricial retraction, and the patient remained asymptomatic. CONCLUSIONS: Careful inspection of the oral cavity and pharynx should be incorporated into routine endoscopy in patients at high risk for SCC, because early detection may allow curative treatment with minimally invasive endoscopic technique.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS), a rare disease with limited research, exhibits resistance to radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Few reports have analyzed the tumor microenvironment of retroperitoneal undifferentiated liposarcoma using single-cell sequencing. METHODS: Single-cell analysis of three retroperitoneal DDLPS cases characterized the cellular and immune microenvironment. RESULTS: Our findings reveal significant heterogeneity among malignant cells in DDLPS, with chromosome 6 deletions being prevalent across malignant cell subpopulations and potentially linked to reduced immunogenicity based on pathway analyses. Notably, the coexistence of CD8 + T cell exhaustion and cytotoxicity reflects a continuum of exhaustion transition. Moreover, we identify a C3 + malignant cell subpopulation with ECM remodeling, angiogenesis, and activated complement pathway. Further exploration suggested that C3 + malignant cells may recruit IL2RA+ regulatory T cells and SPP1 + macrophages through the C3-C3aR1 axis. CONCLUSION: Our findings provide new insights into the application of immunotherapy in sarcoma.

papers.abstract_en: The 4-nitroquinoline-1-oxide (4NQO) model closely recapitulates oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) progression but is limited by cumulative toxicity in conventional protocols. This study aimed to develop a modified 4NQO regimen with defined carcinogen-free intervals and evaluate the chemopreventive potential of black tea-derived polyphenols. C57BL/6 mice were subjected to conventional and modified 4NQO regimens (50 and 100 ppm). Tumour incidence, multiplicity, and volume were assessed alongside histopathology. Systemic toxicity was monitored using body weight, fluid intake, and serum biochemistry. Chemoprevention was evaluated using thearubigins and decaffeinated extracts (1.5% and 10%) administered during pre- and concurrent intervention phases. Molecular analyses included western blotting and qualitative immunohistochemistry. The modified regimen improved body weight maintenance without compromising tumour incidence or progression. No significant differences in tumour burden were observed between the 50 and 100 ppm groups. Histopathological analysis confirmed the presence of lesions across the disease spectrum in all carcinogen-treated groups. In chemoprevention studies, tumour incidence remained unchanged; however, the 10% decaffeinated extract significantly reduced tumour volume, while thearubigins showed a non-significant trend. Molecular analyses revealed no statistically significant differences, though directional changes were observed. The modified protocol enables defined intervention windows, addressing limitations of continuous carcinogen exposure, and the reduction in tumour volume without changes in incidence suggests an effect on tumour progression rather than initiation. Collectively, the modified 4NQO model provides a robust platform for stage-specific chemoprevention evaluation, with black tea polyphenols, particularly decaffeinated extracts, demonstrating modest progression-modulating effects that warrant further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is known to have a very high incidence and mortality rate. Trans-cinnamic acid (tCA) is a phenolic compound found in various fruits and vegetables and is known to have many effects such as antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and anticancer. In this study, molecular docking analysis was performed to predict the binding affinities of tCA toward apoptosis- and ER stress-related target proteins. The effects of tCA on proliferation, apoptosis and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress gene expression, colony forming ability, total antioxidant status (TAS) and total oxidant status (TOS) in A549 human lung cancer cells were investigated. Cell proliferation and, expression levels of genes associated with apoptosis and ER stress determined using XTT and qRT-PCR, respectively. ELISA test was used for TAS, TOS and caspase-3 levels. Molecular docking analysis predicted favorable binding affinities of tCA toward the investigated target proteins. The IC50 value of tCA in A549 cells was found to be 2.59 mM at 48 h. Treatment with tCA significantly increased the expression of apoptosis genes including BAX, CASP3, CASP7, CASP8, CASP9, CYCS, and FADD. Among the ER stress-associated genes analyzed, only PERK and CHOP showed significant upregulation following tCA treatment, while no significant changes were observed in the remaining ER stress-related genes. Furthermore, tCA treatment caused a decrease in TAS level but an increase in TOS level. tCA suppressed the ability to form colonies in A549 cells according to the colony assay. In conclusion, tCA inhibited proliferation and colony formation, modulated selected apoptosis- and ER stress-related genes, and altered oxidative stress parameters in A549 cells. These in vitro findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the potential anticancer activity of tCA; however, further protein-level, functional, and in vivo studies are required to confirm the underlying mechanisms and therapeutic potential. The image outlines a study evaluating the anticancer effects of trans-cinnamic acid (tCA) on A549 lung cancer cells. Molecular docking analysis showed tCA has potential binding affinity to target proteins. In cell experiments, the IC50 of tCA was 2.59 mM at 48 h, determined by an XTT test. Treatment with tCA reduced TAS and caspase-3 levels while increasing TOS. RNA isolation and cDNA synthesis were followed by quantitative RT-PCR analysis, indicating that tCA may induce upregulation of ER stress and apoptotic markers in A549 cells. A colony assay demonstrated that tCA suppressed colony formation in these cells. ELISA assays for TAS, TOS, and caspase-3 were also performed as part of the analysis.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent advances in direct rat sarcoma (RAS) inhibition and downstream pathway targeting have created novel therapeutic strategies which can be utilized in gynecologic oncology. This review examines RAS biology, lessons learned from other malignancies, and emerging strategies for gynecological malignancies. RECENT FINDINGS: KRAS G12C inhibitors in lung cancer established the clinical feasibility of direct RAS targeting, while colorectal cancer studies demonstrated the importance of lineage-specific combinations. KRAS G12D inhibitors, targeted protein degraders, and multiselective RAS(ON) inhibitors represent the next frontier in RAS inhibition, expanding therapeutic options across both gynecologic and nongynecologic tumors. In recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, therapeutic advances have centered on inhibiting the downstream RAS-mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)-extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling pathway using MEK or combined RAF/MEK and focal adhesion kinase inhibitors, rather than direct RAS inhibition, demonstrating encouraging clinical responses, leading to accelerated approval for KRAS-mutant disease. SUMMARY: RAS-pathway directed therapy requires consideration of tumor lineage, specific alleles, and functional pathway dependence. Although clinical progress in gynecologic oncology is most relevant in low-grade serous ovarian cancer, emerging non-G12C therapies warrant further evaluation across gynecologic malignancies. Novel combinations and integrated biomarkers will be necessary to improve patient selection and overcome therapeutic resistance.

papers.abstract_en: Pituitary metastases are uncommon, and most cases originate from breast or lung cancer. Tumor-to-tumor metastasis, in which one neoplasm metastasizes into another, is particularly rare in the sellar region. We report a 66-year-old man with metastatic sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma treated with modified FOLFOX6 (5-fluorouracil, L-leucovorin, and oxaliplatin) plus panitumumab; extracranial disease was controlled, whereas a sellar mass initially suspected as a pituitary adenoma slowly enlarged over 2 years. Endocrine testing showed anterior hypopituitarism without arginine vasopressin deficiency. Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery was performed for continued enlargement and diagnostic uncertainty. Histopathology demonstrated a gonadotroph pituitary adenoma infiltrated by colorectal adenocarcinoma, with extensive intermingling of the 2 components rather than discrete nests, favoring tumor-to-tumor metastasis over a collision tumor. The metastatic component consisted of viable tumor cells without necrosis or convincing treatment effect despite prolonged chemotherapy. This case underscores that metastatic tumor within a pituitary adenoma may enlarge despite favorable systemic therapy outcomes. Metastasis should therefore remain a key differential diagnosis for a sellar mass radiologically suggestive of a pituitary adenoma.

papers.abstract_en: Neurodegenerative diseases are a growing cause of disability worldwide, particularly as populations age. Although these disorders differ in etiology and clinical presentation, advances in genetics, neuropathology, and biomarker research have identified shared disturbances in protein homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and immune regulation. These processes may contribute to selective neuronal vulnerability and neural circuit dysfunction. These findings are refining disease classification and diagnosis, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Disease-specific abnormalities remain essential to clinical interpretation and treatment selection. Existing reviews often focus on individual disorders or isolated mechanisms, leaving the links between shared biology and disease-specific phenotypes insufficiently clear. We synthesize evidence on the epidemiology, risk factors, classification, and pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, frontotemporal dementia, Friedreich's ataxia, and multiple sclerosis. We compare their clinical manifestations and diagnostic approaches, including the evolving role of biomarkers, and critically assess established and emerging therapies. By distinguishing shared mechanisms from disease-specific abnormalities, we identify key translational gaps and explore how common biological disturbances may lead to distinct clinical trajectories. This cross-disease perspective may inform diagnostic reasoning, treatment development, and future comparative research.

papers.abstract_en: MRI is a reference-standard modality for an expanding range of clinical questions, yet it remains among the most unevenly distributed technologies in medicine. Portable low- and ultra-low-field MRI, compact permanent-magnet systems that operate without cryogens or need for in-room radiofrequency shielding, have been proposed as a means of extending imaging to settings where fixed scanners are unavailable or cannot be reached safely. A growing evidence base indicates that these systems can address a defined set of high-value clinical questions, including the detection of intracerebral hemorrhage and large ischemic infarcts, the assessment of hydrocephalus, and the monitoring of critically ill patients at the bedside. This article synthesises the technical basis, clinical applications, and equity implications of portable MRI and argues that the technology's equity impact depends less on the device than on how it is implemented and financed. Consistent with the inverse-equity hypothesis, an imaging technology introduced without deliberate design tends to reach advantaged populations first, and may transiently widen the disparities it is intended to reduce. Drawing on implementation science, change management, and financial reasoning, this article reframes portable MRI as a socio-technical intervention whose equitable benefit depends on the coordinated design of three domains: (1) device capability, (2) implementation and organizational change, and (3) sustainable financing matched to local context. The Canadian setting, including remote and Indigenous communities, is used to illustrate both the opportunity and the conditions required to realize the benefits of portable MRI. A deployment framework is proposed to support radiology leaders and health systems.

papers.abstract_en: The two earthquakes that recently struck the northern coast of Venezuela will deepen a health crisis that has troubled the country for twenty years. They have exposed how weak its health infrastructure is, how scarce medicines are, how little epidemiological surveillance remains, and how long investment has been lacking. The humanitarian health crisis in Venezuela did not arise from armed conflict, as it has elsewhere. Its roots lie in decades of authoritarian rule and institutional decay, which have eroded public health capacity, research infrastructure, vaccination coverage and the control of infectious diseases in general. Because these weaknesses have accumulated, the earthquakes may well turn into an even graver humanitarian emergency. Recovery that lasts will not be secured by short-term international aid alone. It will require the rebuilding of accountable institutions able to govern transparently and to apply equitable health policies, so that the health system can regain its resilience.

papers.abstract_en: Wild emmer wheat (Triticum turgidum ssp. dicoccoides, BBAA), the wild progenitor of cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats, provides an important reference for investigating centromere reorganization during polyploidization and domestication. Here we generated a near-complete genome assembly of wild emmer wheat, including centromeric regions for all 14 centromeres. Comparative analyses with cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats revealed extensive variation in centromere-associated sequences and centromere-proximal structure, as well as distinct subgenome-associated patterns in the A and B subgenomes. The A subgenome was characterized by positional shifts and sequence turnover of CRW-rich centromere-derived blocks, whereas the B subgenome showed reduced CentT566 satellite abundance accompanied by localized retention or expansion on specific chromosomes. These results provide a high-resolution tetraploid wheat reference and reveal subgenome-associated patterns of centromere remodeling during wheat polyploid evolution.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The clinical significance and biological roles of PSMB7 in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize PSMB7 expression, prognostic value, epigenetic regulation, immune associations, and in vitro functions in LUAD. METHODS: PSMB7 expression, clinicopathological associations, prognostic value, epigenetic regulation, co-expression networks, functional pathways, and relationships with the tumor immune microenvironment were systematically evaluated across multiple datasets. External validation was performed in the GSE31210 cohort. Prognostic nomogram performance was additionally evaluated using Harrell's concordance index (C-index) and time-dependent decision curve analysis (DCA). In vitro experiments, including Western blotting, CCK-8 assays, and flow cytometry, were conducted to assess the effects of PSMB7 on cell proliferation and irradiation-induced apoptosis in LUAD cell lines. RESULTS: PSMB7 was significantly upregulated in LUAD and was associated with advanced pathological T and N stages and overall clinical stage. ROC analysis indicated that PSMB7 showed potential discriminatory ability between LUAD and normal lung tissues. High PSMB7 expression independently predicted unfavorable outcomes across multiple prognostic endpoints. Nomogram evaluation using calibration, C-index, and DCA provided complementary evidence for prognostic performance. PSMB7 hypomethylation was associated with poorer survival. PSMB7 expression was positively correlated with DNA mismatch repair genes, RNA modification regulators, and malignant tumor phenotypes. GSEA showed significant enrichment of oncogenic, cell-cycle, metabolic, DNA-repair, and stress-response pathways. In addition, PSMB7 expression was strongly associated with immune scores, immune-cell infiltration, and the expression of immune modulators, MHC molecules, chemokines, and chemokine receptors in LUAD. In vitro, PSMB7 knockdown suppressed cell proliferation and enhanced irradiation-induced apoptosis, whereas PSMB7 overexpression promoted proliferation and reduced apoptosis after irradiation. CONCLUSION: PSMB7 is a candidate independent prognostic biomarker in LUAD and is associated with malignant progression, immune microenvironment features, and cellular responses to irradiation consistent with a potential role in radioresistance. These findings support PSMB7 as a potential therapeutic target in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: To investigate the biological functions of PPP1R14B in lung adenocarcinoma and further elucidate its underlying regulatory mechanisms. The Cancer Genome Atlas clinical cohorts, single-cell sequencing, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot were performed to assess the expression and prognostic value of PPP1R14B in lung adenocarcinoma. Then, PPP1R14B-silenced A549 cells and PPP1R14B-overexpressing H1650 cells were constructed. Colony formation, CCK-8, EdU assay, flow cytometry, scratch, and Transwell chamber assays were utilized to evaluate cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and paclitaxel (PTX) resistance. To elucidate the molecular mechanism of PPP1R14B, transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) and co-immunoprecipitation assays were conducted. Additionally, a xenograft tumor mouse model was established to explore the in vivo role of PPP1R14B. PPP1R14B exhibited high expression in lung adenocarcinoma and correlated with an unfavorable prognosis. Silencing of PPP1R14B markedly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and invasion of A549 cells, while concurrently promoting apoptosis and sensitizing cells to PTX. Nevertheless, overexpression of PPP1R14B in H1650 cells displayed an opposite trend. PPP1R14B directly interacted with ARPC1A and promoted its expression. Overexpression of ARPC1A reversed the inhibitory effects of PPP1R14B silencing on the malignant biological behaviors of A549 cells. In vivo, silencing of PPP1R14B repressed tumor growth, as evidenced by smaller tumor volume, lower tumor weight, fewer Ki67-positive cells, and more TUNEL-positive cells. PPP1R14B directly binds ARPC1A and increases its expression to facilitate lung adenocarcinoma tumorigenesis and PTX resistance.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells frequently depend on Nrf2/ARE-driven antioxidant programs to maintain redox balance and evade apoptosis. This study investigated whether sinensetin, a naturally occurring polymethoxylated flavone, reduces NSCLC cell survival by interfering with this cytoprotective pathway. A549 and H1299 NSCLC cells and normal BEAS-2B bronchial epithelial cells were exposed to sinensetin. Cell viability was measured by MTT assay, apoptosis was quantified by Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry, and pathway- and apoptosis-related proteins were analyzed by western blotting. Nrf2 distribution was evaluated by nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation, ARE-dependent transcription was assessed using a dual-luciferase reporter system, and Nrf2 was silenced by shRNA. Intracellular ROS was measured by DCFH-DA, antioxidant rescue was assessed with N-acetyl-l-cysteine (NAC), Nrf2/ARE-related proteins were examined in BEAS-2B cells, and Nrf2 overexpression was used as a rescue approach in A549 cells. Sinensetin inhibited NSCLC cell growth, increased apoptosis, reduced total and nuclear Nrf2, decreased ARE reporter activity, and downregulated HO-1 and NQO1. Sinensetin also increased intracellular ROS, whereas NAC partially reduced ROS accumulation, restored cell viability, and decreased apoptosis. BEAS-2B cells showed comparatively modest Nrf2/ARE pathway changes. Nrf2 overexpression partially restored HO-1 and NQO1, reduced apoptotic signaling, and attenuated sinensetin-induced loss of viability and apoptosis. These results support a model in which sinensetin promotes oxidative stress-mediated apoptosis in NSCLC cells, at least in part, through suppression of Nrf2/ARE-dependent antioxidant defense.

papers.title_zh: 奥希替尼联合赛沃替尼对比铂类-培美曲塞治疗奥希替尼进展后MET过表达或扩增的EGFR突变晚期NSCLC：III期随机试验显示无进展生存与总生存显著延长
papers.title_en: Osimertinib-Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy.
papers.authors: Lu S, Girard N, Yang JC, Shepherd FA, Dong X, Arulananda S, Metro G, Hayashi H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Shanghai Chest Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Medicine, Shanghai.
papers.results: 主要终点PFS（盲法独立中心评估）：疾病进展或死亡HR 0.55（95%CI 0.42–0.72），P<0.001；OS：死亡HR 0.68（95%CI 0.50–0.91），P=0.01（最终分析）；12个月PFS率36% vs 10%，12个月OS率70% vs 53%；治疗期间最常见不良事件为外周水肿（49%）、贫血（26%）、腹泻（26%）；≥3级不良事件64% vs 63%
papers.authors_conclusion: 在奥希替尼治疗期间进展、伴MET过表达或MET扩增或两者兼有的EGFR突变局部晚期或转移性NSCLC患者中，奥希替尼-赛沃替尼较铂类-培美曲塞显著延长无进展生存和总生存（由阿斯利康资助；SAFFRON，NCT05261399）
papers.ai_note: 开放标签设计，PFS依赖盲法独立中心评估以部分抵消偏倚，但症状性毒性（外周水肿49%）可能影响治疗中止与后续治疗；OS为最终分析且阳性，摘要未交代交叉用药、后续治疗分布及多重性检验策略对OS解释的影响；人群经严格生物标志物限定（IHC 3+≥90%或FISH ≥10拷贝），筛查1746例仅随机338例，结论外推至其他MET定义（如低水平扩增、蛋白中等表达）需谨慎；对照组为化疗，未设奥希替尼+安慰剂臂，故不能区分赛沃替尼的增量贡献；摘要未报告客观缓解率、缓解持续时间及PFS2等次要终点。

pico.p: EGFR突变、局部晚期或转移性NSCLC，伴MET过表达（IHC 3+且≥90%肿瘤细胞）或MET扩增（FISH ≥10基因拷贝）或两者兼有，且在奥希替尼治疗期间进展；筛查1746例，随机338例（奥希替尼-赛沃替尼组171例，铂类-培美曲塞组167例）
pico.ic: 奥希替尼80 mg每日一次联合赛沃替尼300 mg每日两次 vs 静脉铂类-培美曲塞化疗

papers.reason: 为EGFR-TKI耐药后MET驱动耐药这一常见临床困境确立了一个III期级别的联合靶向方案，直接改变奥希替尼进展后伴MET过表达/扩增患者的治疗选择与耐药再活检（MET IHC/FISH）的临床路径，并为后续MET-TKI联合研究提供对照基线。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy. METHODS: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety. RESULTS: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group. CONCLUSIONS: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

papers.reason: 为EGFR-TKI耐药后MET扩增晚期NSCLC提供随机III期证据，可能改变该生物标志物人群的后线治疗选择，并支持双EGFR/MET抑制策略的临床定位。
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: MET amplification accounts for up to 30% of acquired resistance to EGFR-TKI, especially following third-generation EGFR-TKI treatment, yet precision-targeted therapeutic options remain limited. Early-phase studies demonstrated promising antitumor activity with the MET-TKI dalmelitinib combined with the third-generation EGFR-TKI aumolertinib. This phase 3 trial compared dalmelitinib-aumolertinib with platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified advanced NSCLC after EGFR-TKIs progression. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial (NCT06110663) enrolled patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified NSCLC after EGFR-TKI progression. MET amplification was defined by fluorescence in situ hybridization as a mean MET copy number ≥5 or MET/CEP7 ratio ≥2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to dalmelitinib-aumolertinib or platinum-based chemotherapy groups. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review per RECIST 1.1. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DoR), and safety. RESULTS: A total of 314 enrolled patients were assigned to dalmelitinib-aumolertinib (n=156) or platinum-based chemotherapy (n=158). Median follow-up was 11.2 months at the data cutoff date (December 10, 2025). Median PFS was 6.2 months with dalmelitinib-aumolertinib and 4.4 months with chemotherapy (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.81; P <0.001). Corresponding ORRs were 59.6% and 38.6%, and median DoRs were 9.7 months and 4.4 months, respectively. Overall survival data were immature. Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50.0% and 51.0% of patients, respectively. Toxicity profiles differed, with more hepatic laboratory abnormalities with dalmelitinib-aumolertinib and more hematologic toxicities with chemotherapy. CONCLUSION: The dalmelitinib-aumolertinib combination significantly improved PFS versus chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile in advanced EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified NSCLC after progression on EGFR-TKI. These findings support dual EGFR/ MET inhibition as a new treatment option in this biomarker selected population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear. METHODS: In this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; P<0.001). The median progression-free survival was 7.4 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.1) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 1.9 months (95% CI, 1.9 to 2.0) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.42; P<0.001). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 46.8% of the patients who received tarlatamab-durvalumab and in 40.6% of those who received durvalumab alone. Cytokine release syndrome, mainly of grade 1 or 2, was seen in nearly half the patients receiving tarlatamab-durvalumab. CONCLUSIONS: Tarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. (Funded by Amgen and AstraZeneca; DeLLphi-305 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06211036.).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis. RESULTS: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib is a first-line standard of care for advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma (ccRCC). The phase 3 LITESPARK-012 study (NCT04736706) evaluated efficacy and safety of adding belzutifan (HIF-2α inhibitor) or quavonlimab (anti-CTLA-4) to this regimen. PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Adults with previously untreated advanced ccRCC were randomized 1:1:1 to 400 mg pembrolizumab IV Q6W plus 20 mg lenvatinib orally daily and 120 mg belzutifan orally daily (Arm A); coformulated quavonlimab/pembrolizumab 25 mg/400 mg IV Q6W (collectively called MK-1308A) plus lenvatinib (Arm B); or standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib (Control). Treatment continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal from study; pembrolizumab or quavonlimab/pembrolizumab were administered for a maximum of ∼2 years. Progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review and overall survival (OS) were dual primary endpoints, tested in all randomized participants for Arm A versus Control, and in participants with IMDC intermediate/poor risk or all participants for Arm B versus Control. Safety was a secondary endpoint. RESULTS: Overall, 560 participants were randomized to Arm A, 562 to Arm B, and 566 to Control. As of the data cutoff date (February 4, 2026), median follow-up was 43.6 months (range, 31.8-57.4). Among all participants, median PFS was 20.8 months in Arm A (HR vs Control: 1.08, 95%CI 0.93-1.26; P=0.8408), 20.7 months in Arm B (HR vs Control: 1.07, 95%CI 0.92-1.25; nominal P=0.8174), and 23.7 months in the Control arm; median OS was 52.0 months in Arm A (HR vs Control: 1.04, 95%CI 0.87-1.25; P=0.6622), not reached (NR) in Arm B (HR vs Control: 1.12, 95%CI 0.94-1.35; nominal P=0.8955), and NR in the Control arm. Among participants with intermediate/poor risk, median PFS was 20.5 months in Arm B and 23.5 months in the Control arm (HR 1.12, 95%CI 0.94-1.33; P=0.8954); median OS was 39.1 versus 46.2 months (HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.96-1.42; P=0.9419). Any-grade all-cause adverse events led to any-drug discontinuation in 51.6%, 51.4%, and 36.2% of participants in the A, B, and Control arms. CONCLUSIONS: Neither addition of the HIF-2α inhibitor belzutifan nor the CTLA-4 inhibitor quavonlimab to pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib improved outcomes in participants with previously untreated advanced RCC versus pembrolizumab and lenvatinib alone. Higher drug discontinuation rates due to adverse events occurred in the investigational arms. Efficacy and safety of standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib was consistent with prior reports.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab, alone or combined with platinum-based chemotherapy, is a standard first-line treatment for patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable oncogenic alterations and with high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. We conducted a head-to-head comparison of these two treatment strategies. METHODS: In this multicenter, phase III trial (PERSEE, NCT04547504), adult patients with treatment-naïve stage IV or unresectable stage III NSCLC not amenable to definitive radiotherapy and PD-L1 expression ≥50% were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive pembrolizumab (200 mg every 3 weeks, for up to 35 cycles) or pembrolizumab in combination with four cycles of induction chemotherapy, stratified according to the presence of brain metastases and histologic subtype. Patients with non-squamous histology received cisplatin or carboplatin (AUC 5) plus pemetrexed, followed by pembrolizumab-pemetrexed maintenance; patients with squamous histology received carboplatin (AUC 6) plus paclitaxel, followed by pembrolizumab maintenance. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by blinded central review according to RECIST v1.1. Key secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate, duration of response, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 321 patients underwent randomization, with 160 assigned to pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and 161 to pembrolizumab monotherapy. At a median follow-up of 38.7 months, median PFS was significantly longer with combination therapy than with monotherapy (16.1 months [95% CI, 11.0-34.1] vs. 6.9 months [95% CI, 5.5-9.3]; hazard ratio (HR), 0.56; 95% CI, 0.43-0.74; P<0.001). Median OS was 50.2 months versus 29.9 months, respectively (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.56-1.05). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 54% and 19% of patients, respectively; grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events occurred in 13% of patients in each group. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with treatment-naïve advanced NSCLC and high PD-L1 expression, the addition of platinum-based chemotherapy to pembrolizumab significantly prolonged PFS compared with pembrolizumab monotherapy.

Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. Fewer grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were noted with divarasib (24.6%) than with control treatment (34.5%). papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is highly lethal owing to its early and aggressive metastasis, yet the underlying multi-layer molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood, limiting therapeutic advances. METHODS: We performed integrative multi-omics profiling (including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and lactylome) on 99 matched primary tumor, metastatic lymph nodes, and normal esophagus tissue samples from 36 patients with metastatic ESCC. Molecular changes and cross-omics interactions associated with the metastatic cascades were characterized. Key findings were validated by immunohistochemistry and survival analysis in an independent cohort of 116 ESCC patients. Further functional and mechanistic studies were conducted using in vitro and a tail-vein experimental lung metastasis model. RESULTS: Our analysis revealed pronounced disturbance in immune-related pathways closely associated with metastatic progression and poor prognosis. Intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM1) was identified as a critical factor of ESCC invasion and metastasis. Additionally, lysine-lactylated proteins were predominantly involved in cytoskeleton, focal adhesion and glycolysis pathways during ESCC metastasis. Integrative analysis revealed that the lactylome interacts with the genome and transcriptome through both cis- and trans-regulatory mechanisms, primarily in immune and metabolic pathways. Notably, lactylation of phosphoglycerate mutase 1 (PGAM1) at residue K251 enhances its interaction with actin gamma 1 and promotes metastatic phenotypes. ICAM1 and PGAM1 K251 lactylation represent two independent metastasis-associated mechanisms identified from the same multi-omics dataset. CONCLUSIONS: This integrative multi-omics characterization provides a comprehensive resource for metastatic ESCC research and identifies K251-lactylated PGAM1 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and mechanistic lead warranting further preclinical validation.

papers.abstract_en: Advanced thymic carcinoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options after chemotherapy failure. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AL3810-202) aimed to evaluate lucitanib, a novel, orally potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR1‒3, FGFR1‒3, and PDGFRα/β in patients with advanced thymic carcinoma progressing after chemotherapy. Sixty-eight patients were randomized (2:1) to receive 10 mg lucitanib daily (n = 46) or placebo (n = 22). Although this study did not meet its primary endpoint of independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) (median 5.8 vs. 3.7 months; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60; p = 0.1050), the prespecified log-rank test may have underestimated the treatment effect due to an observed non-proportional hazards pattern. Subsequent restricted mean survival time analysis demonstrated a statistically significant PFS benefit (p < 0.05), which was further supported by significantly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (6.6 vs. 1.9 months; HR: 0.53; p = 0.0306). The most common grade 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were hypertension (50%), proteinuria (15.2%), and thrombocytopenia (8.7%), with no grade 4/5 events. Considering the totality of the evidence and an acceptable safety profile, lucitanib may confer a meaningful clinical benefit for patients with advanced thymic carcinoma, warranting further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose ENTRÉE Lung (NCT03739710) was a global, open-label, platform study investigating novel immunotherapy combinations in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following progression on anti-PD-(L)1 and platinum-based treatment. We report findings with dostarlimab (anti-PD-1) plus belrestotug (anti-TIGIT) with or without nelistotug (anti-CD96). Patients and Methods The study included safety cohorts with dose escalation and expansion: Arm 4 safety cohort (Arm4-safety), dostarlimab 500 mg plus belrestotug 200-1000 mg (initial dose level: 400 mg); Arm5-safety, dostarlimab 500 mg plus belrestotug 400 mg and nelistotug 210-1400 mg (initial dose level: 700 mg); study treatments were administered intravenously every 3 weeks. A randomized cohort was added to Arm 5 (Arm5-randomized), assigning patients to nelistotug 210 or 1400 mg in the triplet combination. Primary endpoints were safety and tolerability. Results Sixty-two patients were enrolled (n=24 Arm4-safety; n=17 Arm5-safety; n=21 Arm5-randomized [n=11, 200 mg; n=10, 1400 mg]). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 4 (17%), 1 (6%) and 3 (14%) patients in Arm4-safety, Arm5-safety and Arm5-randomized, respectively. There were few treatment discontinuations due to adverse events. Most patients exhibited progressive disease as best response. There was one partial response (Arm5-randomized, 210 mg); stable disease ≥12 weeks was experienced by 4 (17%), 5 (29%) and 2 (10%) patients in Arm4-safety, Arm5-safety and Arm5-randomized, respectively. Conclusions Dostarlimab plus belrestotug, with or without nelistotug, was well tolerated but demonstrated no clinically meaningful activity in previously treated advanced NSCLC. Further research is required to identify patients who may benefit from other immunotherapy combinations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Anastomotic leakage after oesophagectomy is common, and associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence angiography has emerged as a promising intraoperative adjunct for perfusion assessment at the anastomotic site. This study aims to assess the impact of ICG use on anastomotic leakage rates and postoperative outcomes. METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic search of Medline, PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library was performed. The primary outcome was anastomotic leakage. Key secondary outcomes were conduit necrosis, mortality, and reoperation; all secondary outcomes were reported. The Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) and Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tools were used for investigating risk of bias. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) was used to assess certainty of evidence. A random-effects meta-analysis and meta-regression as well as subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: From 902 identified studies, 23 met the inclusion criteria (including 4 RCTs; 2845 patients, of whom 1154 underwent ICG assessment). ICG use was associated with reduced anastomotic leakage rates (OR 0.44 (95% c.i. 0.29 to 0.65), P < 0.001; number needed to treat = 13) and conduit necrosis rates (OR 0.32 (95% c.i. 0.12 to 0.85), P = 0.022). Mortality (OR 1.43 (95% c.i. 0.69 to 2.97), P = 0.335), reoperation (OR 0.84 (95% c.i. 0.51 to 1.39), P = 0.500), severe anastomotic leakage, overall morbidity, readmission, operating time, and length of stay did not differ between groups. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes (GRADE), predominantly driven by the observational study design of many of the studies. CONCLUSION: Use of ICG appears to be associated with reduced anastomotic leak in oesophagectomy, although certainty of evidence is low. Assessment remains qualitative and operator-dependent.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Risk stratification before esophageal and gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) in older adults often relies on age and comorbidity; however, these measures may not capture vulnerability reflected in routinely collected claims data. We aimed to evaluate the claims-based frailty and short-term adverse events association after esophageal and gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection. METHODS: We used a nationwide Japanese administrative database to identify patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent first esophageal or gastric ESD. Frailty was defined using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS), calculated from diagnoses during a 2 year lookback period. After 1:1 propensity score matching, frail and non-frail patients were compared. The primary outcome was binary composite of short-term adverse events, including in-hospital perforation/peritonitis, delayed bleeding, thromboembolism, aspiration pneumonia, and 30 day all-cause mortality. Component outcomes, survival, length of stay, costs, and readmission were also evaluated. RESULTS: Among 15,184 eligible patients, 4,970 matched pairs were included. Frailty was associated with the composite adverse outcome (adjusted odds ratio 1.35; 95% confidence interval 1.19-1.53), driven mainly by perforation/peritonitis and delayed bleeding. No significant differences were observed for 30 day mortality, thromboembolic events, or aspiration pneumonia. Frailty was also associated with lower overall survival during follow-up, whereas median length of stay was identical between groups. CONCLUSION: Among older adults undergoing esophageal or gastric ESD, HFRS-defined claims-based frailty was associated with higher rates of short-term adverse events, particularly perforation/peritonitis and delayed bleeding. These findings suggest that routinely collected claims data may help identify vulnerable patients who warrant closer peri-procedural assessment and monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: Trimerization motifs play pivotal roles in structural biology and therapeutic protein engineering. Here, we describe a short trimerization motif (rFd1303) derived from the Reoviridae family reovirus σ1 protein. Compared with the widely used T4-Foldon, the rFd1303 increased recombinant protein yields. The rFd1303-fused immunogens of SARS-CoV-2 spike and influenza hemagglutinin elicited antibody responses comparable to T4-Foldon-fused controls in mice. Using this tag, we engineered a trimeric ACE2-Ig fusion protein (TriACE2-Ig) that remained stable after 30 days at room temperature and neutralized a broad range of ACE2-utilizing sarbecoviruses, including 19 SARS-CoV-2 variants, SARS-CoV, and pangolin coronaviruses GD and GX, with higher potency than monomeric ACE2-Ig. In the hamster model challenged with various SARS-CoV-2 variants, our data demonstrated that intranasal TriACE2-Ig administration markedly reduced viral loads, virus-induced body-weight loss, lung pathology, and decreased within-cage virus transmission. These findings highlight rFd1303 as a versatile trimerization platform for vaccine and therapeutic protein development.

papers.abstract_en: VEGF-A/VEGF-R axis is well recognized for its role in tumor angiogenesis as well as tumor-induced immunosuppressive mechanisms. Targeting this pathway can help to switch tumor microenvironment toward a more immune-permissive state. Inhibition of VEGF-A/VEGFR has emerged as a strategy to enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy in some cancers leading to the approval of anti-VEGF-A/anti-PD(L)1 combinations in advanced renal cell cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and endometrial cancer. However, in other tumor types, and particularly in colorectal cancer or glioblastoma, results remain limited. In this review, we discuss the biological rationale underlying anti-VEGF-A/PD-(L)1 combinations, summarize the clinical evidence supporting their use across tumor types, discuss the disappointing results in colorectal cancer and glioblastoma, and highlight emerging strategies to improve their therapeutic efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic interstitial lung disease with high morbidity and mortality. Inhaled treprostinil showed pulmonary vascular and lung-function signals in pulmonary hypertension associated with Interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and was subsequently tested in IPF trials. OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the efficacy and safety of inhaled treprostinil in adults with IPF. METHODS: PubMed, Google Scholar and the Cochrane Library/CENTRAL were searched for records published from January 2000 to 2026. A random-effects meta-analysis used the DerSimonian-Laird tau squared and inverse-variance weighting methods. Continuous outcomes were pooled as generic inverse-variance effects from reported estimates and 95% confidence intervals. Hazard ratios were pooled on the log scale. Safety outcomes were pooled as risk ratios from event counts. RESULTS: The searches identified 1552 records. After deduplication, 379 records were screened and 85 full-text reports were assessed. Eleven reports were included in the systematic review. TETON-1 and TETON-2 were the two direct-IPF randomized trials within the coordinated TETON program eligible for primary meta-analysis. Inhaled treprostinil improved absolute forced vital capacity (FVC) change at 52 weeks compared with placebo (MD 111.28 mL, 95% CI 77.61 to 144.95, p < 0.001; I squared 8.5%). Clinical worsening was reduced (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.84, p < 0.001; I squared 0.0%). Acute exacerbation was lower in pooled analysis (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30 to 0.91, p = 0.022), while all-cause mortality did not differ significantly (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.47 to 1.05, p = 0.086). Adverse-event discontinuation, cough and headache were more frequent with treprostinil. CONCLUSIONS: In direct IPF randomized evidence, inhaled treprostinil preserved lung function and reduced clinical worsening at 52 weeks.

papers.abstract_en: Population-based lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is expanding across Europe, including a publicly funded Polish programme starting in October 2026. Because screening-eligible individuals share substantial tobacco-related cardiovascular risk, LDCT also offers cardiovascular risk assessment without additional radiation. We conducted a narrative review of the PubMed literature published up to September 2026, prioritising guidelines, lung cancer screening cohorts and systematic reviews. We summarise the cardiovascular findings on non-contrast, non-electrocardiography (ECG)-gated LDCT: coronary artery, aortic valve, mitral annular and thoracic aortic calcification, ascending aortic dilatation, pericardial effusion, and pulmonary artery enlargement, as well as investigational cardiac volumetry, epicardial adipose tissue and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted quantification. We grade each finding by reportability, defined downstream action and supporting evidence, and align reporting thresholds with the European Respiratory Society/European Society of Thoracic Imaging (ERS/ESTI) statement on incidental findings. LDCT cannot replace dedicated cardiac imaging or establish haemodynamic diagnoses. The prognostic value of coronary and aortic valve calcification and of ascending aortic dilatation is established, whereas the evidence for mitral annular calcification and pulmonary artery enlargement is more limited; observational data indicate that reporting these markers changes preventive management, but whether this improves cardiovascular outcomes has not yet been demonstrated. Standardised reporting, proportionate thresholds, and coordinated pathways linking radiology, pulmonology, primary care and cardiology are needed to translate incidental cardiovascular findings into scalable prevention and should be evaluated in implementation studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The marked heterogeneity of primary liver cancer (PLC), together with the dynamic influence of the tumor microenvironment (TME), remains a major challenge to precision oncology. As currently available therapies provide limited benefit for many patients and robust preclinical platforms for rapid, patient-specific treatment stratification are lacking, there is an urgent need for models that faithfully preserve individual tumor architecture and cellular diversity. METHODS: We established three-dimensional bioprinted primary liver cancer (3DP-PLC) models comprising 61 patient-derived monocultures and 34 co-culture models with patient-matched cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). To explore the correlation between ex vivo models and clinical drug response, we developed a clinically anchored hybrid stratification framework for response classification. In parallel, the 3DP-PLC/CAF co-culture biobank was used to investigate stromal regulation of therapeutic response. RESULTS: These 3DP-PLC constructs preserved the histological features, biomarker expression patterns, mutational landscapes, and transcriptomic profiles of their corresponding parental tumors. Drug-sensitivity profiling across the biobank revealed substantial intertumoral heterogeneity in therapeutic responses. The clinically anchored hybrid stratification framework integrating ex vivo pharmaceutical profiles with external clinical benchmark data enabled interpretable response classification and demonstrated clinical relevance in patients receiving neoadjuvant or adjuvant targeted therapy. In parallel, the 3DP-PLC/CAF co-culture biobank, combined with single-cell transcriptomic analysis, recapitulated fibrous ring-like architecture and revealed CAF-associated drug-resistant states. CONCLUSIONS: These findings support 3DP-PLC as a high-fidelity and scalable platform for personalized therapeutic stratification and mechanistic investigation of tumor-stroma interactions in PLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Global antibiotic use during the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact remain unclear. This study analysed antibiotic use, bacterial co-infections, and the association between antibiotic use and in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalised for COVID-19, using a WHO database. METHODS: We conducted a multicountry cohort study using anonymised patient-level data from The WHO Global Clinical Platform for COVID-19. Data were collected across 64 countries in all six WHO regions between January, 2020, and October, 2023. The study included hospitalised patients of all ages with suspected or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. We obtained patient-level data from standardised WHO case report forms completed prospectively or retrospectively and from harmonised national registries, research studies, and hospital databases. Patients without a suspected or confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis or missing information on hospital admission date, antibiotic use, or outcome were excluded from the analysis. Patients were followed up from hospital admission until death, discharge, transfer, or 28 days, whichever occurred first. Follow-up data were collected at hospital discharge or death by the treating facility and entered into the platform. The primary outcome was 28-day in-hospital mortality, and we analysed this outcome using Cox proportional hazards models with a shared frailty term to account for country-level clustering. FINDINGS: The median age of the study population was 61·9 years (±21·7), with 198 223 women and 251 990 men with data available on antibiotic use. Of the 592 898 patients enrolled, 451 291 (76·1%) had data on antibiotic use and were included in the descriptive analysis; 122 854 had complete data on empirical treatment type, of whom 47 359 (38·5%) were included in the regression analysis. Among the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use, 341 125 (75·6%) received antibiotics, more frequently in severe to critical cases than in mild to moderate cases (80·5% vs 71·6%). Prescribing was highest in the Eastern Mediterranean (83·0%) and African (82·7%) regions and lowest in the Western Pacific region (32·8%), declining in the European region and region of the Americas but increasing in the African region between 2020 and 2022. Treatment was predominantly empirical and involved Watch antibiotics of the WHO Access, Watch, and Reserve classification. Clinically suspected co-infections were reported in 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 patients; among those with positive cultures, 1815 (42·8%) of 4237 had multidrug-resistant bacteria. In the unadjusted analyses, empirical antibiotic use was associated with higher mortality across severity strata. After adjustment for age, sex, comorbidities, and disease severity, empirical antibiotic use remained associated with increased mortality in mild to moderate cases (adjusted hazard ratio 1·80, 95% CI 1·36-2·38) and severe to critical cases (1·16, 1·08-1·24). INTERPRETATION: Despite clinically suspected co-infections being reported in only 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 enrolled patients, 341 125 (75·6%) of the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use received antibiotic therapy, predominantly broad-spectrum agents. As antibiotic use was not associated with improved clinical outcomes and is known to increase antimicrobial resistance, it should be rationalised through strengthened antimicrobial stewardship and behavioural interventions, particularly during respiratory viral epidemics. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA-IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively4. Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11-0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02-0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lacks effective targeted therapies, and how metabolic reprogramming drives oncogenic signaling remains poorly defined. Here, we identify histone H3 lysine 23 lactylation (H3K23la) as a key epigenetic mediator linking lactate accumulation to tumor progression. H3K23la is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with poor prognosis. Mechanistically, H3K23la promotes WNK lysine deficient protein kinase 1 (WNK1) transcription, which increases histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation (p-H3S10) and enhances AKT transcription, thereby driving PI3K-AKT signaling. This defines a lactate-H3K23la-WNK1-p-H3S10-AKT axis connecting metabolism to oncogenic signaling. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of WNK1 by CD03017 disrupts this pathway and suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. In conclusion, our findings define a metabolic-epigenetic-signaling axis in ESCC and establish WNK1 as a potential therapeutic target downstream of histone lactylation.

papers.abstract_en: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic was a prolonged period of traumatic stress with potentially lasting health impacts, especially for vulnerable groups including pregnant individuals. Prenatal stress has been associated with greater risk of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD), warranting investigation of prenatal pandemic-related traumatic stress (PTS) as a risk factor for NDD. METHODS: We surveyed Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC) members who were ≥ 12 weeks pregnant between June 2020 and September 2022. PTS was measured using the 10-item PTS Scale and modeled as a continuous total symptom score (range: 0-10) and binary exposure (high, ≥ 9; low, < 9). We prospectively followed children through July 2025 and linked to sociodemographic and medical characteristics, including NDD diagnoses, in KPNC electronic records. We fit Cox regression models adjusted for maternal age, race and ethnicity, insurance type, SARS-CoV-2 infection, pre-pregnancy BMI, pre-pregnancy depression, child birthyear and sex to estimate hazard ratios (HR) for any NDD and separately for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) associated with PTS and evaluated effect modification by child sex. RESULTS: Of 13,859 mothers, 21.1% identified as Asian, 3.0% as Black, 19.6% as Hispanic, 4.6% as Multiracial, < 1.0% as Native American or Pacific Islander, 49.0% as White, and 1.7% were of Unknown race. The mean (SD) PTS score was 3.9 (2.6) and 722 (5.2%) mothers had high PTS (≥ 9); 2,750 (19.8%) children were diagnosed with any NDD and 651 (4.7%) with ASD. Higher PTS symptom score was associated with significantly greater risk of any NDD (HR = 1.02, 95% CI = 1.01-1.04) and ASD (HR = 1.04 [1.01-1.07]) per 1-point increase in continuous score. High compared to low PTS was associated with greater risk of NDD diagnoses (HR = 1.18 [1.01-1.37]) and ASD (HR = 1.20 [0.89-1.62]), although not statistically significant for ASD. Associations did not differ by sex for NDD (HRFemales= 1.20 [0.92-1.56], HRMales= 1.17 [0.96-1.41]; interaction P = 0.78) or ASD (HRFemales= 1.31 [0.73-2.34], HRMales= 1.17 [0.82-1.65]; interaction P = 0.60). CONCLUSIONS: Among this cohort of mothers who were pregnant during the COVID-19 pandemic, higher PTS was associated with greater risk of child NDD diagnoses. Further research is needed to investigate the potential biologic mechanisms underlying this association.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bipolar disorder (BD) manifests both genetic predispositions and brain imaging abnormalities. Genetic analyses provide a powerful approach to disentangling the associations between BD and brain imaging-derived phenotype (IDP). However, in East Asian (EAS) populations, the genetic basis of these neuroimaging changes and their clinical relevance remains underexplored due to limited integrative evidence. METHODS: We investigated the genetic architecture and clinical relevance of BD and brain IDPs in East Asian populations using individual-level data from the Chinese Bipolar Disorder (CN-BD) cohort (N = 3,920), summary statistics of BD from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC) (N = 16,915) and of IDPs from the CHIMGEN Consortium (N = 7,058), and genotype and clinical data from the Chinese Longitudinal and Systematic Study of Bipolar Disorder cohort (CLASS-BD). We employed genetic correlation (GNOVA), multi-trait meta-analysis (MTAG, CPASSOC), and ancestry-specific fine-mapping (MESuSiE) to identify shared genetic loci. Functional annotation, protein association (SMR, BLISS), and spatiotemporal expression trajectory analyses were conducted. Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization (MR) assessed causal relationships, and polygenic risk score (PRS)-PheWAS explored phenome-level associations with clinical traits. RESULTS: Our multi-trait meta-analysis identified 11 pleiotropic single nucleotide variants (SNVs) implicated in BD-IDP pairs, showing convergent enrichment in lipid metabolism and neurotransmitter biosynthesis pathways. Fine-mapping revealed an EAS-specific causal signal (rs7941324 near RPS27P20), which demonstrated high posterior inclusion probability in EAS but not European ancestries, and colocalized with BD and specific brain alterations. MR revealed 27 IDP-to-BD and 35 BD-to-IDP causal relationships, distinguishing structural changes of the parietal and temporal gyri as markers preceding BD onset and the right precuneus area as a state marker that followed BD onset. Clinically, BD-IDP polygenic risk scores were significantly associated with depressive symptoms, anxiety, and suicide risk. Mediation analysis further indicated that depressive and anxiety symptoms statistically mediated the relationship between BD-IDP PRS and suicide risk. Moreover, PRS-PheWAS identified 135 significant associations with metabolic phenotypes, highlighting a psycho-metabolic nexus in BD. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings reveal associations between polygenicity and distinct BD brain patterns and clinical profiles. We identified ancestry-specific causal variants and bidirectional BD-IDP relationships. PRS associations with depressive symptoms, anxiety, suicide risk, and metabolic phenotypes highlight precision medicine potential for BD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is increasingly attributed to thromboinflammation and microvascular platelet activation. Accordingly, we aimed to characterize longitudinal platelet aggregation, platelet activation, and platelet morphology in patients with aSAH and assessed their association with DCI. METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort consisted of 206 patients with aSAH. Of the 206 patients, 144 were analyzed via platelet aggregometry, 148 via flow cytometry, and 129 had both aggregometry and flow cytometry data. An additional 52 patients had morphology data. Peripheral blood was sampled on post-bleed days 1, 2, 4, 7, and 10. Platelet aggregation was measured by Chrono-Log aggregometry; platelet activation (PAC-1, CD62P) was measured by flow cytometry; platelet morphology was measured by microscopy. Patient-level area-under-the-curve summaries were entered into binary logistic regression. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery rate (FDR) was applied across the analyte × parameter grid. RESULTS: Sixty patients (29.1%) developed DCI. papers.abstract_en: Tendon healing is the primary goal of tendinopathy therapy. However, the therapeutic response of adjacent muscles remains uninvestigated. MR-elastography (MRE) can assess muscle biomechanical properties and function. This study investigated muscle biomechanical responses in patients treated for patellar (PT) or Achilles tendinopathy (AT).
