papers.abstract_en: The reliable room-temperature (RT) detection of organophosphorus (OP) nerve agents remains a critical challenge for public safety, hindered by sluggish diffusion and poor adsorption affinity of targets like sarin (GB) and its simulant dimethyl methylphosphonate (DMMP). Here, by mimicking the structure and function of natural enzyme, we rationally designed a bioinspired, repairable hybrid architecture that achieves highly sensitive and selective RT detection of DMMP. Our design integrates a self-assembled porous L-cystine layer derived from a two-dimensional MoS2 modified with L-cysteine. This hierarchical structure uniquely enables a synergistic "recognition-enrichment-transport-sensing" cascade elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations: the porous layer enriches DMMP molecules and facilitates their diffusion to underlying MoS2 interface, where specific adsorption triggers significant electron transfer. The sensor demonstrates an ultra-low RT practical detection limit down to 10 ppb, along with fast response, excellent selectivity, and long-term stability. Furthermore, when integrated into a flexible wearable device, the sensor exhibits outstanding mechanical bending stability and easy repairability enabled by the reversible disulfide bonds, allowing for architectural reconstruction after damage. This work offers a promising biomimetic strategy to overcome the intrinsic limitations of OP sensing and paves the way for durable, RT-wearable detection technologies in practical security applications.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Impact assessment surveys (IAS) are central to monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of mass drug administration (MDA) programs targeting soil-transmitted helminths (STH). Current survey designs often follow guidelines that lack flexibility and spatial representativeness. There is a need for more efficient and context-adaptable methodologies that can guide programmatic decision-making using available data. METHODS: We developed a three-step geostatistical framework for optimal IAS design that integrates baseline prevalence data, environmental covariates, and treatment history. A geostatistical model is used to estimate baseline prevalence. A Markov model, coupled with a local spatial thinning algorithm, is then applied to forecast post-MDA prevalence surfaces. These projections guide the simulation and evaluation of candidate survey designs across different sampling intensities and spatial configurations. Design performance was assessed based on classification accuracy and survey cost. RESULTS: The methodology was applied to datasets from Kenya, Sierra Leone, and Zimbabwe. Compared to conventional survey designs, our model-based approach achieved similar classification accuracy with 60-90% lower survey costs. These gains were consistent across settings with different endemicity levels and deworming histories. The results also highlight the importance of leveraging spatial correlation and historical program data to inform efficient design. CONCLUSIONS: Our approach offers a flexible and cost-effective solution for designing IAS under real-world constraints. By incorporating spatial modeling and intervention history, it enables evidence-based decision-making and resource allocation. This framework is disease-agnostic and can be adapted to other neglected tropical diseases to support progress toward control and elimination goals.

papers.abstract_en: Protein fingerprinting with nanopores enables single-molecule proteoform analysis but is often limited by conformational heterogeneity of flexible polypeptides. Here, we reduce this stochasticity through a geometric relocalization strategy by engineering dual hydrophobic anchoring sites (T83F/R118F) in the vestibule of the Mycobacterium smegmatis porin A (M2MspA) nanopore. These substitutions are proposed to create localized aromatic interaction sites that alter the docking geometry of the folded Smt3 domain and improve the reproducibility of sensing-segment presentation near the constriction. We demonstrated that this reconfiguration could convert stochastic, tail-dominated signals into regulated, segment-resolved readouts. Analysis of the single-site mutants suggests that R118F makes the predominant contribution to the observed reporter-positioning phenotype, enabling discrimination of peptide sequences unresolved in M2MspA. Using this spatial control, we achieve single-molecule detection of lysine acetylation in a tau-derived peptide via distinct noise signatures. These results support a nanopore design strategy that emphasizes spatial alignment for high-fidelity proteoform analysis.

papers.abstract_en: Compact photoacoustic trace-gas sensors require acoustic detectors that combine high sensitivity with mechanical integrability, but conventional high-performance detectors are typically rigid, discrete components that are difficult to merge with shape-adaptive acoustic architectures. Here, we report a monolithic photoacoustic CO2 sensor enabled by an interface-engineered reconfigurable piezocomposite, in which the sensing film itself can serve as both the acoustic cavity wall and the piezoelectric detector. The water-processed composite combines Cu@PZT metal-ferroelectric heterointerfaces, sparse MWCNT electrical bridges and a glucose-urea-reconstructed cellulose matrix. Surface-anchored Cu domains on PZT act as localized charge-regulation sites that mitigate polymer dielectric shielding and depolarization effects, yielding a piezoelectric coefficient of 83.2 pC N-1, while the dynamic hydrogen-bonded cellulose network provides the deformability required for conformal and tubular architectures. In a planar PAS configuration, the piezocomposite functions as a flexible acoustic detector attached to a discrete resonant cavity, giving a CO2 sensitivity of 2.92 mV ppm-1 and a detection limit of 148 ppb. When rolled into a monolithic tubular sensor, the same film forms the resonant cavity wall and performs wall-active acoustic-to-electrical transduction, increasing the sensitivity to 7.11 mV ppm-1 and lowering the detection limit to 13 ppb at a 10 s integration time, with a normalized noise equivalent absorption of 2.03 × 10-8 cm-1 W Hz-1/2. This work establishes a material-to-sensor-architecture route for wall-active photoacoustic trace-gas detection, showing how reconfigurable piezocomposites can integrate acoustic resonance and electrical detection within a single deformable sensing structure.

papers.abstract_en: Single-cell Assay for Transposase Accessible Chromatin (scATAC-seq) is increasingly used at population scale to study how genetic variation shapes chromatin accessibility. Method development is limited by the lack of flexible simulation tools with known ground truth. Here, we present simPIC, a fast, memory-efficient framework for simulating realistic single-cell ATAC-seq count data across individuals and populations. simPIC models cell groups, batch effects, and genotype-dependent accessibility variation, enabling evaluation of population-scale methods, including chromatin accessibility quantitative trait locus mapping. Across multiple datasets and cell types, simPIC closely matches real data distributions while scaling to cohort sizes impractical for current tools.

pico.ic: 无干预与对照；定性研究，分析从业人员记录的家长获取与参与整合性儿童健康服务的障碍与促进因素

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Families from underserved communities face disproportionate barriers to accessing early years support. In response, Early Years GP Child Health Hub Pilots were set up in three North West London boroughs (Brent, Ealing, Harrow) between 2023 and 2025 to improve access to integrated services, reflecting the NHS 10-Year Plan’s ambition for neighbourhood-based care. The hubs have been funded to continue supporting local communities. However, there is limited understanding of how parents from underserved communities experience these services and the challenges they encounter in engaging with them. This study explored practitioner-reported barriers parents face in accessing and engaging with integrated child health services. METHODS: We used qualitative multiple practitioner-generated case study data specifically for families with children aged 0–5 years from the three pilot sites. We applied the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) framework to analyse the data thematically, guided deductively by the framework and inductively allowing for emergent themes. RESULTS: Twenty-one case studies, collected between September 2024 and January 2025, were generated by practitioners using information they recorded from contact with each family. Barriers were identified across all COM-B domains and multiple barriers overlapping domains. Capability barriers were reported to be the most common (eg, poor parental mental health, low parenting confidence and limited health literacy). Opportunity barriers included financial hardship, competing priorities, social isolation and family interference. Motivational barriers included fear of judgement, emotional stress and previous negative experiences with services. The case studies also identified several enablers including trusted practitioner relationships, culturally sensitive care, proactive follow-up and multidisciplinary collaboration. CONCLUSION: Families living in disadvantaged areas face multiple, intersecting barriers to engaging with integrated services. Child Health Hubs should adopt co-produced, community-informed approaches with parents that integrate health and social support to improve equitable access and sustained engagement for families experiencing adversity.

papers.abstract_en: The real-time, in vivo measurement of drugs, metabolites, and biomarkers in awake animals could enable unprecedented insights into metabolic regulation, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and behavioral response. In pursuit of this vision, here we demonstrate a subcutaneous electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensor architecture that (i) supports the seconds-resolved, real-time measurement of specific molecular analytes over extended periods in freely moving, normally behaving rats and (ii) we believe is easily transferrable to other researchers. The approach also enables concurrent behavioral tracking captured ambulation metrics, which can reveal correlations between the in vivo concentrations of psychoactive drugs and locomotor behavior. The results of this multimodal approach validate EAB sensors for multianalyte detection in dynamic physiological contexts and highlights the physiological and psychobiological relevance of interstitial fluid drug concentrations, with implications for precision dosing, real-time molecular diagnostics, and behavioral pharmacology.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF THE REVIEW: We reviewed how heat exposure is defined using thresholds and reference temperatures derived from the temperature-mortality exposure-response curve in time-series and case-crossover studies using distributed lag non-linear models and propose a harmonisation framework relevant to climate change research and heat disaster preparedness. RECENT FINDINGS: The rapid review identified variation across studies in heat thresholds and reference temperatures, affecting the comparability of estimates. A case study in Spain illustrates how the minimum mortality temperature (MMT) approach estimates overall heat-related mortality and its contributions from moderate and extreme heat, whereas the percentile-based approach estimates excessive heat mortality that could potentially be prevented by protective measures operating above the heat threshold. Differences in heat thresholds and reference temperatures make findings harder to compare across studies and complicate risk communication. Explicit reporting of these two components and their relevance to the research question and intended application would improve interpretation and translation to public health action.

papers.abstract_en: Developing effective nanomedicines for pulmonary metastasis remains challenging because of systemic clearance and local stromal barriers. Guided by single-cell transcriptomic profiling, we characterized a compartmentalized immunosuppressive network involving PGE2 and provide a biological rationale for coordinated EP2/EP4 antagonism. We therefore engineered an inhalable biomimetic platform (PD-1@E2/4 Exo) comprising PD-1-displaying exosomes co-loaded with EP2 and EP4 antagonists. Compared with intravenous administration, nebulized delivery increased pulmonary exposure of the engineered vesicles. Within the pulmonary tumor setting, surface PD-1 is intended to interfere with PD-1/PD-L1 signaling, while the co-delivered antagonists target the EP2/EP4 immunosuppressive axis. Treatment was associated with macrophage reprogramming, increased oxidative stress, and enhanced ICD-related responses in tumor cells. In the experimental breast-cancer lung-colonization model, the inhaled formulation reduced established pulmonary tumor burden and was accompanied by systemic immune-memory responses. These findings provide a preclinical study for integrating local pulmonary delivery with coordinated metabolic and immune modulation in breast cancer lung disease.

papers.title_en: The Proteasomal Switch as a Kinetic Battleground for Influenza A Virus Pathogenesis.
papers.authors: Soni S, Anang V, Kumar P, Tizazu AM, Arega EG, Nho RS, Mora AL, Rojas M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Internal Medicine, Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep Medicine, Davis Heart and Lung Institute…
papers.authors_conclusion: 免疫蛋白酶体既是宿主防御效应器，也是病毒颠覆的靶点；提出IAV蛋白选择性干扰蛋白酶体亚基以稳定促病毒因子的工作模型，并将iP与UPS/ERAD/自噬共同视为蛋白稳态缓冲；提出时间依赖的双相蛋白酶体调控框架，认为晚期β5i抑制有临床前支持，早期激活仍属理论概念。

papers.reason: 为流感相关急性肺损伤与炎症老化中的蛋白酶体调控假说提供背景框架，但不直接改变胸外科/胸部肿瘤的患者选择、手术决策或随访判断；可作为围术期呼吸道病毒感染与肺上皮应激机制的背景阅读。
papers.abstract_en: AbstractInfluenza A virus (IAV) infection initiates a high-stakes competition for proteostatic control. While the host reconfigures its degradative machinery for defense, the virus simultaneously hijacks host proteostatic and degradative pathways to facilitate replication and evade immunity. Central to this conflict is the proteasomal switch, a process in which constitutive proteasome subunits (β1, β2, β5) are replaced by their inducible counterparts (β1i, β2i, β5i) to form the immunoproteasome (iP). Although iP is classically recognized for optimizing MHC class I antigen presentation, emerging evidence reveals more nuanced roles in IAV infections. This review synthesizes current knowledge on iP as an effector of host defense and target for viral subversion. We synthesize emerging evidence and propose working models detailing how IAV proteins may selectively interfere with proteasomal subunits to stabilize pro-viral factors. Furthermore, we examine the hypothesis that the iP functions alongside broader ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD), and autophagic pathways as a proteostatic buffer to mitigate proteotoxic and oxidative stress in the infected epithelium. By evaluating how age-related proteostatic decay and viral subversion could impair cellular clearance machinery, we provide a conceptual framework for understanding how proteasomal dysregulation contributes to acute lung injury and the chronic inflammatory state termed as inflammaging. Finally, we propose a hypothesis-generating, biphasic framework for timing-dependent proteasomal modulation, contrasting preclinically supported late-stage β5i inhibition against the theoretical concept of early-stage activation to highlight translational hurdles in severe influenza.

papers.abstract_en: Deciphering structurally similar thiol analogues is vital for disease diagnosis, yet conventional one-to-one sensing strategies are intrinsically bottlenecked by signal cross-interference. Herein, we report an in situ reconstructed interfacial oxygen vacancies engineering strategy to prepare vacancy-rich Pt-CeO2 nanozymes for intelligent thiol differentiation. By combining incipient wetness impregnation with subsequent H2 reduction, isolated Pt single atoms were transformed into uniformly dispersed Pt clusters on CeO2 nanorods, simultaneously inducing abundant oxygen vacancies and dynamically coupled Pt-CeO2 interfaces. The optimized nanozyme exhibited significantly enhanced peroxidase-like catalytic activity over its single-atom state or directly deposited cluster counterparts. Crucially, the boosted catalytic kinetics significantly amplified the subtle response discrepancies among different thiols, yielding highly resolved time-dependent fingerprints. By integrating these distinct kinetic profiles with multivariate statistical analysis and predictive machine learning models, accurate differentiation of thiol species, complex multicomponent mixtures and clinical serum samples was achieved. This work not only provides insights into reconstruction-induced interfacial defect engineering but also establishes an effective framework for intelligent kinetic sensing in early disease screening.

papers.abstract_en: Nanofluidic ion gating underpins both biological signal transduction and iontronic signal processing. However, a simple and reliable mechanism that functions independently of local electrochemical conditions remains unavailable, hindering interference-free integration of artificial iontronic components with biological counterparts. Here, we present a nanofluidic device that enabled ionic gating through pervaporation-driven precipitation and rehydration-driven dissolution (PP&RD) of salt solutions within a nanochannel. Pervaporation induced local salt precipitation in the nanochannel, forming an electrical blockage that suppressed conductance (OFF state), whereas rehydration dissolved the precipitate and restored the conductance (ON state). The ionic gating device exhibited an ON-OFF conductance ratio exceeding 100, fully reversible operation performance, and robust switching across experimental conditions. By integrating two ionic gates in parallel or in series within a single device, we further implement Boolean OR and AND logic operations. PP&RD-based ionic gating thus provided a simple, versatile, and practical foundation for scalable iontronic circuit architecture.

papers.abstract_en: Non-Hermitian systems host a wealth of exotic phenomena, yet their temporal topology-particularly in time-reversal-symmetry-broken conditions-remains largely unexplored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate topological memory emerging from hysteresis-driven dynamics in a nonreciprocal microwave scattering system. The scattering singularity, encompassing both backscattering zeros and nonreciprocal exceptional points (EPs), serves as the cornerstone of this effect. Magnetic hysteresis induces a history-dependent trajectory of the complex scattering parameter that winds around such singularities, giving rise to quantized topological charges and sharp transitions when crossing them. At the limit of infinite nonreciprocity, backscattering zeros facilitate access to EPs, drastically easing their realization and yielding enhanced frequency combs near the transition. Extending these dynamics to free-space broadcasting and circulator-based topological insulators, we demonstrate nonreciprocity-assisted transport and long-distance preservation of scattering singularities. Our results uncover the interplay among singularity, nonreciprocity, and Floquet engineering, establishing a unified platform for exploring temporal topology and in-memory non-Hermitian photonics.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Glioblastoma is the most aggressive and fatal primary malignant brain tumour in adults, characterised by extensive intra-tumour heterogeneity, diffuse infiltration into surrounding brain tissue. Despite advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, patient prognosis remains poor, underscoring the critical need for improved biological insight to guide precision medicine potential strategies. Although traditional bulk genomic and transcriptomic analyses have made a substantial contribution to understanding glioblastoma pathophysiology, such average molecular signals across cell populations obscures tumour microenvironment influence and clinically significant cellular states. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics technologies have revolutionised glioblastoma research by enabling high-resolution analysis of tumour composition, cellular plasticity, and spatial organisation. These modalities have revealed that glioblastoma is composed of dynamic and plastic cellular states as opposed to fixed molecular subtypes, including stem-like and therapy-resistant populations that contribute to recurrence. The tumour architecture is preserved by spatially resolved transcriptomic and proteomic approaches, which reveal regional transcriptional programmes influenced by the tumour ecosystem. The findings provide a more resolved view of glioblastoma evolution and treatment resistance, challenging current classification systems. However, significant challenges remain in integrating these high-dimensional datasets, managing technical and computational demands, and translating these approaches into clinically scalable workflows which collectively hinder their translational adoption. This review aims to synthesise recent advances in glioblastoma single-cell and spatial omics, critically evaluating both advantages and limitations in understanding tumour heterogeneity and tumour microenvironmental interactions. Furthermore, it assesses the current challenges of glioblastoma precision medicine and evaluates the potential of these technologies to advance such approaches.

papers.abstract_en: Microplastics (MPs) pollution has emerged as a pervasive contaminant in remote environments; however, its occurrence in high-altitude snow remains poorly constrained. Here, we provide baseline evidence of MP contamination in snow from four mountaineering camps on Mount Aconcagua (6,962 masl), the highest peak in the Americas and in the entire Western and Southern Hemispheres. Microplastics were identified using µFTIR-ATR spectroscopy. The mean MPs concentration was 38 MP L-1, with site-specific values of 79 ± 37, 27 ± 8.3, 40 ± 16, and 5 ± 1 MP L-1 at the Plaza de Mulas base camp, and at the Canada, Nido de Condores, and Berlin higher elevations camps, respectively. Significantly higher concentrations at the base camp highlight the influence of intense human activity on MP accumulation, even in these remote high-mountain settings. Fibers (<5 mm), predominantly blue, were the dominant shape (90%), and polymer analysis revealed polyester, polyethylene, and epoxy as the main constituents. These findings indicate that snow is an effective matrix for assessing atmospheric deposition of MPs in andine environments. The spatial distribution of MPs suggests that local emissions associated with mountaineering activities represent a key source, although long-range atmospheric transport cannot be excluded. Our study provides the first documented evidence of the pollution of MPs in this world-famous climbing area, underscoring the vulnerability of high-altitude ecosystems to plastic pollution. Given the ecological significance and increasing human pressure in the Aconcagua Provincial Park, these results highlight the urgent need for targeted waste management strategies and regulatory actions to mitigate MP inputs in this fragile mountain environment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cannabis is the most used illicit substance among adolescents. Regular cannabis use is linked to cognitive and psychosocial difficulties. As no pharmacological treatment has proven effective, psychological interventions, including motivational interviewing (MI), cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and family-based approaches, remain central. However, adolescent-specific evidence remains limited. TIMCA was developed as a ten-session integrative psychotherapy combining MI, CBT, and integrated attachment therapy. While family therapy may not be indicated for all adolescents, parental involvement remains important for the adolescent-parent relationship. TIMCA therefore combines individual and parent-adolescent sessions to address cannabis use alongside attachment-related and emotion-regulation processes. OBJECTIVES: This pilot randomized controlled trial evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of TIMCA and explored changes over time in cannabis use and relational, emotional, anxiety/depressive, and treatment-adherence outcomes compared with treatment as usual (TAU). METHODS: Thirty-nine adolescents with cannabis use disorder were randomly assigned to TIMCA (n = 19) or TAU (n = 20) in two outpatient addiction services in the Paris metropolitan area. Cannabis use, attachment security, emotion regulation, anxiety, and depressive symptoms were assessed at baseline, mid-treatment, post-treatment, and 1-month follow-up using self-report measures and urine toxicology. RESULTS: TIMCA was feasible and acceptable, with high treatment adherence. Exploratory analyses showed significant within-group changes, including reductions in cannabis use, emotion dysregulation, and depressive symptoms, along with improved attachment security. In TAU, within-group changes did not reach statistical significance, and no significant between-group differences were detected. CONCLUSION: TIMCA appears feasible and acceptable, supporting further evaluation in adequately powered trials with longer follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: To address low affinity and reaction rate in monovalent ligand-aptamer binding, herein, we propose a bivalent binding-cooperated hybridization assembly (bbHA) strategy to light up the ratiometric fluorescence of convertible Ag nanoclusters (cAgNC) for detecting adenosine triphosphate (ATP). Two identical repeats of ATP-recognizable aptamer splits (a1 and a2) are separately programmed in an aptamer templating strand (aT) and an aptamer converter strand (aC), while two pairs of cAgNC-clustering and emission-converting segments are tethered in aT (template-a1-a1-template) and aC (converter-a2-a2-converter), respectively. Two tandem red cAgNC emitters are preferably developed in aT. Upon presenting ATP, the affinity recognition by a specific aptamer (a1/a2) entity enables cooperative binding events for triggering rapid complementary hybridization of aT and aC. The other proximal a1/a2 pair is bulged and merged to speed up the second ATP affinity binding. The structurally stable aT·2ATP·aC complex is formed to orient two ended converters and clusters together, thereby modulating its red fluorescence into green through electronic interactions between Ag0 and particular nucleobases. The resulting signal ratio of dual-emissive cAgNC exhibits a linear dependence on ATP, achieving sensitive and accurate quantification via inherent built-in correction. In contrast to the monovalent mechanism, the bbHA-based strategy features superior assay performances such as higher target responsiveness, faster reaction kinetics, and more efficient transduction. Thus, this label-free method would offer a new paradigm to construct simplified, specific, robust, and cost-effective sensing platforms for applicable assay of various small-molecule analytes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: As climate-related events, such as floods and bushfires, become more frequent and severe, it is increasingly important to understand health consumers' needs during these crises. This study explored the lived experiences of Australians who managed a health condition-either their own or as a carer-during climate events. METHODS: In-depth, one-on-one online interviews were conducted with 20 participants aged 18-80 years living with a range of chronic and acute health conditions. Findings were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Participants faced challenges, including the exacerbation of existing and newly developed health conditions, disruptions to healthcare services and the home environment, as well as knowledge or information barriers, that complicated health condition management. Participants adopted various strategies for these challenges, including self-management practices, accessing social support, leveraging communication channels, and seeking alternative care pathways. CONCLUSIONS: Clear, accessible communication and consumer preparedness support are critical for maintaining care continuity during climate events. Developing system-level contingency plans for alternative care could ensure care continuity. While digital tools can facilitate access to information, their availability could be limited when infrastructure is disrupted.

papers.abstract_en: Targeting interleukin (IL) signaling has long been constrained by the extensive, topologically flat and dynamic nature of cytokine-receptor interfaces. While monoclonal antibodies have validated these pathways clinically, achieving comparable efficacy with small molecules or non-antibody modalities demands overcoming steep pharmacokinetic and structural hurdles. In this review, we examine the translational trajectory across IL-17, IL-23, IL-1-family and IL-6 pathways-tracing compounds from in silico and biophysical hit identification to cellular and clinical validation. Rather than focusing merely on surface binding, we dissect the interplay between pocket dynamics (cryptic sites), modality selection (orally bioavailable macrocycles and traditional Rule-of-Five chemotypes) and the systemic liabilities of pathway crosstalk. These case studies provide pragmatic frameworks for converting structural ligandability into durable clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: The 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), involved limited international exportation but remained centred in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The outbreak tested whether earlier institutional mobilisation translated into timely field delivery. We conducted a structured narrative review of peer-reviewed research, official reports and operational guidance on epidemiology, diagnostics, medical countermeasures (MCMs), One Health surveillance, clinical care, infection prevention and control (IPC), community engagement and cross-border preparedness. Key institutional mechanisms for emergency decision-making, coordination and MCM prioritisation were activated earlier than during the 2013-2016 Ebola virus disease epidemic in West Africa, widening the window for action. Field delivery nevertheless remained uneven: the model-adjusted median onset-to-sampling delay was 4.8 days among 129 confirmed patients, while insecurity posed additional challenges for field response. Preparedness was further constrained by uncertainty about reservoir ecology, limited clinical validation of BDBV-specific diagnostics and the absence of MCMs with established efficacy in BVD. We therefore propose a One Health alert-to-action pathway linking human, animal, environmental and community signals to BDBV-inclusive confirmation, safe care, IPC, cross-border continuity, accountable governance and feedback-informed adaptation. Earlier activation is a preparedness gain, but protection depends on whether that advantage is carried through reliable, traceable and equitable operational hand-offs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Socially interactive AI can elicit meaningful relational experiences. Studies often conflate attachment, anthropomorphism, companionship, dependence, and addiction, and group embodied robots with dissimilar software. METHODS: This critical narrative review of a reconstructed, non-exhaustive corpus (Grant & Booth, 2009) is interpretive, not aggregative, because the initial search records disagree. We rebuilt the evidence set from the initially identified literature, separated primary from contextual sources, and sorted them by embodiment and dialogue architecture. Coding kept attachment functions distinct from related constructs. A reproducible OpenAlex and PubMed search (2010-2025) retrieved only one of the 12 primary reports. A coverage probe found 34 further provisionally eligible reports. We claim no exhaustive coverage or full PRISMA compliance. RESULTS: Reclassification left 12 primary reports and seven contextual sources. In these reports, relational significance appeared with embodied robots, non-LLM systems, and generative systems, carried by co-presence and touch or by conversational contingency, personalisation, and apparent continuity. Most measured companionship, trust, social presence, perceived support, or one problematic-use indicator. Few covered more than one attachment-system function. None established a behavioural-addiction syndrome. The predominantly cross-sectional, self-selected evidence cannot establish whether heavier use causes loneliness. CONCLUSIONS: A relationship with an AI system can matter without amounting to reciprocal human attachment or behavioural addiction. Within the reviewed corpus, the evidence supports a broad, uneven continuum of involvement. Omitted studies may change the apparent mix of constructs, technologies, and outcomes. Progress requires longitudinal, technology-stratified studies with construct-specific measures that establish temporal order and impairment and separate embodiment from generative capability.

papers.abstract_en: Despite major scientific advances, pharmaceutical R&D productivity remains a persistent challenge. This study motivates a network-centric model in which R&D performance can depend not only on firm-level scientific capabilities, but also increasingly on effective positioning and orchestration within innovation networks. Bibliometric analysis showed that previously reported network reconfiguration during the mid-2010s was temporally aligned with the rise of precision medicine. Approval-based analysis revealed the growing contribution of spin-offs and changing roles of large pharmaceutical companies, particularly for new modalities. An exploratory case analysis revealed distinct strategic trajectories in two spin-offs developing conventional or new modality products. Together, these observations converge to suggest strategic implications for pharmaceutical companies, investors, and policymakers navigating the era of precision medicine and new modalities.

papers.abstract_en: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) plays a crucial role in environmental remediation, chemical synthesis, and energy storage. Nevertheless, its industrial production is energy consuming with significant environmental burdens. Here we show a proof-of-concept thermoelectrocatalytic strategy for H2O2 production directly from seawater, driven solely by low-grade waste heat. A low-temperature thermoelectric (TE) material, Na- and Pb-codoped SnSe, is designed as a catalyst that enables efficient H2O2 generation under a moderate temperature gradient (ΔT). This system achieves an H2O2 production rate of 6.1 mmol g-1 h-1 from seawater under ΔT = 120 K, which is competitive with the representative photocatalytic systems. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that Na/Pb-codoping improves the TE properties, promotes charge carrier migration under ΔT, and promotes the oxygen reduction reaction toward H2O2 formation. The naturally formed strong electric layer at the catalyst-seawater interface further promotes both reaction kinetics and thermodynamic driving forces. Our finding provides a sustainable route for H2O2 production from seawater using waste heat and demonstrates great potential of TE-catalysis for waste heat utilization.

papers.abstract_en: Methadone is a long-standing synthetic opioid that remains clinically important for pain management and opioid use disorder, yet it exemplifies the dual nature of opioid drug discovery. Despite its therapeutic success, methadone exhibits complex pharmacokinetics, polypharmacology and safety liabilities that have limited its broader clinical application. This review examines methadone as a case study to illustrate how chemical structure, stereochemistry, receptor pharmacology and pharmacokinetic properties collectively shape therapeutic outcomes and risk. We summarize key advances in methadone synthesis, structure-activity relationships, pharmacology and clinical limitations and discuss how lessons learned from methadone continue to inform modern opioid drug discovery. Particular emphasis is placed on balancing efficacy, duration of action and safety in the design of next-generation opioid therapeutics.

papers.authors_conclusion: 健康新生儿、婴儿与儿童的止血系统并非发育不足，而是针对其生理情境被精确设计和校准；年龄特异性参考区间变化与功能性代偿机制支持“儿科止血是发育适应的生理学范本”这一观点；作者批判“immature”等过时术语，指出误标在儿童血栓与止血领域的下游后果，并呼吁修订术语体系以更准确反映发育中止血系统的功能复杂性。

papers.abstract_en: The hemostatic system of neonates, infants, and children has historically and recently been described using the term "immature", a label that implies deficiency, incompleteness, or even developmental failure. We challenge that characterization. Drawing on more than three decades of advances in developmental hemostasis, we argue that the hemostatic system of healthy newborns, infants, and children is not underdeveloped, but rather precisely designed and calibrated for its physiological context. Age-specific changes reflected in reference ranges, and functional compensatory mechanisms, support the view that pediatric hemostasis represents a physiological masterclass in developmental adaptation, not an imperfect approximation of adult function. We examine the historical trajectory of this field, critique the use of outdated terminology, identify key conceptual gaps, and discuss the downstream consequences of mislabeling in the context of pediatric thrombosis and hemostasis. We conclude with a call for a revised lexicon that more accurately reflects the functional sophistication of the developing hemostatic system.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. Disulfide-bond oxidized HMGB1 (ds-HMGB1) functions as a core damage-associated molecular pattern that mediates acute myocardial injury. Nevertheless, commercially available HMGB1 reagents exhibit mixed proteoforms, unstable biological activity and low receptor affinity, which greatly hinder mechanistic investigations in this field. This study generated a novel mutant full-length murine ds-HMGB1, systematically dissected its molecular mechanisms underlying aggravated ischemic myocardial injury, and sought to provide a standardized protein reagent and theoretical framework for HMGB1-targeted therapies against myocardial damage. A K184S/K185S mutant HMGB1 plasmid was constructed, and protein purified by three-step chromatography. Structural modeling, mass spectrometry, SPR and PLA were used to analyze conformation, modification and receptor binding kinetics. Hypoxic cardiomyocyte co-culture and mouse myocardial infarction models were established. Flow cytometry, echocardiography, histological staining, qPCR, Western blot and RNA-seq were applied to detect molecular phenotypes and signaling pathways. The K184S/K185S mutation preserved the native overall conformation and functional disulfide bond of HMGB1, while markedly enhancing HMGB1 binding to RAGE and promoting TLR4-MD2 complex assembly. In vitro experiments revealed that mutant ds-HMGB1 either acted directly on cardiomyocytes or synergized hypoxia through endothelial-cardiomyocyte paracrine signaling to induce robust intracellular ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. In vivo administration expanded myocardial infarct size, impaired cardiac systolic performance and exacerbated inflammatory infiltration in cardiac tissue. Transcriptomic profiling identified 53 core injury genes specifically upregulated by ds-HMGB1 under ischemic stress. The mutant ds-HMGB1 developed in this study addresses the intrinsic drawbacks of commercial HMGB1 preparations. We further identified 53 key myocardial injury genes modulated by ds-HMGB1. This work delivers a standardized experimental reagent and multi-layered mechanistic evidence supporting HMGB1 as a therapeutic target for acute myocardial infarction.

papers.abstract_en: Direct photolithography offers a transformative photoresist-free route for high-precision integration in electronic and optoelectronic platforms. Despite significant advancements in quantum dots (QDs), existing methods often degrade optoelectronic performance due to the inherent surface ligand changes during photolithographic processing. Here, we introduce a reversible photolithography strategy to overcome this bottleneck. This strategy is based on the first wavelength-gated, reversible ligand crosslinking and decrosslinking cycle, enabling the dynamic and reversible control over the photolithographic process. Using this approach, we achieve high-efficient and high-fidelity QD photolithography with restored QD structure and functionality. The reversible process further enables high-performance electroluminescence, with one of the highest luminance values of 125,016 cd m-2 at 5.0 V and a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.41%. Moreover, we demonstrate an ultrahigh-resolution nano-pixelated device with a peak EQE of 17.08% at 21,000 PPI. This work presents a photo-reversible crosslinking system that decouples photolithographic patterning from performance degradation, offering a versatile platform for high-end QD-based displays and other advanced optoelectronics.

papers.abstract_en: Simultaneously monitoring ammonia (NH3) leakage and human motion is desirable for safeguarding astronauts' safety in spacecraft equipped with NH3-driven propulsion, in which stable and selective NH3 sensing combined with reliable pressure detection is highly required. However, little is reported on a sensing material that synergistically presents the required NH3 and pressure sensing. Here, wearable NH3 and pressure sensing has been developed using PANI-wrapping carbon-intermixed Fe2O3 hierarchical microarchitectures (PANI@C-Fe2O3 HMAs), which have been synthesized by employing fern-shaped C-Fe2O3 HMAs with trunk/branches as structural precursors, followed by conformal PANI-wrapping. Beneficially, PANI@C-Fe2O3 HMAs present a wide detection range of 0.1 ppm-10 v/v%, 167-day-long stability and high selectivity toward NH3. Further, a pressure sensor prototype has been constructed by laminating PET tapes onto the HMAs-integrated flexible electrode, revealing an excellent pressure-dependent response and machine-learning-assisted human-motion recognition. Such superior dual sensing is attributed to the texturing behavior, in which conformal texturing of PANI along the hierarchical surface of C-Fe2O3 HMAs establishes heterojunctions with a built-in electric field to amplify resistance modulation, while fern-shaped HMAs with trunk/branches provide abundant active interfaces and electron transport pathways. Practically, a wearable dual-sensing device that integrates flexible NH3 and pressure sensor prototypes has been built with reliable dual-sensing responses.

papers.abstract_en: We review the genotoxic effects of trace metal exposure and evaluate an efficient treatment strategy. Toxic metal(loid)s cause significant risks to animal health and ecosystems because of their toxicity and bioaccumulation potential. We then examine the mechanisms of genotoxicity, which include direct DNA damage, oxidative stress, epigenetic alterations, and interference with DNA repair mechanisms. This review highlights the health implications of toxic metal exposure: symptoms like increased cancer risks, reproductive and developmental toxicity, and chronic health disorders. Various assessment and biomonitoring techniques for toxic metal genotoxicity, including biomarkers like DNA adducts and chromosomal aberrations, and analytical methods such as the comet assay and PCR-based molecular assays, are discussed. We evaluate treatment strategies, including chelation therapy, antioxidant supplementation, and phytoremediation, emphasizing their efficacy and limitations. The importance of regulatory frameworks, public health interventions, and environmental remediation programs in mitigating toxic metal exposure is also discussed. We identify research gaps in understanding the long-term effects of low-dose chronic exposure and interactions between multiple toxic metals. This comprehensive review contributes to the field by synthesizing current knowledge on toxic metal genotoxicity and treatment strategies. We provide valuable insights for researchers, healthcare professionals, and policymakers toward the development of more effective prevention and intervention strategies. We emphasize challenges and future directions and highlight the importance of continued research in this critical area of public health and environmental science.

papers.abstract_en: We have developed a trilayered nanofiber composite (KTP) via successive electrospinning, engineered with hydrophilicity gradients supporting rapid hemostasis and wound healing. The innermost hydrophilic keratin-PVA layer initiated clotting, middle TEOS-PVA coaxial layer enhanced hemostatic efficacy, and outer PVDF layer provided protective barrier. KTP showed robust mechanical strength, cyto- and hemocompatibility, and supported cell migration. It triggered both intrinsic and extrinsic coagulation pathways and enabled platelet- and RBC-independent plasma clotting. Consistent with this, KTP upregulates tissue factor (TF) and modulates factor XII (FXII) levels in contact with plasma, indicating coordinated activation of extrinsic and contact pathways. Fibrinogen adsorption and fibrin clot stabilization occurred within 2 min, surpassing commercial dressings. Molecular docking revealed keratin's binding with coagulation proteins, which supports its mechanistic role in blood clotting. FE-SEM confirmed platelet adhesion and RBC entrapment; immunofluorescence imaging showed strong CD62P and vinculin expression, indicating active platelet engagement. In vivo injury models demonstrated rapid and stable clot formation within 35-40 s. KTP also accelerated tissue repair fully closing wounds by day 10, with complete re-epithelialization and hair follicle regeneration by day 12. Overall, this functionally graded nanofiber patch demonstrates strong potential for rapid hemorrhage control and accelerated wound healing for trauma care.

papers.abstract_en: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) involves impaired bone remodeling, intestinal dysbiosis, and immune imbalance, which together limit the long-term benefit of conventional oral bisphosphonate therapy. Here, we report LpEVs@ALN, a probiotic extracellular vesicle-based oral nanoplatform constructed by loading alendronate (ALN) into Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-derived extracellular vesicles. LpEVs@ALN maintains vesicle integrity and epithelial compatibility, improves ALN retention under acidic exposure, and enables sustained ALN release at intestinal pH conditions. In dexamethasone-suppressed BMSCs, LpEVs@ALN enhances osteogenic differentiation, as evidenced by increased ALP activity and matrix mineralization. In zebrafish GIOP models, LpEVs@ALN improves cranial mineralization, new bone formation, scale regeneration, and locomotor/shoaling performance; accompanied by reduced inflammatory tone, improved ALP/RANKL-associated bone turnover readouts, and rebalanced oxidative-stress indices. Microbiome profiling shows recovery of richness/diversity and reduced Proteobacteria dominance, while scale RNA-seq reveals broad reversal of glucocorticoid-driven dysregulation toward pro-osteogenic and anti-inflammatory programs. Integrated correlation analysis further linked microbial remodeling with systemic and skeletal responses, suggesting involvement of the gut-immune-bone axis. Collectively, LpEVs@ALN alleviates GIOP by combining ALN-mediated bone protection with probiotic extracellular vesicle-associated regulation of intestinal and systemic homeostasis, highlighting its potential as an oral therapeutic strategy for GIOP.

papers.abstract_en: Bacterial-fungal consortia (BFC) consistently outperform aseptic or single-species cultures in producing high-value secondary metabolites, yet the underlying cross-kingdom interaction mechanisms remain poorly understood. In food fermentations, BFCs enhance process robustness, substrate turnover, and bioactive profiles for sustainable functional foods. In these consortia, bacteria and fungi engage in complex cooperative and competitive interactions, involving signaling molecules, genetic regulation, and metabolic flux redistribution to enhance secondary metabolite yields. Based on the ecological compatibility and molecular communication mechanisms, a synthetic microbiology framework for constructing high-yield BFCs was proposed. This systematic approach included selecting appropriate coculture partners, setting up the BFC, and optimizing cultivation conditions. Functional BFCs can be effectively applied to: food fermentation, improving fermentation efficiency, nutritional value, flavor complexity, and food safety. The review provides an overview of BFCs for secondary metabolite production, with emphasis on their cross-kingdom communication mechanisms. It explores the construction and optimization of BFCs and their applications in food fermentation, identifying future directions for enhancing secondary metabolite yields.

papers.abstract_en: Top-down proteomics and top-down mass spectrometry approaches provide direct characterization of proteoforms; the specific molecular forms of proteins, including post-translational modifications, truncations, alternative splicing, and sequence variants. To date, most top-down studies have been performed under denaturing conditions, losing critical information about protein folding and noncovalent protein-protein and protein-ligand interactions. However, recent efforts to apply non-denaturing, or native, ionization to top-down mass spectrometry and top-down proteomics have shown substantial promise for characterizing these higher-order and more transient interactions. This review covers progress over the last 35 years in non-denaturing top-down approaches and addresses the inherent strengths and challenges of the technique. We cover three major areas of applications: (1) Ligand binding and drug discovery, (2) Structural biology, and (3) Proteomics aspects and bioinformatics.

papers.abstract_en: Spherical nucleic acids (SNAs) are a unique class of nucleic acid nanotherapeutics characterized by densely packed, radially arranged oligonucleotides surrounding a nanoparticle or molecular core, or core-free nanoscale structures. Compared with conventional linear nucleic acids, SNAs exhibit excellent cellular uptake, resistance to nuclease degradation, and efficient target recognition without the help of transfection agents. This review summarizes SNAs' structural diversity, design principles, and the multiscale delivery barriers they encounter. We mainly focus on liposomal SNAs (LSNAs) as programmable platforms for cancer immunotherapy. We emphasize how lipid chemistry, membrane architecture, and anchor stability control lymphoid distribution, immune-cell uptake, antigen presentation, and strong antitumor immunity, rather than seeing lipids as inert carriers. Furthermore, we also discuss current developments in gene silencing, CRISPR-based genome editing, and stimulus-responsive multimodal therapies, highlighting the significant therapeutic advancements of SNAs like clinical trial NU-0129 and LSNAs like cavrotolimod. Finally, we describe present translational obstacles and potential prospects by using SNAs as next-generation precision immunotherapeutics.

papers.abstract_en: Enantioselective construction of unnatural α-amino acids is highly desirable due to their widespread applications across biochemistry, medicinal industry and materials science. Herein, we report a straightforward and efficient method for the assembly of structurally diverse enantioenriched α-amino acid derivatives from readily accessible enamides and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) by merging nickel hydride catalysis and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). The protocol affords good yields and high enantioselectivities of products which easily can be converted into unprotected unnatural α-amino acids and other valuable chiral building blocks. Notably, the enantiopurity of the products can be further enhanced by normal flash chromatography on silica gel, providing a practical platform for enantiopurification of both oily and solid products. This radical cross-coupling reaction proceeds under mild conditions, tolerates a broad range of functional groups and is amenable to the construction of enantioenriched α-amino amides bearing active pharmaceutical ingredients on the sidechain.

papers.abstract_en: Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells have played a central role in the production of therapeutic proteins since their initial isolation in the 1950s. Over the decades, scientific innovations have transformed CHO cells into the powerhouse of the biopharmaceutical industry. From rudimentary culture conditions and random integration of transgenes into the host genome, to synthetic biology, genetic engineering, high-performing chemically defined media, targeted transgene integration and AI-driven cell line development strategies, each decade has introduced transformative tools, knowledge, and insights to improve CHO cell line development and characterization processes. This review outlines the chronological history of the CHO cell line development process, decade by decade, highlighting central milestones and innovations, technological breakthroughs, and the role of key innovative steps that have enabled modern cell line development workflows and ultimately the industrial-scale manufacturing of biologics.

papers.abstract_en: Malaria and neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) affect over 1 billion people worldwide. Both disease categories share overlapping geographical regions, dependence on broad-spectrum treatments and common vectors, justifying their co-consideration as a unified therapeutic challenge. The broad-spectrum action of current treatments renders them susceptible to emerging drug resistance and off-target toxicity, which requires platforms that are specific yet effective across diverse pathogens. Aptamers are single-stranded oligonucleotides that fold into three-dimensional structures, enabling high-affinity binding to specific molecular targets and functioning as direct therapeutics or targeted delivery vehicles. We evaluate aptamers developed for malaria and NTDs, classify them into direct and delivery therapeutics and map candidates by preclinical validation stage, thereby constructing a translational road map that positions aptamers as a structurally adaptable platform addressing unmet treatment needs.

papers.abstract_en: Caffeoylquinic acids (CQAs) are phenolic compounds found in a wide variety of plants. These are a broad class of secondary metabolites that are primarily synthesized by esterifying quinic acids and hydroxycinnamic acids (ferulic acid, p-coumaric acid, and caffeic acid). The most common and significant of these in the human diet is chlorogenic acid, also known as 5-O-caffeoylquinic acid (5-CQA). In addition, plants have been found to contain mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra-esters. CQAs exhibit a wide range of biological activities, including anti-inflammatory, anti-cancer, neuroprotective, antiviral, antibacterial, antiparasitic, and antidiabetic effects. In addition to their dietary significance, CQAs are used extensively in pharmacology, animal husbandry, food preservation, and the manufacturing of skin care products. CQA accumulation varies greatly across several species, plant parts, and organs. As a result, in vitro cell and organ culture techniques have been used by researchers to produce CQAs. In a variety of plant species, callus, cells, adventitious/hairy roots, and plantlet cultures have been established. In these culture types, several techniques, including cell line selection, appropriate media, salt strength, plant growth regulators, chemical and physical variables, and elicitation, have been successfully assessed.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, and many current drugs and devices are limited by off-target exposure, weak responsiveness to pathological cues, and reduced performance under pulsatile blood flow. Biomolecule-assembled materials, constructed from nucleic acids, proteins/peptides, polysaccharides, and lipids/vesicles, offer a promising way to address these limitations. Their functions arise from sequence- or chemistry-governed assembly rules that encode molecular recognition, transport, and mechanical behavior across multiple scales, from nanostructures to tissue-facing interfaces. This review summarizes recent progress in biomolecule-assembled materials across CVD prevention, diagnosis, therapy, and regeneration. Programmable bio-assemblies support rapid sensing and lesion-localized intervention, while also enabling bioactive coatings, injectable depots, and membrane-mimetic carriers for plaque targeting and drug delivery. By comparing material classes through shared cardiovascular tasks and hemodynamic constraints, modular hybrids suggest potential advantages that merit further investigation under physiologically relevant conditions. Clinical translation will depend on predictive assembly design, standardized manufacturing and quality control, and in vivo validation under physiologically relevant flow. Through converting molecular assembly rules into scalable, hemodynamically robust functions, biomolecule-assembled materials offer a unifying design language for next-generation cardiovascular diagnosis and therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Neuropathy target esterase (NTE), localized predominantly to the endoplasmic reticulum, is highly expressed within the nervous system. Under physiological conditions, NTE functions mainly as a phospholipase B/lysophospholipase involved in phosphatidylcholine and lysophosphatidylcholine turnover, thereby maintaining phospholipid homeostasis, membrane integrity, and axonal stability. In toxicology, NTE is of particular interest as the principal molecular target in organophosphorus-induced delayed neurotoxicity (OPIDN), a syndrome that develops days to weeks after exposure to certain organophosphorus (OP) compounds. Unlike acute cholinergic toxicity caused by acetylcholinesterase inhibition, OPIDN is initiated by inhibition of NTE followed by "aging" of the enzyme-inhibitor complex, an essentially irreversible process considered critical for neuropathic outcome. The resulting loss of NTE activity disrupts phospholipid metabolism, promotes lysophospholipid accumulation, endoplasmic reticulum stress, calcium dyshomeostasis, and cytoskeletal breakdown, leading to distal axon degeneration in both the central and peripheral nervous systems. Clinically, OPIDN manifests after a latent phase with progressive weakness, sensory abnormalities, gait impairment, and in severe cases persistent spasticity or paralysis. This review summarizes the current knowledge on NTE structure, catalytic function, tissue distribution, and physiological significance, and integrates these findings with the molecular and clinical features of OPIDN. Particular attention is paid to the distinction between aging (neuropathic) and non-aging (non-neuropathic) NTE inhibitors, the structural determinants of neuropathic potential, and its clinical implications.

papers.abstract_en: Ophthalmic engineering is defined by a rigorous set of constraints including the need for absolute optical clarity, precise viscoelasticity, and the ability to navigate formidable physiological barriers. Polymeric hydrogels have ascended as the quintessential material class to resolve these conflicts by leveraging their high content of water to create a seamless interface with native ocular tissues. This review critically examines the transition of these materials from passive structural substitutes to dynamic and stimulus-responsive systems. The molecular strategies required to balance mechanical robustness with biodegradation are dissected alongside the integration of responsive moieties that react to physiological cues. These principles are explored through cutting-edge clinical applications including suprachoroidal drug depots, bio-integrative tissue sealants, and closed-loop biosensing contact lenses. Finally, the discussion addresses the translational gap separating laboratory innovation from industrial manufacturing. By identifying persistent hurdles such as the inherent trade-off between long-term stability and transparency as well as sterilization compatibility, a strategic roadmap is outlined for the next generation of vision-restoring technologies.

papers.abstract_en: Brain-computer interface (BCI) provides a direct communication pathway between the brain and external devices and has been applied in neurological disease treatment, motor rehabilitation, and human-computer interaction. Electrodes play essential roles in recording and modulating neural signals, and their performance directly affects signal quality, spatial resolution, and long-term stability. Traditional rigid electrodes suffer from mechanical mismatch with brain tissue, which may induce tissue damage and reduce recording stability during long-term implantation. Flexible electrodes offer improved mechanical compatibility and have emerged as promising alternatives. Recent advances in materials science, micro/nanofabrication, and interface engineering have enhanced the electrical, mechanical, and biological performance of flexible BCI electrodes. This review summarizes neural signal characteristics, electrode requirements, fabrication strategies, and performance optimization approaches. The major fabrication methods include microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), printing and transfer, laser processing and thermal drawing, and electrospinning, while deposition and surface modification are discussed as functional enhancement strategies. The review also highlights challenges associated with large-scale manufacturing, long-term stability, and the physical and clinical limitations of invasive, semi-invasive, and noninvasive electrodes. Future directions involving intelligent, wireless, and self-powered systems, together with clinical translation, are discussed to promote the development of flexible electrodes for BCI applications.

papers.abstract_en: Mitigating on-target off-tumor toxicity remains a central challenge for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy for solid tumors. We developed a hypoxia-inducible CAR-T-cell product targeting carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) that restricts CAR activation to hypoxic tumor niches via oxygen-dependent expression control. In this first-in-human, phase I trial enrolling heavily pretreated patients with relapsed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), a single infusion of the investigational product achieved an objective response rate of 47% and a disease control rate of 87%, with a manageable safety profile. Exploratory analyses showed that clinical outcomes were associated with baseline factors. Deep single-cell profiling indicated that the clinical response was associated with the expansion of hypoxia-adapted, tumor-reactive-like CD8+ T cells alongside coordinated functional maturation of natural killer (NK) cells. Collectively, these data provide clinical proof-of-concept for hypoxia-inducible CAR design and inform the rational development of strategies leveraging tumor microenvironmental features in solid tumor cellular immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Interim analysis of the Neotorch study demonstrated significant benefit in event-free survival (EFS) and major pathological response (MPR) rate for perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable Stage Ⅲ non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here, we report the final analysis results of the overall Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients from this study. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients with treatment-naïve resectable Stage II, or Stage IIIA, IIIB (N2) NSCLC, were randomized to receive toripalimab or placebo plus chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment (3 cycles), adjuvant treatment (1 cycle), and toripalimab or placebo monotherapy as maintenance treatment (up to 13 cycles). The primary endpoints of this study were EFS assessed by investigators and MPR evaluated by blinded independent pathologic review (BIPR) in Stage Ⅲ patients, as well as the overall Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients. RESULTS: A total of 501 patients in China were randomized (toripalimab arm: N=250, placebo arm: N=251). The baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the 2 arms. At the final analysis (median follow-up of 48.2 months), the investigator-assessed EFS was significantly improved in the toripalimab arm with stratified hazard ratio (HR) of 0.52 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.39, 0.68; stratified P <0.0001), and the median EFS in the toripalimab arm was not reached, while 20.2 months in the placebo arm. The inter-arm difference of MPR rate was statistically significant and clinically meaningful (47% vs 9%, P<0.0001). The OS prolongation was also statistically significant in the toripalimab arm (HR 0.66; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.89, P=0.0072), with median survival not reached in either arm. The safety profile was consistent with the interim analysis, with no new safety signals identified. CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy demonstrated durable and significant benefits on EFS, MPR, and OS in resectable Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ NSCLC patients, with a manageable safety profile.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In the DeLLphi-304 trial, at a median follow-up of <12 months, tarlatamab significantly improved overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and patient-reported outcomes (PROs), and demonstrated a favorable safety profile versus chemotherapy. We report efficacy and safety outcomes after extended follow-up in patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this phase 3, open-label trial, patients with SCLC whose disease had progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy were randomized (1:1) to receive either tarlatamab or chemotherapy (topotecan, lurbinectedin, or amrubicin) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death. The primary endpoint was OS. Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed PFS, objective response, disease control, duration of response per RECIST v1.1, PROs, and safety. RESULTS: As of data cutoff (18 February 2026), median OS was 13.6 and 8.4 months with tarlatamab and chemotherapy, respectively (median follow-up, 23.3 and 22.8 months). Median PFS was 4.2 and 3.2 months, respectively (median follow-up, 22.2 and 21.9 months). Kaplan-Meier estimated OS rates at 12/24 months were 55.9%/30.3% with tarlatamab versus 39.0%/14.9% with chemotherapy; corresponding PFS rates at 12/24 months were 20.6%/14.2% versus 5.9%/2.3%. Objective response rate was 35.4% with tarlatamab, including six confirmed complete responses versus 20.4% with chemotherapy; at data cutoff, ongoing responses were observed in 31.1% (28/90) versus 3.8% (2/52) of responders, respectively. Sustained disease control for ≥52 weeks was observed in 24.4% versus 4.3%. Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 3.2% versus 6.6%; grade ≥3 events decreased over time, with no serious TRAEs with onset ≥12 months. CRS and ICANS occurred early in treatment and were predominantly low grade. CONCLUSIONS: With extended follow-up, tarlatamab continues to demonstrate sustained and durable clinical benefit and a favorable long-term tolerability profile versus chemotherapy, in patients with SCLC after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, supporting its use as the standard of care in this setting.

papers.abstract_en: Background Low-dose CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening enables opportunistic volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) assessment, but its prognostic value is unclear. Purpose To evaluate fully automated LDCT-derived vBMD for predicting vertebral fractures and its association with mortality in individuals who heavily smoke. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included 55-74-year-old individuals who heavily smoked (≥30 pack-years) from the CT arm of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST), a multicenter randomized controlled trial of LDCT versus radiography (participants recruited August 2002 to April 2004). Automated SpineQ software (Bonescreen) was used to measure thoracic and lumbar vBMD (normal, ≥120 mg/cm3; low bone mass [osteopenia], 80 to <120 mg/cm3; osteoporosis, <80 mg/cm3) and vertebral fractures (Genant scale). The outcomes included 1- and 2-year incident vertebral fractures and 6-year mortality (active follow-up to 2009). Poisson and Cox models were adjusted for demographic variables, available comorbidities, and baseline vertebral fractures. Results The NLST included 26 722 participants in the CT arm, with 21 856 included in the present analysis (mean age, 61 years ± 5 [SD]; 12 854 male participants). The 2-year vertebral fracture incidence (n = 18 211 participants with 2-year LDCT) was 0.9% for those with normal bone mass, 2.0% for those with low bone mass (adjusted relative risk, 2.07 [95% CI: 1.70, 2.53]), and 5.9% for those with osteoporosis (adjusted relative risk, 3.40 [95% CI: 2.69, 4.30]). Mortality risk (n = 21 447 participants with completed follow-up [median, 6.65 years]) was associated with osteoporotic vBMD in men (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.24 [95% CI: 1.02, 1.50]). Conclusion Fully automated opportunistic assessment of spinal vBMD predicted vertebral fracture risk and was associated with mortality in men after adjustment. Individuals with osteoporotic vBMD who heavily smoked had a 2-year fracture incidence above the 5% treatment threshold according to current osteoporosis guidelines. Clinical trial registration no. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116. FINDINGS: Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group. INTERPRETATION: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. METHODS: HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 101 (41%) of 248 patients receiving ruzaltatug rezetecan and 93 (39%) of 239 patients receiving chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (64 [26%] of 248 patients vs 46 [19%] of 239 patients), decreased white blood cell count (29 [12%] vs 29 [12%]), and anaemia (15 [6%] vs 26 [11%]). TRAEs led to treatment discontinuation in three (1%) patients in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group and three (1%) in the chemotherapy group. One death (unknown cause) in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group was considered by the investigator to be possibly treatment related. INTERPRETATION: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting. FUNDING: Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Evidence regarding the effectiveness of physical activity (PA) policies within preschool settings remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of a cocreated preschool-level PA policy on children's accelerometer-measured PA during preschool hours. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-blind, parallel-group, cluster randomized clinical trial was performed at public preschools in Stockholm, Sweden. Of 156 randomly sampled preschools invited, 124 were randomized. Children aged 3 to 5 years with parental consent were recruited from September 14 to December 11, 2020, baseline measurements from September 23, 2020, to January 22, 2021, and 6-month follow-up from March 8 to June 11, 2021. Statistical analyses were performed from March 6, 2023, to October 25, 2024. INTERVENTION: A cocreated preschool-level PA policy implemented for 6 months vs usual practice. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Prespecified primary outcomes were between-group differences in change in moderate to vigorous PA, total PA, and steps during preschool hours, measured using wearable accelerometers. RESULTS: Among 3751 children (mean [SD] age, 4.44 [0.86] years; 1934 male [51.6%]), 1960 attended intervention preschools and 1791 attended control preschools. All 124 preschools completed follow-up; data were available for 1530 children (78.1%) in intervention schools at baseline and 1435 (73.2%) at follow-up and 1430 children (79.8%) in control schools at baseline and 1356 (75.7%) at follow-up. Intention-to-treat analyses included 3417 children (1770 intervention and 1647 control). Moderate to vigorous PA increased from 27.4 to 33.0 minutes per day in the intervention group and from 27.6 to 33.0 minutes per day in the control group (difference in change, 0.3 [95% CI, -0.7 to 1.3] minutes per day; P = .57). Total PA increased from 177.7 to 185.3 minutes per day in the intervention group and from 176.5 to 184.5 minutes per day in the control group (difference, -0.3 [95% CI, -3.3 to 2.7] minutes per day; P = .84). Steps increased from 5415 to 5953 per day in the intervention and from 5549 to 6078 per day in the control groups (difference, 8 [95% CI, -118 to 133] steps per day; P = .90). No participants withdrew because of adverse events. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cluster randomized clinical trial, a cocreated preschool PA policy did not increase children's PA beyond usual practice after 6 months. These findings highlight the complexity of translating policy adoption into measurable behavioral change and of detecting such change in preschool settings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04569578.
