papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Next-generation long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) treated with more than one insecticide have been insufficiently evaluated in West Africa. METHODS: In this cluster randomized clinical trial, 33 clusters of villages (1-3 villages per cluster) in Côte d'Ivoire were randomly assigned (11 clusters per group) to use pyrethroid-only (py-only; MAGNet) (control), piperonyl butoxide-pyrethroid (PBO-py; Veeralin), or chlorfenapyr-pyrethroid (CFP-py; Interceptor G2) LLINs. One net was distributed for every two people, followed by door-to-door visits to assist with hanging the nets and to promote their use. The primary outcome was the incidence of malaria cases among children aged 6 months to 9 years over the year following net distribution. Incidence rate ratios compared cases per child-year between clusters randomly assigned to use PBO-py versus py-only nets and CFP-py versus py-only nets. RESULTS: A total of 25,660 LLINs were distributed to 11,283 households (py-only, n=3797; PBO-py, n=3559; and CFP-py, n=3927). The primary outcome analyses included 549, 551, and 549 children in the py-only, PBO-py, and CFP-py groups, respectively. Mean malaria incidence over 12 months was 1.11 cases per child-year in the py-only group (control), 0.84 in the PBO-py group, and 0.65 in the CFP-py group. The incidence rate ratios were as follows: PBO-py versus py-only nets, 0.72 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.52 to 0.99; P=0.045); and CFP-py versus py-only nets, 0.57 (95% CI, 0.43 to 0.75; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Malaria incidence over 12 months was significantly reduced among children aged 6 months to 9 years residing in clusters of villages in Côte d'Ivoire that were randomly assigned to use CFP-py versus py-only LLINs and PBO-py versus py-only LLINs. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Certain nutrient supplements enhance immune responses to vaccination; however, no randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have assessed the impact of a whole food. Almonds may benefit immune function through immunoregulatory nutrients and fiber, which interacts with the immune system via the gut microbiota. OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the effect of almonds on the immune response following influenza vaccination, compared to an isocaloric snack, in healthy adults. METHODS: In this RCT, healthy adults (40-64 years) consumed almonds (56 g/d) or an isocaloric control (86 g/d pretzels) for 8 weeks. Participants received seasonal influenza vaccine at week 4. The primary outcome was seroconversion rates for ≥1 strain at week 8. Antigen-specific antibody titers (HI assay) were quantified pre- (week 4) and post-vaccination (week 8), and seroconversion and seroprotection were calculated. The gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), stool output and gut symptoms were measured at baseline, midpoint and endpoint. RESULTS: Ninety participants were randomized (mean age 51 years, 73% females). Seroconversion rate for ≥1 strain was high and not significantly different between groups [almond: 38/41 (93%) versus control: 37/39 (95%), P=1.000], nor were strain-specific seroconversion or seroprotection rates. Almonds resulted in higher antibody titers for A/Wisconsin/67/2022 (H1N1) strain, compared to control [geometric mean (95% CI): almond 359 (146, 881) versus control 110 (51, 235)], and greater fold-change for A/Wisconsin/67/2022 (H1N1) [geometric mean fold change (95% CI): almond 18 (7, 48) versus control 4 (3, 7)] and B/Yamagata [almond 10 (6, 16) versus control 5 (3, 7)]. Absolute abundance of Roseburia hominis was significantly higher in the almond group compared to control (q=0.049). There was no effect on SCFAs or stool consistency. CONCLUSIONS: Almonds increased influenza vaccine antibody titers but did not affect seroconversion in a healthy population where vaccines are already highly effective. This trial was pre-registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05515263 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05515263).

papers.abstract_en: Background: Dentoalveolar transverse constriction is frequently encountered during orthodontic treatment in adolescents. Although both fixed appliances and clear aligners can produce transverse dental arch changes, comparative evidence regarding their expansion patterns in growing patients remains limited. This study aimed to compare dentoalveolar transverse changes associated with two fixed treatment groups and two clear aligner systems in an adolescent population. Methods: This retrospective, non-randomized comparative study included 85 adolescents treated without extractions using conventional MBT fixed appliances (n = 22), Damon Q passive self-ligating appliances (n = 19), Invisalign (n = 21), or ClearCorrect (n = 23). Pretreatment (T0) and post-treatment (T1) digital dental models obtained using a 3Shape TRIOS intraoral scanner were evaluated for maxillary and mandibular transverse arch dimensions, projected palatal area, and maxillary first-molar crown inclination. Intergroup differences in treatment-related changes were compared among the four treatment groups. Results: Significant increases in maxillary transverse dimensions were observed after treatment in all four groups. The greatest mean increases at several maxillary levels were observed in the Damon Q group, including intercanine width (3.66 ± 1.34 mm) and first-molar width (3.69 ± 1.70 mm). In the ClearCorrect group, the mean increases were 3.12 ± 1.90 mm for intercanine width and 2.46 ± 1.42 mm for first-molar width. Projected palatal area increased in all groups, with the greatest mean increase observed with Damon Q (115.16 ± 29.70 mm2). Exploratory assessment of maxillary first-molar clinical crown inclination showed comparatively smaller changes in the ClearCorrect group than in the other treatment groups. Conclusions: All four treatment groups demonstrated increases in dentoalveolar transverse dimensions in this adolescent sample, although the magnitude and pattern of the observed changes differed among groups. Greater transverse increases at several maxillary levels were observed in the Damon Q group, whereas comparatively smaller changes in posterior crown inclination were observed in the ClearCorrect group. Because skeletal maturation was not directly assessed and an untreated control group was unavailable, these findings represent comparative changes observed during treatment and cannot distinguish appliance-related effects from physiological growth or other treatment-related factors.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis. METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete. FINDINGS: Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment. INTERPRETATION: Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis. FUNDING: aTyr and Kyorin.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Tramadol is commonly used to manage pain in patients with osteoarthritis, but its comparative safety in this population remains largely unknown. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using Optum Clinformatics® Data Mart (2005-2021). papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Obesity and early-onset cancer are both increasing among young adults, yet evidence remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To assess associations between obesity and early-onset cancer risk in young adults. DESIGN: Nationwide population-based cohort study. SETTING: Korean National Health Insurance Service database, 2009 to 2021. PATIENTS: 6 313 338 adults aged 20 to 39 years without prior cancer, from a national health screening program. RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 11.2 years, 151 893 cancer cases occurred. The relative association was more pronounced in men, and absolute risk differences were greater in women. In combined BMI-waist circumference analyses, people with class I obesity based on BMI and with abdominal obesity had higher 10-year cumulative incidence (2.45% [CI, 2.41% to 2.50%]) than those without abdominal obesity (2.13% [CI, 2.10% to 2.16%]), exceeding that of those with class II obesity without abdominal obesity (2.20% [CI, 2.03% to 2.36%]). The highest cumulative incidence was observed for thyroid, endometrial, and ovarian cancer. Obesity was not associated with higher risk for breast cancer diagnosed by age 50 years. LIMITATIONS: Observational design; nonrepresentative sample limited to screening participants; and unmeasured confounding, including smoking burden. CONCLUSION: Obesity in young Korean adults, measured by BMI and waist circumference, is associated with higher early-onset cancer risk persisting into midlife, with patterns varying by cancer type. Early weight management may be important for prevention. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: None.

The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up. RESULTS: Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline. INTERPRETATION: Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Higher ultra-processed food (UPF) consumption has been linked to chronic disease, but prospective evidence for incident myeloid neoplasms remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To examine ultra-processed food consumption, quantified as UPF energy percentage, in relation to incident myeloid neoplasms. METHODS: We analyzed 204,494 UK Biobank participants without prevalent hospital-recorded myeloid neoplasms. The primary outcome was ascertained from hospital inpatient records. Cause-specific Cox models adjusted for demographic, behavioral, socioeconomic, dietary, physical-activity, and anthropometric factors. Secondary analyses examined myeloid-neoplasm subtypes, alternative UPF metrics, baseline CHIP status, and circulating molecular signatures. RESULTS: During a median 10.5 years of follow-up, 848 participants developed an incident hospital-recorded myeloid neoplasm. Each 1-SD higher UPF energy percentage was associated with a higher hazard of myeloid neoplasms (HR, 1.12; 95% CI (1.05, 1.21); P = 0.001). MPN showed the clearest subtype association (HR, 1.15; 95% CI (1.04, 1.27); P = 0.006; FDR-adjusted P = 0.019). The association was also observed using UPF weight percentage. Among participants without detectable CHIP at baseline, the corresponding HR was 1.10 (95% CI (1.01, 1.20); P = 0.032), with no evidence of interaction by baseline CHIP status (P for interaction = 0.528). Exploratory molecular analyses identified lipid-related, inflammatory, hematologic, and immune/myeloid correlates, with several UPF-molecular associations showing cross-cohort consistency in external datasets. CONCLUSIONS: Higher UPF consumption was prospectively associated with a higher hazard of hospital-recorded incident myeloid neoplasms, with MPN showing the clearest major subtype association. The association was also observed among participants without detectable CHIP at baseline. Molecular and cross-cohort findings provide complementary biological context but do not establish a causal pathway.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: In Korea, the proportion of preterm and low-birth-weight infants has risen even as total births have fallen, changing the population at risk for eye disease of prematurity. Whether nationwide trends in retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) and strabismus reflect true temporal change or the shifting composition of this high-risk birth cohort is unclear. We examined 13-year trends in both conditions and assessed whether they persisted after adjustment for major risk factors. METHODS: We analyzed nationwide Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service claims from 2010 to 2022. Infants born at a gestational age below 37 weeks and/or with a birth weight below 2500 g were included. ROP and strabismus were identified from diagnostic codes, and gestational age and birth weight strata from perinatal diagnosis codes. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios for calendar-year trends and for joint gestational age and birth weight subgroups. RESULTS: Among 195,551 eligible infants, ROP was recorded in 55,457 (28.4%) and strabismus in 48,301 (24.7%). Claims-recorded cumulative incidence of both conditions declined from 2010 to 2022 even though the cohort became progressively more immature. After adjustment, the odds in 2022 relative to 2010 were 0.27 (95% confidence interval, 0.25-0.28) for ROP and 0.17 (0.16-0.18) for strabismus. Risk remained concentrated in the most immature infants: among those born below 28 weeks with a birth weight below 1000 g, the adjusted odds ratio was 21.54 (19.41-23.91) for ROP and 2.74 (2.52-2.97) for strabismus. The decline was not uniform. Among infants born below 28 weeks, ROP stayed between 73% and 84% throughout with no downward trend, whereas strabismus fell from 55.9% to 15.7%. CONCLUSIONS: Claims-recorded ROP and strabismus declined nationwide from 2010 to 2022 despite an increasingly vulnerable birth cohort, and these declines persisted after adjustment. Gestational age and birth weight remained the dominant determinants of risk, supporting continued risk-based screening. These findings do not establish trends in severe ROP, and the apparent decline in strabismus should be interpreted cautiously because later birth cohorts had shorter follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) generally follows a milder clinical course in children than in adults. The clinical characteristics of pediatric severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection have evolved throughout the pandemic and longitudinal data comparing successive pandemic years remain limited. OBJECTIVE: To compare the epidemiological, clinical, and laboratory characteristics of children hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2 infection during 2020-2022 and to identify factors associated with disease severity. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children aged 1 month to 18 years hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Bucharest, Romania, between January 2020 and December 2022. RESULTS: Of 669 eligible patients, 519 met the inclusion criteria (118 in 2020, 168 in 2021, and 233 in 2022). The proportion of hospitalized infants increased over time, whereas adolescent admissions declined (p < 0.001). Respiratory manifestations remained predominant, while gastrointestinal involvement was consistently common. Respiratory manifestations increased from 61.9% in 2020 to 77.3% in 2022 (p = 0.01), while gastrointestinal manifestations remained consistently frequent. Cardiovascular manifestations were reported in 28.9% of patients, without significant differences across the study years (p = 0.06). Neuromuscular manifestations declined from 43.2% in 2020 to 12.0% in 2022 (p < 0.001). Leukocyte count, lymphocyte count, and hemoglobin differed significantly across the study period, whereas C-reactive protein remained unchanged. Moderate-to-severe disease was associated with digestive, cardiovascular, and reno-urinary involvement but not with sex or residence. CONCLUSIONS: The epidemiological and clinical profile of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection changed substantially across the first three years of the pandemic. These findings highlight the importance of continued surveillance and comprehensive clinical assessment to optimize the management of pediatric COVID-19.

papers.abstract_en: Introduction: Methylphenidate (MPH) is a first-line treatment for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). MPH blocks dopamine and norepinephrine transporters, increasing synaptic catecholamine levels. Neurotransmitter release depends on presynaptic vesicle docking and fusion mediated by synaptosomal-associated protein 25 kDa (SNAP-25), a target-soluble NSF attachment protein receptor (SNARE) protein encoded by the SNAP-25 gene. This study aimed to investigate whether genetic variations in the SNAP-25 gene contribute to variability in clinical response to MPH in pediatric patients with ADHD. Methods: Forty-two children and adolescents aged 6-16 years who presented to the outpatient clinic and were diagnosed with ADHD according to DSM-5-TR criteria were prospectively treated with MPH for two months. Clinical response was assessed using the Conners' Parent Rating Scale (CPRS) and the Turgay DSM-based Disruptive Behavior Disorders Rating Scale (T-DSM-IV-S). SNAP-25 exons were sequenced using targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS). Results: Three common variants in SNAP-25 (rs363006, rs362585, and rs362998) were analyzed. Based on CPRS-defined outcomes, a significant association was observed between the rs362998:C > T polymorphism and response to MPH. In the genotypic model, the CT genotype was more frequent among responders (34.78%) than non-responders (5.26%) (p = 0.026, FDR-adjusted p = 0.049). In the dominant model, CT + TT genotypes were more frequent in responders (p = 0.026, FDR-adjusted p = 0.049). papers.abstract_en: Introduction: Chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis (CNO) is a rare autoinflammatory bone disorder. To standardize management, the Childhood Arthritis and Rheumatology Research Alliance (CARRA) developed three consensus treatment plans (CTPs) (1: methotrexate or sulfasalazine [conventional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs; DMARDs], 2: tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha inhibitors (TNFi), and 3: bisphosphonates). The Clinical Disease Activity Score (CNO CDAS) was introduced to assess disease activity without relying solely on imaging. Objective: The objectives were to evaluate clinicians' tendencies in applying CNO-CTPs and to assess treatment responses using CNO CDAS in real-world practice, including therapeutic strategies and outcomes at final follow-up. Methods: A retrospective cohort study of 171 pediatric patients with CNO from 18 centers was conducted. Disease activity was assessed using CDAS at diagnosis, at treatment modification, and at the last visit. This score incorporates clinically active lesions, patient pain, and global assessment. Treatments included NSAIDs, DMARDs, TNFi, and pamidronate. Results: Median age was 10 years at onset and 14 years at last follow-up, with a median follow-up of 36 months. The most frequent symptoms were bone pain (95.3%), activity limitation (67.8%), and fatigue (35.1%). All patients received NSAIDs; methotrexate (85.4%) and TNFi (54.4%) were commonly used. TNF inhibitors were the most used CTP, especially in patients with spinal involvement or higher MRI lesion counts, and they achieved the highest remission rate (40.4%). Of the 89 (52.0%) patients who changed treatment, 93.2% switched from DMARDs to TNFi. At the final follow-up, 62% were in medicated remission, 29.2% were in unmedicated remission, and 8.8% had active disease. CDAS scores significantly improved over time (p < 0.05). Conclusions: CARRA CTPs are effective in clinical practice, with anti-TNF therapy yielding the highest remission rates and marked improvement in CDAS.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accurate field triage is a cornerstone of an inclusive trauma system, but pediatric undertriage remains poorly characterized outside North America. We aimed to estimate the rate of major trauma undertriage in a Spanish pediatric trauma center, to identify patient factors associated with it, and to explore its relationship with early clinical outcomes. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study (2016-2025) of children aged 0-14 years admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) of the reference pediatric trauma center for the province of Granada, Spain. Major trauma was defined using a composite of the Cribari Matrix (ISS > 15) and/or the Need for Trauma Intervention (NFTI) criteria. Undertriage was defined as delayed (>2 h) or non-direct transport to the trauma center despite proximity (<30 min). The primary outcomes were the undertriage rate and the patient factors associated with it, examined by bivariate analysis and by Firth-penalized logistic regression with intercept correction (FLIC). Clinical outcomes (Glasgow Outcome Scale, PICU and total hospital length of stay) were prespecified as exploratory and analyzed with generalized linear models-binomial for binary outcomes and negative binomial for counts-and, as a sensitivity analysis, with targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE). RESULTS: Out of 1716 PICU admissions during the study period, 157 (9.1%) were due to injury, 131 (7.6%) were eligible traumatic injuries and 94 (5.5%) children met major trauma criteria (median age 8.0 years; 73.4% male; 78.7% blunt trauma; and median ISS 18.5). The undertriage rate was 23.4% (22/94; 95% CI 15.3-33.3). No patient characteristic differed significantly between undertriaged and correctly triaged children. Undertriaged children tended to be older (median 11.0 vs. 7.0 years; p = 0.117), and the overall association between age category and undertriage did not reach significance in the FLIC model (p = 0.069). One child (1.1%) died in PICU and 75 (79.8%) achieved a good functional recovery (Glasgow Outcome Scale 5). Undertriage was not associated with functional outcome, PICU length of stay or total hospital length of stay in either unadjusted or adjusted analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one in four children with major trauma who reached this pediatric trauma center met the predefined criteria for undertriage. This rate should be interpreted as undertriage conditional on arrival at the Pediatric Trauma Center and not as a system-level or provincial estimate. Multicenter prospective studies using standardized definitions and incorporating prehospital transport data are needed to better characterize the population-level burden and clinical impact of pediatric undertriage.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Early identification of brain dysfunction in preterm infants remains challenging because cranial ultrasonography (CUS) may not capture early neurophysiological abnormalities. Serum S100B has been proposed as a marker of neonatal brain injury, but its relationship with electroencephalographic (EEG) abnormalities in preterm infants remains unclear. Objectives: Our objectives were to evaluate the association between early neonatal serum S100B concentrations and EEG abnormality severity in preterm infants and to determine whether similar associations are observed with structural brain injury detected by CUS. Methods: This prospective observational cohort included 116 preterm infants from 281 prospectively enrolled neonates. Serum S100B was measured within the first 24 h of life. Conventional multichannel EEG was performed at 10-14 days of life, and CUS was performed serially to assess intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) and periventricular leukomalacia (PVL). Associations with EEG severity were evaluated using correlation analysis and ordinal logistic regression. A sensitivity analysis was restricted to infants with a postmenstrual age (PMA) ≤ 36 weeks at EEG and used a preterm-specific EEG grading system. Results: Higher log10(S100B) concentrations were associated with greater EEG abnormality severity (Spearman's ρ = 0.49, p < 0.001) and remained independently associated after adjustment for gestational age and Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) (adjusted OR 19.95, 95% CI 4.97-80.16; p < 0.001). No significant associations were observed between S100B concentrations and IVH or PVL severity. In the PMA-restricted sensitivity analysis (n = 89), the association between S100B and EEG abnormality severity remained significant using the preterm-specific grading system (ρ = 0.54, p < 0.001). Conclusions: During the early neonatal period, higher serum S100B concentrations were associated with greater neurophysiological abnormality severity in preterm infants, whereas associations with ultrasound-defined IVH or PVL were not demonstrated. The persistence of the S100B-EEG association in the PMA-specific sensitivity analysis supports the robustness of this finding across EEG grading approaches.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Substance use among adolescents is a growing global health problem, and psychoactive substances may damage the myocardium before conventional echocardiographic parameters change. We aimed to determine whether two-dimensional speckle-tracking strain echocardiography can unmask early myocardial impairment in adolescents with substance-use disorder. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional case-control study, 29 adolescents with substance-use disorder followed at a Child and Adolescent Substance Dependence Treatment Center and 29 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent conventional echocardiography and strain analysis (segmental, territorial, and global longitudinal strain [GLS]) performed by two blinded pediatric cardiologists. Between-group comparisons were adjusted for multiple testing; discriminative performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap internal validation, and multivariable logistic regression tested the independence of the association. Results: Patients had a median substance exposure of 3 years, and 75.9% reported polysubstance use (most commonly pregabalin, 41.4%, and methamphetamine, 34.5%). Current cigarette smoking was reported by 75.9% of patients and none of the controls. Ejection fraction was lower in patients but remained within the normal range (62.3% vs. 68.4%; p = 0.016). GLS was significantly impaired in the patient group (-17.0% vs. -20.4%; p < 0.001; median difference 3.4 percentage points; Hedges' g = 2.00), with diffuse segmental involvement across all three apical views. GLS discriminated patients from controls with an area under the curve of 0.913; at the Youden-optimal cut-off of -19.3%, sensitivity was 79.3% and specificity 96.6%. Conclusions: Strain echocardiography can unmask early myocardial impairment in adolescent substance and tobacco users, while ejection fraction and other conventional parameters, although differing modestly, remained within their normal reference ranges. Adding GLS to routine cardiac surveillance may improve early detection; however, reversibility with abstinence and prognostic value require prospective longitudinal studies.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Speech sound disorders (SSDs) are common in childhood and affect literacy and academic achievement. Standardized assessments such as the Urimal Test of Articulation and Phonology (UTAP) rely on time-intensive manual scoring. We evaluated the reliability and validity of Hi-DongDong, a Delphi-developed digital articulation assessment. Methods: This prospective multicenter study across five institutions recruited in total 931 children aged 2-13 years from outpatient clinics and community childcare facilities. Speech samples obtained with Hi-DongDong and UTAP-1 or UTAP-2 were independently evaluated by three experienced speech-language pathologists. Analyses were conducted on participants with valid paired datasets, using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), Pearson correlations, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Bland-Altman analyses. Results: Inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC ≥ 0.96). Inter-instrument reliability was good to excellent for total percentage of correct consonants (PCC) and total PCC-revised. All outcomes correlated significantly with UTAP (r = 0.347-0.939, p < 0.001). Utterance-level consonant accuracy indices showed minimal mean bias, whereas phonological mean length of utterance, vowel accuracy, and word accuracy showed systematic bias or wide limits of agreement, precluding interchangeable use. Conclusions: Hi-DongDong showed excellent inter-rater reliability and concurrent validity, particularly for consonant accuracy; however, its diagnostic accuracy remains unknown, and it cannot yet replace standardized diagnostic thresholds.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thoracoscopic repair of esophageal atresia with tracheoesophageal fistula (EA/TEF) remains technically challenging due to the rarity of these procedures and the demanding intracorporeal suturing within the confined neonatal thorax. The aim of this study is to report the learning curve and early outcomes during the transition from open to thoracoscopic EA/TEF repair at a single center, evaluated using the cumulative sum (CUSUM) method. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed data of 79 consecutive EA/TEF patients operated on between January 2015 and June 2026. Twenty-eight underwent thoracoscopic repair and 51 open repairs. The open cohort served as a historical institutional comparator, reflecting the standard of care prior to the adoption of thoracoscopic technique. The thoracoscopic group was stratified into three learning curve phases: Early (n = 9), Intermediate (n = 9), and Proficient (n = 10). Anastomotic leak was defined by contrast extravasation on postoperative esophagogram. Complications were graded using the Clavien-Dindo classification. RESULTS: The mean operative time was 2.9 ± 1.2 h (thoracoscopic) vs. 2.3 ± 1.2 h (open; p = 0.036). CUSUM analysis demonstrated a learning curve of approximately 15 cases, with operative time decreasing from 3.4 h (Phase 1) to 2.5 h (Phase 3; p = 0.034). Anastomotic leak occurred in 9/28 (32.1%) vs. 7/51 (13.7%; p = 0.137; underpowered comparison). Within the thoracoscopic group, long-gap patients (n = 8) had significantly higher stricture rates (37.5% vs. 0%; p = 0.017) and longer hospital stays (66 vs. 30 days; p = 0.005). The three long-gap patients with stricture required 11 total endoscopic dilation sessions. No statistically significant difference in mortality was observed (7.1% vs. 5.9%; p = 1.000). CONCLUSIONS: Thoracoscopic EA/TEF repair is feasible in an emerging MIS program with acceptable complication rates. The CUSUM-based learning curve was 15 cases. Long-gap thoracoscopic repair carries significantly higher stricture risk.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) risk evolves as clinical information accumulates after birth. This study evaluated the incremental predictive value of routinely available data from birth through the first week of life using cumulative, time-aligned feature sets. Methods: The primary analysis of this retrospective cohort study included 2153 preterm infants who survived to 36 weeks' postmenstrual age and had ascertainable BPD status and complete predictor data. The outcome was clinically documented BPD at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age, based on the treating neonatologists' assessment of continued supplemental oxygen and/or respiratory-support requirements. Three cumulative feature sets were constructed using variables available at or immediately after birth (Step 1), additional clinical and laboratory variables available within the first 24 h (Step 2), and further clinical-course variables available through postnatal day 7 (Step 3). Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost models were developed using a stratified 70:30 training-test split and five-fold stratified cross-validation. Internal validation assessed discrimination, calibration, and Brier scores in the held-out test set. AUROC confidence intervals and paired differences between prediction windows were estimated using 2000 bootstrap resamples. Predictor contributions were examined using SHapley Additive exPlanations. A multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis evaluated logistic regression and random forest in all 2616 infants with ascertainable BPD status. Results: Of the 2153 infants, 1154 (53.6%) had clinically documented BPD. Logistic regression achieved the highest held-out test-set AUROC at each prediction window: 0.751 (95% CI, 0.714-0.788) in Step 1, 0.897 (0.873-0.919) in Step 2, and 0.923 (0.902-0.942) in Step 3. Paired AUROC increases were 0.146 (95% CI, 0.110-0.181) from Step 1 to Step 2 and 0.026 (0.015-0.036) from Step 2 to Step 3. Logistic regression Brier scores decreased from 0.202 to 0.130 and 0.112, respectively. In the Step 3 logistic regression model, the leading predictors by mean absolute SHAP value were mean SpO2 during the first 24 h, mean arterial pressure, initial feeding approach, FiO2 at 24 h, and C-reactive protein. In the expanded sensitivity-analysis test cohort, logistic-regression AUROCs were 0.747, 0.893, and 0.913 for Steps 1-3, respectively. Conclusions: The addition of first-24 h clinical information substantially improved BPD prediction beyond birth variables, with further improvement from data accumulated through postnatal day 7. The primary analysis did not demonstrate an added predictive benefit of the evaluated tree-based algorithms over logistic regression. The primary findings apply to a selected cohort of survivors with complete data and should not be generalized to all initially eligible infants or interpreted as prediction of BPD or death. Temporal and external validation and prospective evaluation of clinical utility are required before implementation.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: This study examined annual probabilistic network structures among dietary habits, health-related attitudes, lifestyle behaviors, and body mass index (BMI) during implementation of the PETICA school-based program. Methods: This was a three-year prospective, uncontrolled school-based intervention with repeated measurements of the same cohort in Grades 2-4. The BMI analytic samples comprised 915 pupils in Grade 2 (461 boys, 454 girls; mean age 7.9 ± 0.4), 840 in Grade 3 (429 boys, 411 girls; mean age 8.9 ± 0.5), and 684 in Grade 4 (341 boys, 343 girls; mean age 9.9 ± 0.4). BMI was recalculated from measured body mass and height and used as the continuous network outcome. BMI-for-age percentiles were retained for age- and sex-specific descriptive classification and sensitivity analysis. Separate score-based Bayesian networks were estimated for each grade. Network stability was assessed using 200 nonparametric bootstrap samples, with stable adjacency defined as a bootstrap frequency of at least 50%. Results: Fruit and vegetable intake formed a stable adjacency in all three grades, with bootstrap frequencies of 100.0% in Grade 2, 98.0% in Grade 3, and 99.0% in Grade 4. The sex of the pupil and computer/video-game use were stably connected in Grades 3 and 4 (100.0% in both grades). Stable connections among health-related attitudes were more prominent in later grades. In Grade 4, at-home breakfast consumption was connected with water intake (57.5%) and vegetable intake (52.0%). No behavioral adjacency with continuous BMI reached the prespecified 50% stability threshold in any grade. The largest subthreshold behavior-BMI signal was observed for at-home breakfast consumption in Grade 4 (39.0%). Conclusions: Selected relationships among reported health-related behaviors were reproducible across annual assessments, whereas direct behavior-BMI connections were year-specific and did not reach the stability threshold. The greater integration of attitudes and healthy habits in later grades is compatible with cumulative, age-adapted health education, but the absence of an untreated comparison group prevents attribution of these patterns to PETICA. The findings do not establish causal effects or program effectiveness, but may contribute to hypotheses generation for future evaluations of multi-component school-based obesityprevention programs.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Advances in neonatal care have substantially improved the survival of preterm infants; however, longitudinal changes in caregiver psychological well-being and infant temperament during follow-up remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize changes in caregiver psychological measures and infant temperament from enrollment through 12 months corrected age (CA) and to explore their clinical and socioeconomic correlates. Methods: This prospective longitudinal cohort study included 35 preterm infant-parent dyads assessed at enrollment (mean CA, 2.3 ± 1.3 months), 6 months CA, and 12 months CA. The same parent completed measures of depressive symptoms (Korean Beck Depression Inventory-II [K-BDI-II]), parenting stress (Korean Parenting Stress Index, Fourth Edition [K-PSI-4]), general self-efficacy, and infant temperament (Infant Behavior Questionnaire-Revised [IBQ-R]) across available assessments. Developmental outcomes were assessed using the Bayley Scales of Infant Development, Second Edition (BSID-II) at 12 months CA. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate (FDR) correction across the eight domain-level questionnaire outcomes comprising the main longitudinal analysis family; additional analyses were exploratory. Results: K-BDI-II depressive symptom scores (FDR q = 0.022) and K-PSI-4 Parent-domain stress (q = 0.011) decreased over time, whereas Total Stress, Child-domain stress, and general self-efficacy did not change significantly. Infant Surgency/Extraversion (q < 0.008) and Negative Affectivity (q = 0.008) increased, whereas Orienting/Regulation did not change significantly. No associations between clinical or socioeconomic characteristics and study outcomes remained significant after FDR correction. At 12 months CA, K-PSI-4 Total Stress was positively correlated with parent-reported infant Negative Affectivity (r = 0.47, q = 0.039). Conclusions: Caregiver psychological measures and infant temperament showed distinct longitudinal changes from enrollment through 12 months CA following preterm birth. Repeated assessment of caregiver psychological well-being may complement developmental follow-up of preterm infants. These within-cohort findings, particularly the exploratory associations, require confirmation in larger and more diverse longitudinal cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Composite biomarkers combining inflammatory or metabolic markers with a negative acute-phase protein predict outcomes in critically ill patients, but fibrinogen-based ratios grounded in the "lethal triad" of trauma-induced coagulopathy remain unexplored in pediatric trauma. We evaluated novel lactate/fibrinogen (LFR) and procalcitonin/fibrinogen (PFR) ratios alongside the procalcitonin/albumin ratio (PAR), a composite triple inflammation-perfusion index (TIPI, combining procalcitonin, CRP, and lactate relative to albumin), and established albumin-based ratios and severity scores for mortality prediction. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 200 pediatric trauma patients admitted to the PICU of İzmir City Hospital (27 October 2023-27 October 2025) were analyzed. All ratios were calculated serially over the first 72 h and at PICU discharge. Discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis. Independent predictors were identified using Firth penalized logistic regression, with bootstrap validation (B = 1000). RESULTS: Thirteen patients (6.5%) died. LFR achieved the highest point-estimate discrimination (AUC 0.848), numerically exceeding LAR (0.829), though not significantly (p = 0.399). PAR, TIPI, and PFR were also independently associated with mortality (all p < 0.05), whereas CAR and NLR were not. LFR correlated strongly with LAR (ρ = 0.873), indicating overlapping information despite differing denominators. Serial trajectories provided only limited, largely inconclusive incremental value. A sensitivity analysis including early deaths and rapid discharges (n = 274) confirmed LFR/LAR's robust discrimination. but not that of PAR, TIPI, or PFR. CONCLUSIONS: Lactate-based ratios showed the strongest single-timepoint discrimination, with the novel LFR performing comparably to LAR via a distinct coagulopathy-based mechanism. Lactate- and fibrinogen-based ratios were robust to inclusion of early deaths, whereas inflammation-based ratios were not, indicating that biomarker validity may depend on injury-to-death timing in pediatric trauma.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Human bocavirus (HBoV) is frequently detected by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) in respiratory samples from children with acute respiratory tract disease, but prolonged viral DNA persistence and frequent co-detection complicate interpretation of its clinical significance. We evaluated whether early hemogram-derived inflammatory indices are associated with clinical outcomes in hospitalized children with PCR-detected HBoV. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 170 hospitalized children aged 1 month to 18 years with HBoV detected by PCR in nasopharyngeal samples between July 2022 and June 2025. Data obtained within the first 24 h of hospitalization were analyzed. Systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) were calculated. Associations with clinical outcomes were assessed using correlation analyses, and multivariable generalized linear modeling was used to evaluate factors associated with length of hospital stay. RESULTS: Median age was 18 months (IQR, 11-33), and microbiological co-detection was present in 60.4%. Oxygen therapy was required in 82.8%, high-flow nasal cannula support in 22.0%, and PICU admission in 5.4%. All four indices were inversely correlated with length of hospital stay and blood gas bicarbonate levels. However, none independently predicted length of stay after adjustment. Neurological disease, neutrophil percentage, and tachycardia remained independently associated with length of stay; neurological disease was associated with a 1.56-fold longer expected hospitalization, whereas higher neutrophil percentage and tachycardia were associated with shorter expected hospitalization. CONCLUSIONS: Early hemogram-derived inflammatory indices were associated with clinical course but did not independently predict hospitalization duration in children with PCR-detected HBoV. Their prognostic value should be interpreted cautiously, particularly when length of stay is used as a process-sensitive outcome, and the observed associations should not be considered HBoV-specific.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: National cancer control plans (NCCPs) vary in scope and comprehensiveness, yet expert-led review is resource intensive and limits cross-country comparability. We aimed to assess NCCP comprehensiveness across 50 countries using the policy reasoning integrated sequential model (PRISM), a validated multiagent artificial intelligence (AI) system. METHODS: We identified the most recent national NCCP for each country from the International Cancer Control Partnership repository, the WHO Noncommunicable Disease Document Repository, and government websites; sub-national plans, broader non-communicable disease or health-sector strategies, drafts, and superseded versions were excluded. We developed an analytical framework of 12 elements and 76 sub-elements, aligned with WHO, International Cancer Control Partnership, and Union for International Cancer Control guidance and validated it through a modified two-stage Delphi process (online survey of 67 experts; triangulation workshop with 31 participants). PRISM comprised document ingestion (Qwen2.5-VL-72B), policy analysis with retrieval-augmented generation (Llama 4 Scout, 109B), and semantic quality assurance. PRISM was validated against masked dual-expert ratings for six purposely selected NCCPs, then applied to all NCCPs. Scores were normalised to 0-5 and medians compared across World Bank income group and WHO region. FINDINGS: We identified 50 NCCPs that met the inclusion criteria. Median overall comprehensiveness was 2·78 (IQR 2·25-3·09), with high comprehensiveness classified as 4·0-5·0, moderate as 2·0-3·9, and low as 0-1·9. Europe (2·96; 2·78-3·35) and lower-middle-income countries (2·97; 2·48-3·15) had the highest medians; the western Pacific (2·21; 1·78-2·87) and low-income countries (2·05; 1·94-2·22) had the lowest. Element-level medians were highest for implementation (4·17; 3·54-4·38), health services (3·89; 2·63-4·19), and governance and organisation (3·67; 3·35-3·98), and lowest for financing (1·88; 1·00-2·69), outcomes (1·83; 1·33-2·33), and threats (2·19; 1·72-2·34). Financing showed the largest gaps-only five of eleven financing sub-elements had median scores of 1·0 or less. INTERPRETATION: Our analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data. FUNDING: Harvard University.

papers.abstract_en: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit. Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro-myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage.

papers.abstract_en: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal-fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1R+ erythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4+CSF1R- Erythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4+ nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal-fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals.

papers.abstract_en: Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping, colocalization and transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to contextualize genome-wide association study loci, yet the impact of upstream RNA-sequencing processing choices on these analyses remains critically unexplored. Two poorly characterized decisions include the transcriptomic reference annotation used for quantification of short-read RNA-sequencing samples, which defines transcript composition and structure, and the quantification method itself. Here, through a comprehensive analysis spanning 48 tissues in GTEx and 7 widely studied and diverse phenotypes, we find that these choices substantially affect eQTL detection and gene expression prediction with significant downstream impacts on colocalization and TWAS results. Concordant results across pipelines are further enriched for longer genes, genes with more isoforms, and greater expression heritability. Our findings demonstrate that seemingly minor methodological decisions substantially affect these common analyses, highlighting the need for standardized practices to ensure reproducible genetic association studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accurate detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) are essential for effective treatment yet frequently require specialist expertise and advanced equipment. To address this requirement, we aimed to develop a deep learning-based diagnostic model for the automatic detection and staging of ONFH using x-ray images, and compared its performance with clinicians to allow them to improve their diagnostic performance. METHODS: In this retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study, we developed our deep learning model, Osteonecrosis Artificial Intelligence Diagnostician (OsteoAID), which was based on the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) detection network and trained on a multicentre x-ray dataset. The dataset, dated from Jan 1, 2015, to Dec 31, 2023, and obtained from 16 399 patients across six Chinese tertiary hospitals, included 20 722 anteroposterior hip x-ray images of 28 785 hips, including hips with ONFH, healthy hips, and hips with other conditions radiographically similar to ONFH. To establish a rigorous ground truth for model training and evaluation, expert orthopaedists annotated each image to differentiate ONFH from confounding diseases and additionally classified the confirmed ONFH lesions on the basis of the Ficat and Arlet staging system. To verify the diagnostic performance of OsteoAID, we compared the model's accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and area under the curve (AUC) with those of the original YOLOv8 model on the internal testing set for both the staging and detection tasks. Furthermore, the performance of OsteoAID was compared with the performance of radiologists and orthopaedists on two external testing sets, and its diagnostic performance was also benchmarked against MRI-the gold standard for ONFH diagnosis-with a third external testing set in which x-ray images were staged by corresponding MRI scans. Diagnostic metrics were compared with those of clinicians using t tests and McNemar's tests, with significance set at p<0·05. FINDINGS: On the internal testing set, OsteoAID improved the staging accuracy from 87·42% (95% CI 85·88-89·20) to 96·44% (94·73-97·17) and the AUC from 88·54% (86·74-90·37) to 96·94% (95·75-97·98) compared with the original YOLOv8 model. For detection the model had a mean average precision of 92·97% (91·73-94·43) at an intersection-over-union threshold of 50%. In comparisons with clinicians on the external testing set I, the model showed staging accuracy of 96·60% (94·27-97·81), which was significantly higher than radiologists (74·96% [73·38-76·85]; p<0·0001) and junior orthopaedists (83·98% [81·27-84·06]; p<0·0001) and similar to that of expert orthopaedists (96·54% [94·18-97·79]; p=0·20). Furthermore, model-assisted diagnostics improved the accuracy of junior orthopaedists by an absolute difference of 12·70% and of radiologists by 21·47%. Although the accuracy improvement for expert orthopaedists was non-significant (an absolute difference of 0·74%; p=0·080), the diagnostic time was substantially reduced across all groups. On external testing set II (which included challenging cases: low-quality x-ray images affected by improper exposure, poor contrast, incomplete field of view, or foreign-object shadows, as well as smartphone photographs of x-ray films), the model showed robust performance even under extreme conditions, achieving an overall staging accuracy of 93·76% (93·09-95·82). Additionally, combining x-ray imaging with the deep learning model produced diagnostic results similar to MRI on external testing set III with an overall accuracy of 96·63% (95·68-97·86) and an AUC of 97·33% (96·65-98·75). INTERPRETATION: The developed deep learning model shows expert-level diagnostic performance in the dual tasks of detecting and staging ONFH by use of anteroposterior x-rays, which can substantially enhance both the diagnostic proficiency and efficiency of clinicians. Consequently, the model could serve as a highly accessible decision-support tool to optimise clinical triage and guide appropriate treatment strategies. FUNDING: National Natural Science Foundation of China, National High Level Hospital Clinical Research Funding, and Beijing Natural Science Foundation.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Tumour necrosis factor (TNF) and interleukin (IL)-17 are central drivers of axial spondyloarthritis (AxSpA). We previously identified activated CD4+ tissue-resident memory Th17 cells as the principal source of IL-17A/F in AxSpA synovium. We sought to define the cellular source of TNF and mechanisms driving the CCL20+ myeloid phenotype in joint and blood. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of synovial tissue from 5 patients with AxSpA was combined with immunofluorescence, synovial-fluid scRNA-seq, and flow cytometry, as well as comparisons with rheumatoid arthritis datasets. Monocyte-derived macrophages from healthy controls (HCs) and patients with AxSpA were cocultured with activated autologous CD4+ T cells, with blocking and cytokine experiments defining mechanisms of CCL20+ induction. Circulating monocytes were assessed by scRNA-seq and functional assays. RESULTS: CCL20+ macrophages were the predominant source of TNF in AxSpA synovium, with TNF protein confirmed in tissue and synovial fluid. Activated CD4+ T cells induced the CCL20+ phenotype through CD40L-CD40 signalling and an IL-1β/TNF-α autocrine circuit in HC-derived and AxSpA-derived cells. Baseline AxSpA monocytes showed a higher CCL20+ signature than HC monocytes, but this difference largely disappeared after T-cell-mediated induction. Under stimulation, AxSpA monocytes also produced more TNF, IL-6, IL-1β, and IL-23 than HC monocytes, a difference attenuated following IL-1/TNF priming. CONCLUSIONS: CCL20+ macrophages are a major CD40L- and IL-1β/TNF-α-driven source of TNF in AxSpA synovium. AxSpA circulating monocytes exhibit heightened basal CCL20+ signatures and inflammatory responsiveness that converge towards HC responses after inflammatory priming, supporting circulating CCL20+ monocytes as a marker of IL-1β/TNF-α-driven myeloid inflammation.

papers.abstract_en: Barrett's esophagus (BE) patients require improved cancer risk stratification to identify high-risk individuals while reducing over-treatment in low-risk populations. BE evolution towards adenocarcinoma is likely driven by a combination of genomic and microenvironmental factors, suggesting the potential of predictive models that integrate both. Here, we developed BEACON (Barrett's Esophagus DNA content Abnormality and immune ecology for Cancer Outcome), a spatially aware framework integrating deep learning-based prediction of DNA content and immune architecture from routine histopathology. First, DACOR, a multi-instance learning model that predicts DNA content from histopathology, was trained using 777 BE biopsies with flow cytometry-based DNA content data scanned at two institutions, and it demonstrated strong performance across both validation and test datasets for DNA content abnormality prediction. Patients classified as DNA content abnormal by DACOR demonstrated increased cancer progression. Complementary models for cell classification and tissue segmentation enabled spatial immune ecology metric computations. Abnormal regions exhibited increased lymphoplasmacytic inflammation versus normal regions. Among patients with DNA content abnormality, cancer progressors exhibited increased plasma cell clustering adjacent to abnormal epithelium compared to non-progressors. Finally, a logistic regression model was developed that integrated molecular, immune ecological, and epithelial morphology features for cancer risk stratification. The integrated risk classification model stratified DNA content abnormal patients into high- and low-risk groups that corresponded with progression and patient survival. Overall, BEACON spatially integrates molecular abnormality with immune ecology to stratify BE patients by cancer progression risk using routine pathology images.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis disease clusters within households, but the proportion of disease among household contacts that results from recent within-household transmission remains unclear. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex strain discordance among pairs of individuals with tuberculosis and a history of household contact, and the proportion of all tuberculosis disease attributable to recent household transmission. METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we included empirical studies or systematic reviews published in English from Jan 1, 1985, to Jan 26, 2024, that described at least ten pairs of individuals with a history of household contact, in which both people had active tuberculosis and their isolates were strain-typed using RFLP, mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable-number tandem repeat, or whole-genome sequencing. We excluded studies that only collected data on residence for isolates of the same strain and studies that used preselection for both index and secondary cases. Searches of MEDLINE, Embase, Global Health, Web of Science, and POPLINE databases were updated on Jan 26, 2024. Titles and abstracts and then full texts were screened, and data were extracted independently, by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Summary data were extracted from published reports; when necessary, we contacted study authors, some of whom reanalysed data. The main outcome was the prevalence of strain discordance among pairs of individuals with tuberculosis and a history of household contact. Our main analyses excluded studies using 12-loci or 15-loci mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable-number tandem repeat and studies performed during tuberculosis outbreaks, as these were considered to be at high risk of bias. We used an inverse variance heterogeneity model applying a double-arcsine transformation to stabilise variance. The proportion of total variability due to between-study heterogeneity was estimated using I2. We estimated the proportion of all tuberculosis attributable to recent household transmission as the product of strain concordance and the proportion of all cases in the community with a history of household exposure to a putative index case, which we derived from external data. Sensitivity analyses assessed robustness to the choice of model and to varying assumptions about household size when estimating the attributable fraction. Our PROSPERO registration number was CRD42024504096. FINDINGS: The updated searches identified an additional 3735 unique records. Thirty studies from 18 countries met the inclusion criteria. Four studies were omitted from the meta-analysis because they were at high risk of bias. The remaining 26 studies comprised 1544 index-secondary patient pairs. A high proportion of total variability was due to between-study heterogeneity (I2 90·3, 95% CI 69·0-95·3%). The overall pooled estimate of the prevalence of strain discordance was 0·47 (95% CI 0·32-0·62). Pooled estimates differed by tuberculosis incidence: 0·30 (0·25-0·34) in low-incidence settings, 0·25 (0·15-0·36) in moderate-incidence settings, and 0·59 (0·41-0·76) in high-incidence settings (p=0·003). The median proportion of tuberculosis disease attributable to recent household transmission was 10·8% (range 1·4-21·1%). INTERPRETATION: Strain discordance is common, particularly in high-incidence settings. These findings suggest that recent household transmission makes a small contribution to the overall burden of tuberculosis disease. In this study, the number of household pairs and geographical diversity of the studies were strengths. Between-study heterogeneity limited precision. Our estimates of attributable fraction relied on external data. Strain discordance does not necessarily imply discordance in drug susceptibility. These results should motivate a greater focus on social protection and interrupting community transmission. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: Laser-induced electron coherence is a fascinating behavior in quantum materials. However, to date, viable approaches to control this excited-state behavior remain lacking. Here, we overturn this by realizing magnetic-field-controlled spatial self-phase modulation (SSPM), a third-order non-linear optical response. Light-matter interactions in ferromagnetic VSe2 and diamagnetic graphene are observed to be precisely controlled by an external magnetic field, achieving an intriguing anisotropic SSPM, accompanied by prominent optical birefringence. We attribute this magnetic-field-controlled SSPM to the magnetic-field-induced broken symmetry in the collective behavior of flakes. Significantly, the non-linear optical coefficient χ (3) is enhanced by 58%, which breaks the record of largest χ (3). Furthermore, we demonstrate a magnetic-field-controlled all-optical switch based on SSPM in VSe2, achieving an enhancement of 340% in the signal-to-control intensity ratio (manifesting the weak-light-control-strong-light capability). Our findings usher in a new paradigm, controlling (rather than merely monitoring) the laser-induced electron coherence in SSPM, which enables the next generation of all-optical switching based on SSPM.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) medical scribes may reduce documentation burden and clinician burnout. Whether use intensity drives benefits remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between AI scribe (Heidi) enrollment and documentation burden and whether changes differ by use intensity. DESIGN: Retrospective quality improvement study using an interrupted time series (ITS) indexed on each clinician's enrollment month adjusted for patient demographics and visit complexity. A secondary 3-group ITS compared enrolled nonusers, low users, and high users. SETTING: 14-hospital health system in Boston, Massachusetts. PARTICIPANTS: 902 outpatient clinicians enrolled in Heidi; 605 users and 297 enrolled nonusers. INTERVENTION: Heidi enrollment after system-wide implementation beginning January 2025. MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was note-active time. Secondary outcomes included same-day and after-hours note closures, note length, and work relative value units (wRVUs). RESULTS: 1 637 227 encounters had notes authored by enrolled clinicians between 1 July 2024 and 31 January 2026. Enrollment was associated with an immediate reduction in note-active time (-1.21 minutes [95% CI, -1.74 to -0.68 minutes]), with larger reductions among high users (-2.50 minutes [CI, -3.55 to -1.45 minutes]) than nonusers (difference, -2.20 minutes [CI, -3.46 to -0.95 minutes]) and low users (difference, -1.72 minutes [CI, -3.03 to -0.40 minutes]). High users had greater increases in note length than nonusers (difference, +170.90 characters [CI, 21.07 to 320.70 characters]) and low users (difference, +270.70 characters [CI, 131.04 to 410.36 characters]). papers.abstract_en: Glutathione peroxidases (GPX) are primarily selenoproteins that maintain cellular redox balance. GPX1, GPX2 and GPX4 are associated with cancer progression and treatment resistance, but the lack of isoenzyme-specific cellular assays has limited evaluation of GPX-targeting compounds. As GPX1 and GPX2 share high sequence homology, as well as substrate and inhibitor profiles, their individual activities are difficult to distinguish. Here, we present a glutathione reductase (GR)-coupled assay using auranofin to quantify combined GPX1/GPX2 activity and total GPX activity in crude cell lysates. The method was validated using multiple cell lines, with or without selenium supplementation, spiked human recombinant enzymes, and knockdown cells. Combined GPX1/GPX2 activity correlated with GPX1 protein levels and accounted for the majority of GPX activity in selenium-supplemented cells. GPX4's low catalytic turnover limits the feasibility of measuring its activity in cell lysates, so we established a high-throughput cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) using HiBiT-tagging of GPX1 and GPX4 in HT1080 cells to quantify isoenzyme-specific target engagement. Using this new complementary assay platform, we found that ferroptosis inducers RSL3, PACMA-31 and ML-162 destabilized GPX4 in cells, RSL3 and ML-162 destabilized cellular GPX1, but none of these compounds had a strong effect on either total GPX, or GPX1/GPX2 activities in lysates. Additional reported GPX1/GPX2 or GPX4 inhibitors showed minimal GPX4 target engagement, whereas GPX1 was readily targeted in cells. The FDA-approved drugs, ceftibuten and omapatrilat, inhibited GPX1/GPX2 activity more potently than auranofin in cell lysates, suggesting that GPX1/GPX2 suppression may contribute to their cellular effects. Together, these complementary GPX assays presented here provide practical tools for evaluations of specific GPX isoenzyme cellular activities and development of selective GPX-targeted therapies.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a severe vascular disorder, is closely associated with chronic inflammatory states and oxidative stress. Myeloid differentiation protein 2 (MD2), a key co-receptor of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), is well established in mediating various inflammation-driven pathologies. However, its role in pulmonary hypertension and its potential involvement in oxidative stress regulation remain unclear. METHODS AND RESULTS: MD2 expression was upregulated in both PH patients and murine PH models. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of MD2 improved hemodynamic parameters, attenuated pulmonary vascular remodeling, and reduced right ventricular hypertrophy. MD2 inhibition significantly reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that suppression of the membrane protein MD2 activated intracellular AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, leading to enhanced peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) activity. PPARγ, in turn, suppressed nuclear transcription of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), resulting in a marked reduction in mitochondrial oxidative stress. CONCLUSION: This study indicates that MD2 may act as an upstream regulator of mitochondrial oxidative stress in PH. Inhibition of MD2 attenuates pulmonary hypertension through activation of the AMPK/PPARγ axis, which suppresses NOX4 mediated mitochondrial oxidative stress. Targeting MD2 may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for PH.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Multimorbidity is intricately associated with global ageing and presents a key challenge for health systems and individuals. Despite growing recognition of this challenge, the gap in robust, comparable, population-level evidence on multimorbidity in Africa remains substantial. We aimed to describe multimorbidity among older people across five African sites in three countries representing different epidemiological and health-care contexts. METHODS: In this population-based cross-sectional study, we recruited adults aged at least 40 years in rural and urban The Gambia, rural and urban South Africa, and urban Zimbabwe (Feb 10, 2022 to Sept 2, 2024). Participants were stratified by site, age-band (40-54 years, 55-69 years, and ≥70 years), and sex. We included 5296 adults (median age 60 years, 53% were women) and recorded their self-reported medical conditions and current medications. We further assessed their height, weight, blood pressure, blood glucose, mental health symptoms, HIV status, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). We defined multimorbidity as having two or more of 26 chronic conditions. Multimorbidity prevalence was calculated weighted to each country's national population. We evaluated the risk factors for multimorbidity and associations of multimorbidity with HRQoL; multimorbidity clusters were described using latent class analysis. FINDINGS: 1926 (36%) of 5296 adults had multimorbidity. The weighted prevalence of multimorbidity was 36% (95% CI 35-37), ranging from 6·6% (5·1-8·1) in rural The Gambia to 62·0% (58·7-65·3) in urban South Africa. Across the three countries, education level, wealth, smoking, alcohol consumption, and BMI were the lowest in The Gambia and the greatest in South Africa, with a rural-urban gradient. Diabetes, hypertension, HIV, mood disorders, arthritis, and fragility fractures were the most common multimorbidity components. People with multimorbidity had lower HRQoL than those without multimorbidity. In Zimbabwe and South Africa, cardiometabolic (42-57% of the population) and HIV-related (25-48% of the population) multimorbidity clusters emerged, characterised by component diseases, risk factors, and associations with HRQoL. INTERPRETATION: Multimorbidity was found to be common among older people in five study settings in three African countries, with notable trends across sites. The high prevalence of multimorbidity in urban South Africa might foreshadow future trends across the African region as the continent's demographic and health transition advances, underscoring the urgent need for coordinated multisectoral strategies to address multimorbidity. FUNDING: Wellcome, National Institute for Health Research, and Medical Research Council.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Uncontrolled pneumonia induced by influenza virus infection results in severe lung pathology. Timely and proper tissue self-repair is critical to improve survival. This study aimed to identify probiotic strains that confer protection against acute lung injury induced by influenza virus infection and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Significant structural alterations in the gut microbiota were observed in influenza patients, characterized by a marked depletion in Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, whose abundance was negatively correlated with disease severity. In a murine model of influenza infection, oral administration of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and its culture supernatant markedly alleviated lung injury. Targeted metabolomic analysis identified butyrate as the principal metabolite produced by Faecalibacterium prausnitzii that mediates lung tissue protection. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that butyrate promotes the differentiation of pulmonary CD4⁺T cells into a reparative phenotype with enhanced interleukin-22 (IL-22) production. Mechanistically, butyrate facilitates IL-22 secretion through monounsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis via a histone-acetylation-dependent NR4A1-SCD1 axis. Accumulated monounsaturated fatty acids further enhance mitochondrial activities, which are essential for robust IL-22 production. Utilizing an IL-22 knockout mouse model, we confirmed the indispensable protective role of IL-22 in this gut-lung axis during influenza infection. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that butyrate, derived from intestinal commensal Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, plays a crucial role in maintaining pulmonary tissue homeostasis during influenza infection by modulating intrinsic lipid metabolism in CD4+T cells. This study underscores the promising translational potential of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii supplementation as an innovative therapeutic strategy for severe influenza-associated lung injury. papers.abstract_en: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped. We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links ppe1 mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the Mtb Δppe1 mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δppe1 strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing Mtb physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined. OBJECTIVES: To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH. METHODS: Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models. papers.abstract_en: Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy, or SUDEP, is the leading cause of death in persons with epilepsy. Although extensively studied, the events that result in SUDEP remain poorly understood, with no reliable biomarkers to predict SUDEP risk in an individual. This review synthesizes the literature across many domains, discussing clinical and preclinical studies in brain, cardio-respiratory centers in the brainstem, and intrinsic alterations in cardiac excitability leading to arrhythmia, to provide a comprehensive picture of our current understanding of SUDEP mechanisms. What we do know is that SUDEP involves complex, multi-system dysfunction in persons with epilepsy at baseline, during seizures, and in post-ictal periods. This situation is further complicated by cases of SUDEP Plus, in which pre-existing conditions in addition to epilepsy, e.g. Brugada syndrome or Long-QT syndrome, may contribute to death during a seizure. Finally, it is likely that multiple etiologies lead to SUDEP outcomes. Here, we highlight gaps in the field requiring additional research.
