papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Concerns about adolescent smartphone use and mental health have prompted many schools to implement mobile phone bans, but evidence of their effects remains mixed. OBJECTIVE: To examine whether schoolwide mobile phone bans were associated with changes in mental health and associated social and behavioral outcomes among adolescents in Iceland. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This repeated cross-sectional study used difference-in-differences analyses of data from 70 schools across 3 waves of the nationwide Youth in Iceland school survey. The surveys were administered to adolescents aged 13 to 15 years in February 2016, February 2018, and November 2023. Analyses were conducted from February 1, 2025, to January 30, 2026. EXPOSURE: Schoolwide mobile phone bans prohibiting student phone use during school hours. Between 2018 and 2023, 22 of 70 schools implemented a phone ban. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were depressive symptoms, anxiety, hostility, and mental well-being. Secondary outcomes were perceived peer support, screen use (social media use, gaming alone, gaming with friends, and video watching), and bullying (in person and cyberbullying). RESULTS: Among 23 938 adolescent observations across the 3 study years, 11 964 (50.0%) were boys; the mean (SD) age was 13.98 (0.82) years. In the postpolicy period from 2018 to 2023, schoolwide mobile phone bans were not associated with meaningful changes in depressive symptoms (β, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.01-1.30]), anxiety (β, 0.21 [95% CI, -0.08 to 0.50]), hostility (β, 0.23 [95% CI, -0.12 to 0.59]), and mental well-being (β, -0.52 [95% CI, -1.08 to 0.03]). Results were similar in gender-stratified analyses and for the secondary outcomes. Sensitivity analyses examining timing of implementation and more stringent phone restriction criteria were consistent with the main findings. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this repeated cross-sectional study of adolescents in Iceland, schoolwide mobile phone bans were not associated with meaningful changes in adolescent mental health or related social and behavioral outcomes. These findings suggest that school phone bans implemented in isolation may be insufficient to improve adolescent mental health at the population level.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Data to guide use of anti-PD1 immunotherapy with pembrolizumab for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) that is chemotherapy-resistant or in adjuvant settings are limited. We conducted an international retrospective study of pembrolizumab in GTN, including patients with ultra-high-risk choriocarcinoma and poor-prognosis placental site and epithelioid trophoblastic tumors (PSTT/ETT), with up to 8 years of follow-up. Twenty-three samples were characterized by multiplex immunofluorescence, shallow whole-genome, and whole-transcriptome sequencing. RESULTS: We identified 76 patients with drug-resistant GTN treated with pembrolizumab. This included 60 (78.9%) patients with GTN and measurable disease. Complete response was achieved in 71.7% (n=43 of 60; 95% confidence interval [CI], 60.3 to 83.1). Two-year overall survival (OS) was 85.6% (95% CI, 76.7 to 95.4), with median follow-up from pembrolizumab initiation of 25.4 months (range, 1.4 to 95.7). Sixteen (21.1%) received adjuvant pembrolizumab instead of high-dose chemotherapy, of whom 15 had poor-prognosis PSTT/ETT. No deaths were observed with median follow-up of 33.1 months (range, 7.7 to 68.6) from first remission. There were no identified grade 4 or worse immune-related toxicities. Shallow whole-genome and whole-transcriptome sequencing suggested low HLA-G expression could be due to transcriptional control. papers.abstract_en: Aberrant activation of dendritic cells (DCs) is intricately associated with inflammatory diseases, rendering DCs an appealing therapeutic target. Metabolites are emerging as crucial regulators of DCs, yet therapeutic strategies targeting DC metabolism for inflammatory diseases remain underexplored. Our study identifies the Vanin-pantethine-cholesterol axis as a key metabolic pathway that governs DC activation-a classical APC function. We found that Vanin is upregulated in activated DCs from autoimmune patients and mice; DC-specific Vanin deficiency significantly alleviates psoriasiform inflammation in mice. Mechanistically, Vanin hydrolyzes pantethine, leading to cholesterol and lipid raft accumulation on the cell membrane and promoting DC hyperactivation. Pantethine supplementation or pharmacologically induced Vanin inhibition reduces cholesterol overload, impedes DC activation, and mitigates psoriasiform inflammation. Notably, pantethine or RR6 treatment impairs activation of patient-derived DCs, and our investigator-initiated trial shows that pantethine combination therapy relieves clinical symptoms in psoriasis patients. Collectively, these findings establish the Vanin-pantethine-cholesterol axis as a key modulator of APC function, offering a promising metabolic approach for inflammatory diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Biochemicals are increasingly used in plant protection strategies due to their generally favorable safety profiles and rapid environmental degradation and are currently subject to the same extensive data requirements as conventional synthetic chemicals in Europe. The BiochemPPP-STAS framework was developed to consider these differences and to provide a concept for reduced and triggered information requirements. Here, we report on three case studies to compare the outcome of the BiochemPPP-STAS concept with the traditional information requirements for regulatory human health and environmental risk assessment. Three biochemicals, gibberellic acid (GA3), Lysate of Willaertia magna C2c Maky lysate (LWm) and tea tree oil (TTO) were retrospectively assessed using regulatory authority evaluations. For all three case studies, BiochemPPP-STAS adequately identified hazard profiles and supported derivation of reference values comparable to those obtained using full conventional data packages, while substantially reducing resources and in particular animal testing. For GA3 and LWm, the base dataset was sufficient to characterize toxicity and support low-risk conclusions. For TTO, reproductive toxicity signals were identified in base studies and triggered higher-tier testing, demonstrating the responsiveness of the tiered approach. Quantitative differences in reference values compared with classical assessments were generally small and did not alter regulatory outcomes. Environmental assessments similarly showed that base data requirements captured ecotoxicological concerns. The assessments on environmental safety were not different than using the full data set. Although conclusions are limited by the small number of case studies, and additional evaluations are necessary, the findings support, as a proof of concept the scientific adequacy of the BiochemPPP-STAS.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Fracture incidence is high in Norway compared to other European countries. We examined whether ambient air pollution levels are associated with forearm and hip fracture incidence, and whether these associations differed by sex and age. METHODS: Register data on 127,799 forearm fractures (age ≥40 years) and 103,754 hip fractures (age ≥50 years) were linked to population data from Statistics Norway (2008-2018). Fracture Incidence Rate Ratios (IRRs) with 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) by pollutant levels were estimated using Poisson regression, adjusting for education level, marital status, and immigrant background, urban/rural and inland location, health region, and climate, and examining interactions by sex and age (multiplicative and additive). RESULTS: PM2.5 ranged from 0.90-66.1  µg/m3 (mean: 5.5) and NO2 from 0.20-72.2  µg/m3 (mean: 8.1). In the highest PM2.5 tertile compared to the lowest, age- and year-adjusted forearm fracture risk was IRR = 1.22 (95% CI: 1.18, 1.25) in men and IRR = 1.24 (95% CI: 1.22, 1.26) in women. They were partly attenuated after adjusting for annual temperature and geographic variables. Associations with NO2 and with hip fractures were similar, though weaker. Interactions by sex and age were present for both fracture types, most notably a stronger NO2- hip fracture association in individuals aged ≥80 years. CONCLUSION: Ambient air pollution is associated with fracture risk, even at low exposure levels. The most consistent finding was a stronger association among individuals aged 80 years and above.

papers.abstract_en: Mercury exposure during pregnancy remains a public health concern due to its potential impact on foetal neurodevelopment. The randomised HBM4EU-MOM study (2020-2022) evaluated the effect of harmonised dietary advice on mercury exposure among 654 pregnant women from five European coastal countries. Total mercury concentrations in hair were measured at Phase 1 (baseline) and Phase 2 (follow-up). At baseline, mercury exposure varied substantially across countries, with the highest geometric mean (GM) concentrations in Portugal (1.56 μg/g) and Spain (0.90 μg/g), and lower levels in Greece, Iceland, and Cyprus (0.44 μg/g, 0.36 μg/g, and 0.31 μg/g, respectively). Country-specific temporal reductions in Spain and Portugal were observed in both intervention and control groups with similar magnitudes. Although the intervention did not produce a measurable reduction in mercury exposure compared with standard care, the country-specific temporal patterns and reductions in the proportion of women exceeding health-based exposure benchmark highlight the importance of understanding the behavioural, dietary, and contextual factors influencing mercury exposure during pregnancy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide. Although numerous treatment approaches are recommended by international clinical guidelines, there is still limited understanding of which interventions provide the best value for money. We aimed to critically appraise and summarise the evidence on the cost-effectiveness and costs of interventions endorsed in recent guidelines to manage low back pain (LBP), compared to usual care. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We searched 10 electronic databases (e.g., MEDLINE (OvidSP), EMBASE (OvidSP), PsycINFO (OvidSP)) from inception to 9th of February 2026 for cost-effectiveness studies of guideline-recommended treatments to manage non-specific LBP. The primary outcome was cost/quality-adjusted life year (QALY), which was converted to 2024 Great British Pound values, tabulated and summarised qualitatively. Secondary outcomes were direct costs (total, interventional, health service use, community services and out-of-pocket costs) and indirect costs (e.g., lost wages, lost productivity, absenteeism). We assessed methodological quality using the Consensus Health Economics Criteria (CHEC) checklist for within-trial economic evaluations or the Philips checklist for modelling studies. Our review included 20 studies (17 within-trial economic evaluations and three modelling studies), published between 2005 and 2026. Half (n = 10) focussed on chronic LBP (>3-month duration), and eight included mixed populations (i.e., acute, subacute and chronic). All studies were of non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions, both single-modality and multimodal interventions (e.g., exercise plus spinal manipulation; diet plus physical activity). Most interventions are cost-effective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of £20,000. Moreover, interventions aiming to reduce fear and stress or support self-management in people with chronic LBP, as well as clinician-delivered interventions including yoga, acupuncture, cognitive therapy and self-management support are potentially cost-saving from the healthcare, societal and payer's perspectives, as they are both more effective and less costly than usual care (e.g., first contact management, including advice and medication). All of the evidence is derived from high-income countries, and from a considerable heterogenous body of literature. Evidence on cost-effective treatments in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. CONCLUSIONS: Non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions that include education, psychological support, acupuncture and exercise seem to be cost-effective for managing LBP, compared to usual care. Improved access to and implementation of these effective treatments is urgently needed so more people can benefit from them in routine care. REGISTRATION: The review was registered on PROSPERO (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk; CRD42024510270).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pressure injury prevention in critical care remains a persistent global challenge. Despite established guidelines, implementation is often constrained by physiological instability, device burden, and competing clinical priorities. Emerging digital and artificial intelligence approaches offer potential support, yet their role within the complexity of critical care practice remains unclear. AIM: To explore clinicians' perspectives on pressure injury prevention in critical care, with particular attention to complexity, clinical decision-making and the potential role of emerging technologies. DESIGN: Qualitative study using reflexive thematic analysis. METHODS: We analysed 12 brief written reflections from clinicians working in critical care and related roles, predominantly in the United Kingdom. We purposively invited contributors through professional networks, who responded to shared prompts on prevention challenges, practice tensions, and potential roles for artificial intelligence. The first author led iterative semantic and latent coding within a contextualist-constructionist reflexive thematic analysis, supported by reflexive discussion among the author team. FINDINGS: Five interconnected themes emerged: negotiating physiological stability and guideline adherence; device-centred care as a source of iatrogenic harm; organisational constraints, incomplete prevention, and the illusion of compliance; diagnostic and conceptual uncertainty; and technology as supportive, not substitutive. Pressure injury prevention was constructed as a context-dependent process in which clinicians continually negotiated preventive actions against physiological instability, device dependence, organisational capacity and competing treatment priorities. Clinicians viewed technology as potentially supportive of risk recognition and clinical decision-making, but not as a substitute for clinical judgement. DISCUSSION: The findings suggest that guideline-driven pressure injury prevention may not fully accommodate the physiological instability, device dependence and organisational constraints encountered in critical care. They highlight the need for prevention approaches that support context-sensitive clinical judgement while recognising the limits of standardised protocols and emerging technologies. CONCLUSION: Pressure injury prevention in critical care involves context-sensitive clinical decision-making rather than protocol adherence alone. Emerging technologies may have a supportive role, but their clinical value and safety require development and prospective evaluation. IMPACT: This study provides qualitative insights into how clinicians negotiate pressure injury prevention in complex critical care environments and identifies considerations for future development and evaluation of decision-support technologies. REGISTRATION: Not registered.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the potential risk-benefit profile of upper- versus lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates. DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis. METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 6, 2026, for studies comparing upper- versus lower-extremity placement in neonates. Primary outcomes were venous thromboembolism, central line-associated bloodstream infection, and catheter tip malposition; secondary outcomes included phlebitis, catheter migration, catheter leakage, catheter occlusion, catheter breakage, total complications, dwell time, unplanned removal, pericardial or pleural effusion, sepsis, and all-cause mortality. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Crude estimates were pooled, sparse and heterogeneous adjusted estimates were summarised narratively, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. RESULTS: Twenty-one observational studies from 10 countries, involving 15,289 catheters, were included. For primary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism (RR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.30-0.89; P = 0.017; low certainty) but higher risks of central line-associated bloodstream infection (RR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.07-1.95; P = 0.018; very low certainty) and catheter tip malposition (RR = 2.63, 95% CI 1.61-4.30; P < 0.001; very low certainty). For secondary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with lower phlebitis risk (RR = 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.94; P = 0.022; low certainty) but higher risks of catheter migration (RR = 1.74, 95% CI 1.27-2.38; P < 0.001; low certainty), catheter leakage (RR = 2.24, 95% CI 1.35-3.73; P = 0.002; moderate certainty), and a marginally higher risk of unplanned removal (RR = 1.23, 95% CI 1.00-1.51; P = 0.048; very low certainty). A post hoc exploratory analysis suggested a possible higher risk of pericardial or pleural effusion (RR = 3.79, 95% CI 1.20-12.02; P = 0.024; very low certainty). No statistically significant between-site differences were observed for other secondary outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Crude observational evidence suggested a potential bidirectional risk-benefit profile across catheter-related outcomes. The findings should be interpreted cautiously because non-randomised designs remain susceptible to residual confounding. The observed associations may inform risk-informed, individualised site selection but do not establish a universally preferred site. Prospective studies with standardised outcomes and adjusted analyses are needed. REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD420251275788.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cognitive digital therapeutics (CDT) offer a promising non-pharmacological intervention for cognitive impairments in kids and teens (KTs). However, the optimal dosing parameters for CDT in pediatric populations remain unclear. METHODS: This retrospective study aimed to identify the optimal CDT doses for KTs with cognitive impairments across gender and developmental stages, using real-world big data. A total of 38,526 pediatric patients with cognitive impairments who underwent CDT between 2021 and 2025 were included in the analysis. The study assessed cognitive improvement based on the Mean Cognitive Index across varying CDT doses, stratified by age (< 10 vs. ≥10 years) and gender. RESULTS: The optimal daily dose varied by gender and age: boys under 10 required 16-20 min, while girls needed 24-28 min. In the teen group (10-18 years), boys needed 20-24 min, while girls required 16-20 min. The optimal total dose decreased with age, from 6 to 7 months in boys under 10 to 4-5 months in teens, and from 8 to 9 months in girls to 1-2 months in teens. Higher-than-optimal daily digital training doses may lead to diminished cognitive gains. The optimal weekly dose was 7 days/week across all subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first large-scale study to define age- and gender-specific optimal CDT doses in pediatric patients with cognitive impairments. The findings provide robust evidence to support personalized CDT interventions and may inform future treatment guidelines.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: As transmission declines, malaria becomes more spatially and demographically concentrated. This study investigated individual-level malaria characteristics and district-level factors associated with elimination in all 154 districts in Sumatra, Indonesia. METHODS: We analysed individual-level data of 13,386 reported malaria cases from 2019 to 2021. P. falciparum and P. vivax were confirmed by microscopy or rapid diagnostic test, while probable P. knowlesi was defined as microscopically identified P. knowlesi. Cases were classified as imported if they reported travel to endemic region within 2-4 weeks. Multivariable logistic regression with province as a random effect was used to examine individual-level factors associated with imported cases, and district-level socioeconomic and environmental factors associated with elimination. Spatial clustering of indigenous cases was assessed using Global Moran's I and SaTScan. RESULTS: Among reported cases, 71.8% (9,617) were P. vivax, 18.4% (2,467) P. falciparum, and 2.8% (369) probable P. knowlesi. Of 11,390 investigated cases, 8,748 (76.8%) were indigenous, 1,741 (15.3%) imported, and 901 (7.9%) unclassified. Imported cases were associated with older age (adjusted odds ratio 1.79, 95%CI 1.42-2.25 for 15-24 years old, and 1.97, 1.59-2.46 for 25-64 years old, compared to < 15 years old), males (1.70, 1.43-2.03), mobile and migrant population-related occupations (1.46, 1.22-1.76), diagnosed at hospitals or clinics (2.32, 1.85-2.91), infected with P. falciparum (1.48, 1.22-1.80), and hospitalised (15.29, 12.66-18.46). At the district level, a higher human development index (1.15, 1.01-1.34), lower historical annual parasite incidence (0.46, 0.29-0.69), and fewer endemic neighbours (0.78, 0.67-0.89) were associated with a higher likelihood of elimination. Spatial analysis revealed clustering tendencies, with localised clusters for P. falciparum, P. vivax, and probable P. knowlesi. CONCLUSIONS: Dynamics of imported malaria, heterogeneous clusters of local transmission, and lower district-level human development index challenged elimination efforts. This highlights the need for strengthened surveillance and targeted interventions.

papers.abstract_en: APOBEC3 cytosine deaminases are major sources of cancer mutations. In lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), APOBEC3 activity drives tumor evolution and therapy resistance, nominating these enzymes as therapeutic targets. Although APOBEC3A drives most APOBEC3-associated mutational signature burden across cancers, the relative contributions of individual paralogs in LUAD remain unclear. Here, we define the roles of endogenously misregulated APOBEC3 deaminases using CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts and whole-genome sequencing of 197 long-term propagated single-cell clones. APOBEC3 mutagenesis falls into three patterns, driven predominantly by APOBEC3A, by both APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B, or minimal despite detectable enzyme expression. Commonly used surrogate measures, including mRNA and protein levels and in vitro deaminase activity, do not predict these contributions. We also provide the first causal evidence that endogenous APOBEC3A generates the indel signature InD9a, linking it to uracil excision following cytosine deamination. These heterogeneous contributions highlight the need for biomarkers that resolve individual APOBEC3 activities to guide therapeutic targeting.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pediatric obesity is a major public health crisis. Early identification of metabolic traits that increase individual risk are emerging. As such, identification of variability in early energy expenditure would reveal the need for precision nutritional approaches from birth. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the interindividual variability in components of energy expenditure for the purpose of understanding early nutritional considerations in very young infants. METHODS: Infant participants (<3 months of age) underwent extensive energy expenditure phenotyping using a combination of doubly labeled water for total daily energy expenditure and a novel infant metabolic chamber for sleeping energy expenditure. Descriptive statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients, and univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses were used to assess reliability and characterize variability, predictors, and phenotypes of energy expenditure. We identified interindividual variability in total, mass-adjusted, and fat-free mass adjusted energy expenditures. Energy phenotypes (thrifty and spendthrift) were assigned based on the residuals between measured and predicted energy expenditure from metabolic mass. Discrepancies between measured energy expenditure and predicted by national dietary recommendations for infants (2023 DRI) were evaluated. RESULTS: Total daily and sleeping energy expenditures were 368±60 kcal/d and 250±60 kcal/d, respectively. Energy expenditure related to activity accounted for 21±9% of total measured. Age (r=.59), weight (r=.83), length (r=.75), and fat-free mass (r=.82) were positively associated with sleeping energy expenditure. We identified 40% of measured infants with a thrifty energy phenotype, classified as having sleeping energy expenditure under that predicted by cohort age, sex, and fat and fat-free mass. Mean prediction error of the 2023 DRI from our cohort was 10±7% and was positively associated with the amount of energy expenditure attributed to activity. CONCLUSIONS: These findings warrant further comprehensive metabolic phenotyping studies in young infants to understand how early energy expenditure tracks through the life course and influences obesity risk as well as the thorough evaluation and refinement of infant nutritional recommendations.

papers.abstract_en: Transfer RNA (tRNA) modifications are increasingly implicated as posttranscriptional regulators of basic neuronal functions. Characterizing tRNA modification profiles in specific neural circuits that control well-defined behaviors is challenging because of the complexity of conventional neurobiological models. Here, we leveraged the numerically simple central nervous system (CNS) of the marine mollusk Aplysia californica to investigate tRNA modification dynamics during habituation of a defensive reflex. We identified and quantified dozens of tRNA modifications and characterized the distribution of select small RNA modifications across different neuronal and nonneuronal tissues. Upon behavioral habituation of the siphon-elicited siphon withdrawal reflex (SSWR), we found that tRNA modification profiles in the major ganglion that controls the SSWR were repatterned with predictable, learning-related changes. We found a family of anticodon loop modifications that changed with habituation learning, including N6-isopentenyladenosine (i6A), which increased in abundance, and additional modifications N1-methyladenosine (m1A) and N7-methylguanosine (m7G), which decreased. These tRNA modification dynamics occurred independently of changes in the expression of their parent tRNAs, illustrating that behavioral habituation altered the activity of tRNA-modifying enzymes. Overall, our work reveals a link between tRNA modifications and behavioral habituation and provides insights toward understanding the posttranscriptional mechanisms of learning and memory.

papers.abstract_en: Transcription termination by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) prevents polymerase readthrough beyond annotated genes and limits transcriptional interference. Although XRN2-mediated RNA degradation is central to the torpedo model of transcription termination, how XRN2 is coupled to elongating Pol II in mammalian cells remains incompletely understood. Here, we used an endogenous AID2-POLR2G depletion system in HepG2 cells to examine the immediate role of the Pol II stalk subunit POLR2G/RPB7. Acute POLR2G depletion reduced promoter-proximal POLR2A occupancy, accompanied by lower nascent transcription across annotated transcription units. Unexpectedly, downstream of transcription end sites, increased POLR2A occupancy coincided with directional nascent transcription. Besides other Pol II subunits, POLR2G-associated proteomics recovered XRN2. Structural analysis of a published Rat1-bound Pol II termination complex, Ser2-phosphorylated Pol II (Ser2P Pol II) co-immunoprecipitation and XRN2 ChIP-qPCR collectively support a role for POLR2G in promoting XRN2 association with elongating Pol II at gene 3' ends. Re-expression of full-length POLR2G or its XRN2-associated RNA-binding domain reduced readthrough, whereas the N-terminal domain did not. Together, these findings support a model in which POLR2G contributes to efficient transcription termination by facilitating XRN2 association with elongating Pol II.

papers.abstract_en: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has achieved remarkable and durable responses in hematologic malignancies, but its efficacy in solid tumors remains limited and frequently transient. In this Review, we propose that interacting tumor barriers divert persistently engaged CAR-T cells toward dysfunctional and exhausted states. Defective trafficking, antigen heterogeneity, incomplete tumor clearance, metabolic deprivation, stromal exclusion, immunosuppressive cellular networks, inhibitory cytokines, chronic CAR signaling, and manufacturing-imprinted stress collectively shape the stimulation history and functional trajectory of CAR T-cells. Mechanistically, these pressures converge on NFAT-AP-1 imbalance, TOX/TOX2 and NR4A activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and exhaustion-associated epigenetic remodeling. This process creates a clinically relevant continuum between TCF1-positive progenitor-exhausted cells that retain self-renewal and checkpoint-responsive proliferative potential, and terminally exhausted cells with limited regenerative capacity. Building on this failure-pressure-fate model, we propose a mechanism-informed therapy framework that relates dominant failure mechanisms and residual CAR T-cell plasticity to potential intervention priorities. This approach may help match combination strategies to the dominant tumor pressure and CAR T-cell state, including stromal remodeling, metabolic engineering, cytokine armoring, checkpoint modulation, epigenetic intervention, and remanufacturing. Overall, this Review provides a fate-based framework for designing next-generation CAR T-cell therapies capable of achieving durable control in solid tumors.

papers.abstract_en: High-quality reference genomes are essential for comparative and functional genomics yet remain unavailable for many emerging model organisms. Here, we report OctDeg2.0, a chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the degu (Octodon degus), generated using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C scaffolding from a single male individual. Octodon degus is of growing interest as a natural animal model for aging and Alzheimer's disease research. The 3.4 billion base-pair assembly comprises 28 autosomes and both sex chromosomes, with markedly improved contiguity and completeness over the prior short-read assembly while maintaining high base accuracy. The new assembly provides substantially enhanced gene annotation, clearer resolution of chromatin architecture and cis-regulatory element landscapes, with much improved characterization of repetitive and structurally complex regions, including centromeres and segmental duplications. We present a streamlined and reproducible pipeline for high-resolution de novo genome assembly and gene annotation applicable to other emerging model organisms. This work establishes a robust genomic resource for studying molecular and cellular mechanisms in health and disease in Octodon degus.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate an anatomically guided artificial intelligence framework for joint-level detection and multi-label characterization of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) osteoarthritic changes on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). METHODS: CBCT examinations from 71 patients (142 TMJs) were assessed independently by two expert readers for erosion, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, joint-space narrowing, and condylar flattening. Discordant cases underwent third-reader adjudication to establish the reference standard. A 3-dimensional ResNet18 model was trained using patient-level training, validation, and independent test partitions. Joint-level OA-associated features were evaluated. Complete TMJ region-of-interest (ROI) and segmentation-masked condyle inputs were compared. Condylar flattening was analyzed separately. RESULTS: Inter-reader agreement varied by feature, ranging from slight agreement for flattening (κ =  -0.01) and joint-space narrowing (κ = 0.15) to substantial agreement for osteophyte formation (κ = 0.63). Automated condyle segmentation achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.91 ± 0.042. The joint-level model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9325, with sensitivity of 0.8470 and specificity of 0.9081. Feature-level AUCs ranged from 0.6756 to 0.9515. Segmentation-masked condyle input yielded higher classification of erosion (AUC, 0.8685), osteophyte formation (0.9090), subchondral sclerosis (0.9134), and subchondral cysts (0.9515), whereas complete TMJ ROI input performed better for joint-space narrowing (0.8132). CONCLUSIONS: This framework extends CBCT assessment beyond binary detection of TMJ OA-associated changes by providing feature-level characterization. Anatomically guided masking showed higher AUCs for abnormalities intrinsic to the mandibular condyle, whereas joint-space narrowing performed better with broader joint context. These observations require confirmation in larger datasets.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Risk in interstitial pneumonia (IP) is assessed routinely by the Gender-Age-Physiology (GAP) score from pulmonary function and the tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) on echocardiography. This study evaluated whether the percent perfusion defect (%PPD) on short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold (STDIBH) pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT carries prognostic information that neither captures. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ninety-one consecutive patients with IP who underwent STDIBH perfusion SPECT/CT between 2012 and 2023 were analyzed retrospectively. The primary endpoint was a composite major adverse event (MAE) of all-cause death, acute exacerbation of IP, respiratory-failure hospitalization, and initiation of home oxygen therapy. Association was assessed by Cox regression and discrimination by censoring-weighted time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: MAE occurred in 66 of 91 patients (72.5%) over a median follow-up of 45.9 months. %PPD was associated with MAE after adjustment for the GAP score and antifibrotic therapy (adjusted hazard ratio 1.2304 per 10 percentage points, 95% CI 1.0568-1.4325; P = 0.008), and, in exploratory analyses, for TRPG and the GAP score together (1.2058, 1.0314-1.4096; P = 0.019). It showed no significant correlation with TRPG (Spearman r = 0.164; P = 0.140). Time-dependent discrimination did not differ significantly between %PPD and the GAP score at 6, 12, and 24 months, and adding %PPD to the GAP score changed the Harrell C-index from 0.692 to 0.719 (difference 0.027, 95% CI - 0.009 to 0.107). %PPD was obtained in all 91 patients and the GAP score in 68 (74.7%). CONCLUSION: In IP, %PPD measures a dimension of risk that the GAP score does not capture, and exploratory analyses suggest that echocardiography does not capture it either. %PPD is obtainable when the GAP score is not. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Gynecologic diseases are a significant yet often underrecognized global health burden, negatively impacting women's quality of life. In China, county-level public hospitals serve as the primary providers of care or first line of defense for managing these conditions, highlighting the urgent need for improved service quality. However, a systematic framework with specific quality indicators for gynecologic care remains underdeveloped both in China and internationally. Compared with obstetrics, progress in gynecologic care quality assessment has lagged, creating a gap between evidence and practice. The authors aimed to develop and preliminarily implement a quality indicator system to guide gynecologic care quality improvement efforts. METHODS: Quality indicators were identified through a comprehensive literature review and refined using a two-round modified Delphi survey (January-April 2024) involving 29 experts. Expert consensus on the importance and feasibility of each indicator was obtained. Based on this indicator system, the authors conducted the China Gynaecological Healthcare Quality Survey, a national cross-sectional survey across 31 provinces in mainland China (April-December 2024), sampling 435 hospitals of different types and levels. After data cleaning, a final sample of 178 hospitals was included for analysis. A hybrid weighting approach combining subjective expert judgment (percentage weight and multiplicative methods) with objective empirical data (entropy weight method) was applied. The TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) method was used to derive a comprehensive quality score (closeness coefficient [Ci]) for each hospital. RESULTS: The Delphi process yielded a final framework comprising three first-level, 16 second-level, and 43 third-level indicators. Mean importance scores ranged from 7.69 to 8.97 on a nine-point scale, with variation coefficients between 0.02 and 0.20. Kendall's W coefficients increased from 0.149 to 0.220 between rounds, indicating growing consensus. The average authority coefficient across experts was 0.90, supporting the reliability of the results. The combined weights assigned to structure, process, and outcome domains were 0.455, 0.301, and 0.245, respectively. In the national survey, 178 hospitals (84 county-level and 94 provincial and municipal) were analyzed. Provincial and municipal hospitals achieved significantly higher comprehensive quality scores than county-level hospitals (median Ci: 0.421 vs. 0.397; z=-5.533, P<0.001). A significant regional difference was observed, with the eastern region scoring higher than the central and western regions (median Ci: 0.425, 0.407, and 0.402; χ2=12.214, P=0.002). No significant differences were found among hospital types (χ2=4.174, P=0.124). CONCLUSIONS: The authors established mainland China's first validated indicator system for gynecologic care quality. National implementation across 178 hospitals demonstrates the framework's practical utility while revealing significant quality differences across hospital tiers and regions. This standardized evaluation framework provides a practical tool for targeted quality assessment and precision improvement in primary gynecologic care.

papers.abstract_en: Urban soils contaminated with persistent and toxic heavy metals are found worldwide. Their remediation is essential to prevent harm to humans and the environment. The integration of portable X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy (pXRF) as a field analytical instrument in remediation projects offers the possibility to rapidly assess soils at low costs. In this study, we test the potential of pXRF in contaminated soil assessment at a former battery factory "Varta Insel" in Hagen, Germany. Soil samples were analyzed (1) by pXRF on site, (2) by pXRF under laboratory conditions, and (3) by microwave assisted aqua regia digestion with inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES). Direct on-site measurements were useful for supporting field decisions and selecting samples for further analysis, but results were strongly influenced by matrix effects, grain size, and moisture content, limiting their reliability. Dried and sieved samples were measured by pXRF under laboratory conditions through low-density polyethylene sample bags. The laboratory pXRF results agreed with the more expensive ICP-OES analysis in 94% of cases when classifying samples above or below German regulatory limits. However, pXRF systematically underestimated lead concentrations and overestimated arsenic and chromium. Hence, we conclude that pXRF is not a stand-alone solution for heavy metal analysis of contaminated soil samples. However, it can effectively guide the selection of samples requiring detailed ICP-OES analysis and contribute to higher-density data collection, ultimately enhancing spatial resolution.

papers.abstract_en: Charcoal rot (CRD), caused by Macrophomina phaseolina, is a major soil-borne disease of cotton, and conventional chemical control often provides inconsistent suppression. This study aimed to characterize management-associated patterns among culture-recovered cotton root-associated fungi and to identify fungal interactions relevant to M. phaseolina suppression. Roots were collected from asymptomatic and symptomatic cotton plants at mid-season and end-season in a field subjected to chemical, Trichoderma-based, and integrated CRD management. Root-associated isolates were recovered by culture-dependent methods and identified using molecular markers and phylogenetic analyses. Selected fungal taxa were evaluated in vitro and in a 33-day greenhouse seedling assay, while commercial 6-pentyl-α-pyrone (6-PP) was examined in a targeted antifungal assay. From approximately 300 recovered isolates, 66 representative morphotypes were selected and molecularly identified, including 56 fungal and 10 bacterial isolates. Aspergillus was the most frequently recovered fungal genus at mid-season, whereas Alternaria became predominant at season's end, particularly in symptomatic plants. The numbers of recovered fungal isolates and taxa increased modestly in asymptomatic plants but more strongly in symptomatic plants, while Trichoderma-based management was associated with markedly lower numbers of recovered fungal isolates and taxa. Commercial 6-PP inhibited M. phaseolina in a concentration- and time-dependent manner (94.5-100% at nominal 400-800 µg mL-¹ through 72 h). Greenhouse assays showed limited effects on early seedling development during the latent disease stage. Nevertheless, qPCR revealed mean reductions of 92%, 94%, and 99% in M. phaseolina DNA following co-inoculation with A. niger, N. solani, and A. alternata, respectively, compared with 47% for R. arrhizus. Only the reduction associated with A. alternata remained significant after multiplicity adjustment. These findings associate biological and integrated management with distinct patterns in culture-recovered root-associated fungi and identify microbial interactions and natural product activity relevant to future CRD management.

papers.abstract_en: People living with multiple long-term conditions (MLTC, also called multimorbidity) experience substantial health burden, with those from ethnic minority populations disproportionately affected due to persistent health inequalities. This scoping review identified health promotion interventions designed to address MLTC in ethnic minority populations. Five databases and Google Scholar were searched from inception to June 2025 for studies conducted in the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries that included ≥50% ethnic minority participants living with MLTC. Health promotion interventions were defined as programmes, activities, or initiatives delivered in any setting that operate at one or more levels (individual, health system, community, societal, and policy), consistent with the five action areas of the Ottawa Charter for Health promotion. Descriptive and qualitative content analysis was undertaken, with interventions mapped against the Ottawa Charter action areas. Twenty-six studies were included in total, with the majority from the United States of America (USA; n = 24, 92%). One study each was conducted in Canada (n = 1, 4%) and Australia (n = 1, 4%). The interventions aligned with four of the five Ottawa Charter action areas: developing personal skills (26, 100%), creating supportive environments (n = 23, 88%), strengthening community action (n = 14, 54%), and reorienting health services (n = 21, 81%). No intervention directly addressed building healthy public policy. Evidence on health promotion interventions for ethnic minority populations with MLTC is currently underdeveloped, concentrated in the USA, with clear gap in policy action. There is an urgent need for research in OECD countries embedding a multi-level approach to address gaps in policy-actions.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Food allergy represents a significant public health burden with implications on quality of life and persistent risk of accidental allergic reactions. Therapeutic immunomodulation for food allergy has only recently entered clinical practice. Oral immunotherapy (OIT) has emerged as an effective approach for increasing allergen reaction thresholds; however, its implementation remains limited due to systemic factors. This review aims to describe the development, implementation, and outcomes of a standardized OIT program for immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated food allergy at an academic pediatric allergy institution. RECENT FINDINGS: An OIT program was developed with the objectives of improving accessibility, standardizing treatment approaches, minimizing adverse events, and allowing individualized treatment goals ranging from protection against accidental exposure to dietary liberalization. SUMMARY: OIT represents an effective, safe immunomodulatory treatment for IgE-mediated food allergy. The implementation of a standardized OIT program allowed expansion from an initial pilot program to a large clinical service involving thousands of patients. Both single-food and multifood OIT protocols were feasible and safe. Most adverse reactions were mild-moderate and gastrointestinal or cutaneous in nature. Severe reactions and eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) were uncommon when patients were appropriately selected and monitored. Standardized protocols, careful patient selection, extensive counseling, and systematic monitoring are essential to optimize outcomes and minimize risks.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Paroxysmal movement disorders are a clinically and genetically diverse group of rare childhood-onset movement disorders that are challenging to diagnose and treat. Thus, this review highlights recent advancements in the epidemiology, diagnosis, classification, and management of pediatric paroxysmal movement disorders. RECENT FINDINGS: The classification of paroxysmal movement disorders has evolved from clinical descriptions to an etiology-descriptive, genotype-phenotype approach. While next-generation sequencing has increased diagnostic yield, 17.5-65% of patients remain without a genetic diagnosis. Recent publications underscore the co-occurrence of PxMDs within developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and epilepsy-dyskinesia syndromes. Novel causative genes (e.g., TMEM151A, KCNJ10, FGF13A) and new phenotypic associations (RHOBTB2) have been identified. Therapeutic strategies are moving to genotype-directed treatments. SUMMARY: Despite recent advances in genetics, detailed clinical history, video analysis, and neurological examination are still key to diagnosing paroxysmal movement disorders and guiding genetic testing. Though next-generation sequencing has provided insights with new genes and disease mechanisms, there is still much to be understood.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Resurgent outbreaks and declining childhood vaccination coverage have amplified the need for pediatricians to promptly recognize and manage vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs). This review summarizes the epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, initial management, public health reporting, and prevention of selected VPDs relevant to pediatric practice. RECENT FINDINGS: Childhood vaccination coverage has declined in recent years, coinciding with renewed outbreaks and continued transmission of measles, mumps, pertussis, meningococcal disease, and hepatitis B in the United States. Recent federal immunization schedule changes for children and adolescents (e.g., revised hepatitis B birth-dose guidance, altered meningococcal vaccine decision-making, and expanded pentavalent meningococcal vaccine options) highlight the need for pediatricians to remain familiar with evolving vaccine recommendations. SUMMARY: Although routine immunization has dramatically reduced the burden of many VPDs, recent declines in vaccine coverage and notable outbreaks have renewed the need for clinical vigilance. Pediatricians should be prepared to identify characteristic presentations, implement appropriate isolation and infection-control measures, obtain timely diagnostic testing, initiate treatment or postexposure management when indicated, and reinforce vaccination as the cornerstone of prevention. This review provides a practical guide to the recognition and management of measles, mumps, pertussis, meningococcal disease, and hepatitis B in pediatric settings.

papers.abstract_en: Background and Clinical Significance: Octreotide is widely used off-label for neonatal postoperative chylothorax, although dosing is not standardised, and the supporting evidence comes mainly from case reports and case series. Somatostatin receptor (SSTR) subtypes 2 and 5 (SSTR2 and SSTR5) are expressed in the human thoracic duct, which provides a biological rationale for its use. Case Presentation: A term female neonate developed a massive left-sided chylothorax on initiation of enteral feeding, eight days after repair of a left congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Chest drainage yielded milky fluid with high triglyceride levels. Management comprised pleural drainage, total parenteral nutrition, fluid restriction, albumin, furosemide, antibiotics and continuous intravenous octreotide, started at 2 μg/kg/h and increased by 2 μg/kg/h daily to 12 μg/kg/h. Drainage declined after about 10 days, and radiological resolution after 20 days of treatment allowed for drain removal, extubation and reintroduction of feeding with a medium-chain triglyceride formula. Octreotide was tapered after 30 days. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Conclusions: In this single case, postoperative chylothorax resolved during multimodal conservative management that included step-dose-escalated octreotide; the contribution of octreotide cannot be separated from that of the concurrent therapies. We discuss the differential diagnosis of pleural effusion after CDH repair and summarise the experimental rationale for octreotide, namely reduced splanchnic lymph production and an increased thoracic duct contraction rate ex vivo, which was not assessed in our patient. Prospective studies are needed to define evidence-based dosing and monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: Background and Objectives: Self-regulation is important for children's learning, social participation and everyday functioning, yet intervention evidence for autistic children and young people is fragmented across intervention approaches and regulatory constructs. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to characterise and critically evaluate non-pharmacological randomised controlled trials targeting self-regulation in autistic children and young people and to quantify effects on both self-regulation and separate child functional outcomes. Methods: MEDLINE, PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL and ERIC were searched to 24 May 2026. Eligible studies were randomised controlled trials involving autistic children and young people aged 0-18 years that targeted at least one domain of self-regulation and assessed both self-regulation and child function. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB-2. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted for self-regulation and functional outcomes, with moderator, meta-regression and sensitivity analyses examining sources of variation. Functional proximity and intervention-mechanism moderator analyses were exploratory and were not prespecified in the registered protocol. Results: Twenty-five studies involving 1655 randomised participants were included. Self-regulation improved significantly across 27 intervention-comparator effects from 25 studies (Hedges' g = 0.605, 95% CI 0.454-0.756; 95% prediction interval 0.027-1.183). Functional outcomes also improved across 25 effects from 23 studies (g = 0.527, 95% CI 0.356-0.698; 95% prediction interval -0.158-1.212). Functional effects were substantially larger for direct/target-aligned outcomes (g = 0.761) than for distal/generalisation outcomes (g = 0.250; Qβ = 11.034, p < .001). The direct-distal contrast attenuated when restricted to active-comparator studies (Qβ = 3.770, p = .052), although distal effects remained positive. Comparator type moderated both outcome streams, whereas self-regulation construct coverage, age, intervention duration, target-skill application and explicit generalisation support did not significantly moderate effects. Conclusions: Self-regulation-focused interventions produce beneficial average effects on both regulatory and functional outcomes. Functional improvement is strongest when outcomes align closely with intervention targets, although smaller positive effects also extend to distal outcomes. Future trials should distinguish proximal regulatory change from target-aligned and distal functional outcomes and explicitly test pathways of generalisation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Hypoxemia after bidirectional Glenn palliation can result from distinct physiological mechanisms that may produce similar arterial oxygen saturation. We evaluated whether routinely available bedside markers could recover physiological states encoded in a mechanistic virtual-patient model. METHODS: A steady-state zero-dimensional closed-loop model generated five causes of Glenn hypoxemia: elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, veno-venous collateral shunting, pulmonary gas-exchange impairment, increased metabolic demand, and ventricular dysfunction. Hidden physiological variables were withheld from the classifier; inputs were SpO2, heart rate, mean arterial pressure, hemoglobin, Glenn/SVC pressure, and SVC oxygen saturation. Because bedside patterns arise downstream from prespecified equations and phenotype perturbations, classification was interpreted as internal mechanistic recoverability rather than clinical diagnostic performance. RESULTS: Of 150,000 generated states, 127,162 passed broad physiological criteria and 66,269 met strict hypoxemia/hemodynamic criteria. After balancing, 26,400 virtual patients were analyzed (5280 per mechanism; 19,800 training and 6600 held-out testing). SpO2 alone achieved 26.1% accuracy (macro-AUROC 0.580); the primary bedside model achieved 56.1% accuracy (95% CI 55.0-57.4%) and macro-AUROC 0.845 (95% CI 0.840-0.851). Elevated PVR was the most readily recovered phenotype. Glenn/SVC pressure and SVC saturation provided the largest incremental contributions, while broader measurement-error assumptions substantially reduced performance. CONCLUSIONS: Within this mechanistic simulation, multivariable bedside patterns allowed partial recovery of physiological states encoded by the model. Because phenotypes and their observable consequences were generated from prespecified assumptions, the reported performance quantifies internal recoverability under those assumptions and should not be interpreted as diagnostic accuracy or as independent evidence of bedside information content in patients. The model identifies testable physiologic signatures and areas of overlap for prospective clinical validation.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Childhood mental health problems are often organized into interrelated emotional, attentional, and behavioral domains. However, little is known about how low frustration tolerance and childhood perfectionism are connected with these domains in school-aged children. This study aimed to estimate the network structure of low frustration tolerance, childhood perfectionism, and mental health problems in Peruvian children aged 8 to 12 years. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 707 Peruvian children from public and private schools in Lima, Peru. The assessed variables were low frustration tolerance, perfectionistic self-demands, reaction to failure, internalizing problems, attention problems, and externalizing problems. A non-regularized Gaussian graphical model was estimated using Spearman correlations. Expected influence was calculated to identify central nodes. Network accuracy and stability were evaluated using nonparametric bootstrap and case-dropping procedures. Network comparisons were performed according to sex and school type. Results: In the full-sample dimension-level network, eight edges were identified, all of which were positive. Low frustration tolerance and reaction to failure showed the highest observed expected influence values. The strongest associations were observed between reaction to failure and internalizing problems, low frustration tolerance and externalizing problems, perfectionistic self-demands and reaction to failure, and low frustration tolerance and reaction to failure. Expected influence showed adequate case-dropping stability. Exploratory network comparisons identified the largest observed sex difference in the association between reaction to failure and internalizing problems, whereas global strength was descriptively higher in public than private schools; however, these omnibus group differences did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple grouping comparisons. Conclusions: Low frustration tolerance and reaction to failure emerged as highly connected dimensions within the estimated network. These findings identify candidate processes for further longitudinal and preventive research focused on emotional regulation and adaptive responses to failure while not implying causal or intervention effects.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted youth movement behaviours and mental health, but evidence on post-pandemic trends remains limited. Therefore, this study examined differences in compliance with the 24-h movement behaviour guidelines and their association with mental health outcomes among Portuguese children and adolescents between 2022 and 2024. Methods: This repeated cross-sectional study included two independent samples of Portuguese children and adolescents from the 2022 and 2024 waves of the Health Behaviour in School-aged Children study (2022: n = 2775; 2024: n = 2381). The 24-h movement behaviours (physical activity, sleep and screen time) and mental health outcomes, assessed by Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21), were self-reported. Prevalences of attaining the 24-h movement guidelines and DASS-21 categories were calculated and compared between 2022 and 2024 using chi-square tests. Adjusted logistic regression models were used to examine the associations between movement behaviour compliance and mental health outcomes. Results: From 2022 to 2024, the proportion meeting physical activity (7.5% to 13.7%; p < 0.001) and screen-time (12.8% to 28.2%; p < 0.001) guidelines increased, while adherence to sleep recommendations did not differ significantly (42.4% to 41.2%; p = 0.365). The proportion meeting two or more guidelines was also higher in 2024 (9.5% to 20.1%; p < 0.001). The prevalence of mild-to-extremely severe symptoms was lower in 2024 than in 2022 for depression (34.2% to 43.9%; p < 0.001), anxiety (38.1% to 43.2%; p = 0.001) and stress (23.6% to 31.0%; p < 0.001). Meeting screen-time and sleep guidelines was associated with at least 31% lower odds of having depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms (p < 0.001). Conclusions: More favourable prevalence estimates for movement behaviours and mental health outcomes were observed in 2024 than in 2022. Compliance with screen-time and sleep guidelines was associated with lower odds of depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a major and growing public health challenge worldwide. Although parental misperception of children's weight is well documented, how children perceive their parents' body size and whether parental body size is associated with children's expressed desire to be like the parent have received little attention. We examined children's perception of parental body size and whether parental BMI was associated with their expressed desire to be like the parent in a primary care sample. METHODS: This single-center, cross-sectional study included 229 parent-child pairs consecutively recruited from a family medicine outpatient clinic in Türkiye between January and March 2026. Children aged 4-8 years rated the accompanying parent's body size and reported whether they wanted to be like that parent, while parents independently rated their own body size. The BMI-based Body Size Guide was used for all figure selections, and the classification derived from objectively measured parental BMI served as the primary reference. Agreement was evaluated using Cohen's kappa coefficients, associations were examined using multivariable logistic regression, and the children's spontaneous explanations were examined using qualitative content analysis. RESULTS: Parents showed moderate weighted agreement with the BMI-derived classification (weighted κ = 0.536, 95% CI: 0.456-0.612; exact agreement: 59.4%), whereas children showed fair weighted agreement (weighted κ = 0.315, 95% CI: 0.231-0.392; exact agreement: 42.8%). After adjustment for child age, child sex, child weight status, parent sex, and parent age, parental overweight (aOR = 0.353, 95% CI: 0.170-0.733) and parental obesity (aOR = 0.133, 95% CI: 0.057-0.307) were associated with lower odds of the child reporting a desire to be like the parent. After adjustment for child age, child sex, parent sex, and parent age, parental overweight (aOR = 2.818, 95% CI: 1.101-7.211) and parental obesity (aOR = 4.774, 95% CI: 1.816-12.546) were associated with higher odds of child overweight/obesity. Among the 53 children who provided an explanation, responses referred to body size, weight, health, appearance, affection, and identification with the parent, illustrating the broad interpretation of the question. CONCLUSIONS: Children aged 4-8 years were able to rate parental body size, although their agreement with the BMI-derived classification was limited. Children's expressed desire to be like the parent varied according to parental BMI; however, this broad question may reflect emotional, relational, behavioural, and appearance-related considerations rather than bodily resemblance alone. The open-ended responses provide context by showing that only some children spontaneously referred to body size or weight. These findings support further research using developmentally validated and stigma-sensitive measures to clarify how young children perceive parental body size and interpret questions about identification with a parent.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smartphones have become indispensable tools for communication, entertainment, and information access among children and adolescents. Excessive smartphone use may interfere with daily activities and contribute to problematic smartphone use. This study aimed to investigate age-related differences in smartphone use patterns and their impact on health among children and adolescents. METHODS: A cross-sectional, online questionnaire-based study was conducted between March and May 2021 among 415 smartphone users aged 7-18 years. Participants were divided into two age groups (group 1: 7-12 and group 2: 13-18 years). Sociodemographic characteristics, smartphone use patterns, lifestyle factors, and health-related outcomes were assessed. Statistical analyses were performed in R version 4.3.3. RESULTS: In group 1, daily smartphone use was mostly 1-3 h (40.35%), whereas in adolescents it was 3-5 h (40.85%). Female adolescents spent significantly more time using smartphones than males (p < 0.0001), whereas boys had higher odds of using their smartphone for gaming than girls (aOR = 3.55, 95% CI 1.83-7.09). Approximately two-thirds of adolescents in both age groups reported excessive daily smartphone use and perceived themselves as "addicted". Ocular complaints were among the most frequently reported somatic symptoms, particularly among adolescents. Prolonged smartphone use was significantly associated with disturbing dreams OR = 1.89, 95% CI (1.30-2.81) and insufficient sleep OR = 1.60, 95% CI (1.11-2.34) in adolescents; smartphone use before bedtime was significantly associated with daytime sleepiness in both groups (group 1 p = 0.041, group 2 p = 0.040). Anxiety-related symptoms were reported by nearly all participants, while emotional symptoms/experiences suggesting eventual depression appeared more prevalent among younger children. CONCLUSIONS: Excessive smartphone use is highly prevalent among children and adolescents and is associated with sleep disturbances, somatic symptoms, and psychological complaints, highlighting the need for targeted preventive interventions.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Cancer and its subsequent treatments have been shown to cause significant cognitive impairment, known as Cancer-Related Cognitive Impairment (CRCI). CRCI impacts a range of cognitive domains, including working memory and executive function, attention, concentration, short-term memory, visuospatial control, problem solving, and information processing speed. Treatment options for these cancer sequelae are limited, with many patients never receiving any medical rehabilitation efforts. Current treatment recommendations include pharmaceutical intervention, cognitive training (CT), physical activity, and self-management strategies, with a prior meta-analysis in adults supporting CT as the most promising of these options. Thus, this systematic review aims to explore the current body of evidence for the use of CT as a treatment for childhood cancer survivors and assess the strengths and weaknesses of previously utilised programs to determine how to best test and optimise CT for this population. Methods: A systematic search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO and CINAHL. The review was prepared following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 reporting guidelines. Results: From an initial 6172 studies, six were included in the final review, covering 208 intervention participants who completed CT. CT platforms used by the included studies were all technology-mediated, and consisted of 'Cogmed' (n = 4), Attention Process Training (n = 1) and 'Captain's log' (n = 1). Cognitive testing in the included studies covered three domains: working memory, attention and delayed recall (memory). Studies showed varied improvement across these domains, with most positive effects in the domain of working memory, although certainty of evidence across the included studies was all assessed as low or very low. Conclusions: This systematic review provides preliminary evidence for the use of CT in childhood cancer survivors, but also makes a range of recommendations for future studies in this population, given the current gaps in the literature. This includes utilisation of a control group, use of consistent cognitive testing protocols, and CT design that targets the diverse nature of the cognitive change seen in CRCI. Together, these recommendations will allow future studies to more fully probe the utility of CT as an intervention for this population, while also optimising its usage.

papers.abstract_en: Introduction: Survival and short-term neonatal outcomes in preterm infants remain a significant clinical challenge. Although it is known that antenatal corticosteroids reduce neonatal mortality and morbidity when administered between 24 and 34 weeks of gestation, evidence regarding their use in borderline pregnancies is limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of antenatal betamethasone exposure on neonatal mortality and morbidity in infants born between 21 and 25 weeks of gestation. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study includes newborns born at Mersin City Training and Research Hospital between 1 January 2021 and 1 January 2026, at gestational ages ranging from 210/7 to 256/7 weeks, who underwent resuscitation in the delivery room and were admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit. Neonatal clinical and maternal characteristics, pregnancy and delivery characteristics, antenatal corticosteroid exposure, the need for respiratory support, neonatal morbidities, and mortality data were evaluated. The primary outcome was survival to discharge or transfer alive; secondary outcomes included recorded neonatal morbidities and their composites with death. Descriptive statistics were presented as medians (25th-75th percentiles), counts, and percentages. Group comparisons used the Kruskal-Wallis or Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables and Fisher exact or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests for binary categorical variables. Adjusted logistic regression assessed associations with clinical outcomes; sensitivity analyses included restriction to singleton infants. Sibling correlation was not accounted for in the 108-infant analysis. Results: The study included 108 preterm infants born at 21-25 weeks gestation. Thirty of the infants (27.8%) received a full/booster dose of betamethasone, 31 (28.7%) received an incomplete dose, and 47 (43.5%) did not receive betamethasone. Survival rates in the complete, incomplete, and no-betamethasone groups were 66.7%, 41.9%, and 14.9%, respectively (p < 0.001). In the main logistic regression model adjusted for gestational week, sex, and birth weight, compared with the group that did not receive betamethasone, incomplete exposure was associated with a 4.38-fold higher probability of survival, while complete exposure was associated with an 11.95-fold higher probability of survival. Incomplete and complete betamethasone exposure were associated with a lower likelihood of outcomes such as severe intraventricular hemorrhage or death. Complete exposure was also associated with a lower likelihood of the composite outcomes of necrotizing enterocolitis or death and retinopathy of prematurity or death. Conclusions: Antenatal betamethasone exposure in the management of periviable infants may offer potential benefits in terms of neonatal survival and morbidity. However, evaluating survival alone as a measure of a successful neonatal outcome is insufficient; serious neonatal morbidities and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes must also be considered in the clinical decision-making process. To reduce uncertainty in this area, there is a need for studies with larger sample sizes, involving multiple centers, and including long-term follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Supplementary feeding programs are widely used to prevent or manage child undernutrition, but their population-level benefit depends on implementation. Objective: To critically synthesize multilevel determinants of program reach, continuity, utilization, equity and sustainability in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Methods: We conducted a critical narrative review of peer-reviewed and grey literature identified through iterative database searching and targeted verification. Sources were charted by setting, design, program, implementation determinant, consequence, evidence directness, limitation and narrative credibility. Direct, related and indirect evidence were weighted differently in the synthesis. Results: Direct and related evidence most consistently linked program performance to financing and supply continuity, workforce preparation and supervision, food acceptability, caregiver understanding, equitable access and monitoring linked to corrective action. Direct evidence was concentrated in South Asia and selected programs in Indonesia, Iran and Ethiopia. Evidence concerning digital delivery, father-inclusive approaches, community-health-worker incentives and donor transition was largely indirect and supports hypotheses rather than established program effects. Conclusions: Reliable delivery systems and effective child-level utilization are necessary for supplementary feeding programs to contribute to nutritional outcomes. Recommendations supported mainly by indirect evidence require prospective evaluation in supplementary feeding settings, particularly in underrepresented LMIC regions.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Perceived stress and subjective body-shape perception may jointly characterize health-related conditions during adolescence. This study examined health-related outcomes across joint categories of perceived stress and subjective body-shape perception and compared perceived stress across combinations of objective and subjective weight status. Objective weight status and self-perceived body shape were also combined into four categories to compare the odds of high perceived stress. Random Forest and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses were additionally performed as exploratory cross-sectional classification analyses. Results: Compared with the low-stress, self-perceived non-overweight category, the high-stress, self-perceived overweight category showed higher odds of depressive symptoms (AOR = 15.96; 95% CI, 6.52-39.10), poor self-rated health (AOR = 7.55; 95% CI, 3.22-17.73), and alcohol experience (AOR = 3.04; 95% CI, 1.31-7.07). In the objective-subjective weight-status analysis, adolescents with objective non-overweight and self-perceived overweight showed higher odds of high perceived stress than those with concordant non-overweight status (AOR = 1.90; 95% CI, 1.27-2.86). The exploratory Random Forest model showed modest cross-sectional classification performance (ROC-AUC = 0.615; PR-AUC = 0.438), with depressive symptoms showing the largest SHAP contribution among the displayed features. Conclusions: Health-related outcomes differed across joint categories of perceived stress and self-perceived body-shape perception. Adolescents with objective non-overweight but self-perceived overweight also showed higher odds of high perceived stress than those with concordant non-overweight status. These findings highlight the relevance of considering perceived stress, subjective body-shape perception, and objective weight status together when describing adolescent health-related characteristics.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Family-centered services (FCSs) are a key approach in pediatric healthcare and rehabilitation that promotes collaboration between service providers and families. The Measure of Processes of Care for Service Providers (MPOC-SP) is widely used to evaluate family-centered services from the provider perspective; however, no validated Turkish version is available. This study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the MPOC-SP into Turkish and to examine its factor structure, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, measurement error, and supplementary model-based construct indices among Turkish-speaking service providers working in pediatric healthcare, disability, and rehabilitation settings. Methods: The MPOC-SP was translated and culturally adapted following a structured cross-cultural adaptation process. A total of 267 service providers from multiple professional disciplines, institutional settings, and 15 provinces of Türkiye participated in the psychometric evaluation. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Test-retest reliability was evaluated in 86 participants using ICC(2,1), and measurement error was examined using the standard error of measurement (SEM) and minimal detectable change at the 95% confidence level (MDC95). The hypothesized four-factor structure was evaluated in 267 participants using confirmatory factor analysis based on polychoric correlations and diagonally weighted least squares (DWLS). Composite reliability, average variance extracted, the Fornell-Larcker criterion, and the heterotrait-monotrait ratio were examined as supplementary model-based indices. Institutional-group comparisons were exploratory. Results: The four subscales demonstrated high internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging from 0.884 to 0.968 and McDonald's omega coefficients from 0.885 to 0.968. Test-retest reliability was good to excellent (ICC[2,1] = 0.819-0.963), although small systematic decreases were observed for SIS and CSI. SEM values ranged from 0.228 to 0.328 and MDC95 values from 0.633 to 0.908. The four-factor model showed a good fit (χ2(318) = 463.24, CFI = 0.998, TLI = 0.998, RMSEA = 0.041, 90% CI [0.033-0.049], SRMR = 0.057), with standardized factor loadings ranging from 0.761 to 0.933. Composite reliability ranged from 0.899 to 0.976, AVE from 0.640 to 0.800, and HTMT values from 0.372 to 0.664. No substantial ceiling effects were observed at the subscale level; however, 14 of 27 items exceeded the predefined 15% criterion for item-level ceiling effects. Conclusions: The findings provide initial evidence supporting the four-factor structure and reliability of the Turkish MPOC-SP in this sample of service providers. Interpretation should focus on the four established subscales rather than an overall total score. Further studies in independent and more balanced samples are needed to examine external construct validity, measurement invariance, responsiveness, and clinically meaningful change.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical and genetic features of hemimegalencephaly in pediatric patients, and to highlight treatment outcomes in this population. METHODS: This is a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines. We used PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus for this systematic literature review as databases. Clinical data, imaging findings, EEG patterns, genetic variants, associated syndromes and treatment modalities and outcomes were reviewed, analyzed and summarized in tables. A total of 161 pediatric patients with hemimegalencephaly are described. A risk of bias and sensitivity analysis was conducted. RESULTS: Hemimegalencephaly is more frequently reported in males. The most common subtype was isolated hemimegalencephaly followed by the syndromic subtype, in particular the association with Ito's hypomelanosis. The most common seizure type was focal onset with impaired awareness. Genetic analysis showed variants in TSC1, TSC2, NPRL3, and PIK3CA, supporting mTOR pathway involvement. Drug-resistant epilepsy was present in approximately 73.2% (118/161) of the sample size. Hemispherectomy, especially functional, in our sample was more frequently reported and the current limited available literature suggests potentially comparable seizure outcomes compared to anatomical hemispherectomy in terms of seizure reduction. Our biggest limitation is the lack of long-term neurological follow-up in the existing literature. CONCLUSIONS: Hemimegalencephaly presents with a wide clinical and genetic spectrum and frequently results in drug-resistant epilepsy and developmental impairment. Although surgery may offer seizure relief, outcomes vary and the optimal approach remains individualized. Early diagnosis is essential to enable timely intervention and coordinated care. A multidisciplinary team including neurology, genetics, radiology and neurosurgery is key to optimizing outcomes. Broader studies including milder cases and long follow-up are needed to fully understand disease progression and guide management.
