This scoping review synthesised implementation strategies, barriers, facilitators, and evidence gaps regarding school-based PA promotion in under-resourced South African schools. Methods: Guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology, this review is reported following PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost (SPORTDiscus, ERIC, CINAHL, and Academic Search Complete) were searched as electronic databases, while Google Scholar (via Publish or Perish) was searched separately as a supplementary source for eligible peer-reviewed studies and the formal institutional grey literature published between January 2010 and June 2026. Eligible studies examined structured PA interventions in government-funded primary and secondary schools in under-resourced settings. Data were extracted using a standardised form, synthesised descriptively, and appraised using the appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists. Results: Twenty-four studies met the inclusion criteria. Most interventions were curriculum-integrated and delivered during school hours through Physical Education, Life Orientation, classroom activity breaks, or multicomponent programmes. Common barriers included inadequate infrastructure, limited teacher capacity, competing academic demands, constrained instructional time, and challenges in implementation fidelity. Key facilitators included curriculum alignment, teacher training and support, learner engagement, provision of low-cost resources, and culturally appropriate programme delivery. Conclusions: This review mapped the implementation strategies for school-based physical activity in under-resourced South African schools. Curriculum integration, educator support, stakeholder engagement, and low-cost, contextually appropriate approaches were reported as facilitators of programme implementation, whereas resource constraints and limited implementation capacity remained persistent barriers. Given the heterogeneity of the evidence, these findings should be interpreted as reported influences of implementation rather than as established determinants of programme success. Future research should strengthen the evidence base by evaluating interventions in secondary schools and examining implementation fidelity and long-term sustainability.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Osteoporosis is one of the major causes of fractures in individuals over the age of 50 years worldwide and an increasing public health problem. Trustworthy evidence indicates that physical exercise can reduce the risk of fall-related fractures in people with osteoporosis. Patients with suspected or confirmed osteoporosis are frequently referred to physiotherapy to address fall risk, bone health, pain, range of motion, and physical functioning. In Germany, there was no specific guidance on physiotherapeutic management for patients with osteoporosis. Thus, we aimed to identify, translate and adapt the most appropriate international physiotherapy guideline for the management of patients with osteoporosis. METHODS: The guideline adaptation process was informed by internationally accepted methodological frameworks and included six modules. We conducted a systematic review of the literature to identify relevant guideline(s) for adaptation (module 1), assessed guideline quality with AGREE-II (module 2), decided on one source guideline according to prespecified criteria (module 3), translated this guideline into German (module 4), reviewed and revised several guideline drafts by means of an expert committee, 3 physiotherapists and 2 older individuals with osteoporosis and adapted the guideline to the German healthcare context (module 5), and initiated implementation and dissemination of the final German guideline version (module 6). RESULTS: In total, we screened 873 records from databases and via other methods, and finally selected the "APTA Geriatrics' (Academy of Geriatric Physical Therapy, American Physical Therapy Association, USA) guideline published in 2022. Expert, end-user, and patient feedback (module 5) was used to make minor adaptations to the guideline (e.g., adding a glossary). We did not change any recommendation concerning physiotherapy management. A final German version of the guideline was approved by the whole research team and the developers of the source guideline and is now available open access (https://osf.io/yav94/files/s357b). CONCLUSION: The APTA Geriatrics osteoporosis guideline was translated and adapted for German-speaking countries through a structured, participatory process. The guideline can serve as the basis for evidence-based physiotherapy in German-speaking countries. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was published prospectively (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/TYXGF).

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) remains one of the most challenging conditions in neonatal critical care. Despite advances in prenatal assessment and neonatal management, substantial uncertainty persists regarding ECMO selection, mode and duration of support, and timing of diaphragmatic repair. This review summarizes the available evidence and critically examines the major unresolved questions in the management of infants with CDH requiring ECMO. Methods: A narrative review was conducted based on a literature search in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for studies published between June 2005 and June 2026. Additional relevant publications were identified through reference screening, and selected foundational studies predating the search period were included when appropriate. Prospective and retrospective studies, registry-based analyses, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant consensus statements were considered. Evidence was narratively synthesized, with particular attention to disease severity, methodological limitations, and survivor bias. Results: Available evidence highlights substantial heterogeneity in disease severity and management. Prenatal and postnatal markers aid risk stratification, but no single parameter reliably predicts ECMO requirement or defines the optimal management strategy. To date, no clear survival advantage has been demonstrated for either veno-arterial or veno-venous ECMO, although veno-arterial ECMO remains the predominant mode of support in most centers; mode selection should therefore be individualized according to cardiopulmonary physiology, patient characteristics, anatomy, and institutional expertise. Surgical timing remains particularly controversial. While repair after ECMO decannulation has been associated with favorable outcomes, recent observational analyses suggest that early repair during ECMO may be beneficial in selected patients, although the optimal timing remains uncertain. Prolonged ECMO may provide additional time for pulmonary and cardiovascular recovery, although this potential benefit must be weighed against the cumulative morbidity of prolonged support. Conclusions: Management should be individualized according to disease severity, clinical trajectory, cardiopulmonary recovery, and institutional expertise. Current evidence does not support a universal strategy for ECMO initiation, mode, surgical timing, or duration. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized definitions and adequately accounting for disease severity are needed to reduce practice variation and better define optimal management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: To prevent wildfires, electric utilities may preemptively de-energize power lines (public safety power shutoffs [PSPS]). These PSPS events may unintentionally harm health, particularly for those with pre-existing conditions like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or who rely on electricity-dependent medical equipment. Health impacts may worsen further if a wildfire occurs despite the power shutoff. To assess the effect of PSPS events, wildfire fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure, and their co-occurrence on cause-specific healthcare utilization. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We identified PSPS events in California from 2013 to 2019, categorizing magnitude based on number of people without power by zip code. We leveraged zip code-level average daily wildfire PM2.5 estimates and respiratory, COPD-specific, cardiovascular, and psychiatric emergency department visits and unscheduled hospital admissions among adults aged 20+ from the California Department of Health Care Access and Information. Using a time-stratified case-crossover design, we estimated the impact of same-day and lagged PSPS events alone, wildfire PM2.5 alone, and their co-occurrence on healthcare utilization, adjusting for daily temperature. Severe PSPS events were associated with elevated odds of same-day respiratory encounters (OR = 1.06, 95% CI: 1.02, 1.11) and lag0-3 effects were similar. These associations were stronger for COPD. Compared to no PSPS or wildfire exposure, joint PSPS and 10 μg/m3 higher wildfire PM2.5 was associated with higher odds of respiratory encounters (1.16 [95% CI: 1.10, 1.22]), with evidence of multiplicative interaction. Associations were null for cardiovascular and psychiatric encounters. Limitations include exposure misclassification, because we assigned exposure at the residential zip code level, aggregating circuit-level data and not accounting for individual behavior or the potential for PSPS events to impact wildfire PM2.5 exposure. CONCLUSIONS: PSPS events may increase risk of respiratory events requiring acute care utilization, especially when they co-occur with wildfire PM2.5.

papers.abstract_en: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive, and fatal fibrotic lung disease with a poor prognosis. While epigenetic regulation is increasingly recognized as a key driver of fibrogenesis, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unclear. In this study, we identify PR domain-containing protein 16 (PRDM16) as a critical epigenetic repressor of profibrotic gene transcription. PRDM16 expression is significantly downregulated in lungs of IPF patients, in TGF-β1-activated fibroblasts, and in bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse models. Functional analyses demonstrate that fibroblast-specific Prdm16 deletion promotes the progression of pulmonary fibrosis following BLM treatment. In contrast, overexpression of full-length PRDM16 or its truncated variant (PRDM16ΔPR-ZF1) attenuates the fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, thereby mitigating BLM-induced fibrotic phenotypes. Mechanistically, PRDM16 binds to the promoters of TGF-β target genes and recruits the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex to remove H3K27ac, resulting in silencing of profibrotic transcriptional programs. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal role for PRDM16 in maintaining epigenomic homeostasis during pulmonary fibrosis and underscore its potential as a promising therapeutic target for IPF.

papers.abstract_en: Pathological retinal neovascularization (RNV) is the leading cause of blindness. Pericytes are crucial for vascular stability and involved in RNV, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. This study investigates the role and mechanism of Snai1, a transcription factor involved in endothelial-mesenchymal transition, in regulating pericytes during RNV. By analysing single-cell RNA-seq data from oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) mice, we identified a distinct subpopulation of 'dysfunctional' pericytes with enriched pro-angiogenic pathways and upregulated Snai1. Genetic deletion of Snai1 in pericytes markedly reduced pathological neovascular tufts and vascular leakage, while improving retinal function in OIR mice, without affecting physiological angiogenesis. Mechanistically, Snai1 in pericytes directly bound to promoters and upregulated key extracellular matrix (ECM) genes, including collagens and the crosslinking enzyme Lox, which remodelled the perivascular ECM into a pro-angiogenic niche. Indeed, Snai1-overexpressing pericytes enhanced endothelial cell proliferation and tube formation only upon direct cell-cell contacts in vitro, an effect abolished by knocking down Col4a1 or inhibiting Lox activity with β-aminopropionitrile (BAPN). A feedforward loop was identified where hypoxic ECs secreted ANGPT2 and TGFβ1, stabilizing Snai1 protein in pericytes. Importantly, intravitreal injection of BAPN in OIR mice phenocopied the Snai1 ablation in effectively inhibiting RNV and promoting vascular normalization. In summary, Snai1 in pericytes is a master regulator of pathological angiogenesis in RNV, programming pericytes to construct a pro-angiogenic ECM through collagen synthesis and crosslinking, facilitating aberrant vascular growth via contact-dependent pericyte/ECM-endothelial-cell interactions. Targeting the Snai1/ECM axis represents a potential 'vascular normalization' strategy for RNV-related diseases.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDTOs) are strongly influenced by culture medium. We compared OncoPro™ (OP) Tumoroid Culture medium with conventional Wnt/R-spondin/noggin (Wnt) medium. This recently developed OP medium offers a standardized, serum-free alternative to Wnt-based formulations. METHODS: We compared OP and Wnt media across 36 PDTO lines from various malignancies (colorectal, pancreatic, breast, lung, gastric, gastroesophageal junction, biliary head and neck and unknown primary), assessing establishment success. Selected PDTO models were subjected to downstream characterization, including morphological assessment and bulk transcriptomic profiling with comparison to public single-cell RNA sequencing reference datasets (n = 11), whole-exome sequencing (WES) (n = 9), and pharmacological response profiling to a 33-drug panel (n = 3). RESULTS: Adaptation from Wnt medium to OP succeeded in 83.3% (15/18), whereas de novo establishment favored Wnt (33.3% vs 11.1%). Key oncogenic driver alterations were retained across matched organoid cultures, supporting preservation of tumor-relevant genomic features. Transcriptomic profiling confirmed preserved tumor-identity across media, while revealing different epithelial state programs: Wnt upregulated proliferation/stemness-associated genes (e.g. LGR5) and OP enriched adhesion-associated genes and inflammatory/TGF-β programs. In scRNA databases OP signatures preferentially mapped to malignant epithelial compartments in pancreatic cancer, whereas Wnt signatures were linked to non-malignant epithelium. Similarly, in colon cancer OP signature mapped predominantly to the malignant epithelial compartments. Drug (n = 33) screening in pancreatic- and colorectal cancer PDTOs (n = 3) demonstrated consistent medium-dependent shifts: Wnt-grown PDTOs were globally more sensitive in the screened subset, particularly to MAPK-axis inhibitors and apoptosis-sensitizers, while OP-grown PDTOs exhibited relative resistance. CONCLUSIONS: Culture medium composition is a key determinant of PDTO phenotype, transcriptome and drug sensitivity. Wnt medium was associated with drug-sensitive states, whereas OP medium was associated with adhesion- and inflammatory-related programs, relative resistance in the screened subset of 33 drugs and closer alignment with malignant epithelial programs in the analyzed pancreatic / colorectal cancer single-cell atlases.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Cancer metabolism-associated immune suppression remains a major barrier to durable therapeutic responses. Indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 has been pursued as a therapeutic target, but incomplete pathway suppression has limited clinical success. As the aryl hydrocarbon receptor is a ligand-activated transcription factor and downstream effector of tryptophan metabolism, we investigated how myeloid-cell aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling shapes the tumor immune microenvironment and whether its inhibition can restore antitumor immunity. METHODS: Conditional aryl hydrocarbon receptor knockout mice targeting dendritic cells or macrophages were used to evaluate the effects of genetic aryl hydrocarbon receptor ablation. Pharmacologic inhibition was assessed using DA-4505 across syngeneic lung, colorectal, and breast cancer models and an immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory humanized patient-derived xenograft model. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated alone or in combination with anti-programmed cell death protein 1 therapy, chemotherapy, or surgery. Tumor growth, survival, metastasis, and immune remodeling were analyzed by flow cytometry, multiplex immunohistochemistry, single-cell RNA sequencing, cytokine profiling, and human tumor datasets. RESULTS: Conditional aryl hydrocarbon receptor depletion in macrophages and dendritic cells enhanced innate and adaptive immune activation, increased interferon-γ-producing T cells, and strengthened antitumor immunity. In mouse tumor models, pharmacologic aryl hydrocarbon receptor blockade enhanced macrophage chemotaxis and activation programs, promoted M1-like macrophage polarization, increased interferon-γ-producing CD8⁺ T cells, and reduced regulatory T cells and polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells. These changes promoted robust T-cell activation and durable tumor control. Aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition further synergized with chemotherapy, surgery, and immune checkpoint blockade, leading to expansion of effector and memory T-cell populations and sustained antitumor responses. In a humanized lung cancer model, aryl hydrocarbon receptor blockade increased intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and cytotoxic-memory programs while reducing regulatory T-cell enrichment. In human tumor datasets, aryl hydrocarbon receptor-positive macrophages correlated with FOXP3⁺ T-cell infiltration, and higher aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition-associated T-cell signatures were associated with improved patient survival.

papers.abstract_en: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is a gestational liver disorder characterized by impaired placental vascular architecture, leading to placental dysfunction and fetal growth restriction. Our prior work demonstrated that the transcription repressor BACH1 modulates SLC25A51 expression to regulate placental injury under ICP conditions. MOTS-c, a mitochondria-originated peptide, participates in vascular homeostasis, yet its biological functions within the placental vasculature during ICP have not been fully characterized. Clinical analyses revealed significantly reduced MOTS-c protein levels in both maternal serum and placental tissues from ICP patients. In a cholic acid-induced murine model of ICP, MOTS-c administration promoted placental angiogenesis and inhibited apoptosis of placental vascular endothelial cells. These protective effects were recapitulated in vitro, where MOTS-c attenuated oxidative stress and apoptosis in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) exposed to taurocholic acid. Mechanistically, biotinylated MOTS-c pull-down coupled with mass spectrometry identified BACH1 as a direct binding partner; subsequent functional validation demonstrated that MOTS-c binds competitively to the D560 residue of BACH1, thereby displacing the deubiquitinase USP7 and promoting K33-linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of BACH1. Consequently, MOTS-c-mediated BACH1 depletion relieves transcriptional repression of SLC25A51, enhancing mitochondrial NAD+ import, biogenesis, and redox resilience. Importantly, BACH1 overexpression abolished MOTS-c-induced protection in HUVECs, confirming the functional dependency of MOTS-c on this axis. In vivo, MOTS-c treatment in CA-induced ICP mice significantly improved key offspring developmental parameters-including birth weight, placental efficiency, and neonatal survival. Collectively, these findings establish MOTS-c as a placenta-targeted endogenous regulator that ameliorates ICP-associated placental vascular pathology and adverse perinatal outcomes via modulation of the BACH1/SLC25A51 signaling axis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cyclic di-adenosine monophosphate (c-di-AMP) is an essential bacterial second messenger that regulates bacterial physiology, survival, and pathogenesis. While current models describe c-di-AMP regulation as a linear synthesis-degradation paradigm through opposing activities of diadenylate cyclases (DACs) and c-di-AMP-specific phosphodiesterases (PDEs), they fail to capture the temporal complexity of c-di-AMP signaling dynamics in coordination with discrete growth-phase transitions, metabolic state, and redox homeostasis. In Porphyromonas gingivalis, a key Gram-negative proteolytic oral pathobiont relevant to oral and systemic disease, measurable canonical c-di-AMP degradation is absent, suggesting that c-di-AMP signaling operates through an atypical regulatory architecture mediated by the atypical phosphodiesterase PDEPg. Here, we identify rhythmic-phasic c-di-AMP signaling scheme in which PDEPg plays a critical role by coordinating with bacterial growth phase, metabolism, and cell cycle progression. METHODS: We employed an integrated experimental and structural modeling framework that combined bacterial genetics, growth-phase-resolved nucleotide profiling, whole membrane fraction biochemical assays, untargeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, post-translational modification profiling, ultrastructural transmission electron microscopy, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations to dissect the pseudoenzymatic-controlled c-di-AMP regulatory module in P. gingivalis. RESULTS: This study demonstrates that growth phase synchronization in P. gingivalis requires rhythmic-phasic c-di-AMP signaling, characterized by coordinated depletion-replenishment episodes of intracellular c-di-AMP during growth-phase transitions. This regulatory network is orchestrated by two key components: the atypical HD-domain PDE homolog, PDEPg, and the conserved serine residue (Ser-226) within the DACPg SEE loop. PDEPg maintains c-di-AMP homeostasis through a noncanonical regulatory mechanism rather than through measurable PDE-mediated hydrolysis. Disruption of PDEPg profoundly remodels bacterial physiology, resulting in altered c-di-AMP dynamics, impaired peptide-dependent metabolic adaptation, disrupted ATP homeostasis, and widespread post-translational remodeling, including condition-specific phosphorylation of the c-di-AMP cyclase DACPg at the conserved Ser226 residue. Functional genetic analyses demonstrate that Ser226 is required for proper coordination of rhythmic-phasic c-di-AMP signaling and metabolic adaptation, while pantothenate-mediated rescue further supports the contribution of metabolic homeostasis to these processes. Along with structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations, these findings support a model in which noncanonical regulatory protein (pseudoenzymatic function) PDEPg coordinates rhythmic-phasic c-di-AMP signaling and physiological adaptation in P. gingivalis. CONCLUSION: Together, our findings establish a new paradigm in bacterial second messenger signaling, showing that pseudoenzymatic scaffolds coordinate rhythmic c-di-AMP dynamics that synchronize nutrient acquisition, redox metabolism, and cell-cycle progression, with broad implications for microbial physiology and pathogenesis.

papers.abstract_en: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing platform, achieving a throughput of ~5000 cells in a single experiment and significantly reducing the time and costs compared with previous techniques. With cultured mammalian cells, we demonstrated the ability of dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT to detect allele-specific epigenetics, neighboring co-accessibility, and regulatory elements within low-mappability regions. Furthermore, leveraging the haplotype-resolved data generated from dscNanoATAC, we optimized a deep-learning model to predict allele-specific three-dimensional genome structures with high resolution (10 kb). We also applied dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT in complex tissues using the mouse brain as an example, and characterized the allele-specific regulation of the imprinting gene Ube3a in neurons, obtaining insights into the mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of Prader-Willi and Angelman syndrome. With dscNanoCUT, we systematically evaluated the activity of transposon elements and revealed their potential regulatory functions in the mouse brain. Together, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT serve as a versatile and scalable long-read epigenome sequencing platform, enabling multidimensional analyses of elements ranging from chromatin accessibility to histone modifications and their interplay between chromatin structures. This platform may advance our understanding of epigenetic regulation in complex biological systems.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Influenza virus commonly infects children. Children with critical infection may develop influenza-associated encephalopathy or encephalitis, conditions rarely seen in adults and associated with high mortality. This results in growing healthcare resource consumption and family burden. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify the predictors for death in critically ill children with influenza, so as to facilitate early recognition of high-risk patients, guide clinical interventions, and reduce mortality. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of critically ill children with influenza admitted to the Children's Hospital of Soochow University between January 2018 and January 2026. L1-penalized binomial logistic regression (LASSO) was used for variable selection. Variables selected by LASSO were entered into a Firth penalized logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of mortality, based on which a nomogram was constructed to estimate mortality risk. Model discrimination was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and area under the curve (AUC). Bootstrap resampling was performed for internal validation and optimism correction. Model calibration was assessed using calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to evaluate the clinical net benefit of the model. RESULTS: A total of 113 critically ill children with influenza were included, of whom 34 died, corresponding to a mortality rate of 30.1%. LASSO regression was used for variable selection, followed by Firth penalized logistic regression to develop a mortality risk prediction model. The final model included five variables: Hgb, PLT, UREA, ALB, and confusion. A mortality risk nomogram was developed based on these five predictors and internally validated using bootstrap resampling. The ROC curve showed good discrimination of the nomogram in internal validation. The calibration curve demonstrated good agreement between the predicted probabilities and observed outcomes. DCA showed that the nomogram provided a higher net benefit across a certain range of threshold probabilities, indicating its potential clinical utility. CONCLUSIONS: Hgb, PLT, UREA, ALB, and confusion are important predictors of mortality in critically ill children with influenza. The nomogram developed based on these predictors showed good discrimination and calibration, as well as potential clinical net benefit, and may serve as an adjunctive tool for early identification of mortality risk and clinical decision-making in critically ill children with influenza.

papers.abstract_en: Building agents that perceive and act on their environment with a degree of autonomy has long been a focus of artificial intelligence research. This pursuit has become far more practical with the emergence of large language models (LLMs) capable of using natural language to integrate information, follow instructions, and perform forms of reasoning and planning across a wide range of tasks. With its multimodal data streams and orchestrated workflows spanning multiple systems, radiology is uniquely suited to benefit from agents that can adapt to context and automate complex, repetitive tasks. In radiology, LLMs and their multimodal variants have already demonstrated promising performance for individual tasks such as information extraction and report summarization. However, using LLMs in isolation underutilizes their potential to support complex, multistep workflows where decisions depend on evolving context from multiple information sources. Equipping LLMs with external tools and feedback mechanisms enables them to drive systems that exhibit a spectrum of autonomy, ranging from semiautomated workflows to more adaptive agents capable of managing complex processes. This review article examines the design of LLM-driven agentic systems, explores representative radiology applications, discusses evaluation frameworks, and outlines key challenges, including error cascades, tool-use effectiveness, and integration with health information technology infrastructure.

pico.ic: 比较TPE与非TPE的SIRPγ表达；机制上分析SIRPγ–CD47–PI3K/AKT/mTOR–PHGDH–丝氨酸代谢–H3K4me3–NFATC2轴

papers.reason: 为非肿瘤性胸腔积液免疫微环境提供机制线索，但无诊断准确性或临床终点数据，对胸外科肿瘤诊疗决策影响有限；可作为TPE鉴别诊断研究的背景参考。
papers.abstract_en: Previous studies have shown that signal regulatory protein γ (SIRPγ) is an important regulatory factor for T cell function. However, its expression and biological role in tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) remain unknown. In this study, we find that the level of SIRPγ is significantly upregulated in TPE compared to non-TPE. Furthermore, we demonstrate SIRPγ involvement in TPE pathogenesis through the induction of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, SIRPγ interacts with CD47 to activate the phosphatidylinositol 3/kinase-protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway, leading to the upregulation of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) and the enhancement of serine metabolism. Serine, in turn, facilitates S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) epigenetic modification at the NFATC2 locus. This modification, in coordination with TCR-induced calcium signaling, promotes NFATC2 activation, ultimately driving the expression of exhaustion-associated transcription factors and immunosuppressive receptors. Together, our findings identify SIRPγ as a regulator of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion in TPE and suggest its potential as a predictive biomarker for TPE diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: In the field of snapshot hyperspectral imaging, a long-pursuit objective is to develop advanced spectral information encoding elements with both high spatial resolution and large sensor size. Among various strategies, Fabry-Pérot (F-P) cavity color filter, which has both high transmittance and narrow-color filtering function, represents a promising platform. However, it is extremely challenging to make F-P color filters by using multi-layer deposition method. Here, we demonstrate that a commercial-sensor-compatible F-P cavity color filter array can be fabricated through the single-step grayscale electron beam lithography. In the proof-of-concept experiment, the silver-dielectric-silver F-P color filter array, which has spatial resolution of 5.2 µm × 5.2 µm and pixel number of 1.26 million, is successfully used to demonstrate the hyperspectral imaging function. As the diameter of the electron beam is at the level of tens of nanometers, the pixel size of the F-P cavity can be down to 3.45 µm × 3.45 µm and even further. The proposed method may have great potential in high-resolution snapshot hyperspectral imaging and related applications in optical inspection, remote sensing, biomedical imaging and so on.

papers.title_en: Sputum microplastic concentrations and their association with underweight in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: first human evidence combined with integrated network toxicology analysis.
papers.authors: Liu S, Lin D, Yang X, Zhu W, Zheng H, Yang Z, Dong R, Lin Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Clinical Nutrition, the First Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen University, School of Medicine, Xiamen Univers…
papers.results: PVC在97.5%样本中检出且中位浓度最高；PVC与总微塑料同低体重风险呈非线性正相关，全调整OR分别为4.324与4.497，敏感性分析结果相似；较高PVC与总微塑料与脂肪量降低相关（P<0.05），校正全部协变量的线性回归结果相似；探索性中介分析显示校正脂肪量后PVC与BMI的负相关不再存在；网络毒理学识别84个与COPD及体重下降共享的靶点，富集于炎症与脂肪细胞分化信号（校正P=8.4×10⁻¹⁵与2.1×10⁻¹⁰）

pico.p: 40例COPD患者痰液样本，其中12例（30.0%）为低体重；采用生物电阻抗分析评估体成分
pico.ic: 无干预。以热裂解-气相色谱-质谱法测定痰液中13种微塑料作为暴露，比较低体重组与非低体重组的微塑料浓度与体成分差异；并以PVC低分子量组分及添加剂为暴露来源开展网络毒理学分析

papers.reason: 为非肿瘤性呼吸病（COPD）的体重丢失/营养不良机制提供首个痰液微塑料人体关联数据，可作为COPD围手术期营养风险评估与呼吸道暴露因素队列设计的对照基线；与胸外科/胸部肿瘤直接诊疗决策关联有限
papers.abstract_en: Weight loss is a prevalent symptom in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Nevertheless, the role of microplastics (MPs) in this process remains poorly understood, and the underlying mechanisms are still unknown. We measured 13 MPs types by pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry in sputum from 40 COPD patients. Body composition was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis. A hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis explored the potential molecular mechanisms linking MPs exposure to alterations of body composition in COPD. Of the 40 participants, 12 (30.0%) were classified as underweight. Disease stage, nutritional status, and inflammatory indicators did not differ significantly between the two groups. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) was detected in 97.5% of samples and showed the highest median concentration. PVC and total MPs showed non-linear positive associations with the odds of underweight in COPD, with fully adjusted odds ratios of 4.324 and 4.497. Sensitivity analyses also acquired the similar results. Higher PVC and total MPs were associated with reduced fat mass (P < 0.05), and linear regression models adjusted for all covariables showed similar negative associations. Exploratory mediation analysis showed that after adjustment for fat mass, the negative association between PVC exposure and body mass index (BMI) was no longer observed, suggesting that this association may be explained by reduced fat mass. Using the low-molecular-weight constituents of PVC and its additives (vinyl chloride monomer and phthalates) as the exposure sources, hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis identified 84 targets shared with COPD and weight loss, enriched in inflammatory and adipocyte-differentiation signaling (adjusted P = 8.4 × 10⁻15 and 2.1 × 10⁻10). In conclusion, sputum MPs exposure was associated with higher odds of underweight and with lower fat mass in COPD patients. Chemicals-driven inflammatory signaling and impaired adipocyte differentiation may be involved in MPs-associated weight loss in COPD, which needs to be verified by experimental evidences.

papers.title_zh: 端粒生物学疾病：临床遗传学视角下的筛查指征与多学科管理综述
papers.title_en: Telomere biology disorders: recognizing the underrecognized through the lens of clinical genetics.
papers.authors: Lertwilaiwittaya P
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Genetics.
papers.authors_conclusion: 随着TBD表型谱扩大，儿科医生应认识日益增多的临床指征，尤其是器官移植前；筛查可考虑基因检测联合端粒长度测定（flow-FISH）；多学科管理是基石，并应转诊至有经验的大容量中心。
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，无系统检索、证据分级或原始数据；筛查建议基于专家意见而非验证性研究结果；摘要未提供筛查获益、检出率或移植结局的量化证据；将flow-FISH联合基因检测作为筛查路径属推荐性表述。
papers.reason: 为肺移植前及肺纤维化/骨髓衰竭患者的端粒生物学疾病筛查提供遗传学评估框架，影响移植前鉴别诊断与多学科转诊判断；不直接改变胸部肿瘤治疗决策。
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Telomere biology disorders (TBD) is an inherited disease that causes accelerated telomere shortening leading to bone marrow failure, lung fibrosis and/or malignancy. Growing evidence of specific management especially in transplant medicine has warranted clinicians across multiple specialties to improve the diagnostic workflow of TBD. This review aims to address the bottleneck to increase the screening uptake of TBD. RECENT FINDINGS: The availability of genetic testing has further expanded the clinical spectrum of TBD. Correspondingly, the indications to screen for TBD, especially prelung transplantation, have grown. Methods to measure chromosome-specific telomere length have emerged, meanwhile the uptake of long-read sequencing has increased. Curative treatment of TBD remains unavailable with an ongoing clinical trial in nucleoside and gene therapy. SUMMARY: As phenotypic spectrum of TBD is expanding, pediatricians should be aware of growing clinical indications, especially in prior to organ transplantation. A combination of genetic testing and telomere length measurement (flow-FISH method) should be considered for screening of TBD. Multidisciplinary approach is the cornerstone of management of TBD and referral to high-volume center with experience in TBD is warranted.

papers.abstract_en: Objective: This systematic review synthesises current evidence on the role of organisational safety culture and team-based approaches in medication safety and accuracy during paediatric care transitions. Study Setting and Design: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, focusing on studies that examined organizational or team-based approaches to medication safety and medication reconciliation at paediatric transition points, including admission, transfer, handover, and discharge. Data Sources and Analytic Sample: PubMed was systematically searched for studies published up to August 2026, identifying 108 records. After screening and applying predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, 13 studies were included in the final synthesis. Principal Findings: Across heterogeneous study designs and paediatric transition settings, medication discrepancies were frequently identified at admission, transfer, and discharge. Pharmacist involvement, structured medication reconciliation, and standardised communication processes were recurrent components of interventions associated with improved medication-information accuracy. Because the evidence was predominantly observational and quality-improvement-based, findings were interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causality. Conclusions: The available evidence suggests that team-based approaches, particularly pharmacist involvement, structured medication reconciliation, and standardised communication processes, are associated with improved medication safety and accuracy during paediatric care transitions. Organisational support and clearly defined interprofessional roles may facilitate the implementation of these approaches. Further high-quality studies are needed to clarify their effectiveness across different paediatric transition settings.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The role of small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), such as exosomes, in cell-to-cell communication is increasingly recognized. Both during development and postnatally, sEVs have been shown to mediate a multitude of essential functions in the central nervous system. While abnormal sEV biogenesis has been observed in a number of neurodevelopmental disorders, a causal link has been largely lacking. METHODS: We clinically evaluated five families in which newborns presented with a novel neonatal-onset encephalopathy. Positional mapping, exome sequencing, and trio exome sequencing were utilized to identify the underlying genetic variants. Additionally, we utilized Vps25 hypomorphic mouse mutants and performed cellular assays to evaluate ESCRT-II interaction, cellular localization, and sEV secretion and cargo capacities. RESULTS: The observed lethal encephalopathy is characterized by severe hypotonia, brain anomalies, and epilepsy. In families 1, 4, and 5 (multiplex consanguineous), we identified a novel homozygous missense variant in VPS25 as the likely candidate. Family 2 comprises a simplex case with two missense variants in trans in VPS25, one of which impacts the same residue as in the other three families. Family 3 also comprises a simplex case where we revealed a homozygous missense variant. VPS25 is an essential component of ESCRT-II, itself required for sEV biogenesis. We show that Vps25 hypomorphic mouse mutants recapitulate the developmental brain malformation observed in patients. We also show that mutant VPS25 is associated with abnormal ESCRT-II interaction, abnormal cellular localization, and highly abnormal sEVs. Specifically, mutant cells displayed engorged multivesicular bodies and were significantly defective in their capacity to secrete sEVs such as exosomes, while secreted sEVs contained altered cargo, lacking vital proteins for axon protection and maintenance. CONCLUSIONS: We report a novel neurodevelopmental disorder caused by biallelic hypomorphic variants in VPS25. The consistent impact of these variants on sEV biogenesis suggests a potential pathomechanism. While future cases will further delineate the phenotypic spectrum, these findings offer a new perspective on abnormal sEVs as drivers of human neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Safety-net hospitals (SNHs) serve as essential public health hubs, providing direct clinical care and critical social services to vulnerable populations, yet gaps persist in their ability to reliably deliver these essential services during disasters. OBJECTIVE: To identify common challenges faced by SNHs and actionable approaches described by participants to strengthen future emergency response capacity at these critical institutions. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: For this qualitative study, from April through November 2025, key informant interviews were conducted with individuals across SNHs selected to represent a spectrum of SNH types. Thematic analysis of site-level case studies was used to identify cross-cutting and context-specific patterns across 5 domains: load balancing, staffing needs, supply chain, crisis standards of care (CSC), and health care coalitions (HCCs). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Stakeholder perspectives of pandemic preparedness, response, and recovery were evaluated to understand strategies to mitigate future health care disasters. RESULTS: Analysis of interviews with 69 individuals from 10 SNH sites identified systemic vulnerabilities across all 5 domains in SNHs. SNHs rarely succeeded in transferring critically ill patients without extensive staff time spent setting up the transfer. SNHs often experienced severe workforce disruptions from limited staff pools and nurse attrition, leaving them dependent on temporary staff at higher costs. Just-in-time personal protective equipment procurement and constricted manufacturing supply chains created supply crises. Few SNHs implemented full CSC, but many worked to find creative solutions to prevent more extensive changes in care standards. Opinions on written CSC were mixed, with some preferring structured frameworks and others preferring flexibility. Experiences with HCCs varied widely, with SNHs embedded in well-resourced HCCs reporting better coordination and support. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this qualitative study of SNH preparedness and response, findings indicated that SNHs faced challenges with load balancing, supply chain, staffing, CSC, and HCCs. To address such challenges in the future, SNHs, regional coalitions, and the federal government should implement sustainable changes that can be rapidly brought to bear in an emergency. Potential solutions may have outsized benefit for SNHs; however, such solutions must be designed to be accessible to SNHs and feasible in these settings.

papers.abstract_en: Detecting changes in gene coordination patterns between biological conditions and identifying the cell populations in which these changes occur are key challenges in single-cell analysis. Existing approaches often compare gene coexpression between predefined cell clusters or rely on aligning cells across conditions. These strategies can be suboptimal when changes occur within small subpopulations or when batch effects obscure the underlying biological signal. To address these challenges, we introduce DiCoLo, a framework that identifies genes exhibiting differential colocalization, defined as changes in coordinated expression within localized cell neighborhoods - subsets of highly similar cells in the transcriptomic space. Importantly, DiCoLo does not rely on cell clustering or cross-condition alignment. For each condition, DiCoLo constructs a gene graph using Optimal Transport distances that reflect gene colocalization patterns across the cell manifold. Then, it identifies differential gene programs by detecting changes in connectivity patterns between the gene graphs. We show that DiCoLo robustly identifies differential gene colocalization even under weak signals or complex batch effects, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmark datasets. When applied to mouse hair follicle development data, DiCoLo reveals coordinated gene programs and emerging cell populations driven by perturbations in morphogen signaling that underlie dermal condensate differentiation. Overall, these results establish DiCoLo as a powerful framework for uncovering localized differential transcriptional coordinated patterns in single-cell data.

papers.abstract_en: Compound air-soil heatwaves-periods in which extreme air and soil temperatures co-occur-pose a growing threat to terrestrial ecosystems, yet their occurrence and impacts remain poorly understood. Here, we show that compound air-soil heatwaves have become more frequent (0.59 ± 0.07 events decade-1), longer-lasting (0.18 ± 0.04 days decade-1) and more intense (4.02 ± 0.77°C × days decade-1) since 1979. These rates of change far exceed those for independent air and soil heatwaves and are driving increasingly widespread reductions in vegetation productivity. On average, ∼98.5 million km2 of land experienced gross primary productivity (GPP) losses during compound air-soil heatwaves. Globally, annual GPP losses have risen by 0.61 gC m-2 year⁻1 decade⁻1, which is a 30.5- and 12.2-fold increase relative to those of independent air and soil heatwaves, respectively. Climate model projections indicate that compound air-soil heatwaves will continue to intensify and expand spatially under future warming, particularly under the high-emission scenario. Given pronounced GPP reductions during compound heatwaves, their projected intensification is likely to pose an increasing threat to terrestrial ecosystem productivity. Our findings highlight the escalating ecological impacts of compound heatwaves and underscore the urgent need for adaptation and preparedness strategies to address this compound hazard in a warming world.

papers.abstract_en: Autosomal-dominant hyper-IgE syndrome (HIES) is characterized by chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, recurrent sinopulmonary complications, noninflammatory atopic dermatitis, high amounts of serum IgE, and nonimmunological manifestations affecting the musculoskeletal and vascular systems. Most cases are caused by heterozygous loss-of-function, dominant-negative (LOF/DN) variants that affect the DNA binding, SH2, or transactivation domains of STAT3. Here, we report a patient with a unique STAT3 allele affecting the STAT3 N-terminal domain (R31Q), who presented with disseminated invasive aspergillosis affecting the brain and lung, bronchiectasis, and high serum IgE but lacked nonimmune disease manifestations. Biochemical analyses in cell lines demonstrated that R31Q reduced the abundance and transcriptional activity of STAT3 and caused it to exhibit negative dominance on wild-type (WT) STAT3. This was due to preferential STAT3R31Q dimerization with STAT3WT, sequestration of STAT3WT:STAT3R31Q dimers in the cytosol, and a reduction in STAT3 nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity. Lymphocytes from the patient exhibited some typical defects observed in canonical STAT3LOF/DN HIES, such as reduced memory B cells, MAIT cells, and TH17 cytokines. However, naïve B cells from this patient had only a partial impairment in immunoglobulin secretion induced by interleukin-21 (IL-21) in vitro, and the patient had normal numbers of TH2 cells and circulating TFH cells. Our findings reveal that the N-terminal domain regulates STAT3 dimer formation and function and provide a previously unknown biochemical mechanism of disease pathogenesis in STAT3LOF/DN HIES.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations between sleep disturbances, anxiety, and OHRQoL in children during the mixed dentition period. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 100 children aged 7-12 years. Sleep disturbances were assessed using the Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC), anxiety using the Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders (SCARED) and OHRQoL using the Child Oral Health Impact Profile - Short Form (COHIP-SF-19). Spearman's correlation and multivariable regression analyses were performed. RESULTS: Sleep disturbances were identified in 42% of the participants. SDSC scores were positively correlated with anxiety (rho = 0.43) and OHRQoL (rho = 0.34). In multivariable analysis, anxiety showed independent association with sleep disturbance severity. CONCLUSION: Sleep disturbances in children are closely associated with anxiety and perceived oral health impacts highlighting the importance of early identification and multidiciplinary management.

papers.title_zh: 儿童骨骼与牙齿剩余生长评估：Cameriere定量法的横断面研究显示两种成熟指标一致性有限
papers.title_en: Assessment of Residual Skeletal and Dental Growth in Children: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Quantitative Cameriere Methods.
papers.authors: Grimaldi R, Frenna B, Perrotta G, Fiandaca S, Satta C, Cubeddu S, Catalini L, Cameriere R et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Surgical Sciences, Orthodontics School, University of Cagliari, 09124 Cagliari, Italy.
papers.results: 测量可重复性ICC 0.93–1.00；剩余骨骼生长时间（T_skeletal）与剩余牙齿生长时间（T_dental）呈弱正相关（Spearman ρ = 0.18，p = 0.09）；骨骼与牙齿成熟度差异超过预设1年阈值（|ΔT| > 1年）者占48.0%；骨骼发育占优者46.9%，牙齿发育占优者仅1.0%；女性剩余骨骼与牙齿生长均显著大于男性（p < 0.001）
papers.authors_conclusion: 7–11岁儿童骨骼与牙齿成熟度一致性有限，支持两者遵循部分独立的生物学通路这一概念；整合定量骨骼与牙齿评估或可改善个体生长潜能的评价，并支持更个性化的正畸治疗计划
papers.ai_note: 主要相关性结果ρ=0.18且p=0.09未达统计学显著，作者据此得出“部分独立通路”属阴性结果的解读性外推；结论段“改善生长潜能评价、支持个性化正畸计划”缺乏任何治疗决策或纵向结局数据支撑。性别差异仅报p<0.001，未给效应量与置信区间。1年阈值为预设但未在摘要中说明依据。横断面设计无法验证两指标随时间变化的真实独立性；单一人群（高加索）、单中心，外推受限。与胸科/胸部肿瘤业务无实质关联。

pico.p: 98名高加索儿童（男50例、女48例），年龄7.0–11.9岁
pico.ic: 以侧位头影测量第四颈椎比值（C4-Vba）评估骨骼剩余生长、全景片开口根尖法评估牙齿剩余生长（AgEstimation Project v1.0软件），无对照组；行相关性分析与Bland-Altman一致性分析

papers.reason: 研究对象为儿童颅面骨骼与牙齿生长发育，与胸外科及胸部肿瘤临床判断无交集；仅在方法学层面可作为参考：影像定量指标的前处理软件、ICC可重复性报告与Bland-Altman一致性分析范式，可供胸部影像组学/定量测量类研究借鉴。
papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Accurate assessment of biological maturation is essential in pediatric dentistry and orthodontics for optimizing treatment timing. Quantitative methods proposed by Cameriere allow continuous estimation of residual skeletal and dental growth; however, the degree of agreement between these maturation processes remains unclear. This study aimed to assess residual skeletal and dental growth in children using quantitative Cameriere methods and to evaluate the agreement between these two maturation indicators. Methods: This cross-sectional observational study included 98 Caucasian subjects (50 males and 48 females) aged 7.0-11.9 years. Residual skeletal growth was assessed on lateral cephalometric radiographs using the fourth cervical vertebra ratio (C4-Vba), while residual dental growth was evaluated on panoramic radiographs using the open apices method. Measurements were performed using the AgEstimation Project software v1.0. Intra- and inter-observer reproducibility were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Correlation analysis and Bland-Altman analysis were performed to evaluate the association and agreement between skeletal and dental maturation. Results: Excellent reproducibility was observed for all measurements, with ICC values ranging from 0.93 to 1.00. Residual skeletal growth time (T_skeletal) and residual dental growth time (T_dental) showed a weak positive association (Spearman ρ = 0.18, p = 0.09). Discrepancies exceeding the predefined 1-year threshold between skeletal and dental maturation (|ΔT| > 1 year) were observed in 48.0% of subjects. Skeletal predominance was identified in 46.9% of cases, whereas dental predominance was observed in only 1.0%. Females showed significantly greater residual skeletal and dental growth compared with males (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Skeletal and dental maturation showed limited agreement in children aged 7-11 years, supporting the concept that these processes follow partially independent biological pathways. The integration of quantitative skeletal and dental assessments may improve the evaluation of individual growth potential and support more personalized orthodontic treatment planning.

papers.title_zh: IQEQS 模型用于多院区扩张期的医院后勤设施管理：维修流程标准化、数字化闭环与安全治理的单中心前后对比
papers.title_en: The IQEQS Model for Lean Hospital Facility Management: Standardization, Closed-Loop Repair, and Safety Governance During Multicampus Growth.
papers.authors: Ying L, Haoran L, Hongjun F, Lu S, Yueqiang S, Zhengang Z, Yin W, Lu W et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Hospital Facility-Management Professional, Peking University First Hospital, Beijing, China.
papers.results: 中心院区维修工单量由 2024 年约 31,200 单增至 2025 年 33,600 单；维修配件与五金支出下降 20.3%，由 166.32 万元人民币降至 132.48 万元人民币；平均维修时间下降 8.6%；每周误报数由 3–5 次降至少于 2 次；报警确认时间由 1–3 分钟降至约 10 秒；全院临床业务量增速快于部分设施相关运营支出，但院区层面模式异质

papers.ai_note: 无平行对照、无统计学检验与置信区间，属实施前后描述性比较，无法排除季节、业务量增长、采购价格与核算口径变化等混杂；工单量上升 7.7% 与支出下降 20.3% 并存，需警惕统计口径或项目归集差异；误报数采用区间（3–5 次/周）而非精确计数，基线不可核；主要报告指标为运营财务与工单类过程指标，缺乏临床结局或安全事件硬终点，作者亦自认全院费用趋势不可归因，结论以“提供框架”这一弱表述呈现，但摘要行文仍以改善数值为主导。

pico.p: 北京大学第一医院（中心院区及全院），多院区扩张期；未涉及患者人群，无样本量
pico.ic: 干预：IQEQS（Intelligence、Quantity、Effectiveness、Quality、Safeguard）模型，含维修与物资流程标准化、数字化闭环、运营记录与医院资源规划（HRP）系统对接、框架延伸至安防与消防安全治理；对照：分阶段实施前的既往后勤管理状态（自身前后比较，无平行对照）

papers.reason: 与胸部肿瘤临床决策无直接关联，属医院后勤与运营数字化治理的实施案例；其价值在于为围手术期/日间化疗等流程的数字化闭环改造（工单—物资—财务—安全联动）提供可借鉴的指标框架与对照基线思路，并提示此类前后对比设计在归因上的固有局限。
papers.abstract_en: During multicampus expansion, Peking University First Hospital faced fragmented repair and materials-management processes, weak links between operational and financial data, and increasing demands for cost stewardship and safety governance. The hospital implemented the IQEQS (Intelligence, Quantity, Effectiveness, Quality, and Safeguard) model by standardizing repair and materials-management processes, establishing a digital closed loop, linking operational records with the hospital resource planning system, and extending the framework to security and fire safety governance. At the central campus, the number of repair work orders increased from approximately 31,200 in 2024 to 33,600 in 2025, while expenditure on repair parts and hardware decreased by 20.3%, from 1.6632 million renminbi (RMB) to RMB1.3248 million. The average repair time decreased by 8.6%. The number of false alarms per week decreased from 3-5 to fewer than 2, and alarm-confirmation time decreased from 1-3 minutes to approximately 10 seconds. Hospital-wide clinical activity increased faster than selected facility-related operating expenditure, but campus-level patterns were heterogeneous. The IQEQS model provides a practical framework for standardizing repair processes, linking operational and financial data, and strengthening safety governance. Intervention-proximal improvements were observed during phased implementation; however, hospital-wide expenditure trends cannot be attributed to the IQEQS model alone.

papers.title_en: Prognostic Communication at the Limits of Viability: A Retrospective Mixed-Methods Study.
papers.authors: Friedman E, Bertele M, Slutzky NA, Herzlich J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Neonatology, Dana-Dwek Children's Hospital, Tel Aviv Medical Center, Tel Aviv 6423906, Israel.
papers.results: 14名家长参与；识别出5个相互关联主题；10名存活婴儿的家长中有5名报告早期谈话以风险为主导、对不确定性和潜在积极轨迹讨论不足；7名出院时被归类为严重新生儿疾病的婴儿中，5名被其家长评为访谈时总体健康状况良好或极好；4名丧亲家长中3名描述了意义建构与个人转变；创伤后成长未正式评估
papers.authors_conclusion: 部分家长认为以风险为主导的预后沟通塑造了其后续体验的某些方面；在透明呈现风险的同时明确承认不确定性与发育变异性，可能更好地支持家庭度过新生儿期之后

papers.abstract_en: Background: Although advances in neonatal care over the last two decades have improved survival among extremely preterm infants, neurodevelopmental disabilities remain a major concern with substantial uncertainty regarding long-term outcomes. Prognostic counselling at the limit of viability is therefore challenging, with divergent perspectives between parents and clinicians further contributing to this challenge. Objective: To examine parents' retrospective interpretations of prognostic communication in the context of extreme prematurity and their experiences of long-term adaptation and perceived child well-being. Methods: This retrospective mixed-methods study interviewed parents of infants born at 23-25 weeks' gestation, 5-10 years after discharge or death. Qualitative data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic approach and integrated with neonatal clinical data collected from medical records. Results: Fourteen parents participated. Five interrelated themes were identified: forged by adversity, enduring emotional toll, vertigo and decisional overload, limits of prognostic communication and long-term impact. Five of ten parents of surviving infants reported that early discussions were predominantly risk-focused and insufficiently addressed uncertainty or potential positive trajectories. Among seven infants classified as having severe neonatal morbidity at discharge, five were rated by their parents as having good or excellent current overall well-being at the time of interview. Among bereaved parents, three of four described meaning-making and personal transformation reflected in the theme 'Forged by adversity'; these experiences may be consistent with aspects of post-traumatic growth, although post-traumatic growth was not formally assessed. Conclusions: Some parents perceived risk-focused prognostic communication as shaping aspects of their subsequent experience. Counselling that transparently presents risks while explicitly acknowledging uncertainty and developmental variability may better support families beyond the neonatal period.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary vein stenosis (PVS) is a rare but life-threatening disease affecting young children, characterized by progressive narrowing of the pulmonary veins. Multimodal treatment, including surgical and catheter-based interventions combined with medical therapy, can improve survival; however, disease recurrence and progression are common. Currently, there is no therapy able to reverse existing disease, leaving lung transplantation the only option for patients with advanced, treatment-resistant disease. Studies using animal models and human tissue have identified several mechanisms that contribute to PVS, including mechanosensitive signaling and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition. In parallel, advances in cardiac imaging and hemodynamic profiling of individual pulmonary veins have improved risk stratification and provided opportunities to modify treatment strategies. Despite these advances, the development of disease-modifying therapies able to improve patient outcomes will require a more thorough understanding of the underlying pathophysiology. In this review, we examine the histological features of PVS and summarize the cellular contributions and signaling pathways implicated in disease development. We will also explore the potential of integrating patient- and lesion-specific phenotypes and molecular signatures to guide individual treatment strategies, as well as the current limitations and future directions of PVS research.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: A mallet-like posture in a child or adolescent can represent a closed tendon or dorsal avulsion injury, but it may instead signal a physeal or juxtaphyseal distal-phalanx fracture that communicates with the nail unit. We mapped the diagnostic and management evidence and developed a proposed phenotype-based assessment framework whose clinical performance has not been validated. METHODS: Following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), PubMed and OpenAlex were searched without date restrictions through 22 July 2026, with citation chasing and organizational-website searching. Two human reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and assessed potentially eligible reports; disagreements were resolved by discussion and consensus. One reviewer charted standardized data and a second verified the displayed fields. RESULTS: The historical search yielded 219 database occurrences and 161 unique records. After 84 title/abstract exclusions, 77 database reports were assessed; 26 were excluded and 51 included. Other methods contributed nine sources, yielding 60 included sources. Evidence was predominantly retrospective and heterogeneous. Immobilization duration was not comprehensively synthesized in this review; therefore, no universal duration is proposed. No diagnostic-accuracy study, formal certainty grade, universally supported antibiotic regimen, or validated fixation threshold was identified. CONCLUSIONS: Nail-unit findings can raise concern for communication and support urgent specialist assessment under local protocols. Closed, congruent, stable mallet injuries may be considered for splinting after a complete nail-unit examination. The framework is proposed and unvalidated.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by persistent inflammation and dysregulated T cell responses. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have immunomodulatory properties, but their clinical efficacy remains variable. We investigated whether metabolic reprogramming of umbilical cord-derived MSCs (UC-MSCs) toward glycolysis enhances their immunoregulatory function and the underlying mechanisms. METHODS: UC-MSCs were reprogrammed toward glycolysis by pharmacologic inhibition of oxidative phosphorylation using oligomycin. Their immunomodulatory capacity was assessed in coculture with activated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 21 RA patients under direct-contact and conditioned-medium conditions. T cell proliferation, phenotype, and cell cycle were analyzed by flow cytometry. Anti-inflammatory effects were evaluated in a delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) murine model, and the contribution of the UC-MSC secretome and its protein fraction was investigated. RESULTS: Glycolysis-reprogrammed UC-MSCs exhibited enhanced immunosuppressive activity compared with unmodified UC-MSCs, suppressing proinflammatory T cell responses, promoting Treg expansion, and preserving CD4+CD45RA+ naïve T cells. These effects were associated with T cell cycle arrest in G0. Conditioned-medium experiments showed that these effects were largely mediated by the MSC secretome, increasing Treg frequency from 16.5% to 30.2% and enriching the CD4+CD45RA+ naïve T-cell compartment from 9.7% to 29.1%, with the protein fraction accounting for most of this immunomodulatory activity. In vivo, the >3 kDa protein-enriched fraction attenuated DTH-associated inflammation and promoted an anti-inflammatory immune response. CONCLUSION: Metabolic reprogramming of UC-MSCs toward glycolysis enhances their immunomodulatory capacity through secretome-dependent mechanisms, primarily mediated by proteins within the >3 kDa fraction, supporting metabolism-based and cell-free strategies for MSC-based therapy in RA.

papers.abstract_en: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is an unpredictable condition that is commonly encountered in neonatal intensive care units. NEC considered one of the most severe gastrointestinal diseases affecting preterm infants and is often fatal. In this study, we performed a genomic analysis in which 32 Clostridium butyricum strains were compared; 25 strains were isolated from patients with asymptomatic stool carriage and seven were isolated from patients diagnosed with NEC. Phylogenetic analysis revealed two clusters. Cluster 1 was associated with asymptomatic carriers, whereas cluster 2 was associated mainly with NEC patients and was composed of three genetically distinct subclusters. Through genomic analyses, we identified six plasmids, each of which varied in size and gene number. The 21 strains belonging to cluster 1 harboured two specific plasmids, one small conserved plasmid and one large megaplasmid. The strains in subcluster 2.1 harboured two specific plasmids, and the strains in subclusters 2.2 and 2.3 harboured one of two specific plasmids. Interestingly, plasmid profiling revealed specific patterns and the largest C. butyricum plasmid reported to date. The observed differences in plasmids between the two clusters were associated with NEC status and may contribute to the virulence potential that leads to the occurrence of this disease.

papers.abstract_en: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing. Using an evidence-based approach, a standardised guideline for referral for cancer genetics evaluation of childhood cancer survivors at high risk of having a CPS was developed and incorporated into the Children's Oncology Group Long-Term Follow-Up Guidelines for Survivors of Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Cancers. This Policy Review details the importance, development, and anticipated impact of this new guideline. Raising awareness of this guideline is crucial to enhancing the integration of genetics into survivorship care and improving health outcomes for childhood cancer survivors with CPS.

papers.authors_conclusion: 部分成人研究近来对标准预立医疗照护计划方法的有效性提出质疑，而针对AYA癌症人群的新近研究则显示多方面获益；鉴于ACP技术与AYA人群本身均缺乏研究，且数字技术时代沟通偏好持续演变，儿科肿瘤临床医生可能对当前最佳实践并不确定，因此本文综述AYA癌症ACP的最新证据，重点描述实用床旁工具及与专科缓和医疗团队协作的优势。
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，未报告检索数据库、时间范围、纳排标准与文献筛流程，无法评估选择偏倚与证据等级；摘要提及“成人研究质疑标准ACP有效性”与“AYA研究显示多方面获益”这一潜在矛盾，但未给出任何效应量或研究数量，属定性叙述而非证据合成；结论性表述（如协作可“促进最佳结局”）缺乏量化支撑；本文与胸部肿瘤及胸外科决策无直接关联，归入advanced仅为疾病阶段语境下的最接近归类。

papers.abstract_en: Adolescents and young adults (AYAs) diagnosed with cancer experience unique psychosocial distress and worse clinical outcomes compared to their younger and older peers. Additionally, the developmental emergence of identity and independence for AYAs-and the effects of oncology therapy on these milestones-adds complexity to communication and medical decision-making among patients and families. Given these circumstances, AYAs require thoughtful approaches for advance care planning (ACP). In many cases, specialty palliative care (SPC) teams can provide an extra layer of support to both patients and families as well as primary oncology teams in navigating ACP and ensuring goal-concordant care. While some adult studies have recently questioned the effectiveness of standard ACP methods, other new investigations specifically in the AYA cancer population have demonstrated multifaceted benefits. With the understudied nature of both ACP techniques and the AYA population in general and the constant evolution of communication preferences in the digital technology era, pediatric oncology clinicians may be unsure of current best practices for how to guide their older patients during conversations about their illness. We aim to review the most recent evidence regarding ACP for AYAs with cancer, with an emphasis on describing practical bedside tools and the advantages of collaborating with SPC teams to promote optimal outcomes.

papers.authors: Akçay S, Dinç Yavaş A, Poyrazoğlu HG, Cesar NS, Kaplan İN, Uğur CC

papers.results: 母亲焦虑与游戏表现负相关（ρ = -0.564, p < 0.001）、与游戏性负相关（ρ = -0.492, p < 0.001）、与low registration原始分正相关（ρ = 0.474, p < 0.001）、与sensation-seeking原始分正相关（ρ = 0.343, p = 0.008）；多变量模型R2 = 0.516，游戏表现（β = -0.411, p = 0.002）与共病ADHD（β = 0.274, p = 0.027；仅10例ADHD儿童）与母亲焦虑独立相关；母亲教育、就业与学校类型无独立关联

papers.abstract_en: Background: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often show atypical sensory processing and reduced play participation, and their mothers frequently report elevated anxiety. However, maternal anxiety symptoms, sensory processing, and children's play performance and playfulness have rarely been examined together, and the factors independently associated with maternal anxiety symptoms have not yet been clarified. Objective: This study examined relationships between maternal anxiety symptoms and children's sensory processing, play performance, and playfulness in children with ASD aged 4-6 years, and identified factors independently associated with maternal anxiety symptoms. Method: In this cross-sectional study, 58 mother-child dyads were recruited from a special education center in Istanbul, Türkiye. Maternal anxiety was assessed with the Beck Anxiety Inventory, sensory processing with the Dunn Sensory Profile, and play with the Revised Knox Preschool Play Scale and Test of Playfulness. Results: Maternal anxiety was negatively correlated with play performance (ρ = -0.564, p < 0.001) and playfulness (ρ = -0.492, p < 0.001), and positively correlated with low registration and sensation-seeking raw scores (ρ = 0.474, p < 0.001 and ρ = 0.343, p = 0.008, respectively; higher raw scores indicate more typical, less atypical processing). Children with comorbid ADHD had mothers with higher anxiety and lower play scores. In a multivariable model (R2 = 0.516), play performance (β = -0.411, p = 0.002) and, preliminarily, comorbid ADHD (β = 0.274, p = 0.027; only 10 children with ADHD) were independently associated with maternal anxiety; maternal education, employment, and school type were not. Conclusions: In young children with ASD, maternal anxiety symptoms were most strongly associated with the child's play performance, while a preliminary association with co-occurring ADHD requires confirmation in larger samples; these findings support considering maternal wellbeing in family-centered occupational therapy assessment.

papers.abstract_en: AbstractMorning Report is a time-honored tradition where physicians-in-training present cases to their colleagues and clinical experts to collaboratively examine an interesting patient presentation. The Morning Report section seeks to carry on this tradition by presenting a patient's chief concern and story, inviting the reader to develop a differential diagnosis and discover the diagnosis alongside the authors of the case. This report examines the story of a 58-year-old woman who sought evaluation for fever, abdominal pain, and nonproductive cough. Using targeted questions, physical examination, and testing, an illness script for the presentation emerges. As the clinical course progresses, the differential is refined until a final diagnosis is made.

papers.abstract_en: Humans are exposed daily to mixtures of chemicals from multiple sources and routes, including diet and the environment. These combined exposures may cause adverse health effects that are not adequately captured by conventional substance-by-substance risk assessment, due to the inherent complexity of assessing combined risks. To address this gap, the Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals (PARC) Real-life Mixtures project aims to consolidate scientific knowledge regarding mixture risk assessment (MRA). In synergy with ongoing activities of European agencies and other initiatives, this project developed a strategy to perform MRA using human biomonitoring (HBM) data. The approach consists of five steps: (1) prioritisation of chemical mixtures of interest for human health to guide case-study selection; (2) collection and organisation of the data required for MRA, including exposure, hazard, and toxicokinetic information; (3) development of methods for conducting MRA using HBM data; (4) implementation of these methods within the Monte Carlo Risk Assessment (MCRA) toolbox; and (5) application of the strategy to prioritised case studies. Three chemical families and four associated adverse health outcomes were selected based on the results of PARC priority process: pesticides affecting the nervous system, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) affecting the immune system, and metal(loid)s affecting kidney function and neurodevelopment. HBM data from studies conducted across Europe and Greenland were harmonised using the HBM data toolkit. Hazard and toxicokinetic data were compiled to derive internal toxicological values suitable for MRA. The MRA was then performed in a harmonised way for each case study using the MCRA toolbox. The strategy developed within the PARC Real-life Mixtures project provides a proof-of-concept for conducting HBM-based MRA and for informing policymakers. Future research will focus on reducing uncertainties and expanding the approach to additional chemicals with common health endpoints and co-exposure.

papers.title_zh: 爱尔兰多校区理工大学学生横断面调查：大学归属感为幸福感最强预测因子，44.1%学生幸福感偏低、55.4%孤独感升高
papers.title_en: The conditions for connection-belonging as a health-promoting resource within higher education settings in Ireland.
papers.authors: McGrath A, Doyle M, O'Brien N
papers.affiliation_highlight: Centre for Health Behaviour Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, South East Technological University (Waterford Campus)…
papers.results: 低心理健康幸福感者占44.1%；孤独感升高者占55.4%；幸福感与大学归属感正相关（r = .51）、与社会连接感正相关（r = .45）、与孤独感负相关（r = -.41）（均P < .001）；大学归属感为幸福感最强预测因子（β = .325，P < .001），在人口学与情境因素之外解释额外变异；观察到孤独感经大学归属感影响幸福感的显著间接关联；女性、性少数、一年级学生及通勤影响参与的学生在部分指标上结果更差。
papers.authors_conclusion: 研究结果凸显归属感在学生幸福感中的核心作用，提示归属感可视为高等教育环境中重要的健康促进资源；与 Healthy Campus 及 Health Promoting University 路径一致，大学应超越个体化幸福感干预，营造社会、组织与环境条件，为日益多元的学生群体促进公平的连接、参与与归属。
papers.ai_note: ①横断面设计无法确立时序，作者以中介分析表述“孤独感→归属感→幸福感”的间接通路，因果方向不可检验，反向或双向关系同样相容；②摘要仅称“显著间接关联”，未给出间接效应量、BootstraP CI或中介比例，中介结论证据强度不明；③44.1%“低幸福感”与55.4%“孤独感升高”均依赖未在摘要中说明的界值，跨研究可比性受限；④亚组差异（女性、性少数、一年级、通勤受影响）表述为“部分指标更差”，未报告效应量与多重比较校正，存在亚组挖掘风险；⑤结论从单一院校横断面相关性直接推及全校/全国层面的组织与环境政策改造，外推跨度较大；⑥与胸部肿瘤临床诊疗无任何交集。

pico.ic: 无干预对照；横断面测量心理健康幸福感（WEMWBS）、大学归属感、孤独感（UCLA-3）、社会连接感及人口学/情境变量

papers.abstract_en: Student wellbeing has become an increasing concern within higher education, with evidence highlighting the importance of social connection and belonging for mental health. Guided by settings-based health promotion principles, this study examined relationships between wellbeing, belonging, loneliness, and social connectedness among university students. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among students attending a multi-campus technological university in Ireland (N = 409). Participants completed validated measures of mental wellbeing (Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale), university belonging, loneliness (UCLA-3), and social connectedness, alongside demographic, and contextual questions. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlations, group comparisons, hierarchical regression, and mediation analysis. Low mental wellbeing was reported by 44.1% of students, while 55.4% experienced elevated loneliness. Mental wellbeing was positively associated with university belonging (r = .51) and social connectedness (r = .45) and negatively associated with loneliness (r = -.41) (all P < .001). University belonging emerged as the strongest predictor of wellbeing (β = .325, P < .001), explaining variance beyond demographic and contextual factors. A significant indirect association between loneliness and wellbeing through university belonging was also observed. Female, sexual minority, first-year students, and students whose commuting affected participation reported poorer outcomes on selected measures. Findings highlight the central role of belonging in student wellbeing and suggest that belonging functions as an important health-promoting resource within higher education. Consistent with Healthy Campus and Health Promoting University approaches, universities should move beyond individualized wellbeing interventions and create social, organizational, and environmental conditions that foster equitable connection, participation, and belonging for increasingly diverse student populations.
