papers.title_zh: 手法整骨治疗对青少年功能性下肢姿势偏差者足底压力分布的影响：一项单组前后对照预试验
papers.title_en: Effects of Osteopathic Manual Therapy on Plantar Pressure Distribution in Adolescents with Functional Lower Limb Postural Deviations: A Pilot Study.
papers.authors: Cîtea MA, Lucaci P, Neculăeș M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Faculty of Physical Education and Sports, "Alexandru Ioan Cuza" University of Iași, 3 Toma Cozma Street, 700554 Iasi, Ro…
papers.results: 内外侧足底负荷分布无显著变化。前足负荷由 32.65 ± 12.58% 升至 39.67 ± 9.29%，后足负荷相应由 67.35 ± 12.58% 降至 60.34 ± 9.29%（Holm 校正 p = 0.006；Cohen's dz = 0.842）。右侧动态足弓指数由 13.73 ± 8.86% 升至 17.37 ± 7.44%（Holm 校正 p = 0.025；dz = 0.701）。多重检验校正后，其余足弓指数变化均无统计学意义。
papers.authors_conclusion: 在该预试验队列中，OMT 后前足-后足足底负荷分布及右侧动态足弓指数出现可测量的变化；这些发现应被解释为足底负荷的初步功能性变化，而非结构矫正或明确疗效的证据。仍需更大样本的对照研究来确定这些变化是否可特异归因于 OMT。
papers.ai_note: 单臂前后对照、无对照或安慰对照组，且为自身前后比较，无法排除自然生长发育、重复测量回归均值、季节/活动量变化及期望效应；青春期 3 个月内的骨骼肌肉发育本身即可改变足底压力分布。样本量仅 20 例，未报告对多重比较的整体家族控制策略细节，也未报告失访与依从性。主要结果中内外侧分布为阴性，而前足-后足分布与单侧（右侧）足弓指数被突出呈现，存在从多个测量指标中选取阳性结果强调的倾向；右侧足弓指数变化而其他足弓指数不显著，部位偏侧性缺乏机制解释。结论措辞谨慎，但标题与摘要仍以“effects”表述因果倾向。此外该文与胸部肿瘤/胸科临床毫无关联，属明显超出本评审专业范围者。

pico.p: 20 名 14–16 岁、存在功能性姿势偏差但无结构畸形的青少年（女 8 例，男 12 例）
pico.ic: 干预：10 次个体化手法整骨治疗（OMT，以软组织与肌肉能量技术为主），历时 3 个月；对照：无对照组（治疗前后自身比较）

papers.reason: 研究对象为青少年功能性下肢姿势偏差与足底压力分布，干预为手法整骨治疗，与胸外科、胸部肿瘤及呼吸系统疾病的临床决策和科研设计均无交集；仅在“临床研究设计”层面可作为一个单臂前后对照预试验的方法学示例（如多重比较校正、效应量报告的写法）被间接参考，不构成任何胸科判断依据。
papers.abstract_en: (1) Background: Adolescence is a period of rapid musculoskeletal development during which functional postural deviations may occur without structural deformity. This pilot study investigated changes in the plantar pressure distribution following osteopathic manual therapy (OMT) in adolescents with functional postural deviations. (2) Materials and Methods: Twenty adolescents aged 14-16 years (8 females and 12 males) participated in this study. Functional postural status was characterized using clinical screening and Kineod three-dimensional postural assessment, while plantar pressure outcomes were recorded using the BTS P-WALK platform under static and dynamic conditions. Participants completed 10 individualized OMT sessions over three months, consisting primarily of soft-tissue and muscle-energy techniques. (3) Results: Mediolateral plantar load distribution did not change significantly. Forefoot loading increased from 32.65 ± 12.58% to 39.67 ± 9.29%, with a reciprocal reduction in rearfoot loading from 67.35 ± 12.58% to 60.34 ± 9.29% (Holm-adjusted p = 0.006; Cohen's dz = 0.842). The right dynamic Arch Index also increased significantly from 13.73 ± 8.86% to 17.37 ± 7.44% (Holm-adjusted p = 0.025; dz = 0.701). Other Arch Index changes were not significant after correction for multiple testing. (4) Conclusions: In this pilot cohort, OMT was followed by measurable changes in the forefoot-rearfoot plantar load distribution and the right dynamic Arch Index. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary functional changes in plantar loading rather than evidence of structural correction or definitive therapeutic efficacy. Larger controlled studies are needed to determine whether these changes are specifically attributable to OMT.

pico.ic: 干预与对照：丙泊酚/氯胺酮/右美托咪定等镇静方案、瑞马唑仑与艾司氯胺酮等新药、二氧化碳波形监测、经鼻高流量氧疗（HFNO），与常规镇静/监测及全身麻醉相比较（无系统检索与对照合成）

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Endoscopic and interventional procedures in pediatric gastroenterology are increasing in number and complexity, and most require sedation or, in selected cases, general anesthesia (GA); children face a higher risk of serious sedation-related adverse events than adults. Written jointly by pediatric gastroenterologists and anesthesiologists, this review provides a practical, evidence-referenced framework for procedural sedation across pediatric gastrointestinal procedures. Methods: We performed a narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE (inception to 20 June 2026, the date of the final search), prioritizing society guidelines, systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, and large registries on pediatric procedural sedation, sedative agents, capnography, and high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO). Results: Sedation should be matched to the procedure and to a structured risk tier, targeting the lightest depth that allows safe completion. Propofol-, ketamine-, and dexmedetomidine-based regimens dominate; remimazolam and esketamine are emerging, but pediatric data are limited. Capnography detects hypoventilation before desaturation, and HFNO reduces hypoxemia in adults, whereas pediatric-specific evidence remains limited and the pediatric subgroup analysis did not reach statistical significance. Higher-risk groups require tailored planning, monitoring, and rescue readiness; most evidence is observational or extrapolated from adults. Conclusions: Safe pediatric gastrointestinal sedation combines structured risk assessment, rational drug combinations, capnography-supported monitoring, and consistent complication reporting. Who administers deep sedation, and whether general anesthesia is preferred, should depend on patient and procedural risk together with local regulations, institutional policy, training and credentialing, and rescue capability, within a shared gastroenterology-anesthesiology framework. Adequately powered pediatric trials of HFNO and of remimazolam/esketamine, and long-term neurodevelopmental follow-up, are priorities.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (anti-NMDAR) encephalitis is a common autoimmune encephalitis affecting children and adolescents. Its development has been associated with preceding or concomitant infections, particularly herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). This scoping review characterized the association between infections and pediatric anti-NMDAR encephalitis, focusing on epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, treatment, and prognosis from January 2020 to August 2025. Methods: A scoping review was conducted according to the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) framework. PubMed was systematically searched using the terms NMDAR encephalitis AND infections AND children. Of 110 identified records, 13 studies met the predefined eligibility criteria. Results: HSV-1 was the most consistently reported infectious association, particularly in younger children. Clinical phenotype varied with age, with neurological manifestations predominating in younger children and psychiatric, behavioral, and cognitive symptoms becoming more prominent in adolescents. HSV-associated cases, particularly following extensive HSV-related brain injury, were associated with greater residual neurological morbidity and less favorable long-term outcomes. Other infectious agents, including SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza B, and norovirus, were reported less frequently, with limited evidence regarding their impact on disease course. Immunotherapeutic strategies were generally similar irrespective of preceding infection, although active or treatment-associated infections could influence treatment timing, sequencing, and infectious-risk considerations. Earlier immunotherapy was associated with more favorable neurological recovery. Conclusions: Infectious exposures, particularly HSV-1, appear to be associated with pediatric anti-NMDAR encephalitis, although causality cannot be established from the predominantly retrospective and case-based literature. Prospective, multicenter studies using standardized diagnostic and outcome measures are needed to clarify the infection-autoimmunity relationship and optimize early recognition and management.

papers.abstract_en: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a platform to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. HBCXs involve transplanting human pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, glia, or organoids into immunodeficient mice to model human disease. These models have revealed human-specific cellular and molecular phenotypes, developmental trajectories, and disease mechanisms that would otherwise be inaccessible in traditional in vitro systems and animal models. They also provide a scalable, genetically editable framework for functional genomics studies, drug testing, and biomarker discovery. Given the pronounced species differences in microglia and other tissue-resident brain macrophages and their central involvement in neurodegenerative disease, these models also provide an in vivo platform to interrogate human neuroimmunology. In selected settings, they may help guide future cell-based therapeutic strategies. This review provides an overview of the current applications, discusses the challenges and limitations, and highlights future avenues of HBCXs in neuroimmunology and translational research.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is a leading cause of preventable childhood visual impairment, particularly in settings where access to specialized ophthalmologic care is limited. Telemedicine offers an alternative approach to ROP screening and monitoring through remote retinal imaging and expert interpretation. This narrative review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance, clinical benefits, implementation challenges, and future perspectives of telemedicine in ROP screening and management. Methods: A narrative literature review was conducted with consideration of the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) criteria. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched in August and August 2026 for relevant publications from January 2000 to the search date. Two authors independently screened titles and abstracts, followed by full-text assessment according to predefined eligibility criteria. A total of 143 scientific articles and other high-quality sources were included in the final narrative synthesis. Evidence was evaluated qualitatively, without a formal risk-of-bias assessment. Findings: The reviewed literature indicates that telemedicine can expand access to ROP screening, facilitate remote specialist consultation, support longitudinal disease monitoring, and improve the triage of infants requiring urgent assessment. In selected settings, remote retinal image interpretation has demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to conventional examinations for clinically significant and vision-threatening ROP. Artificial intelligence-based assessment and smartphone-based retinal imaging represent promising approaches to improving screening accessibility and workflow efficiency, particularly in resource-limited settings. However, implementation remains constrained by equipment costs, infrastructure limitations, image quality, workforce training requirements, and ethical and legal considerations. Conclusions: Telemedicine represents a promising complementary strategy for ROP screening and management, with the potential to improve access to timely specialist assessment and help prevent ROP-related visual impairment. Its successful integration into clinical practice requires sustainable infrastructure, standardized protocols, trained personnel, and reliable referral pathways that ensure timely in-person examination and treatment when indicated. Further research is needed to establish the effectiveness, cost-efficiency, and long-term sustainability of different telemedicine-based approaches across diverse healthcare settings.

papers.abstract_en: Governments worldwide are investing in ageing in place-that is, policies and programmes that enable older adults to remain in their homes and communities irrespective of income level or functional ability. However, there have been few concerted evaluation efforts to keep up with these reforms. Drawing on country examples from the Netherlands, Norway, and Japan, this Personal View identifies three recurring reform tensions: decentralisation versus coordination, personal versus collective responsibility, and cost containment versus investment. Each reform tension produces unintended consequences that evaluations can detect, prompting midcourse corrections. Importantly, existing evaluation frameworks remain narrowly focused on care expenditure, missing the wider societal consequences of reforms. These frameworks also overlook structural inequities that shape who can and cannot age in place with dignity. We therefore propose an integrated, equity-stratified framework to assess whether ageing in place reforms achieve their stated goals or instead widen the disparities they purport to address.

papers.abstract_en: The first 1000 days of life, spanning from conception to approximately two years of age, represent a period of exceptional biological plasticity during which nutritional, metabolic, inflammatory, psychosocial, microbial, and environmental exposures may shape developmental trajectories across the life course. For this narrative review, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2026, focusing primarily on human cohorts, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and consensus documents, with selected experimental studies included for mechanistic evidence. Within the framework of the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD), we examine the epigenetic, oxidative, inflammatory, mitochondrial, and telomere-related mechanisms proposed to link early-life exposures with lifelong health and biological aging. Because most human evidence in this field is observational, whereas much of the mechanistic evidence derives from experimental models, these relationships are presented as associations and biologically plausible hypotheses rather than as demonstrated causal pathways. We then consider how these processes may become clinically apparent during childhood through four illustrative "sentinel phenotypes"-allergic and atopic disease, respiratory vulnerability, renal-cardiovascular risk, and altered metabolic growth-proposed here as a conceptual framework rather than as an established classification. We also review preventive opportunities during pregnancy, infancy, and early childhood. Overall, the first 1000 days should be viewed as a critical window for developmental health, while the specific contribution of this review is to integrate early-life biological mechanisms with clinically observable pediatric sentinel phenotypes within the broader framework of biological and healthy aging.

papers.abstract_en: Dietary diversity is an important component of complementary feeding and may influence the nutritional status and growth of infants and young children. This review aimed to synthesize evidence on the association between dietary diversity during complementary feeding and nutritional status, with emphasis on Indonesia and relevant international evidence. This study was conducted as a targeted narrative review. A targeted literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar between January and March 2026. Studies were eligible if they included children aged 6-23 months, assessed dietary diversity or minimum dietary diversity, reported nutritional outcomes, and were original research articles published in English between 2004 and 2026. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study designs, populations, dietary diversity measures, and nutritional outcomes. Sixteen studies met the eligibility criteria, comprising 10 Indonesian and 6 non-Indonesian or multi-country studies. Overall, higher dietary diversity was generally associated with more favorable anthropometric outcomes, particularly linear growth and lower odds of stunting, although associations varied across settings and after adjustment for other factors. In Indonesia, socioeconomic, maternal, cultural, and food-access factors were also associated with dietary diversity. Dietary diversity may be associated with more favorable nutritional and growth outcomes among children aged 6-23 months. Improving dietary diversity in Indonesia may benefit from context-specific approaches addressing caregiver practices, food-system constraints, and community and primary healthcare capacity.

papers.abstract_en: Caveolae are specialized plasma membrane invaginations enriched in cholesterol and sphingolipids, playing vital roles in signal transduction, lipid regulation, membrane trafficking, and mechanoprotection. Their formation and function depend on two protein families: caveolins and cavins. Caveolins are integral membrane proteins that contribute to the membrane's curvature and serve as scaffolds for diverse signaling molecules. Cavins support caveolins at the cytoplasmic surface to stabilize caveolar architecture and regulate key processes, including insulin signaling, nitric oxide synthase activity, and lipid droplet formation. Mutations in caveolin or cavin genes can disrupt caveolae formation and function, often impairing cholesterol handling and perturbing key signaling pathways. This has been observed in a spectrum of pathologies such as muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, lipodystrophies, and various cancers. Given the importance of caveolins and cavins in membrane organization, understanding how specific mutations alter caveolin and cavin function is critical for elucidating the molecular basis of various disorders and in the development of targeted therapies. This review explores how caveolin and cavin mutations affect caveolae morphology, function, and signaling, thereby impacting physiology.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Diagnosing the cause of an atraumatic limp in children is challenging, as conditions with overlapping clinical presentations can range from self-limited processes to orthopedic emergencies. Knowledge of evolving risk factors, diagnostic practices, and management approaches is crucial to efficient treatment. This review synthesizes recent evidence on the evaluation of the limping child, focusing on key diagnoses including transient synovitis of the hip (TSH), septic arthritis of the hip (SAH), slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE), and Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease (LCPD). RECENT FINDINGS: For SAH and TSH, emerging evidence supports point-of-care ultrasound alongside clinical findings and inflammatory markers to improve diagnostic differentiation. In SCFE, increasing incidence, recognition of additional risk factors, variable pain presentations, and evolving approaches to surgical timing and contralateral risk have implications for diagnosis and management. For LCPD, current studies highlight variability in pain presentation, advances in radiographic classification, and individualized operative containment strategies. SUMMARY: This review provides a synopsis of recent literature surrounding SAH, TSH, SCFE, and LCPD. Recent advances may facilitate earlier recognition, improve risk stratification, and support more individualized management for children presenting with a new limp. While this article highlights four important diagnoses, clinicians should maintain a broad differential of classic and atypical presentations of limping.

papers.abstract_en: Oral health literacy (OHL) is increasingly recognized as a multidimensional construct associated with oral health behaviors, healthcare utilization, clinical outcomes, and oral health-related quality of life. However, the strength and consistency of these associations vary across populations, outcomes, study designs, and measurement approaches, and much of the available evidence derives from adult populations. This narrative review examines current evidence on OHL-related outcomes with particular attention to children and adolescents and critically evaluates direct and caregiver-based assessment approaches. The review identifies a substantial developmental and measurement gap in pediatric OHL research. Studies involving children have frequently assessed parental or caregiver OHL rather than children's own competencies, although these represent related but distinct constructs. Direct assessment of children and adolescents is feasible, but currently available instruments remain limited, have generally been evaluated within restricted age ranges and sociocultural settings, and predominantly emphasize functional or cognitive competencies. Broader dimensions such as communication, critical appraisal, navigation, decision-making, and application of oral health information are less consistently assessed. Developmentally appropriate OHL assessment should therefore account for cognitive and linguistic development, reading ability, communication skills, and increasing autonomy rather than simply adapting adult instruments. Future research should prioritize age-appropriate, culturally adaptable, and psychometrically robust measures that directly assess children's and adolescents' OHL across developmental stages and help clarify its relationships with oral health behaviors, service utilization, clinical outcomes, and oral health-related quality of life.

papers.abstract_en: Innate immune systems must detect infection rapidly and reliably, yet pathogens can often evade direct recognition by host pattern-recognition receptors. An alternative and increasingly appreciated strategy is damage-driven immune surveillance, whereby hosts detect pathogen-induced perturbations to essential cellular and tissue functions rather than microbial molecules themselves. This mode of detection is particularly prominent in Caenorhabditis elegans, which lacks professional immune cells and most canonical innate immune receptors, and therefore relies extensively on monitoring disruptions to core homeostatic pathways. Perturbations to protein translation, proteostasis, mitochondrial function, genome and nucleolar integrity, lysosomal homeostasis, and Golgi function can all trigger immune responses. Recent studies have further uncovered roles for inter-organelle communication, effector-triggered surveillance of lysosome-related organelles, and physiological signals such as intestinal distension in regulating immune activation. Here, we integrate these advances into an organelle- and tissue-centric framework and explore parallels with other organisms to identify emerging and potentially conserved principles of damage sensing in innate immunity. These findings highlight the surveillance of cellular homeostasis as a central strategy for immunity that operates beyond canonical pattern-recognition mechanisms.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Multimodal treatment approaches to pediatric obesity, including pharmacotherapy, are now recommended as part of an early intervention strategy to improve long-term health outcomes. However, barriers to prescribing obesity medications limit patient access to them. This review summarizes practical approaches to pediatric obesity pharmacotherapy tailored for the general pediatrician, based on evidence and expert opinion. RECENT FINDINGS: The American Academy of Pediatrics clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of pediatric obesity calls for early, individualized intervention, including consideration of pharmacotherapy. Available obesity medications include those that are Federal Drug Administration (FDA)-approved for this indication and those that are used "off-label" with FDA approval for other indications. SUMMARY: Obesity pharmacotherapy should be considered an adjunct to lifestyle interventions for pediatric obesity. Readiness to prescribe these medications is influenced by physician comfort, practice infrastructure, and access-related barriers. Specialty training (i.e., endocrinology, gastroenterology, obesity medicine) does not have to be a requirement for managing obesity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Epithelioid hemangioma is an uncommon benign vascular tumor, and involvement of the glans penis is exceptional in childhood. CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 4-year-old boy who presented with a longstanding, painless, pedunculated pink nodule on the dorsal glans adjacent to the urethral meatus. Previous topical treatment for presumed balanitis relieved pruritus but did not modify the lesion. Complete local excision was performed under general anesthesia with local infiltration, with preservation of the urethral structures. Histopathological examination showed a well-circumscribed polypoid mucosal lesion with epithelioid endothelial proliferation, small vascular channels, and mild stromal inflammation, without cytological atypia. Immunohistochemistry showed strong FLI-1 and CD34 positivity, supporting endothelial differentiation; CD31 was not performed. The morphological features strongly favored benign epithelioid vascular proliferation and were not consistent with epithelioid hemangioendothelioma or epithelioid angiosarcoma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and follow-up at 12 months showed no recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates the need to consider rare vascular tumors in persistent pediatric penile lesions. A treatment-refractory glanular lesion in a child should prompt early histopathological assessment rather than prolonged empirical therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: The action observation and execution network (AOEN) is thought to support action perception-execution coupling and it may contribute to motor learning during development. In cerebral palsy (CP), early brain lesions occur while sensorimotor and cognitive networks are still developing, potentially reshaping AOEN organization and the mechanisms through which children learn from observed actions. This narrative review examines current evidence on AOEN involvement during action observation and execution in CP and proposes a neuroconstructivist framework for personalized observation-based rehabilitation. Methods: We synthesized behavioural, neuroimaging, and intervention studies investigating AOEN functioning, structural and functional reorganization, and Action Observation Treatment (AOT) in children with CP, with particular attention to unilateral and bilateral phenotypes. Results: Available evidence suggests that action observation-execution mechanisms remain functionally responsive in CP, although their organization may be altered according to lesion architecture, distributed network connectivity, and acquired motor experience. Motor impairment may influence the encoding of kinematics, goals, and action sequences, while models whose movements are closer to the child's motor repertoire have been associated with greater neural engagement and preliminary short-term treatment benefits. Praxis, attention, working memory, visuospatial processing, and executive functions may further influence the transformation of observed actions into executable motor programmes. Conclusions: We propose that rehabilitation response may reflect the interaction among structural and functional reorganization, motor phenotype, neuropsychological functioning, environmental experience, and stimulus characteristics. The AOEN may therefore be better conceptualized as a developmentally reconfigured network rather than a uniformly preserved or impaired system. Multimodal phenotyping may help support more developmentally informed and individualized observation-based rehabilitation.

papers.abstract_en: The Planetary Boundaries (PB) framework, first introduced in 2009, has become one of the most influential conceptual tools in Earth system science for defining a 'safe operating space for humanity'. It identifies nine critical Earth system processes, including climate change, biosphere integrity, and ocean acidification, and proposes quantitative boundaries beyond which humanity risks triggering irreversible environmental changes. Despite the ocean covering 71% of Earth's surface and playing a fundamental role in regulating climate, sequestering carbon, and maintaining global biogeochemical cycles, its representation within the PB framework remains notably limited. Only one boundary, ocean acidification, explicitly addresses marine systems, and even this focuses primarily on surface ocean chemistry. The ocean interior, deep-sea processes, subsurface biogeochemistry, large-scale circulation patterns, and marine functional diversity are largely absent. This gap is not merely conceptual. As ocean industrialization accelerates, through deep-sea mining, high-seas fisheries, and the expanding 'blue economy', the need to understand how these activities impact planetary-scale stability becomes increasingly urgent. Meanwhile, the current governance landscape remains fragmented, with different ocean issues addressed under different regimes, lacking a coherent framework to guide decision-making. Against this backdrop, this forum chaired by Professor Minhan Dai of Xiamen University brings together leading scholars in marine and Earth system science to address a pressing question: How can marine processes and ecosystems be effectively incorporated into the PB framework, and what would this mean for science, governance, and sustainability? Deliang Chen Professor, Department of Earth System Science, Tsinghua University, China Sam Dupont Senior Lecturer, Department of Biological & Environmental Sciences, University of Gothenburg, Sweden Minhan Dai (Chair) Professor, College of Ocean and Earth Sciences, Xiamen University, China Ellycia Harrould-Kolieb Lecturer, School of Agriculture, Food and Ecosystem Sciences, University of Melbourne, Australia Ariel Pezner Chancellor's Research Fellow, University of Technology, Australia.

However, accumulating evidence indicates that the Hippo signaling pathway is also closely associated with the onset and progression of autoimmune diseases. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Pediatric mandibular condylar fractures require management that accounts for ongoing craniofacial growth and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) function. This narrative review summarizes contemporary evidence on age- and displacement-sensitive decision-making, functional and orthodontic rehabilitation, imaging, and long-term growth surveillance. METHODS: A structured narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was conducted for English-language human studies published from January 2021 through June 2026, supplemented by citation searching for foundational publications. RESULTS: Management ranges from expectant observation and functional appliance therapy to brief closed stabilization and open reduction with internal fixation (ORIF). Predominantly retrospective and heterogeneous evidence suggests that timely restoration of comfortable mandibular mobility is associated with favorable functional recovery and substantial remodeling potential in many growing patients, although outcomes depend on age, fracture morphology, functional loading, and remaining growth. ORIF may be appropriate for selected severe fractures when acceptable function and occlusion cannot be restored by less invasive measures. CONCLUSIONS: Management should integrate skeletal maturity, fracture level and displacement, laterality, occlusal disturbance, mandibular mobility, cooperation, and remaining growth. Across treatment modalities, avoidance of unnecessary prolonged immobilization, structured functional rehabilitation, and longitudinal orthodontic and craniofacial surveillance are important clinical priorities.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dysfunction of the SHANK3 gene has been linked to several neuropsychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders, such as attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder, and epilepsy. SHANK3 haploinsufficiency is the known etiology of Phelan-McDermid syndrome. CASE PRESENTATION: This report presents a five-year-old boy in whom the c.2062G>C; p.Val688Leu variant was identified in a mosaic state in the SHANK3 gene (40% of heterozygous cells) and classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). The patient was diagnosed with complex mental health problems, which, analogous to typical SHANK3 disruption, included ADHD, oppositional defiant disorder, developmental coordination disorder, Non-REM sleep arousal disorder, insomnia disorder, and avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder. Starting at the age of three years, his psychiatric treatment had included various medication trials over the course of two years. Ultimately, a substantial reduction in emotional outbursts, externalizing behaviors, and parental stress occurred following a multimodal treatment approach comprising psychotropic polypharmacy (PP), i.e., lisdexamfetamine, melatonin, and risperidone, along with behavioral therapy interventions, speech therapy, and occupational therapy. Under this PP, constipation was documented as the only adverse reaction. At the 15-month follow-up, improvements had been quite stable, despite risperidone medication being stopped about 19 weeks after initiation. CONCLUSIONS: As shown in this case report, even very young children with complex neuropsychiatric problems and SHANK3 variants might not be treated sufficiently by therapeutic interventions alone, but might require a combination of therapeutic and psychopharmacological interventions to achieve a substantial symptom reduction. However, PP must be approached with a high degree of caution and subjected to close monitoring in children with SHANK3 variants, who are susceptible to an elevated risk of adverse outcomes. Moreover, given the paucity of research in this population, it seems advisable to follow prevailing general guidelines in child and adolescent psychiatry.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neutrophils, pivotal effector cells of the immune system, are increasingly recognized to have considerable functional and phenotypic heterogeneity. The emergence of immunometabolism has offered a framework for understanding this diversity. Accumulating evidence indicates that shifts in metabolic pathways and their byproducts can reshape the fate and function of neutrophils. MAIN BODY: Neutrophil heterogeneity arises from both distinct developmental stages and specific signals within peripheral tissue microenvironments. Functionally, glycolysis is the central metabolic pathway that fuels core effector responses, while metabolites such as lactate, lipids, and amino acids can further modulate neutrophil phenotypes. In pathological contexts of metabolic dysregulation, metabolic stress induces extensive reprogramming of neutrophils. This process drives the accumulation of specific metabolites, which in turn trigger transcriptional reprogramming through epigenetic remodeling, establishing a self-reinforcing loop that sustains pro-pathological neutrophil states. Targeting key nodes within these dysregulated metabolic pathways has potential as a therapeutic strategy. CONCLUSIONS: Here, we review the metabolic heterogeneity of neutrophil subpopulations and the mechanisms by which distinct metabolic programs drive disease progression in pathological settings. We further discuss current therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways. Through this analysis, we aim to provide a refined perspective on the immune landscape and to identify new possibilities for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is standard of care for inoperable stage I or II non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). KEYNOTE-867 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03924869) evaluated the addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT in participants diagnosed with stage I or II NSCLC that was inoperable or in participants who refused surgery. METHODS: Adults with untreated, stage I or II (T1 to limited T3, N0, M0) NSCLC (AJCC 8th edition) that was inoperable, or adults who refused surgery, were randomly assigned 1:1 to thoracic SBRT to primary tumors for ≤2 weeks concomitantly with pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo once every 3 weeks for ≤17 cycles. The primary end point was event-free survival (EFS) by blinded independent central review. RESULTS: A total of 448 participants were randomly assigned to SBRT plus pembrolizumab (n = 227) or SBRT plus placebo (n = 221). The median time from random assignment to the data cutoff date (June 11, 2024) for the prespecified first interim analysis was 20.6 (range, 1.3-56.8) months. The median EFS (95% CI) was 31.2 (22.5 to 39.1) months and 28.3 (19.8 to 33.1) months for the pembrolizumab and placebo arms, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.69 to 1.24]; P = .2932). Among participants who received ≥1 dose of study treatment, grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 46/226 (20.4%) participants in the pembrolizumab arm and 8/218 (3.7%) participants in the placebo arm. There were five treatment-related deaths all of which occurred in the pembrolizumab arm (2.2%). CONCLUSION: The addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT did not improve EFS and was associated with a higher incidence of treatment-related AEs compared with SBRT alone in participants with inoperable stage I or II NSCLC. Based on the benefit-risk profile, the KEYNOTE-867 trial was prematurely stopped, and all study treatment was discontinued.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria. RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods. CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Physical deterioration and disease progression during neoadjuvant treatment can preclude tumor surgery in patients with gastroesophageal cancer. Whether preoperative exercise training can increase the probability of undergoing tumor surgery remains unknown. OBJECTIVE: To compare exercise training with usual care on the likelihood of not undergoing tumor surgery with curative intent after neoadjuvant treatment for gastroesophageal cancer. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: PRESET-RCT was a single-blinded, parallel-group, 2-arm, superiority randomized clinical trial. Patients with gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma scheduled to undergo treatment with curative intent, including neoadjuvant treatment, and with no contraindication to exercise training were eligible. Participants were enrolled at University Hospital Copenhagen, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark, from August 16, 2018, to September 23, 2022, with final follow-up on October 22, 2024. Data analysis was performed from March 2023 to May 2025. INTERVENTION: The participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative exercise training from diagnosis until tumor surgery or control. The intervention consisted of twice-weekly concurrent aerobic exercise and resistance training. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was not undergoing tumor surgery with curative intent. The secondary outcomes were treatment tolerance and overall survival. RESULTS: In total, 207 participants (73.7%) were randomized and 202 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analyses (mean [SD] age, 65.3 [8.5] years; 161 [78.9%] male; 170 [83.3%] with gastroesophageal junction cancer), with 101 randomized to each group. In the exercise group, 10 (9.9%) did not undergo tumor surgery with curative intent compared with 8 (7.9%) in the control group (odds ratio, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.48-3.38; P = .62). There were no between-group differences in permanent discontinuation of neoadjuvant treatment (odds ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.38-1.72) or postoperative complications (odds ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.61-2.20). The overall survival rates at 3 years for the exercise and control group were 51.0% and 65.0%, respectively (hazard ratio, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.02-2.45). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, preoperative exercise training did not increase the likelihood of undergoing tumor surgery for patients with gastroesophageal cancer. The findings do not support the use of exercise training during neoadjuvant treatment to improve surgical outcomes, and further research is needed to determine its effects on long-term outcomes. papers.abstract_en: Confinement architectures stabilise active metal nanoparticles while preserving molecular accessibility, which proves crucial for heterogeneous catalysis. However, existing methods for preparing encapsulated catalysts such as mesoporous oxides, zeolites, and metal-organic frameworks are costly, complex, and often unreliable. Solid‑state reactions offer a promising alternative, yet conventional pathways yield thermodynamically stable phases that limit activity. Here, we propose a facile, template-free strategy that intercepts amorphous intermediates during solid‑state reactions to form encapsulation layers for active metals. We select ammonia decomposition reaction (ADR, 2NH3 → N2 + 3H2) as the target catalytic reaction, which is a pivotal route to COx‑free hydrogen and affords the high‑temperature, reducing environment that drives solid‑state transformations. During ADR conditions, commercial BaCO3 and Al2O3 act as solid‑state reactants, forming Al2O3-BaO encapsulation layers around Co or Ni nanoparticles. The layers effectively restrict nanoparticle growth. Amorphous Al2O3 facilitates NH3 adsorption, and amorphous BaO accelerates N2/H2 release and enables N-H activation. As a result, the encapsulated catalyst delivers an intrinsic rate of 1,358 mmol H2·gmetal-1·min-1 that surpasses existing non‑noble metal catalysts, alongside excellent durability during 480 h. This approach offers a blueprint for constructing durable confinement architectures in encapsulated metal catalysts.

papers.abstract_en: Metabolic reprogramming, the fundamental process by which cells adapt to fluctuations in energy demands, is pivotal in the pathophysiology of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases (CCVDs). Aberrant reprogramming of glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism is intricately associated with pathological processes in CCVDs such as cardiac hypertrophy, atherosclerosis, and ischemia-reperfusion injury. This metabolic remodeling disrupts the dynamic balance of metabolites (cc, acetyl-CoA and lactate) in the cardio-cerebrovascular systems, thereby inducing abnormal post-translational modifications (PTMs) on histones and non-histone proteins. These PTMs drive disease progression by modulating gene transcription or the activity of key proteins, which subsequently influences downstream signaling pathways. Here, we systematically examine the regulatory enzymes and functional roles of nine recently characterized acylation modifications: crotonylation, β-hydroxybutyrylation, 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation, succinylation, malonylation, glutarylation, lactylation, propionylation, and butyrylation. Furthermore, this review elaborates on the molecular mechanisms, crosstalk and the latest preclinical advancements regarding these acylations in CCVDs, emphasizing the influence of distinct acylation patterns on various pathological processes and highlighting the clinical translational prospects of targeting these novel modifications for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: In clinical trials, the messenger RNA (mRNA)-1345 vaccine provided protection against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) illness. Data on mRNA-1345 effectiveness in broader patient populations are needed. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effectiveness of mRNA-1345 vaccination during a single respiratory illness season. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used a target trial emulation framework to assess veterans 50 years and older receiving care in the Veterans Health Administration. Eligible vaccine recipients were matched with up to 4 unvaccinated individuals in 4 monthly, nested, sequential trials from October 1, 2025, to January 31, 2026. Outcomes were ascertained through May 31, 2026, or 24 weeks. EXPOSURE: A single dose of mRNA-1345 RSV vaccine vs no RSV vaccination. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was any positive RSV test result from day 14 after the matched index date. Secondary outcomes included RSV-associated emergency department (ED) or urgent care (UC) encounters and RSV-associated hospitalizations. Vaccine effectiveness was estimated as 100 × (1 - risk ratio). A sensitivity analysis comparing veterans who received same-day mRNA-1345 and influenza vaccination to influenza vaccination alone (active comparator arm) was performed to explore potential bias from differences in health care-seeking behavior and outcome ascertainment between comparator groups. RESULTS: A total of 74 926 vaccinated veterans were matched to 286 425 unique control individuals, weighted to represent 74 926 individuals, for a total of 149 852 study participants (median [IQR] age, 73.0 [63.3-78.6] years; 136 756 [91.3%] male). During a median (IQR) follow-up of 160 (130-168) days, estimated vaccine effectiveness was 60.3% (95% CI, 49.0%-70.4%) against any documented infection, 60.2% (95% CI, 47.2%-71.5%) against RSV-associated ED or UC encounters, and 81.8% (95% CI, 58.1%-99.9%) against RSV-associated hospitalizations. Estimated effectiveness against documented infections decreased with increasing age, from 82.9% (95% CI, 64.0%-96.7%) in the 50- to 59-year age group to 28.6% (95% CI, -12.0% to 60.4%) in the 80-year or older age group. With an active comparator arm, estimated effectiveness was 67.1% (95% CI, 48.9%-82.6%) against documented RSV infections, 69.5% (95% CI, 49.7%-85.4%) against RSV-associated ED and UC encounters, and 86.9% (95% CI, 56.5%-100.0%) against RSV-associated hospitalizations. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study using a target trial emulation of mRNA-1345 vaccine effectiveness during 24 weeks, vaccination was associated with protection against RSV illness and associated health care use in adults 50 years and older. Comparative effectiveness studies are needed to determine the relative benefits of available RSV vaccine products.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Recurrent pulmonary exacerbations contribute substantially to lung function decline in people with cystic fibrosis (CF). Inhalation therapies are a cornerstone of standard of care, yet adherence to inhalation therapies is variable and data on the relationship between adherence and pulmonary exacerbations remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To assess the impact of multimodal telemonitoring and coaching on adherence and pulmonary exacerbations in people with CF. METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter, unblinded, randomized, controlled trial people with CF aged ≥12 years were randomized (1:1) to either standard of care or an intervention involving continuous objective home monitoring of inhalation adherence, weekly home spirometry, a self-management app, professional telephone coaching, and optional video conferencing over 18 months. The primary endpoint was time to first pulmonary exacerbation. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: 296 participants were included with a mean age of 31.3 (SD 10.8) years, 54.1% females, mean FEV1% predicted of 70.2% (SD 24.7), 52.7% chronically infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and 85.1% on triple CFTR modulator therapy. Baseline adherence was higher in the intervention group (58.1%) than in the control group (44.0%) and remained higher throughout the study (last 6 months: 49.2% vs. 32.6%). Time to first exacerbation did not differ between groups. However, across all participants, a 10% increase in adherence correlated with a 9% reduction in pulmonary exacerbation risk. Participants with FEV1<40% had a 2.4-fold higher risk of exacerbations. CONCLUSION: Multimodal telemedicine improved inhalation therapy adherence. The association between higher adherence and reduced exacerbations highlights the ongoing importance of inhalation therapy in CF, even with widespread CFTR modulator use. Clinical trial registered with German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00024642).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Constipation is common in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD), and individual responses to non-pharmacological interventions may vary substantially. This exploratory study investigated whether baseline gut microbiota characteristics were associated with short-term response to acupressure combined with thermal stimulation in MHD patients with functional constipation. METHODS: This responder analysis was based on a randomized two-sequence crossover study. Clinical data and fecal samples obtained immediately before each participant entered the 14-day intervention period were analyzed. Participants with an increase of ≥1 bowel movement (BM) per week were classified as responders (R), and those with <1 BM/week as non-responders (NR). Baseline gut microbiota were characterized using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and genus-level differential abundance were evaluated. ANCOM-BC2 was performed with adjustment for baseline BM/week, sex, and diabetes mellitus, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction and pseudocount sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Twenty-six participants were included, of whom 9 (34.6%) met the predefined response criterion. Across all participants, weekly BM frequency increased from 1.25 (1.00, 1.50) to 2.00 (1.00, 3.00) (P = 0.0003), while PAC-SYM total and stool-symptom subscale scores decreased (P = 0.0011 and P = 0.0013, respectively). Alpha-diversity did not differ significantly between R and NR groups, and beta-diversity showed no overall community separation (ANOSIM R=-0.044, P = 0.6751). Lactonifactor was nominally higher in responders in the unadjusted analysis (P = 0.015) but was not significant after multiple-testing correction (FDR = 0.86). In adjusted ANCOM-BC2 analysis, Veillonella (β=5.319, FDR = 0.0347) and Lactobacillus (β=3.621, FDR = 0.0459) were associated with responder status; however, neither association was robust to pseudocount sensitivity analysis. PICRUSt2 identified no significant between-group differences in predicted functional pathways. CONCLUSION: Baseline microbial diversity and community structure were similar between responders and non-responders. Veillonella and Lactobacillus showed adjusted associations with response, but neither was robust in sensitivity analysis. These findings should therefore be regarded as exploratory rather than predictive. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to validate these findings and determine their clinical relevance.

papers.abstract_en: T cell correlates of COVID-19 risk are poorly defined, particularly in people with HIV (PWH). CoVPN 3008 ( NCT05168813 ) Part A was a prospective 14,002-participant cohort study that administered one or two doses of mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine, depending on baseline SARS-CoV-2 serostatus, in participants (83% PWH) in sub-Saharan Africa. Participants self-monitored for prespecified COVID-19 symptoms, defined by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention symptom criteria. Previous work showed that protection from COVID-19 was superior for hybrid versus vaccine-induced immunity, and that neutralizing antibody titers inversely associated with COVID-19 risk. In the present work, we measured T cell responses to Spike and Nucleocapsid at baseline and 4 weeks post last-vaccination (Peak) in a case-cohort study and assessed them as correlates of risk. In Hybrid Group PWH (n = 22 cases), COVID-19 risk over 6 months decreased with increasing Peak Spike BA.4/5-specific CD4 + T cell responses, from 15.8%, 4.7%, and 0% risk at 0.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% IFN-γ and/or IL-2 response magnitude, respectively. Including baseline Spike-specific neutralizing antibody titer and Peak CD4 + T cell functionality score in the same model increased the association's strength (overall p < 0.001). Thus, CD4 + T cell responses are an independent correlate of COVID-19 risk among PWH with pre-existing SARS-CoV-2 immunity.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Sepsis-associated lung injury (SALI) is a lethal infection-induced complication with high mortality and limited targeted therapies. Dysregulated lactate metabolism is closely linked to SALI, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the role and molecular mechanism of EZH2 (Enhancer of zeste homolog 2) lactylation in SALI development, thereby uncovering a novel exploitable therapeutic target. METHODS: A total of 209 ICU patients were enrolled and divided into the SALI group (n = 104) and non-SALI group (n = 105) to detect serum lactate levels. Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mouse models and endothelial cell-specific Ezh2 knockout (Ezh2ECKO) mouse models were established. Combined with lactate and lactate dehydrogenase inhibitor intervention, multi-omics analysis, ChIP, qPCR, immunofluorescence and other techniques were used in the study. RESULTS: Serum lactate levels were significantly elevated in patients with SALI and model mice, and lung tissue lactate levels were elevated in model mice. Lactate levels were positively associated with inflammatory markers and lung injury severity. EZH2 underwent site-specific lactylation at lysine 30 and 406 (EZH2 K30/K406la) in SALI, which was enhanced with disease progression. Inhibiting lactate production or EZH2 lactylation improved pulmonary function, reduced inflammatory infiltration and pathological lung tissue damage. EZH2 K30/K406la downregulated CITED2 (CBP-p300 interacting transactivator with Glu/Asp-rich carboxy-terminal domain 2) expression by reducing its occupancy at the CITED2 promoter and altering CITED2 promoter activity, relieving the inhibition of the NF-κB (Nuclear Factor-kappa B) pathway and exacerbating inflammatory responses and endothelial dysfunction. CONCLUSION: EZH2 lactylation aggravates SALI via the CITED2/NF-κB axis, highlighting this epigenetic modification as a promising therapeutic target that opens a new pharmacological avenue for developing site-specific inhibitors to combat SALI.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal cancer (EC) is highly lethal due to late diagnosis, and accurate non-invasive tools for early detection and subtyping remain lacking. Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) fragmentomics offers a promising biomarker source. In this large multi-center study enrolling 1,260 participants spanning healthy control (HC), benign esophageal diseases (BED), precancerous lesions and EC patients, we developed two machine learning models based on plasma ccf-mtDNA fragmentomic profiles: an EC detection (ED) model and a pathological subtyping prediction (PSP) model. The ED model achieved an AUC of 0.9706 (EC vs. non-EC) in the training cohort, with high performance in internal (0.9762), external (0.9748), and Chinese minority (0.9668, Uyghur and Kazakh) validation cohorts. At the optimal cut-off, it yielded 92.16% sensitivity for stage I EC in the combined validation cohort and correctly identified 93.10% of early EC cases missed by preoperative biopsy. It also discriminated high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia from non-EC with an AUC of 0.9597. The PSP model distinguished ESCC from EAC with 89.71% accuracy, improving to 90.74% after integrating key clinical parameters. In summary, ccf-mtDNA fragmentomics provides a robust, non-invasive platform for early EC detection, precancerous risk stratification, and histological subtyping, demonstrating strong potential to transform clinical management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reactivation of human herpesviruses (HHVs), particularly EBV, is associated with more severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of Long COVID (LC). Reactivation of HHVs has been previously implicated in hormonal dysregulation, which has also been observed in LC, suggesting a potential link. This study aims to examine the relationship between LC symptoms and salivary HHV DNA, cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol levels. METHODS: Our cross-sectional, case-control study enrolled 45 participants with LC, and 45 age-sex-matched controls. Surveys and validated health questionnaires were used to collect demographics, medical history, and symptom profiles. Saliva was self-collected at waking, 15, 30, and 45 min, and 8 and 16 h after waking, across two consecutive days. Salivary cortisol, testosterone and oestradiol were measured, and extracted nucleic acid was tested for EBV, HSV 1/2, HCMV and HHV-6 A/B using multiplex qPCR, and for SARS-CoV-2 and RNaseP using RT-qPCR. FINDINGS: Detection of salivary EBV and HHV-6 DNA copies was highest early in the morning. There were no significant differences in salivary cortisol, testosterone, or oestradiol, or in EBV or HHV-6 DNA between the LC and control groups. However, salivary HHV-6 DNA levels were positively associated with a greater aggregated LC propensity score (r = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.02-0.44, p = 0.015, adj. p = 0.030), as well as anxiety (β = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.02-1.36, p = 0.045) and depression (β = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.05-0.42, p = 0.013) scores. INTERPRETATION: The observed correlation between salivary HHV-6 DNA and symptom severity suggests HHV-6 may contribute to post-acute disease, though mechanisms remain unclear. While we did not identify a relationship between salivary EBV DNA and LC, EBV may still play a role at earlier time points in the disease course, or in compartments not sampled in this study. These findings highlight the potential importance of HHV-6 in LC pathophysiology and underscore the need for longitudinal, multi-compartment studies of herpesvirus reactivation in LC. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Inguinal and femoral hernias in women show a reported diagnostic gap, with systematic evidence supported by cohorts composed of approximately 84% men. Findings included indirect inguinal predominance, bilateral distribution in 26.1%, a high proportion of occult hernias, and underreporting in the original radiology report. Resident sensitivity was 100% against both expert reviewers. Specificity was 84.4% against Reviewer 1 and 47.4% against Reviewer 2. Cohen's kappa for resident vs. Reviewer 1 was 0.878; resident vs. Reviewer 2 was 0.326; and Reviewer 1 vs. Reviewer 2 was 0.408. CONCLUSIONS: The radiological prevalence in women sits above the classical clinical range. Extraperitoneal fat is an overlooked differential diagnosis in female cohorts and accounts for a large part of interreviewer discordance. The 2-of-3 rule works as a replicable method for diagnostic studies with limited resources.

papers.abstract_en: Interactions between T cell receptors (TCRs), peptides, and human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) underlie antigen-specific T cell immunity. Despite substantial advances in prediction methods, accurate modeling of coupled TCR-peptide-HLA recognition remains underdeveloped, limiting applications such as TCR and neoepitope prioritization in cancer and antigen identification in autoimmunity. Here we present StriMap, a unified framework for predicting TCR-peptide-HLA interactions by integrating physicochemical, sequence-context, and structural features at recognition interfaces. papers.abstract_en: The world is stochastic, making planning difficult. Despite the ubiquity of stochasticity in real-world environments, it remains an open question how people effectively balance the cognitive costs of planning against its potential benefits when faced with stochasticity. To study this, we designed a planning task where participants face one of three forms of stochasticity commonly encountered in the real world: reliability, volatility, and controllability. We find a robust pattern across all three manipulations: as stochasticity increases, people reduce their planning effort as measured by first-choice response times. To understand the processes underlying this effect, we developed several computational cognitive models to account for participants' choices. We find that rather than calculating expected values optimally, people choose a simpler strategy, acting as if the world were deterministic, a phenomenon known as determinizing. Consistent with our response time findings, we find that people reduce their effort by decreasing their sensitivity to values with increasing stochasticity, a signature of policy compression. Our work highlights the often overlooked role of stochasticity in human planning and its impact on planning strategy and effort. Moreover, it reveals the limitations of studying stochasticity solely through single-shot decisions.

papers.abstract_en: Cycling stability remains a critical challenge in the development of high-nickel positive electrode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Although existing strategies such as delaying the formation of the H3 phase or operating below a cut-off voltage have shown promise, they limit the exploitation of the full energy density. Our comparative analysis reveals that enhanced structural reversibility in the bulk structure is the key factor contributing to this improved cycling performance. The nanorod structure demonstrates an ability to endure the substantial lattice mismatch present in the Li layer at the H2-H3 interphase, thereby facilitating a comprehensive recovery from H3 to the H2 phase during discharge. This work offers insights into optimizing high-nickel positive electrode materials, improving cycling stability in high-energy battery applications.

papers.abstract_en: Carboxylases are among the most important enzymes in nature as they catalyze the fixation of inorganic carbon (CO2), a central step in the global carbon cycle. In addition to their well-known function in autotrophic CO2 fixation, many carboxylases play a role in the heterotrophic assimilation of organic compounds. In this study, we provide genomic evidence for an assimilatory carboxylation pathway involved in acetone degradation in photoheterotrophic bacteria from metagenomes collected along a latitudinal transect of the Arctic Ocean. This curious metabolism was linked to a single population of Gammaproteobacteria (Porticoccus arcticus). P. arcticus has a streamlined genome compared to Porticoccus relatives but has maintained a complete acetone carboxylation pathway while acquiring multiple proteorhodopsin genes by lateral gene transfer. Arctic Ocean metatranscriptomes revealed the acetone carboxylase and rhodopsins genes were among the most highly expressed P. arcticus genes in oligotrophic Arctic surface waters. P. arcticus sequences were consistently detected, and often abundant (up to 9%), in a multiyear Arctic Ocean 16S rRNA time-series, supporting its ecological significance in Arctic marine systems. Overall, this work reports a metabolic module (acetone carboxylation) in the ocean that may allow photoheterotrophic bacteria to enhance their biosynthetic capacity via CO2 assimilation.

papers.abstract_en: Layered oxide cathodes have attracted worldwide attention due to environmentally friendliness, structural diversity, and economic benefits. However, poor long-term cycling and unsatisfactory rate performance hinder the practical application. Hence, an oxide cathode with self-adaptive volume has been designed, achieving stable capacity retention of 82% after 1000 cycles at 2 C. The enhanced long-term performance is attributed to its dynamically adjustable volume reducing the acceleration of stress, enabled by a tunable interlayer distance that expands at the beginning of the charging process and then compresses at the highest voltage. Uniform electric field distribution is depicted by 4-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy showing even Coulombic interactions between the oxide layers leading to high mechanical integrity. Such self-adaptable behavior originates from the reduced repulsive force between interlayered oxygen due to the charge reconfiguration of intralayer oxygen and transition metal ions. Additionally, the charge compensation behavior is detected by in situ X-ray absorption spectra, which would be beneficial to high-rate performance. The self-adaptive volume change driven by charge reconfiguration provides a pathway toward durable materials for sustainable sodium-ion energy storage.

papers.abstract_en: Piezoelectric surface acoustic wave devices can drive charge carriers in semiconductors through the acoustoelectric effect, generating direct currents with potential applications in sensing and biomedicine. The device also supports wireless excitation and accelerates wound healing in a rat full-thickness skin defect model under low-intensity electrical stimulation. These results establish a wireless acoustoelectric platform for stable, tunable, and miniaturized current delivery, suggesting potential for biomedical applications.

papers.abstract_en: Diurnal asymmetric warming profoundly affects lake thermodynamics and aquatic ecosystems, yet its large-scale patterns and drivers remain poorly understood. Here we analyze diurnal surface temperature trends of 613 lakes across China from 2001 to 2025, disentangling climatic and anthropogenic contributions. Nighttime warming drives long-term lake warming nationally, with 84.01% of lakes showing a nighttime-dominant pattern. Nighttime lake surface water temperature (LSWT) rose at +0.34 °C decade-1, while daytime LSWT cooled at -0.24 °C decade-1. Daytime LSWT is primarily controlled by air temperature, whereas nighttime LSWT is dominated by downwelling longwave radiation, with human footprint exerting a persistent influence across the diurnal cycle. Lake area expansion correlates negatively with daytime warming and positively with nighttime warming nationwide, while anthropogenic activity further amplifies this asymmetry, most strongly in the Eastern Plain lakes. These findings highlight nighttime warming as the dominant force in Chinese lake thermal evolution, informing future conservation and management.

papers.abstract_en: Targeted biomolecular modification requires recognizing and binding to extended sequence domains, which can limit product dissociation rates and, therefore, catalytic efficiency. Product removal by downstream enzymes or condensates, common in biological catalysis, pushes catalytic reactions toward product formation, but cannot overcome intrinsically low product off-rates. Here, we demonstrate that designed affinity reagents, termed scavengers, can actively displace a product from an enzyme. Designed scavengers for three nucleic acid enzymes increase catalytic turnover up to 39-fold. Additionally, co-localizing enzymes and substrates, but not scavengers, within a biomolecular condensate further enhances >6-fold in catalytic rate by biasing productive substrate-enzyme interaction over inhibitory substrate-scavenger complexation. Scavenging and colocalization can be combined into a single generalizable and programmable framework, multiphase-controlled product scavenging (MCPS). By enabling rapid and exquisitely specific biomolecular modification, MCPS could lead to the development of potent nucleic acid enzyme therapeutics or efficient, controllable pathways for biomolecular modification, cleavage, and synthesis.

papers.abstract_en: Dengue is the canonical viral disease for which immune history is a determinant of protective versus pathogenic responses and immunogenicity. Yet, because of limitations in animal models and clinical presentation after peak viremia, how preinfection and early immune responses affect dengue outcome is not confirmed. We conducted a phase 1 clinical trial with 45 healthy adults to test whether secondary infection challenge with a heterotypic, full-length, attenuated virus increases viremia and immunogenicity compared with primary and tertiary infection. Viremia was associated with more, but still mild, clinical signs and symptoms, and secondary infection resulted in greater viremia, neutralizing antibodies, and protective T cell responses. However, those whose baseline antibodies most efficiently increased dengue virus replication in an in vitro assay experienced delayed inflammatory and adaptive immune activation, the highest viremia, strong acute immune responses, and waning of potent CD8+ T cells and antibodies. papers.abstract_en: Synovitis is a central driver of osteoarthritis (OA) progression, yet the cellular and molecular mechanisms sustaining inflammatory circuits in the synovium remain incompletely understood. Through integrative analysis of time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing in murine synovium and spatial transcriptomics of human OA tissues, we identified a pathogenic CD74+ macrophage subset that expands in OA and localizes at the synovial-cartilage interface. This subset exhibits a proinflammatory, nonclassical polarization and displays a metabolic dependency on glycolysis. Multiomics and mechanistic studies revealed that CD74 interacts with the glycolytic enzyme enolase 2 (ENO2). This interaction orchestrates a feed-forward signaling axis wherein CD74/ENO2 facilitates the nuclear translocation of hypoxia-inducible factor 1-α (HIF-1α)/β-catenin dimers, which coactivate glycolytic and inflammatory gene programs, thereby sustaining a metabolically driven inflammatory state. Genetic ablation of CD74 in myeloid cells or its pharmacological blockade mitigated synovitis and cartilage degradation in murine OA models. To translate this axis therapeutically, we developed synovium-targeted cationic lipid nanoparticles decorated with MIF-mimetic peptides (PcLNPs) for the delivery of CD74 siRNA. Intra-articular administration of PcLNPs efficiently targeted CD74+ macrophages, attenuated their inflammatory and glycolytic phenotypes, and ameliorated murine OA progression in vivo. Our findings establish the CD74/ENO2/HIF-1α/β-catenin axis as a critical integrator of metabolic reprogramming and inflammation in OA synovitis and present a potential targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for disease modification.

papers.abstract_en: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by hyperproliferative keratinocytes and a dysregulated cytokine milieu, perpetuating a self-reinforcing inflammatory cycle. Despite the key involvement of keratinocytes in this pathogenic loop, the molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify chitinase-like protein CHI3L2 as a key mediator. Elevated CHI3L2 levels were detected in serum and lesional skin from patients with psoriasis, predominantly in keratinocytes, as also verified by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses. In vitro stimulation of keratinocytes with M5 cytokine cocktail (IL-17A, IL-22, oncostatin M, IL-1α, and TNF-α) increased CHI3L2 expression, demonstrating that CHI3L2 is inducible under inflammatory conditions. Transgenic mice expressing human CHI3L2 exhibited aggravated psoriasis-like phenotypes in both imiquimod- and mannan-induced psoriasis models, characterized by epidermal hyperplasia and scaling. To dissect the role of CHI3L2, we used recombinant protein injection, parabiosis, and bone marrow transplantation, identifying keratinocytes as the primary source of pathogenic CHI3L2. This was further confirmed by keratinocyte-specific CHI3L2 knockin mice. CHI3L2 functions in the HaCaT cell line and primary keratinocytes were investigated by recombinant CHI3L2 administration or CHI3L2 knockout. CHI3L2 disrupted phospholipid homeostasis, leading to altered inflammatory responses, proliferation, and differentiation of keratinocytes. CHI3L2 activated secretory phospholipase A2, elevating lysophosphatidylcholine, thereby establishing an autocrine loop perpetuating keratinocyte inflammation and reshaping the immune microenvironment. Therapeutic neutralization of CHI3L2 with antibodies or intervention of phospholipid pathway ameliorated skin inflammation in mouse psoriasis models. Our findings reveal CHI3L2 as an important regulator of keratinocyte-driven lipid remodeling and inflammation in psoriasis, highlighting potential as a therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_en: Infected wounds present a high clinical incidence, and current treatments are inadequate in both effectively eliminating bacterial biofilms and continuously promoting tissue regeneration. To address these challenges, we develop a microwave-responsive thermoelectric nanocomposite of zinc oxide-bismuth telluride (ZnO-Bi2Te3) via hydrothermal synthesis for the treatment of biofilm infected wounds. The heterointerface within the nanocomposite enhances phonon scattering, while the ZnO component provides additional charge carrier transport pathways, collectively significantly improving the thermoelectric conversion performance. Under microwave irradiation, the ZnO-Bi2Te3 rapidly generates substantial amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS), enabling efficient penetration and eradication of biofilms with an antibacterial rate of 99.2%. After irradiation ceases, the ZnO-Bi2Te3 utilizes the wound-environment temperature difference to continuously produce thermoelectric signals. The continuous thermoelectric signals, in synergy with the release of zinc ions, activate the MAPK pathway and promote protein synthesis, processing, and transport, thereby enhancing cell migration, differentiation, and angiogenesis, leading to continuous tissue regeneration. In a mouse model of MRSA-biofilm infected wounds, the ZnO-Bi2Te3 loaded microneedles effectively clear the infection and accelerate healing. This study develops a microwave-responsive thermoelectric system for infected wounds through efficient biofilm clearance and sustained pro-regeneration.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma (PMBCL) is a highly curable lymphoma in which first-line therapy must balance durable disease control with acute and late treatment toxicity. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 98 patients with newly diagnosed PMBCL who received sintilimab plus R-CHOP (group 1, n = 42) or DA-EPOCH-R (group 2, n = 56). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), and secondary endpoints included complete metabolic response (CMR) and safety. Propensity-score matching (PSM) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for baseline imbalances. Molecular profiling was performed in 75 diagnostic samples to characterize immune-escape features, including 9p24.1 alterations and PD-L1/PD-L2 expression. RESULTS: Sintilimab plus R-CHOP produced numerically comparable response and PFS outcomes to DA-EPOCH-R, although equivalence or non-inferiority cannot be inferred from this retrospective, event-limited cohort. CMR rates were 85.7% versus 83.9% before matching (Fisher P = 1.000) and 83.3% versus 80.6% after PSM (P = 1.000; 36 pairs). Estimated 24-, 36-, and 60-month PFS rates were 81.0% versus 83.9% before matching (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.46-3.09; log-rank P = 0.716), 83.3% versus 80.6% after matching (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.28-2.51; P = 0.759), and 83.9% versus 84.6% after IPTW (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.39-2.76; robust P = 0.942), respectively. These estimates were based on 17 PFS events in the full cohort and 13 events after matching. Grade 3-4 neutropenia was less frequent with sintilimab plus R-CHOP before matching (38.1% versus 66.1%; P = 0.008) and remained lower after matching (30.6% versus 61.1%; P = 0.017). In 75 profiled diagnostic samples, group-level molecular data confirmed the expected immune-escape architecture of PMBCL and showed broadly similar distributions of 9p24.1 alterations and PD-L1/PD-L2 expression between treatment groups. CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, sintilimab plus R-CHOP produced overlapping response and PFS estimates relative to DA-EPOCH-R, together with less grade 3-4 neutropenia. The study cannot establish equivalence, non-inferiority, treatment replacement, or radiotherapy omission. These findings support the biological rationale for integrating PD-1 blockade into frontline chemoimmunotherapy and highlight the need for prospective studies to define its role within PET-adapted and immune-driven treatment strategies for PMBCL.

papers.abstract_en: Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm infections pose a severe clinical challenge due to antibiotic resistance driven by quorum sensing (QS). As the master regulator of the P. aeruginosa QS hierarchy, LasR controls biofilm initiation and key virulence factors, establishing it as a high-value therapeutic target. Mechanistically, transcriptomics revealed selective suppression of LasR-regulated virulence pathways, reducing pyocyanin production and bacterial motility. Pharmacokinetic profiling further demonstrated favorable oral bioavailability (26.8%) and a wide safety margin. This work establishes 2g as a machine learning-optimized LasR inhibitor with potent antibiofilm activity and synergistic antibiotic enhancement, offering a translatable strategy against multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa infections.

papers.abstract_en: Macrophages within advanced atherosclerotic lesions typically exhibit impaired efferocytosis and tend to adopt a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype, leading to the progression of atherosclerosis. Despite this challenge, the development of biocompatible nanotherapeutics capable of effectively remodeling macrophage efferocytosis and phenotype remains elusive. Here, we developed engineered targeted-peptide-modified nanocarriers (PP) and demonstrated their potential to restore macrophage efferocytosis while promoting re-polarization towards an anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotype. Furthermore, PP efficiently facilitated the delivery of an inflammation-resolving-drug to lesional macrophages within advanced atherosclerotic lesions. This combination approach substantially enhanced the anti-atherosclerotic efficacy of PP-based nanomedicine, effectively ameliorating atherosclerosis progression. This study not only underscores the new pleiotropic effects of PP to restore macrophage efferocytosis and modulate macrophage phenotype, but also highlights the promising potential of PP for the treatment of atherosclerosis and diseases associated with macrophage dysfunction.
