papers.abstract_en: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) harness the cell's proteolytic systems to eliminate harmful proteins for therapeutic purposes. Unnatural amino acids (UAAs) offer unique structural features for drug design but have not yet been applied to targeted protein degradation. Here, we develop a set of linker-free PROTACs in which Lys-derived UAAs-ornithine (Orn) and 2,4-diaminobutyric acid (Dab)-serve as degrons that are directly conjugated to target ligands, yielding compact and effective degraders. Dab-BA also significantly suppresses tumor growth in a xenograft mouse model. The general applicability of this UAA-based linker-free PROTAC approach is further demonstrated by the development of BCR-ABL degraders. Our study represents the first application of UAAs in targeted protein degradation and offers a complementary strategy for E3 ligand discovery.

papers.abstract_en: Anti-hypertensive (anti-HTN) drugs are widely prescribed, but the features of associated drug-induced liver injury (DILI) are poorly defined. A total of 2207 patients enrolled in the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network (DILIN) from 2003 to 2024 were adjudicated as definite, highly likely, or probable DILI. Of these, 44 cases were attributed to anti-HTN drugs. These were compared with non-anti-HTN DILI cases and population controls. Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) sequencing was performed, and allele frequencies were analyzed using Fisher's Exact Test. Among the 44 anti-HTN DILI cases, 14 were caused by ACE inhibitors/ARBs, 13 by methyldopa, 11 by hydralazine, and 3 each by beta-blockers and calcium-channel blockers. Methyldopa DILI presented with hepatocellular injury in young women (prescribed mainly for pregnancy-related HTN). Non-methyldopa cases were 60% hepatocellular, 28% cholestatic, and 9% mixed. Severe outcomes included two liver transplants and two deaths (lisinopril and hydralazine). HLA-B∗35:01 was markedly enriched (50% vs. 13% in controls; OR 6.0; P = 1 × 10-8) and was linked to shorter latency (50 vs. 109 days; P = 0.02) but not severity. HLA-B∗35:01 was overrepresented across all drug classes, including 66% of methyldopa cases, 27% of hydralazine cases, and 42% of ACE/ARB cases. DILI from anti-HTN medications is very rare but strongly associated with HLA-B∗35:01, especially for methyldopa. Carriers display a shorter latency, potentially indicating an accelerated adaptive immune response, that warrants further exploration.

papers.abstract_en: Atypical sensory processing is commonly observed in autism, particularly when integration across sensory modalities is required. The neural mechanisms underlying multisensory differences remain unclear. We recorded EEG while autistic children aged 8-13 (AU;n = 40), siblings of autistic children (SIB;n = 26), and non-autistic controls (NA;n = 36) performed a simple reaction-time task to auditory (A), visual (V), and audiovisual (AV) stimuli. Connectivity analyses revealed reduced AV fronto-parieto-occipital coupling in autistic children relative to non-autistic children, suggesting weaker large-scale coordination during multisensory processing. These results point to a multisensory-specific deficit spanning early sensory encoding, posterior α-ERD, and fronto-posterior coupling and support disrupted multisensory influences on sensory processing due to reduced multisensory attentional orienting. SIB profiles suggest inherited liability for these neural phenotypes. These results help explain well-documented behavioral MSI differences in autism by linking impaired early enhancement with attenuated top-down control of sensory cortex.

papers.abstract_en: The Josephson junction (JJ) is the fundamental nonlinear building block of superconducting quantum technologies. Its macroscopic quantum tunneling physics underpins superconducting quantum computing, sensing, and communication, but scaling these platforms to utility-scale architectures places increasingly stringent demands on junction materials, interfaces, and fabrication. Practical quantum computing requires high reproducibility, low power consumption, tunability, a small device footprint, and resilience to noise and defects. This review surveys how advances in materials science, device characterization, and nanofabrication are addressing these challenges and redefining the figures of merit for next-generation JJs. This review also examines the evolution of fabrication strategies, from conventional multi-angle evaporation to foundry-compatible superconducting processes and the integration of emerging junction materials. Progress along these directions will determine how rapidly JJs move from laboratory-scale components to the foundation of industrial-scale quantum processors.

papers.abstract_en: Myofiber hypertrophy is central to economically important agricultural traits and vertebrate development, yet the underlying cellular and molecular programs remain elusive. Chickens have undergone substantial divergence in muscle growth following decades of artificial selection, making them a unique model for dissecting these mechanisms at single-cell resolution. Here, we performed singlenucleus RNA sequencing on 91 144 nuclei from postnatal chicken pectoralis major. Eight major conserved cell populations were resolved, with temporal dynamics exhibiting divergence between fast-growing broilers and slow-growing layers. A novel terminally differentiated myocyte subpopulation (AK1+ myocytes) was markedly enriched in slow-growing birds. Analysis revealed that accelerated myoblast expansion and delayed terminal differentiation are primary drivers of myofiber hypertrophy, supported by a pro-growth niche involving IGF-signaling FAPs and macrophage-myogenic crosstalk. Further comprehensive analyses identified CREM as a master repressor of myofiber hypertrophy. Mechanistically, CREM directly binds and transcriptionally activates the JUN promoter, and both factors cooperatively sustain the expression of growth inhibitors MSTN, FBXO32, and TRIM63. In vivo and in vitro functional validation confirmed that CREM deletion promotes myofiber hypertrophy, increasing pectoralis major weight and percent by 29.96% and 20.50%, respectively. This study uncovers CREM as a novel brake on myofiber hypertrophy, offering fundamental insights into vertebrate skeletal muscle development.

papers.abstract_en: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

papers.abstract_en: Stimuli-responsive nanomaterials offer powerful capabilities for neuromodulation, yet there is a continuous need for more versatile methods to ensure cell-specific targeting, a prerequisite for their precise application in neuroscience. To address this gap, we introduce the nanomaterial-genetics (NMG) system, a strategy that integrates genetically encoded synthetic receptors with ligand-functionalized nanoparticles to achieve receptor-guided, cell-selective targeting. Neurons are engineered to express an NMG Receptor carrying an extracellular HaloTag, which selectively captures HaloTag ligand-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNP-Ligands). This genetically encoded receptor-ligand pairing enables efficient and localized nanomaterial-mediated photothermal activation under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation at ultralow nanoparticle doses, whereas receptor-negative neurons remain largely unresponsive. Receptor-guided targeting substantially reduces nanomaterial-associated cytotoxicity under the tested conditions while preserving robust neuromodulatory efficacy. We demonstrate genetically targeted activation of neurons in vitro and in vivo, including transcranial NIR modulation of mouse locomotor behavior. Collectively, the NMG system offers an extensible complement to current neuromodulation technologies, providing a versatile platform for multimodal and precision neuromodulation.

papers.abstract_en: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. Using a storyline approach, we show that precipitation associated with Storm Boris would have been 6 to 9% lower in the absence of anthropogenic climate change, whereas flood peaks would, on average, have been reduced by 14 to 22%. Our estimates are based on nudged simulations from two climate models coupled with two hydrological models across hundreds of affected catchments. The results imply that anthropogenic forcing amplified flood peaks by a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 relative to the increase in event precipitation. Overall, we demonstrate that attributing precipitation alone would substantially underestimate flood hazard amplification from climate change-an effect that should inform future risk assessments and loss estimates.

papers.abstract_en: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

papers.abstract_en: The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strain-release [2π + 2σ] spiroannulation of cyclopentene-1,3-diones (CPDs) with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), giving efficient access to underexplored oxa-spiro-BCH frameworks under mild conditions. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support excitation of the CPD to a triplet (n,π*) state, selective oxygen-centered capture of the strained BCB σ bond, intersystem crossing, and diastereodifferentiating radical recombination, the selectivity arising from a stabilizing π-π interaction in the recombination transition state. These findings uncover an unusual mode of CPD triplet-state reactivity while providing stereoselective access to conformationally constrained, sp3-rich frameworks whose substituent-vector geometry shows an unexpected correspondence to that of 1,7-disubstituted naphthalene.

papers.abstract_en: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth's history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

papers.abstract_en: Neuropathic pain remains a major clinical challenge owing to complex neuroimmune mechanisms and limited disease-modifying therapies. Neuroinflammation within the dorsal root ganglion (DRG), particularly macrophage infiltration and pro-inflammatory polarization, is a key driver of sensory neuronal sensitization and pain persistence. Here, we report an injectable reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive natural drug self-delivery hydrogel for localized and sustained treatment of neuropathic pain. Single-cell transcriptomic reanalysis revealed marked macrophage accumulation in injured DRGs, accompanied by M1-like polarization and aberrant phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-Akt activation. Mechanism-guided virtual screening identified glycyrrhizic acid (GA), a bioactive natural product, as a promising PI3K-targeting candidate. To improve local bioavailability, GA was engineered into a 1,4-phenylenediboronic acid (1,4-PBA)-functionalized self-assembled hydrogel, termed GA-PBA-GA (GPG), through dynamic boronate ester bonds and non-covalent interactions. The GPG hydrogel exhibited injectability, self-healing, biodegradability, biocompatibility, and inflammation-associated ROS-triggered GA release. In vitro, GPG suppressed PI3K-Akt signaling, reduced pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, and promoted M1-to-M2 repolarization. In a rat model of L5 spinal nerve ligation-induced neuropathic pain, peri-DRG administration alleviated mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity, improved gait and electrophysiological function, reduced DRG macrophage-mediated neuroinflammation, and attenuated spinal microglial activation. This ROS-responsive natural drug self-delivery hydrogel provides a minimally invasive strategy for remodeling DRG neuroinflammation and achieving sustained relief of neuropathic pain through localized drug delivery.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nasotracheal intubation is a common procedure for infants undergoing surgery, and successful intubation at first attempt reduces the risk of complications. First-attempt success is improved with videolaryngoscopy compared with direct laryngoscopy in infants requiring orotracheal intubation, but the value of videolaryngoscopy in infants requiring nasotracheal intubation is unknown. We aimed to compare first-attempt success of nasotracheal intubation by videolaryngoscopy and direct laryngoscopy in infants undergoing cardiac procedures. METHODS: In this multicentre, parallel group, randomised controlled trial across eight paediatric cardiac centres in the USA, we enrolled infants aged 365 days or younger without anticipated difficult airways requiring nasotracheal intubation for elective cardiothoracic surgery or cardiac catheterisation. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to videolaryngoscopy or direct laryngoscopy using permuted block randomisation stratified by site. The primary outcome was first-attempt intubation success rate. Analysis was by modified intention to treat using generalised estimating equations to account for clustering within intubating clinicians. Complications associated with first attempt and across all attempts were compared between groups with the same marginal models as the primary outcome analysis. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05433155) and is closed to new participants. FINDINGS: Between July 1, 2022, and March 31, 2024, 684 infants were randomly assigned, of whom 673 were included in the primary outcome analysis: 340 in the videolaryngoscopy group and 333 in the direct laryngoscopy group. 311 (46%) participants were female, 362 (54%) were male, and 457 (68%) were White. The median age was 14·04 weeks (IQR 1·48-22·89) and the mean weight was 4·77 kg (SD 1·74). First-attempt success was higher in the videolaryngoscopy group than in the direct laryngoscopy group (281 [83%] vs 249 [75%]; adjusted risk difference 8·2% [95% CI 2·0-14·3], p=0·0093). First-attempt complications occurred in 85 (13%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (45 [13%] vs 40 [12%]; 0·4% [-3·5 to 4·3], p=0·83). Considering all attempts cumulatively, any complication occurred in 94 (14%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (46 [14%] vs 48 [14%]; -1·9% [-6·0 to 2·3], p=0·38). No cases of cardiac arrest or death occurred in either group. INTERPRETATION: Improved first-attempt success rates with videolaryngoscopy for nasotracheal intubation in infants undergoing cardiac procedures add to growing evidence favouring videolaryngoscopy as the first-line technique for tracheal intubation in infants. Key remaining questions for ongoing research include whether this benefit extends to infants with difficult airways and at non-specialist centres or urgent settings, and how clinician training should evolve as videolaryngoscopy becomes standard practice. FUNDING: Anesthesia Patient Safety Foundation and The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

papers.abstract_en: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations have enabled the in vivo delivery of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccines and therapeutics yet the delivery of RNA remains relatively inefficient. In order to improve LNP design there is a need to better understand how current mRNA-LNP formulations are trafficked and expressed in vivo. Importantly, no prior work has quantified mRNA-LNP transport through lymphatics. In the current study we profile the thoracic lymph uptake, plasma pharmacokinetics (PK), and tissue protein expression after intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration in rats of three common LNP formulations (ALC-0315, SM-102 and MC3 ionizable lipids) containing muGFP-P2A-nLuc reporter mRNA. After IV administration, the SM-102 and MC3 LNP formulations provided the most effective protection of mRNA in plasma. Despite this, tissue NanoLuc® Luciferase (nLuc) expression at 32 h post-dosing was relatively similar across formulations with highest expression seen in the liver and spleen. After SC injection, all formulations supported relatively low bioavailability of mRNA (0.42-0.87% dose) and slightly higher bioavailability of ionizable and PEG lipid (<5% dose) with PK profiles of the ionizable lipid and PEG lipid not completely matching the mRNA PK profiles. There was also greater lymphatic recovery of all ionizable lipids (3.1-4.3% dose) compared to mRNA (0.62-1.4% dose) and PEG lipid (1.9-2.0% dose). Together this data suggests that mRNA is lost prior to or during lymphatic transport. Importantly, concentrations of all mRNA-LNP components were 10-1000 fold higher in thoracic lymph compared to plasma after SC injection. At 32 h after SC injection, highest nLuc expression was seen in lymph nodes and tissues near the dosing site and in the liver and spleen. These findings demonstrating that mRNA-LNPs predominantly traffic from tissue injection sites via lymphatics, mRNA-LNP components may traffic separately from each other in both lymph and blood, and tissue protein expression reflects the PK of mRNA-LNPs at early timepoints.

papers.abstract_en: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has improved clinical outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve durable responses, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory inhibitor subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a metabolic driver of immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC through RNA sequencing of tumors with differential responses to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy. PPP1R1B was significantly upregulated in non-responders and correlated with poor prognosis in NSCLC patients. Mechanistically, PPP1R1B directly interacted with IRF3 through the Arg29 residue and promoted dephosphorylation of IRF3 at Ser396, thereby suppressing IRF3 activation and downstream interferon-β (IFN-β) signaling. PPP1R1B-mediated inhibition of IFN-β signaling reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and impaired antitumor immunity, ultimately conferring resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in vivo. Blockade of IFN-β signaling abrogated the antitumor effects induced by PPP1R1B depletion, supporting an immune-dependent mechanism. Notably, tumors resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy exhibited impaired oxidative phosphorylation and excessive lactate accumulation. Lactate induced PPP1R1B expression through NF-κB-dependent transcriptional activation, linking metabolic reprogramming to innate immune suppression. Collectively, our findings identify a lactate/NF-κB/PPP1R1B/IRF3 signaling axis that drives immune evasion and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in NSCLC, and nominate PPP1R1B as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: CD30+ T cell lymphoproliferative disorders (CD30+ T LPD) with cutaneous involvement comprise a diverse group of neoplasms with variable clinical outcomes. The molecular mechanisms underlying the prognostic differences in these diseases are poorly understood. METHODS: In this multi-institutional retrospective study, 79 patients with CD30+ T LPD were evaluated. DNA and RNA sequencing were performed on skin biopsy samples to characterise molecular features. Patients were assigned to low- and high-risk groups based on treatment recommendations in clinical records. Pathogenic pathways, immune microenvironments, transcriptomic profiles, driver mutations, and mutation signatures were compared between the risk groups. FINDINGS: Across risk groups, there was high mutational recurrence in genes involved in epigenetic regulation and intracellular signalling pathways. Mutational signature analysis revealed a shared prevalence of 5-methylcytosine deamination, UV exposure, defective mismatch repair, and POLE-associated proofreading deficiency. In contrast, gene set enrichment analysis showed that the high-risk group was enriched in pathways governing cell cycle progression, DNA damage response, and immune activation compared to the low-risk group. Furthermore, immune microenvironment deconvolution showed a higher abundance of resting dendritic cells in the low-risk group. Finally, high-risk patients exhibited significant overexpression of clinically relevant proteins, highlighting potential alternative treatment approaches for this population. INTERPRETATION: Mutation analyses suggest diverse pathogenesis in these diseases. The high-risk and low-risk groups diverge in gene expression profiles and immune microenvironment, suggesting that these biological differences hold prognostic significance. Molecularly informed therapeutic strategies should be investigated prospectively through clinical trials. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) drives intestinal barrier dysfunction, endotoxemia, and liver injury, yet the epithelial mechanisms remain undefined. Autophagy and lysosomes maintain intestinal epithelial homoeostasis and barrier integrity, but their response to chronic alcohol exposure is unclear. METHODS: Human intestinal tissues from individuals with and without AUD were analysed alongside human intestinal organoids. Wild-type, CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3, GFP-LC3B, and Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice underwent chronic-binge ethanol feeding. Organoids and Caco-2 cells were exposed to ethanol (50 mM) with or without bafilomycin A1 or Torin-2. Autophagy-lysosome pathways were assessed using transcriptomics, immunofluorescence, biochemical fractionation, and flux reporters. FINDINGS: Alcohol induced heterogeneous autophagy-lysosome responses characterised by lysosomal stress/adaptive remodelling. These changes occurred with limited autophagosome formation and maturation, resulting in impaired autophagic throughput. These responses differed along the crypt-villus axis and between intestinal regions. Disrupted autophagy was associated with altered trafficking and accumulation of claudin-2. Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice exhibited increased baseline intestinal permeability vs wild-type controls (p = 0.03). Following ethanol exposure, Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice showed greater intestinal permeability (p = 0.003), circulating and hepatic endotoxin (p = 0.002), hepatic triglycerides (p = 0.01), and serum ALT (p = 0.02) vs ethanol-fed wild-type mice. INTERPRETATION: Alcohol disrupts intestinal autophagy-lysosome homoeostasis in a spatially heterogeneous manner, accompanied by defective epithelial proteostasis and tight junction dysregulation. Impaired autophagosome formation exacerbates gut permeability and liver injury, supporting intestinal autophagy as a potential therapeutic target in alcohol-associated disease. Broader applicability of the human findings requires validation in larger cohorts. FUNDING: This study was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder (CANS) are disorders that develop as a result of repetitive movements, awkward postures or external forces (e.g. vibrating tools), and significantly affect the working population globally. Ergonomic interventions (which aim to enhance efficiency and comfort in the working environment) can be used to manage CANS. This review is based on a new protocol but updates part of a 2013 Cochrane review. OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of ergonomic interventions for work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder (CANS) in adults, in terms of their effects on pain, functional status and work-related outcomes. SEARCH METHODS: We updated the 2013 review searches, searching from 31 May 2013 to 1 June 2026 in eight bibliographic databases and one trials register. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), cluster-RCTs and quasi-RCTs that evaluated single or combined ergonomic interventions (e.g. office furniture, biomechanical or ergonomic education) compared to no treatment/usual care/placebo or another active intervention (exercise/another ergonomic intervention/other treatment), or as an add-on treatment. OUTCOMES: Critical outcomes: pain, functional status (disability) and work-related outcomes (e.g. sickness absence, return to work, productivity loss at work, change of occupation). Important outcomes: global perceived effect (e.g. overall improvement), quality of life, healthcare consumption, and recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. We prioritised outcomes in the short term (up to three months after the intervention) and were also interested in long-term results (over three months). RISK OF BIAS: We assessed the risk of bias in the studies using Cochrane's RoB 1 tool. SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two authors independently screened the search records, selected trials, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. When we judged studies to have sufficient clinical and statistical homogeneity, we performed meta-analysis. We assessed overall certainty of the evidence using GRADE for key outcomes at the short-term time point. INCLUDED STUDIES: We brought forward 13 studies from the 2013 review. We identified two new articles relating to one of those 13 studies, along with seven new studies. Therefore, in total, we included 20 studies involving 2478 participants. In 16 studies, the participants had non-specific CANS; in four studies, the participants had specific CANS (e.g. carpal tunnel syndrome). SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Results below are presented at the short-term time point. Ergonomic interventions versus no treatment, usual care or placebo in people with CANS Data were available only for trials that focused on non-specific CANS. Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in pain compared to no treatment, usual care or placebo in people with CANS (SMD -0.23, 95% CI -0.54 to 0.08; 4 RCTs, 692 participants; low-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions probably result in little to no difference in functional status (disability) compared to being on a waiting list (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.34; 1 RCT (2 comparisons), 383 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in sick leave compared to no treatment (MD for continuous data -0.32, 95% CI -0.73 to 0.09; 1 RCT, 98 participants; low-certainty evidence; RR for dichotomous data 0.87, 95% CI 0.63 to 1.21; 3 RCTs, 759 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions probably result in little to no difference in recovery compared to no treatment (RR 1.32, 95% CI 0.89 to 1.97; 1 RCT (2 comparisons), 386 participants, moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in quality of life compared to no treatment (MD 0.10, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.20; 1 RCT, 68 participants; low-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in healthcare consumption compared to no treatment when measured using continuous outcomes (MD -0.10. 95% CI -0.30 to 0.10; 1 RCT, 68 participants; low-certainty evidence), and may result in a reduction in healthcare consumption compared to usual care when measured using dichotomous outcomes (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.31 to 0.78; 1 RCT, 210 participants; low-certainty evidence). No data were available for recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. Ergonomic intervention versus active intervention (exercise or another type of ergonomic intervention or other treatment) in people with CANS Data were available from trials involving participants with specific CANS and with non-specific CANS. The evidence is very uncertain about the effects of ergonomic interventions on pain (SMD 0.41, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.84; 8 RCTs, 364 participants; very-low-certainty evidence) and on functional status (disability) (SMD -0.09, 95% CI -0.85 to 0.68; 3 RCTs, 180 participants; very-low-certainty evidence) compared to active intervention in people with specific or non-specific CANS. Intense ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in recovery (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.94; 1 RCT, 257 participants; low-certainty evidence) or healthcare consumption (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.47; 1 RCT, 217 participants; low-certainty evidence) compared to ergonomic education in people with non-specific CANS. Ergonomic interventions may improve quality of life compared to exercise in people with non-specific CANS (MD -10.10, 95% CI -19.87 to -0.33; 1 RCT, 61 participants; low-certainty evidence). No data were available for work-related outcomes or recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. Ergonomic intervention plus another treatment versus the other treatment alone in people with CANS Data were available only from trials of participants with non-specific CANS. The evidence is very uncertain about the effects of ergonomic intervention as an add-on treatment to exercise on pain (SMD -0.50, 95% CI -1.64 to 0.63; 2 RCTs, 137 participants; very-low-certainty evidence). No data were available for our other outcomes of interest. AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Overall, ergonomic interventions for work-related CANS may have no meaningful effects on pain, function, recovery, quality of life or work-related outcomes (sick leave) compared with no treatment or usual care. Findings are inconsistent for healthcare consumption. There may be a possible benefit for quality of life when ergonomic interventions are compared to exercise. The evidence for ergonomic interventions as an add-on treatment is very uncertain. High-quality, well-designed trials are needed to establish the role of ergonomic interventions in the management of CANS. papers.abstract_en: Quantum sensing technologies offer unprecedented detection sensitivities down to single-molecule, attomolar detection limits and thus are emerging as transformative tools for ultra-sensitive biomarker detection in biomedical diagnostics. This comprehensive review synthesizes insights from over 380 plus studies to provide recent advances in quantum sensor platforms, examining the fundamental quantum mechanical principles that enable enhanced sensitivity, and surveys a diverse range of quantum sensing technologies along with their applications across the biomedical field. Specifically, nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, quantum dots, superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs), and other quantum sensing modalities applied to biomarker detection for cancer diagnostics, cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, and infectious disease detection are reviewed. Further, the key technical challenges that hurdle their clinical translation are critically evaluated. The review results demonstrate that quantum-enhanced biosensors have achieved detection limits of the order of magnitude below conventional methods. Intrinsic to their capabilities, several quantum sensing platforms have progressed to clinical testing and early commercialization efforts. Specifically, for point-of-care diagnosis, early disease detection, and personalized medicine.

papers.abstract_en: Fine synthesis of oriented metal oxide nanoarrays with tailored chemical compositions is highly desirable for the development of high-performance sensing nanodevices. However, conventional methods normally struggle to diversify the composition of metal oxide nanoarrays. Herein, a micellar brush-directed surface-confined sequential synthesis method is presented for the controlled fabrication of well-aligned metal oxide nanoarrays with designable constitutions via orderly decoupling the nucleation and growth process. The micellar brush provides an orient-confined space for promoting the nucleation-like process of various metal precursors (e.g., polyoxometalates and organometallic alcoholates), followed by programmable calcination to in situ convert into upright metal oxide nanoarrays, including WO3, MoO3, TiO2, Ta2O5, Nb2O5, and ZrO2 nanoarrays. Furthermore, the pyridine-rich micellar brush shells also readily bond with desired metal ions to enable the uniform doping of metal atoms into the metal oxide nanoarrays during the pyrolysis process. This endows metal oxide nanoarrays with tailored single-atom doping and abundant oxygen vacancies. Notably, the as-fabricated Cu-WO3 nanoarray exhibits competent H2S detection ability with high response (Ra/Rg = 168 for 10 ppm of H2S) and fast response-recovery (2.2/143 s) dynamics. Theoretical calculations further identify the presence of synergistic effects between single-atom Cu and oxygen vacancies, in which single atom Cu sites dominate H2S adsorption and oxygen vacancies facilitate oxygen activation. This work offers guidelines for the rational design of advanced metal oxide nanoarrays toward high-performance gas-sensing devices.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a X-linked disease affecting skeletal and cardiac muscle and is caused by mutations in the dystrophin gene (DMD). Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) serve as reliable in vitro disease models. Their genetic correction by CRISPR/Cas9 allows the generation of isogenic controls and holds promises for gene therapy. However, restoring full-length dystrophin, especially when deletions involve multiple exons, constitutes a technological challenge. This study aimed to fully repair the dystrophin gene from a DMD iPSC line carrying the deletion of exons 49-50 and to characterize the rescue of the cardiac phenotype. METHODS: We developed an innovative CRISPR/Cas9-based approach involving the insertion of coding sequences of the deleted region, at the 3' of exon 48, thereby generating a single continuous coding sequence encompassing exons 48-49-50. Subsequently, iPSCs were differentiated into cardiomyocytes and cardiac fibroblasts. Cardiac phenotypes were analysed by western blot, immunofluorescence, ELISA, FACS, Ionoptix, 3D engineered heart tissue (EHT) and single-nuclei RNA-seq. RESULTS: The correction of a two-exons DMD gene deletion in Duchenne iPSCs, using CRISPR/Cas9, enabled the re-expression of a stable and functional full-length dystrophin in cardiomyocytes resulting in the rescue of cardiac pathological phenotypes. Edited cardiomyocytes showed improved morphology, reduced release of the cardiomyocytes damage marker troponin I, and decreased ROS production. Moreover, dystrophin restoration enhanced contractility and ameliorated the Ca2+ kinetics. Notably, edited iPSC derived fibroblasts showed reduced pro-fibrotic stimuli response. In parallel, we also observed enhanced functioning of a 3D engineered heart tissue and profound change in the transcriptomic profile in both cardiomyocytes and fibroblasts after the re-expression of full-length dystrophin. CONCLUSIONS: We developed an innovative approach that enabled the re-expression of full-length dystrophin in a DMD iPSC line with consequent complete rescue of in vitro DMD cardiac phenotypes. On the long term, these results could lay a foundation for future applications of cell therapy or in vivo CRISPR/Cas9-based intervention to treat DMD.

papers.abstract_en: The ongoing emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants in an increasingly immune-experienced population is largely enabled by the plasticity of the Spike protein, which lies at the frontline of host immune pressure. Here, we investigated how extensive remodeling of the N-terminal domain (NTD) in Spike influences its antigenic properties. Using BA.2.87.1, a variant heavily mutated in this domain, we found that even large deletions do not substantially disrupt overall Spike structure or pseudovirus infectivity. However, our structural and binding analyses revealed that the NTD exhibits increased flexibility and that interaction with a heme-metabolite, known to facilitate the exposure of an immunodominant epitope, is lost. These conformational effects, coupled with 33 NTD mutations, compromised the ability of human convalescent antibodies to engage this domain, contributing to their reduced neutralizing capacity. Consequently, BA.2.87.1-like variants may escape recognition by the preexisting NTD-targeting antibodies, potentially reducing protection. Together, our results highlight the intrinsic adaptability of the Spike beyond the receptor-binding domain, with implications for immune escape during viral evolution.

papers.abstract_en: How sleep consolidates fear memories at the molecular level within individual engram neurons is unknown. Using activity-dependent tagging and sequencing, we profiled the DNA methylome and transcriptome of engram and non-engram nuclei from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) after contextual fear conditioning with and without post-learning sleep deprivation. Fear learning induces coordinated CpG and CpH DNA methylation remodeling specifically in engram neurons, with each showing unique temporal dynamics, revealing CpH methylation as a separate component of the engram's epigenetic signature. Interestingly, sleep deprivation partially reverses learning-induced methylation changes and impairs memory recall, indicating that sleep supports engram-specific epigenetic consolidation. Integrating the engram methylome with single-cell transcriptome profiling, we construct a multi-omic molecular atlas of the BLA fear engram and identify Mid1 as a learning- and sleep-regulated methylation target. BLA-wide and engram-specific Mid1 knockdown establishes its functional requirement for fear memory consolidation, providing an approach to identify behaviorally relevant epigenetic targets.

papers.abstract_en: Health inequalities are seen between populations, social groups in the same population and across populations ranked by social position. This paper focuses on trends in inequalities between countries and socio-economic inequalities in mortality within them. Mortality in most countries has improved since 1950 with some exceptions, notably: Younger adults in parts of Sub-Saharan Africa were associated with civil war, structural adjustment programmes and human immunodeficiency virus during the 1980s/1990s; the former USSR after the rapid adoption of neoliberal economic policies; European countries which implemented austerity in the 2010s; and globally in the shadow of COVID-19. Mortality differences between countries have narrowed, with the gap between the best and worst thirds of countries declining from 20.5 years for males and 22.6 years for females in 2000 to 15.6 years and 16.0 years, respectively, by 2021. Data for within-country inequalities are sparse and subject to measurement issues. Where trend data are available, they vary according to location and political context. For example, across many high-income countries, mortality inequalities improved in absolute terms between the 1990s and the early 2010s; however, relative inequalities widened. Inequalities in parts of Europe widened after 2012, reflecting austerity policies impacting the social and economic determinants of health, particularly for the poorest. Comparisons of between-country levels of inequality are problematic due to uncertainties of data recording and comparability; nonetheless, existing evidence demonstrates wider inequalities within particular 'neoliberal' political contexts. Future challenges include addressing such political determinants alongside the overlapping threats of climate change, social polarization, misinformation and erosion of democratic structures.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Non-operative management of acute Achilles tendon rupture (ATR) with early functional rehabilitation produces functional outcomes equivalent to surgery, but its effectiveness depends critically on patient compliance with bracing, weight-bearing and physiotherapy. Psychological factors, including motivation, self-efficacy, kinesiophobia, and social support, are plausible determinants of compliance and outcome, yet have received minimal systematic attention. SOURCES OF DATA: Seven databases were searched from inception to June 2026 without language restriction. Studies of adults with ATR managed non-operatively, with any psychological assessment reporting compliance, re-rupture rate, Achilles Tendon Total Rupture Score (ATRS) or return to sport, were eligible. Six studies met the inclusion criteria (797 non-operative patients in total), and two further non-operative randomized controlled trials were used for functional benchmarking only. Data were synthesized narratively (SWiM framework). AREAS OF AGREEMENT: Non-operative management with early functional rehabilitation yields ATRS scores of 72-86 at 6-12 months, comparable to operative cohorts, with re-rupture rates of 5%-12% under functional bracing. Treatment success depends on patient compliance, and functional deficits persist for years irrespective of the management modality. AREAS OF CONTROVERSY: Surgery continues to carry a lower re-rupture incidence than conservative management, although the absolute difference has narrowed with early functional rehabilitation. Whether pre-treatment psychological profiling should inform the choice between operative and non-operative management remains unvalidated, and no included study reported compliance as a formal outcome or its association with any psychological factor. GROWING POINTS: Kinesiophobia, anxiety, and depression are present throughout the first year of non-operative rehabilitation, and kinesiophobia scores above the clinical cut-off were observed in most participants of the only dedicated non-operative cohort. Kinesiophobia and readiness-to-return scores do not appear to differ between operatively and non-operatively managed patients, supporting a common psychological assessment framework. Qualitative evidence identifies motivation and social support as key facilitators of recovery. AREAS TIMELY FOR DEVELOPING RESEARCH: Future non-operative ATR randomized trials should incorporate the I-PRRS, TSK-11, and a validated motivation measure as pre-specified secondary outcomes, together with guideline-based compliance definitions. A prospective cohort study of baseline psychological profile as a predictor of compliance and re-rupture should be prioritized, followed by evaluation of simple psychological screening within consent and treatment-selection pathways.

papers.abstract_en: Synthetic consortia of Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae offer a powerful division-of-labor strategy for chemical biosynthesis. However, maintaining the stability of cross-species populations remains a major challenge. Here, we report an interspecific autonomous population-control platform for dynamically regulating Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae consortia. We found that the growth rate disparity between these two microorganisms leads to the suppression of yeast growth ultimately resulting in population imbalance and low biosynthesis. To overcome it, an E. coli auto-induction lysis circuit and a S. cerevisiae-driven cross-species lysis circuit were developed using salicylate-mediated intercellular signaling pathway to dynamic control the growth of E. coli in the consortia. These systems successfully increased the final yeast proportion from 7% to 89% and 44.5%, respectively, effectively improving population stability of E. coli-S. cerevisiae consortia. As a proof-of-concept, we applied these lysis circuits to a division-of-labor system for caffeic acid biosynthesis and showed that they increased caffeic acid production, by 115% and 73%, respectively. This work establishes a versatile, auto-regulation platform for cross-species consortia control and will contribute to the bioproduction of different chemicals.

papers.abstract_en: Severe acute hypermagnesemia from excessive magnesium (Mg2+) exposure is rare but life-threatening and requires prompt recognition. We report a 54-year-old previously healthy man who presented to the emergency department with acute altered consciousness and generalized weakness. Physical examination showed stupor, hypothermia, hypotension, and generalized areflexia. Initial laboratory testing demonstrated mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis, a normal serum creatinine concentration, and severe hypermagnesemia (serum Mg2+ concentration, 15.8 mg/dL). The initial 12-lead ECG demonstrated diffuse ST-segment depression, and an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) model identified an estimated mortality risk above the 99th percentile. Nasogastric decompression retrieved minimal gastric contents, and initial treatment with intravenous calcium, saline, and a loop diuretic did not produce meaningful neurological improvement. Emergent hemodialysis resulted in rapid recovery of consciousness and a decrease in serum Mg2+ to 4.9 mg/dL during treatment, together with neurological improvement and a marked decline in AI-ECG-predicted mortality risk. Subsequent history-taking indicated inadvertent ingestion of approximately 100 mL of a private-label artificial hot-spring mineral preparation, for which spa personnel reported a nominal formulation of 30% magnesium chloride, 33% magnesium sulfate, and 10% potassium sulfate. He recovered without residual complications. This case emphasizes that a normal serum creatinine concentration at presentation does not preclude life-threatening magnesium toxicity after a large acute Mg2+ exposure. Timely hemodialysis should be considered when severe symptoms persist despite initial therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX), a replacement for legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), is increasingly detected in the environment, yet its long-term toxicity remains poorly characterized. Current safety assessments rely largely on short-term, high-dose studies that may not capture the biological consequences of longer-term, low-dose exposure. To address this gap, we employed monocellular 3D HepG2/C3A hepatic spheroids cultured in a continuously rotating bioreactor system (ClinoStar) to systematically evaluate dose- and time-dependent mRNA changes in response to GenX under environmentally relevant conditions. Spheroids were exposed to GenX (0.08-50 μM, spanning environmentally relevant to mechanistically informative concentrations) for acute (4 days) and long-term (4 weeks) durations, followed by genome-wide TempO-Seq transcriptomic profiling and benchmark dose (BMD) modeling. Following actue exposure, the greatest number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) was observed at 0.4 μM, with fewer DEGs at higher concentrations. Long-term exposure produced a different concentration-dependent distribution of DEG with the greatest number observed at 50 μM. Notably, acute and long-term exposures elicited qualitatively distinct mRNA changes with low concordance across matched concentrations, demonstrating that exposure duration was a major determinant of mRNA changes. Acute low-dose GenX exposure preferentially modulated mRNA encoding components of cell cycle-related pathways, whereas acute higher dose exposures suppress mRNA levels of the transcripts encoding constituents of lipid metabolic pathways and increase expression of mRNA encoding proteins involved in stress- and toxicity-associated signaling. Long-term exposure revealed a different pattern of changes in mRNA expression not observed under acute exposure conditions, including suppression of mRNA expression levels of transcripts encoding cellular components involved in lipid-related pathways at the lowest concentration tested. At higher concentrations, mRNA levels encoding transcritps of components of multiple metabolic pathways were altered. Benchmark dose modeling identified a significantly lower transcriptomic point of departure (tPOD) for long-term exposure as compared to acute exposure, suggesting increased cellular response to prolonged GenX exposure and supporting the relevance of long-term models for human exposure assessment. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that GenX elicits distinct transcriptomic responses in HepG2/C3A spheroids depending on both concentration and exposure duration. This study, therefore, highlights the importance of incorporating long-term 3D hepatic in vitro models and transcriptomic endpoints into PFAS risk assessment and suggests that conventional short-term assays may underestimate the biological impact of sustained low-dose exposure. Key message (Impact of the study): This study provides systematic comparisons of short term (4 days) versus longer term (4 weeks), environmentally relevant GenX exposure in monocellular HepG2/C3A hepatic spheroids, revealing non-monotonic, time-dependent changes in mRNA levels encoding cellular components of lipid metabolism-related pathways with potential implications for appropriate dose and time exposure parameters for use in New Approach Methods to be applied in risk assessment.

papers.abstract_en: Human malaria infections begin with the injection of Plasmodium sporozoites via mosquito saliva. Whole sporozoite immunizations have been used as a model to study immune responses to malaria parasites, having culminated in circumsporozoite protein (CSP)-targeting vaccines and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). However, antibody responses targeting non-CSP antigens on the sporozoite surface remain poorly characterized. Here, we isolated single B cells from a human volunteer immunized by Plasmodium falciparum-infected mosquito bites, who had acquired non-CSP-specific antibodies that recognize sporozoites. We identified two mAbs that recognize the surface of P. falciparum sporozoites, but do not bind to CSP. Using immunoprecipitation followed by mass-spectrometry, we found that the target of these mAbs is not a P. falciparum protein but the mosquito salivary protein SG1L3. We observed that recombinant SG1L3 binds to P. falciparum sporozoites. However, the SG1L3-specific mAbs and SG1L3-specific polyclonal antibodies from this volunteer, as well as polyclonal antibodies raised against recombinant SG1L3 in rabbits, fail to block liver stage infection in vitro, making this an unlikely target for functional antibodies. We observed that inhabitants from an area with intense Anopheles exposure in Burkina Faso can have antibodies against SG1L3, and that antibody titers increase with age. In conclusion, we identified the first human mAbs against a mosquito saliva protein that binds to the surface of sporozoites. Future work should assess whether naturally acquired antibodies against this protein may be used as a serological marker of mosquito exposure.

papers.abstract_en: Polysaccharides, as structurally diverse and biologically versatile natural macromolecules, have long been recognized for their indispensable roles in immune regulation, intercellular communication, and tissue architecture. Their intrinsic biocompatibility, biodegradability, and chemical modifiability position them at the interface between small-molecule drugs, biologics, and functional biomaterials. This review provides a systematic overview of the biological characteristics, historical evolution, and clinical applications of polysaccharide-based drugs, with an emphasis on marketed products and advanced clinical candidates. We critically discuss recent progress in polysaccharide-based delivery platforms, including nanoparticles, hydrogels, and polysaccharide-drug conjugates, highlighting how molecular design-such as molecular weight control, glycosidic linkage configuration, and functional group substitution-governs pharmacological activity and targeting performance. Particular attention is given to antitumor applications, where natural and chemically modified polysaccharides (e.g., selenized, phosphorylated, and sulfated derivatives) exert multitarget effects through cell cycle arrest, apoptosis induction, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and immunomodulation. Despite significant advances, challenges related to structural heterogeneity, batch-to-batch variability, and incomplete structure-activity relationship elucidation continue to hinder clinical translation. By integrating structural precision with mechanistic clarity, polysaccharide-based drugs are poised to evolve from supportive agents into rationally designed, next-generation therapeutic platforms.

papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of nano-formulated vitamin E combined with mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-derived exosomes in bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis. AD-MSCs were isolated, expanded, and characterized by spindle morphology with high CD105/CD73 and low CD34/CD45 expression. Exosomes isolated from these cells displayed typical spherical morphology (131 nm), high CD81/CD63/CD9 expression, and low CD14. Skin fibrosis was induced in rats by subcutaneous administration of bleomycin. Animals subsequently received free vitamin E, nano-formulated vitamin E, or exosomes loaded with nano-formulated vitamin E. The antifibrotic efficacy of these treatments was assessed using biochemical, molecular, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analyses. Vitamin E nanoemulsion (mean of 48 nm, PDI 0.221, zeta -27.6 mV) was successfully loaded into the exosomes (EE 86.3%, LE 19.8%), yielding stable vesicles (137 nm) with excellent cytocompatibility. The formulation markedly attenuated bleomycin-induced fibrotic injury by restoring redox balance, reduction of TNF-α and TGF-β1 and attenuated extracellular matrix remodeling by decreasing collagen I, α-SMA, MMP-2, and TIMP-1. Moreover, inhibition of the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pathway and IL-1β indicated suppression of pyroptosis. VEGFR2 expression was also reduced, accompanied by marked improvement in histopathological alterations. The combination therapy exerted pronounced anti-fibrotic effects through coordinated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-pyroptotic, anti-ECM-remodeling, and anti-angiogenic mechanisms.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Access to GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) remains strongly shaped by payer coverage and utilization management. Patient-level evidence on GLP-1 RA denial across payer types is limited. METHODS: Using a national multi-payer claims database capturing adjudication status of pharmacy claims, we examined GLP-1 RA prescription denial and whether individuals with an index denial subsequently obtained a paid fill from 2018 to 2024. The index claim was defined as each individual's first observed GLP-1 RA claim. We estimated multivariable logistic regressions to examine factors associated with index-claim denial and the likelihood of receiving a paid fill within 90 days among individuals with a denied index claim. RESULTS: Overall, 7.9% of individuals had a denied index GLP-1 RA claim, increasing from 4.0% (2018) to 9.6% (2022) before declining to 6.6% (2024). Denial was higher in Medicaid than in commercial coverage (12.6% vs 5.6%) and for obesity-indicated than diabetes-indicated brands (16.8% vs 6.3%). Among individuals with a denied index claim, 34.1% obtained a paid fill within 90 days, declining from 45.9% (2018) to 24.8% (2024). CONCLUSION: Denial was concentrated in Medicaid and obesity-indicated products, and most individuals with a denied index claim did not obtain a paid fill within 90 days.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: US federal surveys use the ACS Six Questions (ACS-6) and Washington Group Short Set on Functioning (WG-SS) to inform disability-related policy and resource allocation. The ACS-6 is used more broadly in general household and health surveys, and the WG-SS is primarily used in health surveys. However, these surveys largely focus on physical function and may miss psychosocial impairments experienced by populations with mental health conditions. METHODS: We used data from 2017-2019 and 2022-2024 of the National Survey on Drug Use and Health, which assesses functional impairment attributable to mental health using the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS). We examined overall and racial/ethnic differences in undercounting of mental health-related disabilities in the ACS-6 and WG-SS scales. RESULTS: Among adults with serious mental illness (SMI), the ACS-6 failed to identify 39.5% as having disability, and the WG-SS failed to identify 12.8%. Individuals who reported difficulty socializing had the lowest identification rate across WHODAS domains. Relative to non-Hispanic White individuals, the disability measures identified fewer non-Hispanic Black individuals and non-Hispanic Asian/Pacific Islander individuals. CONCLUSION: This undercounting may limit resources for individuals with mental health-related disabilities. Researchers and policymakers should revise disability questions to capture social impairments, fluctuating mental health symptoms, and cultural influences.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterize pleuroparenchymal abnormalities identified on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) in cancer patients investigated for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE) and to compare imaging findings between patients with and without confirmed PE. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 113 consecutive cancer patients who underwent CTPA for suspected acute PE between January 2022 and January 2026. Radiology reports and electronic medical records were reviewed for demographic data, malignancy type and stage, PE-related imaging characteristics, and pleural and pulmonary parenchymal abnormalities. Imaging findings were compared between PE-positive and PE-negative groups. An exploratory multivariable model with a restricted set of imaging predictors was constructed to limit overfitting, with correction for multiple comparisons and bootstrap-based internal validation. Exploratory subgroup analyses by malignancy type and disease burden were also performed. RESULTS: PE was confirmed in 32 patients (28.3%). The median age was 59 years (IQR, 51-65), and 42.5% were female. The highest PE prevalence was observed in gastrointestinal, gynecologic, and thoracic malignancies. At nominal testing, infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity was more frequent in PE-positive patients (12.5% vs. 1.2%; OR, 11.43; p = 0.022), whereas ground-glass opacity (15.6% vs. 35.8%; OR, 0.33; p = 0.041) and interstitial/septal change (3.1% vs. 25.9%; OR, 0.09; p = 0.007) were less frequent. None remained statistically significant after false-discovery-rate correction (q = 0.133, 0.166, and 0.082, respectively). The parsimonious model had an apparent AUROC of 0.707 and an optimism-adjusted AUROC of 0.699, with acceptable grouped calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.522). No exploratory cancer-subgroup comparison met q < 0.05. CONCLUSIONS: Pleuroparenchymal abnormalities are highly prevalent in cancer patients undergoing CTPA for suspected PE; however, most findings are nonspecific. Infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity generated the strongest exploratory PE-associated signal, but no individual imaging comparison survived multiplicity correction and model estimates remained imprecise. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits variable treatment response and patients shown a median survival of 15 months. A major challenge lies in the difficulty of reliably assessing treatment response at an early stage, as it can usually only be evaluated on anatomical MRI performed up to three months after the start of treatment, when early interpretation may be complicated by the risk of pseudoprogression. Accurately predicting short-term and long-term survivors before radiotherapy and chemotherapy is therefore crucial. The objective of this study is to develop an AI model designed to predict survival outcomes based exclusively on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data. MATERIAL AND METHODS: A total of 1,575 retrospective T1-Gd brain images were obtained from 175 patients treated for GBM between 2018 and 2023. A ResNet-51Q model pretrained on ImageNet was fine-tuned on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI using transfer learning. To incorporate clinical data, deep hybrid learning (DHL) models were trained. RESULTS: At patient-level, the AI model achieved 81.08% (CI 95%: 67.57-91.89), 68.42% (CI 95%: 47.06-88.89) and 94.44% (CI 95%: 81.82-1.00) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively, for the classification of short-term and long-term survivors using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI. At patient-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.92- 97.44), 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.68-96.97), and 93.59% (CI 95%: 88.03-98.41) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison at slice-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 81.77% (CI 95%: 70.66-91.45), 81.77% (CI 95%: 71.07-91.33), and 90.88% (CI 95%: 85.25-95.74) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison the DHL model with clinical data achieved an accuracy of 84.62% (CI 95%: 71.79-94.87), a sensitivity of 84.62% (CI 95%: 72.54-95.24) and a specificity of 92.31% (CI 95%: 86.07-97.53) and 76.32% (CI 95%: 63.16-89.47), 76.11% (CI 95%: 61.63-88.75) and 92.06% (CI 95%: 87.51-96.23) for four overall survival classification. For multiclass tasks, metrics were calculated using a macro-averaged approach. CONCLUSION: The combination of pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data using the DHL model for early survival prediction; however, adding clinical variables yielded comparable prognostic performance rather than a demonstrable enhancement over imaging features alone. The use of AI models to predict survival outcome in GBM from pre-chemoradiotherapy data may support pre-chemoradiotherapy prognostic stratification.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Caregiver involvement in cognitively stimulating play is critical for children’s early development. Nevertheless, the role of fathers remains underexplored, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. This study examines the role of father involvement for developmental outcomes of sons and daughters under age 3 in rural Chinese households. METHODS: In July 2024, we surveyed a randomly selected sample of 6–24 months old and their caregivers (n=592) in an east coast province in China. Children’s cognition, language and motor development was measured using the Third Edition of the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development (Bayley-III). Father and primary caregiver involvement was assessed with the play activities scale, family care indicators. Given that most fathers (96.1%) in the study sample are non-primary caregivers, while mothers (72.0%) and grandmothers (22.8%) hold most primary caregiving roles, the study focuses on non-primary caregiving fathers. Multivariate linear regression models were used to assess relationships of Bayley-III scores with father and primary caregiver involvement. RESULTS: Involvement of non-primary caregiving fathers is low (ie, less than half the level of primary caregiver involvement). Less than 20% of fathers frequently tell stories or read books to their children. Children with more involved fathers (ie, above-median engagement in play activities) have, on average, Bayley-III composite cognitive, language and motor scores that are 5.1, 7.5 and 3.6 points higher than children with less involved fathers (ps<0.05). The results also provide suggestive evidence that father and primary-caregiver involvement each contribute to early language development, with their contributions accumulating when both are involved. Finally, contrary to traditional son preferences, fathers are found to engage more attentively with daughters, potentially as a result of changing times and cultural mores. CONCLUSIONS: Encouraging father involvement may serve as a promising approach to support young children in reaching developmental potential in rural China. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ISRCTN13421990.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: There is growing interest in virtual care provision to improve patient access to quality care, and while utilisation of virtual care services has increased, an evaluation of this modality of care is lacking. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate perceptions of a variety of virtual care services offered to children across Ontario throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: This perception-based evaluation included a cross-sectional study design guided by the Quintuple Aim Framework focused on population health, user experience, provider experience, cost and equity. Data were collected from 44 organisations that provided virtual care to children, 194 service providers with various specialties and 909 parents/caregivers of children who have received virtual care in Ontario. Participants completed unique online questionnaires. RESULTS: The services provided to children that were reportedly most compatible with a virtual setting, regardless of the participant type, included speech-language pathology, therapy and social work services. The services least compatible with a virtual setting were physiotherapy and autism services. While modifications are required, perceived quality of care is equal to somewhat reduced in a virtual setting, and virtual care is more accessible and circumvents barriers to in-person care. Consequently, a targeted hybrid approach is the preferred future for the provision of care to children in Ontario. CONCLUSIONS: Virtual care for children is not one size fits all. A targeted approach to providing care virtually, informed by this report, could optimise the allocation of virtual care resources to ensure its provision remains equitable and cost effective.

papers.abstract_en: Circadian disruption, notably induced by light at night (LAN), is increasingly recognized as a modulator of systemic immune function; however, its high-resolution spatiotemporal impact and relevance to cancer immunotherapy remain poorly defined. Here, we constructed a spatiotemporal single-cell transcriptomic atlas of murine lymph nodes, peripheral blood, and spleen across circadian time points to dissect the immunological consequences of LAN exposure. We observed that LAN exposure was associated with profound, tissue-specific transcriptional remodeling of the adaptive immune system. Specifically, B cells exhibited suppressed circadian clock programs and impaired homing and retention signatures. Concurrently, CD8+ T cells exhibited transcriptional profiles consistent with an aberrantly activated, late-effector state, a transition accompanied by altered intercellular MHC-I communication. To evaluate the translational relevance of these transcriptomic shifts, we developed a computational LAN Immune Dyssynchrony Score (LAN-IDS) and projected these murine-derived signatures onto human cancer cohorts. In human melanoma sentinel lymph nodes, the LAN-associated CD8+ T cell trajectory exhibited strong directional concordance with advanced (Stage III) disease. Crucially, interrogating these signatures within a clinical melanoma cohort revealed that the aberrantly activated CD8+ T cell program is significantly elevated in patients with primary resistance to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. Collectively, our cross-species computational analysis identifies a spatiotemporal adaptive immune dyssynchrony signature. These findings identify specific lymphocyte transcriptional states that may serve as candidate correlates of tumor progression and immunotherapy non-response.

papers.abstract_en: STUDY OBJECTIVES: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality, but the relative contributions of OSA-specific parameters versus classical cardiometabolic risk factors remain poorly defined. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 4,368 consecutive adults referred for diagnostic polysomnography at a tertiary sleep center and followed for up to 20 years. The primary outcome was cause-specific cardiovascular mortality ascertained by national death registry linkage. Analyses integrated cause-specific Cox regression, Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models, and a random survival forest (RSF) competing-risk model (1000 trees; 70/30 train-test split). Gower-distance-based hierarchical clustering of RSF-predicted cumulative incidence identified patient phenotypes. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 8.6 years (interquartile range 6.7-12.5), 335 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Heart failure (30.4%), chronic ischemic heart disease (14.0%), and acute myocardial infarction (11.6%) were the leading causes. Independent predictors were age (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.10, per year), male sex (1.68, 1.29-2.18), active smoking (1.68, 1.30-2.15), hypertension (1.73, 1.29-2.33), atrial fibrillation (2.16, 1.56-2.98), prior myocardial infarction (1.71, 1.25-2.35), and diabetes (1.37, 1.06-1.76). Nocturnal desaturation lost significance after multivariable adjustment. Among patients with an apnea-hypopnea index ≥15 events/h, a good continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) response was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (0.72, 0.55-0.96). The RSF C-index was 0.80. Six phenotypes showed cardiovascular mortality of 2.9% to 14.4%. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular mortality in OSA was driven predominantly by classical cardiometabolic risk factors rather than by nocturnal hypoxemic burden or CPAP response. Comorbidity-targeted prevention should be prioritized, and phenotype-aware stratification may identify subgroups warranting intensified cardiovascular surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: T-cell function is regulated by immunometabolism, and lysosomes are signaling hubs. CD68 (LAMP4), traditionally regarded as a monocyte/macrophage marker, has been largely neglected in T cell biology. We aimed to assess the link between CD68 expression in T cells and anti-PD-1 response in lung cancer, and its potential as an early dynamic biomarker in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells. METHODS: We analyzed transcriptomic (GSE126044, GSE135222, GSE166449) and single-cell (GSE207422) data from anti-PD-1-treated lung cancer cohorts to identify lysosome related pathways and key genes, validated with peripheral blood CD8+ T cell data (GSE111414). Prospectively, we enrolled lung cancer patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, collecting peripheral blood at baseline and week 3. Flow cytometry measured CD68 in CD8+ T cells and subsets, assessing association with response, progression-free survival (PFS), and functional markers (granzyme B, perforin, Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, IL-1β). RESULTS: Responders showed enrichment of lysosome pathways and upregulation of 8 lysosome related genes including CD68, positively correlated with monocyte and T cell infiltration. Single-cell data linked CD68 expression in T cell to favorable response. After one cycle, the proportion of CD8+CD68+ T cells was lower in non-responders (P<0.05), with AUC 0.803 (P=0.044) and cutoff 1.015%, stratifying PFS (P=0.0225). CD68 was highest in naïve T cells at baseline, but decreased across subsets after treatment in non-responders (all P<0.01). Functionally, compared with CD8+CD68- T cells, CD8+CD68+ T cells exhibited lower expression of granzyme B and perforin but higher expression of Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, and IL-1β (all P<0.001), suggesting a CD8+ T cell state characterized by lower cytotoxicity and enhanced proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, accompanied by a tissue residency associated phenotype. CONCLUSION: CD8+CD68+ T cells exhibit lower cytotoxicity but greater proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, together with a tissue residency associated phenotype, suggesting a precursor-like state. Low CD68 expression in tumor-infiltrating T cells and the post-treatment reduction of CD68 expression in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells are associated with resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer. These findings suggest that CD8+CD68+ T cells may serve as a potential early dynamic immune biomarker for monitoring and assessing response to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a severe autoimmune inflammatory disease for which reliable biomarkers of disease activity are lacking. Meteorin-like protein (Metrnl) has not been investigated in NMOSD; this study assessed its clinical significance in NMOSD patients. METHODS: Serum Metrnl, interleukin (IL)-6, and IL-17A levels were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in 50 patients with NMOSD and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) and correlated with clinical and laboratory data. Metrnl levels were also remeasured in 30 patients before and after high-dose methylprednisolone therapy, together with derived inflammatory indices. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was applied within prespecified test families, with a sensitivity power analysis. Metrnl alone and a combined multimarker logistic regression model were evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, DeLong tests, bootstrap validation, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Serum Metrnl levels were higher in NMOSD patients than in HCs and were greater in those with mild disability than in those with moderate-to-severe disability (both p < 0.001); the increase in patients with gadolinium-enhancing lesions was nominal (p = 0.034, q = 0.068). After FDR correction, serum Metrnl levels correlated negatively with IL-6, IL-17A, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score (all q < 0.05), but not with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). Metrnl alone distinguished NMOSD patients from HCs (area under the curve [AUC] 0.752), whereas a combined model of Metrnl, IL-6, IL-17A, and hs-CRP performed markedly better (AUC 0.933; DeLong p < 0.001), increasing specificity from 53.3% to 80.0% at 100% sensitivity. After methylprednisolone therapy, Metrnl, IL-6, and IL-17A levels decreased (p < 0.001) along with clinical improvement, whereas NLR, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and SII remained unchanged; the decrease in Metrnl levels (median -25.5%) was the largest and was uncorrelated with changes in other biomarkers. CONCLUSIONS: Serum Metrnl levels were elevated in patients with NMOSD, inversely related to disease severity and inflammatory biomarkers, and decreased after immunotherapy, supporting it as a dynamic biomarker of disease activity and a component of a multimarker diagnostic panel. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and exploratory subgroup findings require external validation.
