papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) can produce analgesia, but its associated cortical, brainstem, and spinal response patterns in humans remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: To compare the analgesic effects and associated brain-spinal response patterns of two TENS protocols: high-frequency/low-intensity and low-frequency/high-intensity stimulation. METHODS: Ninety-two healthy adults were randomized to high-frequency TENS, low-frequency TENS, or sham stimulation. Bilateral heat-pain responses were assessed using simultaneous brain-spinal functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) before and after a 30-min intervention. Pain ratings, regional activation, and periaqueductal gray (PAG)-centered functional connectivity were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with correction for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: The two TENS protocols produced different spatial profiles of analgesia. High-frequency/low-intensity TENS produced treated-side analgesia relative to sham for pain intensity (β = -2.57, 95 % confidence interval [CI] [-3.26, -1.87]) and unpleasantness (β = -2.53, 95 % CI [-3.51, -1.55]). Treated-side analgesia was accompanied by reduced heat-evoked activity in the secondary somatosensory cortex (S2), PAG, rostral ventromedial medulla (RVM), and C6 spinal cord, increased ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) activity, and altered PAG-spinal connectivity. Low-frequency/high-intensity TENS produced bilateral analgesia, reducing pain intensity on the treated and untreated sides (β = -2.07 and -1.75, respectively) and unpleasantness (β = -1.98 and -1.70, respectively). This bilateral effect was accompanied by reduced activity in primary somatosensory cortex (S1)/dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC)/supplementary motor area (SMA), S2, and spinal cord, together with PAG-S1 and PAG-spinal connectivity changes. CONCLUSION: TENS analgesia was associated with protocol-specific brain-spinal response patterns. High-frequency/low-intensity TENS produced localized analgesia with neural changes consistent with spinal and supraspinal modulation, whereas low-frequency/high-intensity TENS produced bilateral analgesia with broader PAG-sensorimotor-spinal involvement.

papers.abstract_en: Root-associated fungi and bacteria play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystem processes. However, identifying keystone taxa driving below-ground microbial assembly remains a major challenge. Here, we present a statistical framework for identifying microbes that reorganize microbiome assembly. Using 1,270 root samples collected from a cool-temperate forest in Japan, we reconstruct assembly landscapes describing the probabilistic structure of community states. We then find that several endophytic fungi (e.g., Phialocephala and Oidiodendron) are strongly associated with the reorganization of assembly landscape topography along abundance gradients, coinciding with shifts in mycorrhizal symbiosis. Independent datasets from Europe confirm that the highlighted genera are significantly associated with changes in mycorrhizal colonization patterns. Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes.

papers.abstract_en: We examined whether the impact on quality of life (QOL) of early palliative care delivered via video versus in-person visits varied across patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Between 6/2018 and 5/2023, 1250 patients with advanced NSCLC enrolled in a randomized trial comparing early palliative care delivered via video or in-person visits at 22 cancer centers. Using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Lung scale, we examined whether the effect of palliative care delivery modality on patient-reported QOL at 24 weeks post-enrollment varied by baseline sociodemographic and other factors. Black patients, Hispanic/Latino patients, and those with incomes <$50,000 reported better QOL in the video visit group versus the in-person group. However, Asian patients in the video visit group reported worse QOL than the in-person group. Early palliative care delivered via video may provide greater QOL benefits for Black and Hispanic/Latino patients with advanced NSCLC and those with lower incomes. Trial Registration: NCT03375489.

papers.abstract_en: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains one of the most lethal thoracic malignancies, characterized by rapid progression, early metastasis, and limited durable responses to conventional therapy. Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3), a Notch pathway inhibitory ligand aberrantly overexpressed on the surface of approximately 70-85% of SCLC tumor cells but largely absent from normal adult tissue, has emerged as a compelling and therapeutically actionable target. Early efforts to exploit DLL3 through the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) rovalpituzumab tesirine (Rova-T) yielded important mechanistic insights despite failing to demonstrate survival benefit in phase III trials and have since catalyzed a new generation of more refined DLL3-directed strategies. This review critically examines the evolving portfolio of DLL3-targeted therapies across three principal modalities: T-cell engagers, ADCs, and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies. In parallel, we examine emerging non-DLL3 therapeutic strategies reshaping the broader SCLC landscape. We additionally discuss the translational science underpinning DLL3 as a biomarker, including the emerging roles of circulating tumor cell-based liquid biopsy and DLL3-directed immunoPET-CT imaging in patient selection and treatment monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: Surgical repair of gastroesophageal (GE) defects is a formidable clinical challenge, plagued by high leakage, fistula recurrence and life-threatening complications due to gastric acid exposure and persistent mechanical stress. To address this unmet need, we developed a robust bio-supportive (RBS) hydrogel patch for immediate fluid-tight closure and full-thickness tissue regeneration. Fabricated from highly crystalline polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel, the RBS patch has a double-disc architecture, inherent porous network and weakly bound water. The double-disc design ensures effective sealing and deformation resistance; high crystallinity confers adequate mechanical strength and long-term acid/enzyme resistance. Moreover, its porous microstructure and weakly bound water synergistically promote cellular adhesion, migration and tissue infiltration for functional repair. In rat and rabbit models, the RBS patch achieved remarkable healing of gastric perforations (GP), esophageal perforations (EP) and tracheoesophageal fistulas (TEF), with intact mucosal, submucosal and muscular layers regeneration. Its efficacy and safety were further validated in beagle dog models, highlighting clinical translation potential. This RBS patch serves as a versatile bio-supportive technology for GE defects and a promising platform for tissue repair in dynamic physiological environments.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Double-blind, placebo-controlled food challenges (DBPCFCs) are regarded as the reference standard for diagnosing IgE-mediated food allergy owing to their objectivity and ability to minimize bias. However, DBPCFCs are logistically complex, time-consuming, and not always feasible in routine clinical settings. In contrast, open oral food challenges (OFCs) are more accessible and widely used but potentially less reliable due to a lack of blinding. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of open OFCs and descriptively compared their clinical utility. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of literature available in the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PubMed, and Ichushi databases between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2024, incorporating randomized controlled trials and observational studies in which both open OFCs and DBPCFCs were performed. Risk of bias (RoB) was assessed using QUADAS-2. RESULTS: Eight studies were included. Using DBPCFC as the reference standard, the diagnostic performance of open OFC was as follows: sensitivity, 0.91-0.92 (n = 2); specificity, 0.83-1.00 (n = 3); positive predictive value, 0.00-0.89 (n = 6); and negative predictive value, 0.88-0.97 (n = 2). RoB was high mainly owing to the patient selection and the flow and timing domains. CONCLUSIONS: Given the small number of studies examined, high RoB, and heterogeneity among studies, caution is needed in generalizing these results. Although a negative open OFC result may be reliable, the current evidence is insufficient to establish open OFCs as a complete substitute for DBPCFCs, and large-scale, standardized studies in more diverse populations are needed to clarify their diagnostic performance and clinical utility.

papers.abstract_en: STUDY OBJECTIVE: To compare ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block with transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block on recovery quality 24 h after septorhinoplasty. DESIGN: Prospective, randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, parallel-group trial. SETTING: Tertiary training hospital; operating room and postoperative ward. PATIENTS: Ninety adults aged 18 to 65 years, ASA physical status I or II, undergoing elective septorhinoplasty; 89 were analyzed. INTERVENTIONS: After induction of general anesthesia, patients received bilateral transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block (SPG group) or bilateral ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block (IO group), 2 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine per side. Surgical infiltration and multimodal analgesia were identical in both groups. MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was the total Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 h. Secondary outcomes were QoR-15 domains, visual analog scale pain scores, rescue morphine, nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption, emergence agitation, edema, ecchymosis and recovery room stay. MAIN RESULTS: Total QoR-15 at 24 h was higher in the IO group (129.1 ± 9.4 versus 116.6 ± 11.7; mean difference 12.5 points, 95% CI 8.01 to 17.01; P = 0.001), above the prespecified minimal clinically important difference of 8. More IO patients crossed the acceptable symptom state threshold of 118 (86.4% versus 35.6%; P < 0.001). Pain scores were lower at every time point and fewer IO patients needed rescue analgesia (11.4% versus 53.3%; P = 0.001). Nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption and recovery room stay did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: Infraorbital nerve block gave better 24 h patient-reported recovery than sphenopalatine ganglion block after septorhinoplasty. Secondary findings are hypothesis-generating. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.govNCT06929429.

papers.abstract_en: Perioperative durvalumab plus fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) has established a new curative-intent standard for resectable gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. Recurrence after this regimen creates a clinically distinct, pre-exposed metastatic state for which no prospective sequencing standard exists. Because direct post-D-FLOT evidence is absent, treatment decisions should distinguish exposure-analogous evidence from extrapolation from conventional metastatic trials. In practice, we first determine whether recurrence after perioperative durvalumab plus fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) is potentially amenable to local treatment and, if systemic therapy is required, document the recurrence phase, the dates of the last FLOT and durvalumab doses, prior radiographic and pathological response, residual neuropathy, immune-related adverse events, organ function, performance status, and disease tempo. We then obtain recurrent-tumor tissue when feasible and reassess human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2), and microsatellite instability/mismatch repair status; programmed death-ligand 1 results are interpreted in the context of assay differences and prior durvalumab exposure. If HER2 is positive and no prior HER2-directed therapy was given, we prioritize a HER2-directed strategy. If CLDN18.2 is positive and HER2 negative, zolbetuximab-based therapy is reasonable when oxaliplatin re-use is clinically defensible, but very early relapse or persistent neuropathy should favor an alternative strategy or a clinical trial. Microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair-deficient disease remains immunologically compelling, although checkpoint-inhibitor re-use after durvalumab is not established. In biomarker-negative disease recurring during treatment or within about 6 months, we favor a non-cross-resistant approach, using ramucirumab- or irinotecan-based therapy according to prior taxane exposure, neuropathy, and regional availability. With a longer treatment-free interval and recovered toxicity, selective fluoropyrimidine/platinum reintroduction becomes more reasonable. We avoid routine checkpoint-inhibitor rechallenge solely because programmed death-ligand 1 is positive. For trial eligibility and line-of-therapy nomenclature, we count recurrence within 12 months of the last administered perioperative systemic dose (chemotherapy or durvalumab, whichever was later) as one prior systemic line, while recognizing that this is a pragmatic classification rather than a validated biologic cutoff.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Subspecialty interstitial lung disease (ILD) clinics are associated with improved outcomes, yet access remains uneven. Even within tertiary health systems, patients with ILD are managed across diverse ambulatory settings, with unclear implications for care and outcomes. RESEARCH QUESTION: Within a single academic health system, do patient characteristics, care delivery, and outcomes differ between individuals with ILD managed in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus other ambulatory settings? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ILD at a large academic medical center. Identified patients were stratified by care in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus non-specialty setting. Demographic, diagnostic testing, treatment, health care utilization, and survival data were extracted from the electronic health record. Diagnostic and treatment measures were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Hospitalization, emergency department visit, and death were analyzed as time-to-event outcomes. RESULTS: Among 6,637 patients with ILD, 4,371 (66%) were seen in the subspecialty ILD clinic. The 2,266 patients (34%) managed in non-specialty settings were more likely to identify as Black or Latinx, reside in more socioeconomically deprived neighborhoods, and have an unspecified ILD diagnosis (all p < 0.001). In the peri-diagnostic period, ILD clinic care was associated with higher adjusted odds of chest CT imaging (OR 2.51, 2.07-3.05) and antifibrotic therapy (OR 1.54, 1.32-1.80), and lower odds of lung biopsy (OR 0.47, 0.32-0.68). ILD clinic care was associated with a lower adjusted hazards of all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.46, 0.42-0.51), emergency department visit (HR 0.68, 0.59-0.78), and death (HR 0.57, 0.45-0.72). P-value <0.001 for all. INTERPRETATION: Within a single health system, subspecialty ILD clinic care was associated with more guideline-concordant care and improved outcomes. Differences in access to subspecialty expertise may contribute to inequities in care delivery, underscoring the need for scalable strategies, referral optimization, telemedicine, and clinical decision support, to extend ILD expertise and improve outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved. RESEARCH QUESTION: Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. The prespecified exposure was at least 3,000 mg of azithromycin with at least two prescriptions redeemed in the preceding 12 months, with a 3-month lag. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for inhaled and oral corticosteroids. Exploratory analyses examined an active comparator at matched thresholds, recency, and outcome stringency. RESULTS: The analyses comprised 173 cases and 3,409 controls (bronchiectasis) and 365 and 7,300 (COPD). Under the prespecified definition, azithromycin was not associated with incident NTM isolation (bronchiectasis: OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.79-2.18; COPD: 1.29; 0.78-2.13). In COPD, the OR was 1.61 (1.14-2.28) for one or more prescriptions and 1.29 (0.78-2.13) for two or more. The COPD association was concentrated within 90 days of the index date (2.55; 1.73-3.76) and attenuated with microbiological stringency (definite isolates: 0.77; 0.27-2.20). Non-macrolide antibacterials were more strongly associated than azithromycin at every matched threshold in bronchiectasis (one or more prescriptions: 1.90 [1.36-2.65] vs 1.15 [0.75-1.75]), and at the two higher thresholds in COPD (two or more: 1.48 [1.17-1.86] vs 1.24 [0.75-2.05]). INTERPRETATION: Azithromycin was not associated with NTM isolation under the prespecified definition. Associations under broader definitions were not dose-dependent and clustered close to the index date, more consistent with indication-driven testing than a drug effect, although in COPD an association with any exposure persisted after accounting for other antibacterials.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Only a subset of patients with esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) achieve complete or partial histopathological response to immunotherapy, highlighting the need for better understanding of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Despite efforts to characterize the EAC TME at the molecular level, its epigenetic landscape remains understudied. METHODS: We combined bulk DNA methylation data from a large Norwegian multicenter EAC cohort (n = 232) with immune gene annotations to identify immune-related CpG sites differentially methylated between tumor and normal tissue. Hierarchical consensus clustering of EAC samples based on these sites was performed, and the identified subtypes were characterized according to their immune cell type composition, association with clinical features and potential prognostic relevance. RESULTS: We identified four immune subtypes (IS1-IS4) with distinct DNA methylation patterns and tumor-infiltrating immune cell composition. The highest DNA methylation levels at immune-related CpG sites were found in IS3, which showed the lowest relative fractions of CD8+ T cells and the highest fractions of regulatory T cells (Tregs), consistent with an immunosuppressed phenotype. Conversely, IS1, with the lowest DNA methylation levels at immune-related CpG sites, displayed the highest relative fractions of CD8+ T cells and the lowest fractions of Tregs, aligning with an "inflamed" immune profile. These findings were validated in an independent multicenter cohort (n = 285). No significant differences in 5-year overall survival were observed across immune subtypes, possibly reflecting the influence of variable response to neoadjuvant treatment. CONCLUSION: The identified immune subtypes offer new insights into the epigenetic landscape of the EAC TME and reveal differences in its cellular composition.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: We aimed to validate individual endoscopic parameters against clinical and functional testing and to build a simple classification of fundoplication integrity. SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: Endoscopy is the main tool to assess the gastroesophageal valve after antireflux surgery (ARS), but existing classifications are complex and have never been validated against objective pathophysiologic data. METHODS: This was a single-center, two-phase cohort study of adults undergoing endoscopy, high-resolution manometry (HRM), and reflux monitoring after ARS. Retroflexed videoclips were reviewed blinded to functional results. In the development cohort (2018-2024), endoscopic parameters were tested against pathologic GERD (Lyon 2.0 criteria); those correlating with reflux were included in the classification and the population was stratified according to the number of impaired mechanisms (0-3). In the second phase, the classification was validated prospectively (2024-2026). RESULTS: Of 122 patients, 73 formed the development and 49 the validation cohort. Three parameters were associated with pathologic GERD: intrathoracic valve, disrupted valve, and visible hiatus. Clinical, manometric, and reflux metrics worsened stepwise with the number of impaired mechanisms, and pathologic GERD rose from 11.8% to 37.5% to 85.7%. The new classification discriminated pathologic GERD with an area under the curve of 0.860 in the development and 0.870 in the validation cohort (0.869 overall). CONCLUSIONS: A simple endoscopic classification based on valve location, disruption, and hiatal opening reliably identifies fundoplication failure and correlates with symptoms, manometric features, and reflux burden.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse. Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings. Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest. CONCLUSION: In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Several case series have noted an association between Barrett's esophagus (BE) and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). METHODS: Consecutive male participants who underwent endoscopy at 17 health check-up institutes in Japan between 2013 and 2017 and had follow-up endoscopy by December 2022 were enrolled. Baseline endoscopic images were reviewed to assess GA and BE status. The primary outcome was ESCC development during follow-up. Multivariable analysis revealed that USSBE was independently associated with ESCC (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.82, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-3.24). In exploratory subgroup analyses, USSBE was independently associated with ESCC (adjusted HR 2.40, 95% CI 1.13-5.13) among individuals with extensive GA, while no significant association was observed among those without (adjusted HR 1.34, 95% CI 0.64-2.81; p for interaction = 0.369). CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to demonstrate a significant association between USSBE and ESCC. USSBE may help identify individuals at increased risk of ESCC. papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Whether frequent emergency department (ED) use (≥4 ED visits per calendar year) reflects a persistent patient phenotype or predominantly transient episodes remains unknown in France. This study characterised longitudinal trajectories and predictors of persistence, lack of primary care affiliation and very frequent use (VFU). METHODS: Two-year retrospective cohort study at a French tertiary-care university hospital (2023-2024). Individual patient-level linkage classified patients as persistent, incident, or remitting frequent users. Forced-entry multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of persistence, lack of primary care affiliation, and VFU (≥6 visits/year). RESULTS: Linkage identified 196 persistent users (16.7% of 2023 frequent ED users), 982 incident, and 976 remitting. Persistent users were younger (49.3 vs 55.4 years; p = 0.001) and more often in the ≥6 visits/year stratum (51.5%vs 24.9%; p < 0.001). Persistence increased steeply with index-year visit intensity (adjusted OR 8.78 for ≥10 vs 4 visits/year). Repeat attendance was mostly for differing reasons (identical chief complaint at every visit: 1.9%). Mental-health, haematological, and addiction-related presentations were over-represented among VFU. Lack of primary care affiliation was predicted by male sex (aOR = 2.25) and younger age (aOR = 0.97/year), and was higher among out-of-catchment patients (28.1%vs 13.5%; p = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: Frequent ED use was predominantly transient, with only 16.7% of patients remaining frequent users across consecutive years; persistent users were younger and concentrated in the highest-use stratum. Lack of primary care affiliation reflected sociodemographic factors (male sex, younger age). These findings identify persistent users as a priority target for future coordinated interventions.

papers.abstract_en: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. DNA polymerase η (Pol η) tolerates UV-induced lesions via translesion synthesis (TLS), but may contribute more broadly to DNA synthesis. Using polymerase usage sequencing (Pu-seq), we map Pol η activity genome-wide during unperturbed replication in human cells. Pol η preferentially participates in lagging strand replication, as in budding yeast. This bias requires direct PCNA interaction, suggesting stochastic engagement of PCNA-bound intermediates at replication forks. Pol η usage also varies across S phase, with PCNA ubiquitylation-dependent enrichment in late-replicating domains. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes.

papers.abstract_en: Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, and an increasing proportion of cases occur in lifetime nonsmokers, particularly East Asian women. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in outdoor air pollution is classified as a Group 1 carcinogen and increasingly seen as an important modifiable exposure associated with lung cancer in nonsmokers. This narrative review summarizes epidemiologic and toxicological evidence linking environmental and microenvironmental PM2.5 exposures to lung cancer in nonsmokers, defined as individuals who have smoked fewer than 100 cigarettes in their lifetime. Global cohort and meta-analytic data, including dose-response findings and studies from Asian populations, are reviewed. Biological pathways linking PM2.5 to lung carcinogenesis are then examined, including oxidative stress, pulmonary inflammation, and particle-triggered cytokine and growth-factor signaling. Particular emphasis is placed on macrophage-derived interleukin-1β (IL-1β) signaling, which promotes epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. High-exposure microenvironments such as religious incense burning, residential cooking and solid-fuel use, urban transit systems (subway, bus, motorbike, and professional driving), and selected occupational settings (career and wildland firefighters, construction trades, informal e-waste recycling) are identified. These settings might contribute significantly to daily PM2.5 exposure in some individuals. Finally, future research priorities, including incorporation of cumulative PM2.5 exposure into lung cancer risk prediction models and development of cost-effective strategies for lung cancer screening in nonsmokers with high PM2.5 exposure, are presented.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterise transient immediate systemic side effects (TISSE) following long-acting cabotegravir/rilpivirine (CAB-RPV-LA) injections, estimate their incidence, assess treatment continuation, and investigate associated plasma drug concentrations. METHODS: This prospective single-centre French cohort included adults with HIV receiving CAB-RPV-LA during 2021-2026. Nurses prospectively documented unexpected systemic symptoms. Treatment discontinuation was compared by TISSE status. Plasma concentrations were measured by LC-MS/MS after TISSE events and compared with post-injection concentrations in 24 matched asymptomatic controls and routine trough measurements. RESULTS: Among 308 participants receiving 4,644 monitored on-site injection sessions, 24 experienced 28 TISSE episodes: 0.60% per session (exact Poisson 95% CI, 0.40-0.87%). Symptoms occurred during or shortly after injection, predominantly intense lumbar pain (18 episodes) and dyspnea/chest oppression (16), co-occurring in seven. All symptoms resolved within 15 minutes; none required hospitalisation. No difference in treatment discontinuation was detected (2/24 versus 38/284; Fisher's exact test, p=0.75). In all 17 sampled episodes, RPV and/or CAB concentrations were markedly elevated. RPV elevations occurred in 14 episodes, (up to 767-fold the upper concentration bound at trough), and CAB elevations in four, including one involving both drugs. CONCLUSIONS: TISSE episodes were brief and self-limited but clinically striking, potentially mimicking cardiovascular emergencies. Post-event concentration elevations suggest inadvertent systemic passage, predominantly involving RPV, without establishing causality. Possible CAB involvement remains exploratory. Recognising TISSE is important, and healthcare professionals should be familiar with its clinical presentation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT02898987.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate segmentation of brain tissues from MRI scans is critical for neuroscience and clinical applications, but achieving consistent performance across the human lifespan remains challenging due to dynamic, age-related changes in brain appearance and morphology. While prior work has sought to mitigate these shifts by using self-supervised regularization with paired longitudinal data, such data are often unavailable in practice. To address this, we propose DuMeta++, a dual meta-learning framework that operates without paired longitudinal data. Our approach integrates: (1) meta-feature learning to extract age-agnostic semantic representations of spatiotemporally evolving brain structures, and (2) meta-initialization learning to enable data-efficient adaptation of the segmentation model. Furthermore, we propose a memory-bank-based class-aware regularization strategy to enforce longitudinal consistency without explicit longitudinal super-vision. We further characterize the convergence of the dual meta-learning pipeline under standard smoothness assumptions. Extensive experiments on the iSeg-2019 and ADNI datasets under one- and five-shot settings demonstrate that DuMeta++ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both segmentation accuracy and longitudinal consistency. Code will be available at https:// github.com/ladderlab-xjtu/DuMeta++.

papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG) is the most scalable window onto brain dynamics, yet how cortical activity is transformed before reaching extracranial electrodes has largely been inferred from forward models rather than directly measured. We built a dual-scale sensing platform in awake mice that records a 16-channel flexible micro-electrocorticography (micro-ECoG) array and five skull-screw EEG electrodes on a single 30-kHz clock, enabling sample-aligned comparison of cortical and skull-level signals. Across 115 simultaneously recorded ECoG-EEG pairs from three mice, cortex-to-skull spectral gain was not frequency-flat but increased with frequency following a power law, indicating that skull EEG relatively preserves high-frequency cortical activity rather than acting as a simple low-pass copy. This gain was also non-stationary: it shifted across blocks of a fixed-order auditory protocol and was not explained by measured video motion, whereas trial-matched cross-scale coherence depended on the reference transform. With channel number equalized, micro-ECoG retained a larger unique spatial component than skull EEG. These results convert the cortex-to-skull relationship from a static modeling assumption into a measurable, frequency- and state-dependent quantity. For neural sensing, they provide an empirical calibration target for choosing electrode scale, reference, and analysis band and for validating EEG forward models and EEG-to-intracranial translation. More broadly, they indicate that noninvasive biomarkers and brain-computer interface features, particularly in high-frequency bands, should be interpreted through frequency- and state-aware cortex-to-skull mappings.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Food allergy (FA) restrictive policies (RPs) are widely used in daycares/schools, but clinicians and families worry policies may increase stigma, bullying, or anxiety; these psychosocial effects have not been characterized. OBJECTIVE: We sought to examine how FA RPs in daycares/schools impact the psychosocial wellbeing of children with IgE-mediated FA and their parents. METHODS: We conducted a survey of child-parent pairs recruited from Boston Children's Hospital and through social media. Participants completed self-administered electronic surveys on daycare/school FA policies and validated instruments assessing FA-related psychosocial wellbeing. Inclusion criteria were children aged <18 years with IgE-mediated FA to peanut and/or tree nut who attended daycare/school. Children attending daycares/schools with or without peanut/tree nut RPs and their parents were compared on validated instruments assessing FA-related psychosocial wellbeing. RESULTS: The cohort included 652 child-parent dyads. Parents were primarily mothers (96.7%). Median child age was 6.0 years. papers.abstract_en: Itch and inflammation in atopic dermatitis (AD) have long been read as two parallel outputs of a single disease process. That framing sits awkwardly with the anatomy. Cutaneous sensory neurons and immune cells sit side by side in the skin and speak a shared language of ligand-receptor pairs. We recast that interface here as a bidirectional regulatory network, not a one-way road running from inflammation to itch. Going in one direction, type 2 and innate cytokines act straight on sensory neurons as pruritogens, each through its own receptor and signalling route. Going the other way, neuron-derived mediators such as substance P, VIP and NGF reshape how immune cells are recruited, polarized and how tissue is remodelled. Put together, the two arms form a feed-forward loop. Scratching, barrier disruption, cutaneous dysbiosis and central sensitization all feed one another. Within this framework, several counter-regulatory mechanisms have also been identified, including the capacity of CGRP to restrain type 2 immunity and the immunomodulatory functions of IL-31 that extend beyond its pruritogenic role. What the circuit does, then, hinges on how the work is split among sensory neuron subsets and on the state of each node, rather than on any linear cascade. Seen through this lens, today's and tomorrow's therapies-dupilumab, tralokinumab, nemolizumab, JAK inhibitors and kappa-opioid agonists-each land on a specific node of the circuit. The picture helps make sense of treatment-resistant itch and argues for rational, combination targeting of the circuit.

papers.abstract_en: Allergic disease has risen too rapidly for inherited susceptibility to explain it, and the risk variants so far reported lie in the epithelial barrier and in type-2 immunity. We propose a five-layer model in which epithelial barrier and bioenergetic dysfunction may precede and promote type-2 immune deviation rather than arise solely as its consequence, progressing from (1) barrier and bioenergetic dysfunction, with mitochondrial DNA escaping into the cytosol, through (2) danger sensing and (3) epithelial-immune communication, to (4) type-2 immune amplification and (5) a systemic layer of circulating IgE, neurogenic amplification and the atopic march, with reciprocal inflammatory feedback. Layer 1 is also the least measured: standard immune panels carry almost none of these genes, and no genome-wide association study has implicated the mitochondrial genome or its nuclear regulators. From 1856 catalogued transcriptomic series, 985 of them expression series, we drew 116 case-control cohorts from 110 series, 3776 patients and 2164 controls, with Layer 1 prespecified as 350 genes across 19 domains. Of 212 module estimates nine survived false-discovery correction: two type-2 positive controls, two cytosolic sensing and inflammasome modules, raised in oesophageal tissue (Hedges' g +1.70) and atopic skin (+1.27), and five bioenergetic modules in oesophageal tissue. In eosinophilic oesophagitis the mitochondrial clearance limb was reduced in every one of thirteen cohorts (HIF1A -1.94, BNIP3-1.98). STING1 increased in all thirteen skin cohorts that measured it while MAVS fell in ten of thirteen oesophageal cohorts, and a STING1 minus MAVS contrast separated the allergic epithelia from psoriasis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma without exception (exact p 0.029). In one series of clinically uninvolved atopic skin KEAP1 increased while NFE2L2, claudin-1 and filaggrin decreased (p < 0.001), in tissue that is not inflamed; pooled across nine series the directions largely hold without reaching significance. Broad suppression of mitochondrial programmes across allergic tissues was not supported: the phenotype is tissue-dependent, present in eosinophilic oesophagitis and atopic dermatitis, absent in nasal polyposis and established asthma and conditional in allergic rhinitis. Prospective and experimental studies must establish temporal and causal relationships.

papers.abstract_en: The locus coeruleus (LC) brainstem cell group is evolutionarily conserved across vertebrates and influences both mind (cognition) and body (cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and immune functions) via two-putatively distinct-spontaneous activity patterns. Yet, the degree to which spontaneous LC firing rates and patterns are homogeneous across species has never been assessed due to inherently limited sample sizes. To remedy this, we pooled cross-species data from 20 laboratories to show that firing rates differ across species and are modulated by sex, age, and type of in vitro or in vivo preparation. Contrary to the prevailing dual-mode firing pattern schema, we observed patterns spread across a low-dimensional manifold, with subregions enriched for specific biological factors and neurodegenerative disease models. Our findings show considerable diversity in an ancestral vertebrate neuromodulatory system.

papers.abstract_en: Neurons depend on tightly regulated positioning of cellular components to maintain long-distance signaling, but the mechanisms guiding specific mRNAs to distant regions remain unclear. Here, we show that late endosomes function as selective RNA carriers in human motor neurons and uncover the molecular logic guiding their loading. Using APEX2-mediated proximity labeling, we identify the external transcriptome of RAB7A-positive endosomes and find a specific population of mRNAs enriched for endosomal, axonal, and synaptic functions. We find that mRNAs enriched in RAB7A endosomes contain evolutionarily conserved 5'UTRs that act as localization signals, and that the RNA-binding protein GEMIN5 interacts with these regions to promote endosomal RNA recruitment. Finally, we show that there is a conspicuous loss of endosome-associated transcripts in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-associated conditions, accompanied by the mislocalization of GEMIN5 from endosomes. These findings uncover fundamental principles of RNA compartmentalization and highlight endosomal mRNA loading as a vulnerable axis in neuronal homeostasis.

papers.abstract_en: The pulp and paper industry produces large volumes of condensed kraft lignin, which is challenging to convert to single chemical products. For this purpose, tandem chemical depolymerization and bioconversion to a single atom-efficient product is a potentially promising strategy. In this study, we conducted copper-catalyzed oxidative depolymerization using pine-derived kraft lignin to generate multiple bioavailable aromatic monomers at a yield of 4.5 weight% (wt%; g monomers per g lignin) from both C-O and C-C bond cleavage, followed by counter-current extraction with a 52 wt% monomer recovery. This resulted in an oxidized lignin product containing vanillin, vanillate, 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde, 4-hydroxybenzoate, 5-formylvanillin, 5-carboxyvanillin, 5-carboxyvanillate, acetovanillone, and vanillyl glyoxylate. Based on this stream composition, we engineered the industrially relevant soil bacterium Pseudomonas putida KT2440 to catabolize the latter five compounds via overexpression of ten heterologous genes (acvABCDEFSYK-6, vceABSYK-6, ligW2SYK-6, and mdlCPP). We combined these engineered pathways with previously reported strategies for muconate production from G- and H-type monomers to generate P. putida KMM428, which utilized 93.6 ± 0.2 mol% of the quantified aromatic monomers in a depolymerized kraft lignin mixture, and produced muconate at a yield of 99 ± 3 mol%, on a quantified monomer basis. Together, this work increases the theoretical carbon conversion efficiency of this process by 37.6 ± 0.1 mol% through incorporation of three β-5 cleavage products, in addition to traditional G-type monomers.

papers.abstract_en: Obesity arises from dietary energy intake-expenditure imbalance. 5'-Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), a core regulator of biological energy metabolism, is a key target for obesity research and can be activated by endogenous stimuli, such as cellular stress and physical exercise. As natural active components with diverse sources and biological functions, dietary polysaccharides have shown potential lipid-lowering and antiobesity effects in preclinical studies. This narrative review systematically summarizes their structural characteristics, sources, absorption-utilization mechanisms and structure-activity relationships, focusing on their regulatory effects on obesity via the AMPK pathway. We searched PubMed and Web of Science for publications (2014-2026) using "dietary polysaccharides,""AMPK,""obesity," and "gut microbiota" as key words, screening original studies and reviews relevant to the core topic. Correlative evidence suggests that dietary polysaccharides are associated with altered expression of lipid metabolism-related factors through potential modulation of gut microbiota and its metabolites, with indirect links to AMPK activation. Such AMPK regulatory effects have tissue/organ specificity, and the causal relationship of each link remains to be rigorously established. Notably, the majority of current evidence derives from in vitro and rodent models, and extrapolation to human obesity management requires caution, as high-quality human clinical trials are urgently needed to validate the translational potential of these preclinical findings. This review clarifies the potential mechanism and existing research gaps of dietary polysaccharides in obesity alleviation, providing a scientific basis for the research and development of lipid-lowering functional foods based on dietary polysaccharides.

papers.abstract_en: Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid derived from Cannabis sativa L. has gained significant attention in biomedical research due to its broad spectrum of therapeutic properties, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antioxidant, neuroprotective, and anticancer activities. However, its clinical translation remains limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, rapid metabolism, and instability under physiological conditions. To overcome these challenges, advanced drug delivery platforms based on 3D bioprinting technologies have emerged as promising strategies for controlled and site-specific delivery of CBD. This review provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art CBD delivery systems, including polymeric biomaterials such as PLGA, PEG derivatives, chitosan, alginate, and cellulose-based hybrids, which enhance drug stability and enable sustained release profiles. Nano- and microstructured systems, including liposomes, nanoparticles, nanoemulsions, microspheres, and electrospun nanofibers, are discussed for their ability to improve bioavailability and facilitate targeted delivery at the cellular level. Hydrogel-based platforms, particularly injectable and stimuli-responsive systems, are highlighted for their role in localised therapy and tissue engineering applications. Furthermore, the integration of 3D bioprinting technologies enables the fabrication of patient-specific scaffolds and implantable constructs for precision medicine and regenerative therapies. Stimuli-responsive systems, including pH-, temperature-, enzyme-, and externally triggered release platforms, further enhance on-demand drug release in diseased microenvironments. The biomedical applications of CBD-based systems are critically evaluated in antimicrobial therapy, wound healing, tumour-targeted cancer therapy, immunomodulation, microbiome regulation, and regenerative medicine. Finally, this review addresses current translational challenges such as drug loading efficiency, stability issues, scalability, and regulatory barriers, while highlighting future perspectives involving artificial intelligence-guided design, personalised nanomedicine, and advanced biomanufacturing technologies. Overall, CBD-based smart biomaterial platforms represent a highly promising approach for next-generation therapeutic systems with improved efficacy, safety, and clinical potential.

papers.abstract_en: This narrative Review provides a synthesis of the current evidence on the epidemiology, mechanisms, and interventions for unhealthy alcohol use (UAU) in people living with HIV (PLWH). UAU and HIV form a syndemic relationship that negatively impacts HIV treatment outcomes, including reduced antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence and viral suppression, and increased mortality. Despite the high prevalence rates of UAU among PLWH, screening and treatment gaps persist in this population. Behavioral factors-such as intentional ART skipping and condomless sex-and structural barriers, including poverty and alcohol-related stigma, further worsen HIV outcomes. Moreover, underutilized screening tools and provider hesitancy continue to hinder alcohol treatment for PLWH. Consequently, UAU remains underdiagnosed in PLWH, while those diagnosed are less likely to receive treatment. Promising interventions such as pharmacotherapy (e.g., naltrexone), cognitive behavioral interventions (e.g., motivational interviewing and contingency management), and combination economic empowerment programs (e.g. conditional and non-conditional cash transfers) are currently inconsistently implemented. Action is urgently needed to implement and standardize UAU screening and management in PLWH. Addressing this syndemic phenomenon demands a holistic approach combining medical/clinical, behavioral, and structural solutions to improve survival and quality of life for PLWH.

Content validity was assessed with 50 patients and 7 healthcare professionals in the first round, and 10 patients in the second round, evaluating the relevance, comprehensibility, and comprehensiveness of the French ED PREM. The endpoint was an item-level content validity index (I-CVI) > 0.78 and a scale-level content validity index (S-CVI) > 0.90 without suggestions for revision. RESULTS: Consensus was achieved in two rounds, with 100% expert participation and agreement. All French ED PREM items achieved a robust content validity (I-CVI > 0.78, S-CVI > 0,90) and demonstrated excellent agreement among evaluators beyond chance (k > 0.74). CONCLUSION: Through a rigorous cross-cultural adaptation of the ED PREM, this international collaborative research has demonstrated the content validity of the French ED PREM. This work contributes to the international harmonization of patient experience measures and may facilitate future comparisons across healthcare systems.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Adolescent alcohol consumption has declined across many high-income countries since the early 2000s, yet it remains unclear whether these reductions have led to less alcohol-related harm, particularly among higher-risk groups. METHODS: Using the National Ambulance Surveillance System, we examined ambulance attendances for alcohol intoxication among adolescents (10-19 years) in Victoria, Australia, from January 2012 and December 2023. Multivariable regression, stratified by gender, assessed monthly changes in attendance rates per 10 000 by remoteness, adjusting for seasonality and COVID-19 lockdowns. RESULTS: A total of 25 928 attendances were recorded. A small but significant monthly decline in alcohol intoxication ambulance attendance was observed among males in major cities (B = -0.01 [0.01], P < .001). No significant trends were identified for males in regional areas or for females in metropolitan or regional areas. CONCLUSION: Despite declining adolescent alcohol consumption, intoxication-related ambulance attendances have remained largely stable over the past decade. The modest decline among males in metropolitan areas was considerably smaller than survey-reported declines in consumption, suggesting that population surveys capture different drinking patterns than those leading to acute harms. These findings highlight the need for ongoing monitoring and targeted prevention strategies, particularly for high-risk subgroups and regional populations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Coastal communities in England and Wales face unique challenges that may contribute to disparities in healthy life expectancy (HLE). METHODS: This study uses 2021 Census data and mortality records to estimate HLE at birth across 7264 Middle-Layer Super Output Areas (MSOAs) in England and Wales. HLE was calculated using the Sullivan method. Coastal MSOAs were identified using population-weighted centroids within 2 km of the UK coastline. Linear regression models assessed the association between coastal classification and HLE, adjusting for region, deprivation, educational attainment, and industry of employment. Interaction terms explored whether deprivation moderated coastal health disparities. RESULTS: Coastal MSOAs exhibited significantly lower HLE than inland MSOAs, particularly in the South East and East of England regions. After adjusting for socioeconomic factors, the coastal disadvantage was attenuated but remained significant in the most deprived areas of select regions. Area deprivation was a strong predictor of reduced HLE, with each decile increase associated with a 1.5-year reduction in HLE. CONCLUSIONS: The findings challenge the notion of a uniform coastal health penalty, highlighting the importance of regional context and deprivation in shaping health outcomes. Targeted public health interventions should prioritize deprived coastal communities through fairer resource allocation and decentralization of decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: Radiotherapy can enhance anti-tumor immunity by modulating the tumor microenvironment. However, its direct effects on dendritic cells (DCs) as key antigen-presenting cells remain poorly studied. Although DCs are considered relatively radioresistant, their functional capacity following irradiation is controversial and likely subset-dependent. In this study, we systematically analyzed the radiosensitivity and post-irradiation functional capacity of murine bone marrow-derived conventional type 1 DCs (cDC1s), which play a pivotal role in initiating CD8+ T cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity, conventional type 2 DCs (cDC2s), and monocyte-derived DCs (MoDCs) in vitro. After irradiation, DC viability and surface marker expression were assessed. To evaluate functional competence, DCs were stimulated with high hydrostatic pressure-inactivated tumor cells in combination with the adjuvants poly I:C and α-CD40 as a model system for therapeutic tumor vaccination, and the phagocytic activity, activation, and cytokine/chemokine secretion of the DCs were analyzed. DC radiosensitivity depended strongly on both the subset and maturation state, with mature DCs showing higher radioresistance than their immature counterparts, and with immature cDC1s being particularly more susceptible. Nevertheless, surviving DCs retained their ability to phagocytose tumor cells and, upon stimulation, upregulate activation- and migration-associated markers and secrete cytokines and chemokines. In vivo, radio-immunotherapy promoted DC migration to the tumor-draining lymph node and induced DC activation, as indicated by elevated concentrations of DC-related cytokines in the peripheral blood. Within a fixed radiotherapy plus checkpoint inhibition regimen, tumor growth delay was largely preserved in Batf3-/- mice, lacking the cDC1 subset. Collectively, irradiation does not abrogate DC function, and anti-tumor immunity in radio-immunotherapy does not strictly require cDC1s.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Despite substantial reductions in stillbirth rate (SBR) over the past two decades, India continues to bear one of the highest burden of stillbirths worldwide. The available national evidence on stillbirth is fragmented, regionally variable, and often limited in scope. We aimed to determine stillbirth burden and risk factors leveraging a pooled cohort from ten prospective studies conducted across various settings in India. METHODS: We established the Indian Council of Medical Research-Stillbirth Pooled India Cohort (ICMR-SPIC), combining individual-level data from ten prospective cohort studies conducted across multiple sites of India. The pooled dataset included prospective pregnancy cohort studies conducted across India between 1994 and 2023 from rural, urban, hospital, and community settings, with participant recruitment and follow-up periods varying across individual studies. After exclusions, 227,821 pregnancies were included. Harmonised analytical datasets were constructed, and weighted SBR was estimated. Multivariable mixed-effects modified Poisson regression was used to evaluate the association between stillbirth and independent maternal and antenatal risk factors. Population attributable fractions (PAFs) were calculated for modifiable exposures. FINDINGS: A total of 3935 stillbirths occurred among 227,821 pregnancies, yielding a pooled weighted stillbirth rate of 14.8 per 1000 births (95% CI: 13.4-16.3). Independent risk factors included maternal age (>30 years) (aIRR 1.64, 95% CI: 1.55-1.72; PAF 3.23%, 95% CI: 2.97-3.48), informal maternal education (aIRR 1.45, 95% CI: 1.32-1.58; PAF 8.86%, 95% CI: 7.07-10.66), biomass fuel use (aIRR 1.37, 95% CI: 1.21-1.57; PAF 13.95%, 95% CI: 9.11-18.79), maternal height (<145 cm) (aIRR 1.32, 95% CI: 1.21-1.44; PAF 2.47%, 95% CI: 1.81-3.13), nulliparity (aIRR 1.36, 95% CI: 1.27-1.45; PAF 13.66%, 95% CI: 11.03-16.28), and previous history of stillbirth (aIRR 2.14, 95% CI: 1.15-3.97; PAF 2.13%, 95% CI: 0.97-3.29). Among obstetric complications, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (aIRR 4.18, 95% CI: 3.54-4.94; PAF 10.27%, 95% CI: 9.74-10.81) and antepartum haemorrhage (aIRR 12.12, 95% CI: 9.54-15.40; PAF 6.33%, 95% CI: 6.19-6.47) showed strong associations. INTERPRETATION: Our study shows that stillbirth burden remains high and factors such as women's education, biomass fuel use, hypertensive disorders, and antepartum haemorrhage were associated with higher risk of stillbirths. FUNDING: Indian Council of Medical Research, India.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: There has long been an interest in the association between family planning (contraception and abortion) and women's empowerment, with mixed evidence as to an association and most studies relying on cross sectional data. Within this body of work, less focus has been on how family planning impacts women's empowerment The aim of this study is to understand the impact of abortion denial resulting in having an unwanted birth on women's empowerment, measured by education, mobility and decision-making. METHODS: In the Nepal Turnaway Study, we followed women seeking abortions from 2019 to 2020 in Nepal and assessed whether receiving versus being denied an abortion was negatively associated with women's empowerment over five years (longitudinal cohort). We used linear and logistic mixed effects regression models to assess the effects of obtaining an abortion compared to carrying an unwanted pregnancy to term on education, mobility outside the home and household decision-making power. FINDINGS: We followed 1742 for 5 years and find that women who did not give birth were more likely to be in school (Risk Difference (RD) = 0.2 starting 18 months post-abortion seeking) and have greater decision-making power over five years (Risk Difference (RD) = -0.2 starting 12 months post-abortion seeking) and both of these continued for the remainder of the time period. We find no evidence that giving birth affects a woman's freedom to leave her home for shopping or connections to family and friends. INTERPRETATION: These findings suggest that being able to decide the timing and circumstances of childbearing has wide-ranging effects on women's empowerment (as measured by schooling and decision-making). papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Women may have adverse physical health following abortion denial and childbirth, particularly where maternal morbidity is high. This study aims to investigate mobility, self-rated physical health, and chronic pain associated with unwanted pregnancy among women seeking facility-based abortion services in Nepal. METHODS: Women seeking abortion at 22 facilities across Nepal in 2019-2020 completed surveys every six months for five years. This longitudinal cohort study assessed limited mobility, self-rated poor health, and chronic pain using weighted linear and logistic mixed effects regression, including among those seeking abortion for health reasons. We report time-specific marginal predicted probabilities for those denied (who gave birth and did not give birth) and those who obtained abortion. FINDINGS: Of the sample (n = 1742), 51% obtained care (Abortions), 15% gave birth (Turnaway-Births), and 33% were denied but did not give birth (Turnaway-NoBirths). Risk of any limited mobility was 15 percentage points higher (95% CI: 7%, 22%, p = 0.0001) for Turnaway-Births (predicted probability: 47%) versus Abortions (32%), and 2.5 days longer on average (95% CI: 1.42, 3.59, p < 0.0001; 5.3 versus 2.8 days); differences were larger among those seeking abortion for health reasons. Self-rated poor health, pelvic pain, and head pain did not differ for Turnaway-Births versus Abortions overall. Among the subsample, Turnaway-Births had poorer self-rated health at 18 months (0.09, [0.01, 0.16], p = 0.026), more back pain at 24-36 months (maximum risk difference: 0.17 [0.04, 0.31], p = 0.012), and less pelvic pain at 6 months (-0.08, [-0.015, -0.01], p = 0.036) compared to the Abortions. INTERPRETATION: Compared to the Abortions, Turnaway-Births experienced more limited mobility, and, among those who sought abortion for health reasons, poorer self-rated health and more chronic pain. Support for women seeking abortion, especially for health reasons, in obtaining timely care is needed to limit adverse physical health. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Rapid and precise pathogen identification is crucial for managing lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs). While metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) and targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) are emerging as valuable diagnostic tools, large-scale studies directly evaluating their real-world impact on antimicrobial stewardship remain scarce. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study encompassing 941 patients with suspected LRTIs who underwent bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) sequencing. Patients were evaluated in either an mNGS cohort (n = 479; DNA-only sequencing) or a tNGS cohort (n = 462; DNA and RNA sequencing). Diagnostic performance, pathogen spectrum, and clinical utility were compared against a composite final clinical diagnosis, which served as the reference standard. RESULTS: Both sequencing platforms demonstrated diagnostic efficacy superior to traditional laboratory tests. In the tNGS cohort, polymicrobial infections were highly prevalent (93.5%). Furthermore, tNGS demonstrated high sensitivity for fastidious pathogens, identifying 54 cases of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (a cohort in which routine smears missed 77.8% of cases) and effectively detecting Pneumocystis jirovecii. The overall diagnostic sensitivity was 90.6% (95% CI: 87.5-93.1%) for mNGS and 73.4% (95% CI:69.2%-77.3%) for tNGS. Guided by tNGS results, clinicians escalated antimicrobial therapy in 22.6% of positive cases. The clinical improvement rate following this targeted escalation was 66.2%, comparable to the 66.7% improvement rate observed in patients receiving appropriate initial empirical therapy (P = 0.946). CONCLUSION: Both tNGS and mNGS offer substantial diagnostic value for LRTIs, with tNGS showing particular utility in identifying fastidious and low-titer pathogens. Sequencing-guided diagnostics frequently informed antimicrobial adjustments and were associated with favorable clinical progress; however, future prospective paired-testing studies are required to isolate the direct impact of sequencing on patient survival outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is increasingly recognized in non-neutropenic patients, but validated bedside risk stratification tools remain scarce. We developed a machine learning model to predict IPA and tested whether corticosteroid effect depends on bacterial co-pathogen. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 837 non-neutropenic adults hospitalized with pulmonary infections across three tertiary hospitals in China between December 2020 and December 2025. The discovery cohort was split into training and internal validation sets. Four classifiers were compared, with Random Forest selected for optimal performance. The final model was externally validated in an independent cohort. Feature importance was assessed using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis. Corticosteroid-bacteria interactions were examined using subgroup analyses and propensity score matching, with the synergy index S calculated to quantify biological interaction. A simplified bedside score was derived from the top-ranking predictors. RESULTS: The Random Forest model achieved external validation AUC of 0.865. Six predictors consistently dominated across all assessments: Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation, hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 <200 mmHg), diabetes mellitus, organ failure (Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, SOFA >5), lymphopenia (lymphocyte count <0.8×109/L), and ICU (intensive care unit) admission. Corticosteroid exposure did not rank among the top six predictors. However, its association with IPA diverged sharply by bacterial context: OR below 1 with P. aeruginosa (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.214-1.283) but OR above 1 with other Gram-negative bacilli (OR 2.17, 95% CI 0.722-6.535); P for interaction = 0.131; a directional pattern that persisted after propensity matching. The six-variable score derived from these predictors showed AUCs of 0.869 (training), 0.774 (internal validation), and 0.719 (external validation). CONCLUSIONS: IPA risk in non-neutropenic ICU patients is shaped more by bacterial co-pathogen context than by corticosteroid exposure alone. The divergent corticosteroid effects across bacterial species challenge the conventional assumption of a uniform steroid-associated risk. The externally validated six-variable score offers a practical, software-free tool to support pathogen-informed, individualized risk stratification and clinical decision-making in the ICU.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: State Entropy (SE) and Surgical Pleth Index (SPI) parameters aim to optimise anaesthetic depth and intraoperative opioid administration, but their impact on postoperative complications remains unclear. Insufficient training and limited decision support may contribute to inconsistent findings. Thus, we evaluated whether tailored training to improve SE and SPI compliance reduced major postoperative complications. METHODS: Adult inpatients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk noncardiac surgery were included in this prospective single-centre before-after study in France. The educational intervention and outcomes were based on the Kirkpatrick framework. All anaesthesia providers were invited to participate voluntarily in lectures and bedside training on SE and SPI monitoring. Training impact was assessed using a composite of major postoperative complications within 28 days as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included changes in monitoring practices. RESULTS: Among 1,623 eligible patients, 1,025 were included over a 13-month period (517 before and 508 after training). Of 202 eligible providers, 91 participated in the one-month training programme (45%). After training, simultaneous SE and SPI sensor use increased from 26% to 42% (P < 0.001), and combined SE-SPI compliance increased from 23% to 39% (P < 0.001). Major postoperative complications occurred in 66/517 patients (13%) before and 71/508 patients (14%) after training (P = 0.6). Multivariable and propensity score analyses showed no significant association between the intervention and the primary outcome. CONCLUSION: This training did not reduce the incidence of major postoperative complications, despite improvements in intraoperative monitoring practices. Future educational strategies should strengthen provider engagement and reinforcement to translate improved monitoring practices into clinical benefit. REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06111248.

papers.abstract_en: Most advanced cancers eventually develop therapeutic resistance, often considered as a clinical endpoint but can be interpreted as an evolutionary state that exposes newly acquired dependencies and therefore creates a rationale for vulnerability-based treatment after standard options fail. This review summarizes resistance-associated vulnerabilities across genomic, epigenomic, signaling, cellular, and microenvironmental layers. At the genomic level, homologous recombination deficiency, deficient mismatch repair, chromosomal instability, and replication stress can inform DNA repair-directed, checkpoint-targeting, or immune-based strategies with different clinical evidence levels. At the epigenomic level, we propose chromatin-state maintenance vulnerability as an organizing concept describing adaptive dependence on chromatin-regulatory programs sustaining resistant phenotypes. This concept shifts epigenetic targeting away from isolated epigenetic marks to the machinery required to maintain a resistant phenotype. Compensatory signaling creates dependencies on specific network nodes, providing a rationale for combinations that suppress the pathways required for resistant-cell survival. Cancer stemness links molecular adaptations to persistent disease; interactions with a therapy-remodeled microenvironment create opportunities for intervention beyond direct tumor-cell killing. In this setting, therapeutic vulnerability may lie in reprogramming the surrounding ecosystem to restore antitumor immunity and treatment responsiveness. Additionally, we propose the concept of operational vulnerability biomarkers as measurements linked to a treatment-relevant dependency or functional susceptibility and a prespecified therapeutic decision. This decision-oriented framework complements established functional and dynamic biomarker concepts. By connecting resistant states with measurable dependencies, matched interventions, and clinical-trial strategies, the review provides a practical framework for developing and testing rational subsequent-line treatments while addressing the biological, analytical, and practical barriers to implementation.

papers.abstract_en: The 3'UTR encodes regulatory information that shapes transcript abundance and subcellular distribution, yet the underlying sequence rules remain incompletely defined. We quantified the effects of ∼2 million synthetic 3'UTR inserts in A549 and HCT116 cells on RNA output and nuclear-cytoplasmic partitioning. We identified a broad repertoire of short 2- to 8-nt elements. Their effects largely followed a dominant coupled axis linking high RNA output with cytoplasmic enrichment and low RNA output with nuclear enrichment and were predominantly additive. A context-aware deep learning model captures most of this behavior while revealing that strong context dependence is uncommon and emerges mainly in rare, extreme contexts consistent with higher-order constraints. Applying the model to ClinVar 3'UTR variants prioritizes a subset of pathogenic single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with aberrant predicted effects, frequently explained by creation or disruption of splice-site-like U1 motifs that can trigger telescripting-associated readthrough, highlighting a potent route to 3'UTR-driven disease mechanisms. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

papers.abstract_en: The aberrant inflammation that characterizes severe COVID-19 is incompletely understood. Given the persistence of SARS-Cov-2 RNA and nucleocapsid protein (N) and the presence of anti-N antibody during the course of severe infection, we investigated the role of RNA-containing immune complexes (ICs) in driving inflammation. We found that ICs consisting of SARS-CoV-2 RNA, N, and anti-N IgG1 are internalized by primary human monocytes and stimulate inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in a manner dependent on Fcγ receptors and partially dependent on toll-like receptor-8. In addition, the inflammatory response induced in monocytes by RNA-containing ICs caused endothelial dysfunction in vascularized micro-organs. Using nasopharyngeal samples from SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals, SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N were captured by anti-N monoclonal antibody in the absence of lysing reagents, indicating that SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N complexes are present outside of virions and cells. Finally, we found that during an early wave of COVID-19, higher anti-N IgG:IgM ratios were associated with more severe clinical outcomes, consistent with a role for inflammatory, IgG-mediated phagocytic clearance of nucleic acid-containing ICs in SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis, perhaps mitigated by non-inflammatory, IgM-mediated clearance. We conclude that RNA-containing ICs may play a role in the pathogenesis of severe COVID-19. Since all pathogenic viruses encode nucleic acid-binding proteins, such as N, and these proteins often elicit an antibody response, inflammatory clearance of nucleic acid-containing ICs may also contribute to disease severity in other viral infections.

papers.abstract_en: While zinc-ion interference therapy presents a compelling approach for cancer immunotherapy, poor intracellular bioavailability and weak innate immune activation restrict its therapeutic potential. To overcome these bottlenecks, we developed tetrahedral DNA-integrated ZnFe2O4-ZnO Janus nanoparticles (TDN-ZIZJP) to achieve spatiotemporal modulation of immunity. Distinct from conventional cubic nanoparticles, this nail-shaped Janus architecture amplifies cell-particle interactions, substantially improving tumor penetration and cellular uptake. This unique feature endows improved selectively dissolving of ZnO domain within the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment, resulting in a targeted intracellular surge of Zn2+. This enhanced ion flux provokes oxidative stress and endogenous DNA damage, thereby increasing the availability of endogenous cytosolic DNA. Moreover, the integrated tetrahedral DNA nanostructures serve as a robust reservoir, delivering abundant exogenous dsDNA directly into the cytoplasm. Zn2+-induced endogenous DNA release and TDN-derived exogenous dsDNA jointly increase the availability of cytosolic DNA substrates for cGAS. This dual-source DNA supply supports sustained cGAS-STING activation, thereby enhancing type I interferon signaling, promoting dendritic cell maturation and increasing cytotoxic T-cell infiltration. This study provides a new avenue that couples Zn2+-mediated ion interference and endogenous DNA damage with an exogenous dsDNA reservoir, providing a highly tunable platform for metal ion-regulated immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: Most patients with a newly diagnosed desmoid tumor should begin with multidisciplinary evaluation and active surveillance rather than immediate intervention, provided that symptoms are limited and further growth is unlikely to create irreversible morbidity. Treatment should be initiated when pain, functional limitation, sustained progression, or threatened critical structures make continued observation unacceptable. Percutaneous cryoablation is generally favored because the ice ball can be monitored directly, treatment can be personalized/tailored with the synergistic benefit of multiple probes, and the procedure can be repeated or staged when a complete margin would be unsafe. Complete ablation should be targeted when the entire tumor can be covered without jeopardizing skin, nerves, bowel, or other vulnerable structures; deliberate subtotal ablation is appropriate when the principal goal is pain relief or functional improvement and a safe circumferential margin is not achievable. Hydrodissection, skin warming, neural protection, and conservative treatment near critical anatomy are essential. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound is an attractive incisionless alternative for tumors with a favorable acoustic window. Microwave or radiofrequency ablation should be reserved for carefully selected lesions and experienced operators; electrochemotherapy and chemical ablation remain investigational with some promising early evidence. Embolization can be useful for hypervascular tumors that are poorly suited to direct percutaneous treatment. Local and systemic therapy should not be viewed as mutually exclusive: systemic treatment is often preferable for diffuse, intra-abdominal, or anatomically hazardous disease, while ablation can address a dominant symptomatic focus, residual viable tumor, or focal progression. Further study into the benefits and sequencing of combining local therapy with systemic or targeted options will be helpful in the multi-disciplinary evaluation of this complex patient cohort.

papers.abstract_en: Circularly permuted (CP) group II introns are self-splicing ribozymes that undergo a sequential branching and backsplicing reaction to yield branched introns and circular exons (circRNAs). While the initial branching step is structurally characterized, the mechanistic principles that govern the subsequent large-scale active-site remodeling and stringent metal-ion specificity required for backsplicing remain poorly understood. Here, we present a series of high-resolution cryo-EM structures of the CP group II intron from Gluconacetobacter diazotrophicus PAL5 (Gdi-1), capturing the ribozyme at discrete stages along the branching -to- backsplicing pathway under distinct ionic conditions. Comparative analyses under K+/Mg2+, K+/Ca2+, and Cs+/Mg2+ conditions demonstrate that productive backsplicing relies on ion-specific coordination networks that govern 3' splice site (3'SS) docking and catalytic center formation, revealing the precise metal-ion-coordinated conformational rearrangements and dynamic splice-site exchange mechanisms. Crucially, we identify a previously unrecognized, highly selective monovalent cation-binding site, K3, that structurally couples the γ-γ' interaction to reassembly of the heteronuclear four-metal core, thereby promoting productive second-step active-site formation. Together, these findings establish a structural basis for metal-ion-dependent active-site remodeling during group II intron catalysis and provide mechanistic insights into metal-ion selectivity in circRNA biogenesis.
