papers.abstract_en: Accurate quantum many-body calculations often depend on reliable reference states or good human-designed ansätze, yet such knowledge can become unreliable in hard problems like strongly correlated systems. Here we show that high-accuracy many-body ground states can be discovered directly from random Slater determinants. We introduce the Trimmed Configuration Interaction (TrimCI) method, which self-refines by iteratively expanding and trimming configurations in the variational space. TrimCI matches state-of-the-art accuracy using orders of magnitude fewer determinants and computer time: 106-fold fewer than a recent quantum computing calculation on an iron-sulfur cluster, 105-fold fewer than a leading classical method on a larger iron-sulfur cluster in nitrogenase, and over 99% of the ground-state energy of a strongly correlated lattice system from 10-28 of its Hilbert space, exceeding quantum Monte Carlo accuracy by orders of magnitude in some regimes. TrimCI thus provides an auto-initializing, accurate and highly efficient framework for quantum many-body systems, whose compact explicit wavefunctions enable direct and rapid evaluation of observables.

papers.abstract_en: Successful cancer immunotherapy requires not only tumor cell killing but also the activation of innate and adaptive immune responses. The inhibitor of apoptosis (IAP) proteins cIAP1, cIAP2 and XIAP act as key suppressors of RIPK1-driven immunogenic cell death, thereby enabling tumor immune evasion and limiting the effectiveness of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). ASTX660 (tolinapant) is a non-peptidomimetic antagonist with a balanced activity against all clinically relevant IAPs, designed to lower the TNF cytotoxicity threshold and sensitize tumors to T cell-mediated killing. Here, we present results from the phase I ASTEROID trial (NCT05082259), evaluating ASTX660 in combination with pembrolizumab in patients with advanced solid tumors. Primary endpoints were recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) and safety, while secondary endpoints were anti-tumor activity and pharmacokinetics. The combination was well tolerated and demonstrated early evidence of efficacy. RP2D was ASTX660 150 mg (7-days-on/14-days-off) with pembrolizumab. Overall response rate was 33%, including responses in ER⁺ breast cancers typically resistant to ICB. Integrated translational analyses reveal that response is associated with a TNF/IFN-enriched inflammatory tumor microenvironment, increased tumor antigenicity and enhanced TCR clonal diversity, whereas resistance correlates with a CCR4/6/7/8-driven TAM/Treg-dominant niche. Together, these results provide clinical proof-of-concept that dual IAP and PD-1 blockade sensitize tumors, while identifying candidate biomarkers to guide patient stratification in future studies.

papers.abstract_en: A trion is a charged exciton, which can be observed in many low-dimensional semiconductors. Circular dichroism (CD) of trions was demonstrated based on optical transitions following their spin selection rules, such as spin states of semiconductor quantum dots and valley spin polarization in monolayer two-dimensional materials. However, the configurational CD of trions, which is uniquely caused by chiral structures, has never been observed. In this study, the CD of trions in enantiopure single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) is demonstrated. Depending on the right- or left-handedness of the SWCNTs, the sign of the trion CD changes and is the same as that of the original exciton CD. Consequently, chiral trions exist in chiral SWCNTs.

papers.abstract_en: While rational electrode engineering has promoted the kinetics of lithium-sulfur batteries, persistent lithium polysulfide diffusion continues to undermine the cyclability of conventional liquid electrolyte systems. We propose a quasi-solid gel electrode design that integrates the sulfur species-blocking attributes of a solid-state system within a liquid electrolyte framework. This is achieved through a well-designed free radical-controlled-release polymerization strategy, which precisely governs the formation of a processable poly(ethyl cyanoacrylate) network. This approach enables secondary in situ gelation triggered by electrolyte infiltration, forming gel-phase electrode architectures. Mechanistically, the resulting gel-based electrode provides dynamically adaptive stress dissipation to accommodate volume variations, establishes continuous ion-permeable pathways for deeper positive electrode discharge, and acts as a synergistic physico-chemical barrier for sulfur species confinement. As a result, the positive electrode delivers a high initial capacity of 812.8 mA h g-1 at 2 C and sustains stable cycling operation over 1000 cycles. A 1.7 Ah-level pouch cell demonstrates potential for a sustained power supply for an unmanned aerial vehicle.

papers.abstract_en: Reactive gas-phase intermediates are often underappreciated in heterogeneous catalysis, despite their potential to control key catalytic steps. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that ketene can act as an intermediate in acetic acid ketonization, a mechanism that has long been debated. Using faceted TiO2(101) nanoparticles assembled into layers of controlled thickness, we show that ketene, formed from surface acetate, migrates through interparticle voids via desorption-readsorption events before reacting with surface acetate to yield acetone. Surface science and reactor studies reveal a direct correlation between ketene and acetone production and the depth to which the particle layers are saturated. Ab initio calculations support ketene's reactivity via low-barrier coupling pathways that converge on a common β-ketoacid intermediate. Here, we show that ketene can act as a mobile gas-phase intermediate and underscore the broader importance of spatially decoupled elementary steps in determining reactivity and selectivity in catalytic systems.

papers.abstract_en: Cells experiencing mitochondrial stress can undergo apoptosis or cell death that triggers innate immune activation. We examined the mechanisms determining these distinct outcomes in cancer. Abundant mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and high expression of the cGAS-STING pathway were features of KRAS-mutant cancers. In a pharmacological screen, MEK inhibitor (MEKi) effectively induced mtDNA release into the cytosol in KRAS-mutant cancer cells. However, MEKi also induced PRKN-mediated mitophagy, which limited mtDNA release by eliminating damaged mitochondria. Inhibition of mitophagy sustained mtDNA efflux and amplified cGAS-STING signaling. Mechanistically, PRKN-mediated mitophagy restrained mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) to limit mtDNA efflux. The balance between mtDNA and cytochrome c (cyt.c) release defined two immunologically distinct outcomes: immunogenic cell death (ICD) and apoptosis. In preclinical models, combined inhibition of MEK and mitophagy induced robust dendritic cell (DC) activation and promoted CD8+ T cell-mediated antitumor immunity. Consistently, PRKN expression negatively correlated with immune infiltration in human cancers. Collectively, these findings provide a rationale for combination strategies targeting mitochondrial dynamics to augment antitumor immunity.

papers.abstract_en: Sleep is essential for health, yet studying its dynamics requires manual sleep staging, a labor-intensive step in research and clinical care. Across centers, polysomnography (PSG) recordings are traditionally scored in 30-s epochs for pragmatic, not physiological, reasons and vary in electrode count, montage, and subject characteristics. These constraints challenge harmonized multi-center studies and the discovery of robust biomarkers on shorter timescales. We present AnySleep, a deep neural network that scores sleep from any electroencephalography (EEG) or electrooculography (EOG) data at adjustable temporal resolutions. We trained and validated the model on over 20,000 overnight recordings (>200,000 h of EEG and EOG) from 28 datasets across multiple clinics to promote robust generalization across sites. The model attains state-of-the-art performance and surpasses or equals established baselines at 30-s epochs. Performance improves with more channels, yet remains strong when EOG is absent, or only EOG or single EEG derivations (frontal, central, or occipital) are available. On sub-30-s timescales, the model captures short wake intrusions consistent with arousals and improves the prediction of pathophysiological conditions (obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, insomnia) over 30-s scoring. We make the model publicly available to facilitate large-scale studies with heterogeneous electrode setups and accelerate biomarker discovery in sleep.

papers.abstract_en: Maintaining appropriate vascular nitric oxide (NO) levels in pulmonary arteries is crucial for the alleviation of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). However, in the injured vascular microenvironment, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) deplete NO to generate peroxynitrite, which aggravates the oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction. Herein, ROS-responsive, zwitterionic nanogels (NGs), containing arginine pendants as NO precursors and encapsulating resveratrol (RSV) as an anti-oxidant, were developed for PAH management via inhalation. Benefiting from their zwitterionic surface that repels mucin adsorption, the inhaled NGs exhibit effective pulmonary mucus penetration and mucosal absorption, enabling robust diffusion to the injured pulmonary arteries. In the oxidative vascular microenvironment, the diselenide crosslinkers within the NGs are cleaved, promoting NGs dissociation and on-demand RSV release. The released RSV scavenges ROS and the arginine pendants are oxidized to generate NO, which cooperate to interrupt the ROS/NO disequilibrium. In a hypoxia/SU5416-induced PAH mouse model, inhaled NGs efficiently alleviate vascular remodeling and reduce pulmonary arterial pressure. This study offers an effective strategy for pulmonary drug delivery, and holds promising potentials for the management of PAH.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Recent randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses have questioned the safety of early pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants, suggesting possible increases in the risk of mortality and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Whether these risks vary by gestational age remains uncertain. We aimed to compare the effects of pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks versus those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater. METHODS: For this Bayesian model-averaged meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for randomised controlled trials enrolling infants with a gestational age less than 32 weeks and echocardiographically confirmed patent ductus arteriosus who were randomly assigned either to pharmacological treatment or to placebo or expectant management. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality before 36 weeks' postmenstrual age and secondary outcomes were moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated. RRs greater than 1 indicated harm. We calculated the posterior probability of harm (Prharm=P[logRR>0]) and Bayes factors comparing harm versus benefit (BFharm/benefit). This study is registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024622527). FINDINGS: Ten randomised controlled trials including 2365 infants (1133 female and 1232 male) were analysed; 1045 had a gestational age less than 26 weeks. Pharmacological treatment was associated with increased mortality in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks (RR 1·12 [95% CrI 0·90-1·41], Prharm=0·85, BFharm/benefit=5·48), in those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater (1·22 [0·90-1·77], Prharm=0·89, BFharm/benefit=7·82), and in the overall population (1·23 [95% CrI 1·00-1·54], Prharm=0·97, BFharm/benefit=36·04). For bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite outcome of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, analyses explicitly incorporating the possibility of no effect indicated that the data were more consistent with the no-effect model than with either the benefit or the harm model. INTERPRETATION: The currently available randomised evidence is consistent with an increased mortality risk associated with pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment, without evidence of a compensatory reduction in bronchopulmonary dysplasia. This association was evident both below and above the 26-week gestational age threshold. These findings question the safety of routine pharmacological treatment and underscore the need for more selective, evidence-based approaches for patent ductus arteriosus management. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors and antiangiogenic agents has demonstrated a synergistic antitumor effect in numerous solid tumors, but has rarely been investigated in pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC). We assessed the activity and safety of camrelizumab (a programmed cell death-1 inhibitor) plus famitinib (an antiangiogenic agent) in patients with PSC. METHODS: CAPSTONE is an open-label, single-arm, Simon two-stage, phase 2 trial done at eight sites in China. Eligible patients were aged between 18 and 75 years and had previously untreated stage IIIB-IV pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1, and at least one measurable lesion as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Patients received intravenous camrelizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks and oral famitinib 20 mg once daily until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response rate (ORR) as per RECIST version 1.1 in the full analysis set, which included all patients who received at least one dose of study drug. Safety was assessed in all as-treated patients. This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04888429, and enrollment is complete. FINDINGS: Between August 4, 2021 and March 21, 2024, 28 patients were enrolled. With a median follow-up of 18.1 months, the confirmed ORR was 42.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 24.5-62.8). The disease control rate was 85.7% (95% CI 67.3-96.0). The median duration of response was 16.0 months (95% CI 5.0-29.9); the median progression-free survival was 7.1 months (95% CI 3.5-12.5); and the median overall survival was 18.1 months (95% CI 10.3-28.1). Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) of grade 3 or more were observed in 10 (35.7%) patients, the most common being decreased platelet count (four [14.3%]) and decreased neutrophil count (three [10.7%]). Three (10.7%) patients discontinued camrelizumab, and three (10.7%) discontinued famitinib due to TRAEs. Two patients died of unknown cause, which were assessed by the investigator as possibly related to study treatment. INTERPRETATION: Camrelizumab plus famitinib showed antitumor activity in patients with locally advanced or metastatic PSC. This combination may be a potential first-line option for this patient population, and warrants further investigation in a large-sample trial. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Adjunctive psychoeducation can reduce recurrence of mood episodes in bipolar disorder (BD), but evidence from low-resource settings is scarce. We evaluated whether culturally adapted psychoeducation (CaPE) plus treatment-as-usual (TAU) prolongs time to recurrence in adults with BD in remission in Pakistan, a lower-middle-income country. METHODS: In this multi-centre, assessor-masked randomised controlled trial, adults with remitted bipolar I or II disorder at seven urban centres in Pakistan were randomly assigned to CaPE plus TAU or TAU alone. CaPE comprised 12 weekly individual sessions delivered by master's-level psychologists. The primary outcome was time to recurrence of any mood episode over 48 weeks, assessed with the Longitudinal Interval Follow-up Evaluation. Secondary outcomes included recurrence of depressive and manic/hypomanic episodes and clinical and quality-of-life measures. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05223959). FINDINGS: Between June 2022 and March 2025, 303 participants were randomly assigned (148 TAU, 155 CaPE plus TAU); 12-month data were available for 284 of 303 (93.7%). Over 48 weeks, CaPE prolonged time to recurrence of any mood episode versus TAU (adjusted hazard ratio 0.54, 95% CI 0.42-0.69; p < 0.001). At 12 months, CaPE improved recovery (measured with the Bipolar Recovery Questionnaire, on which higher scores indicate greater recovery; adjusted difference 144.8, 95% CI 51.5-238.1; p = 0.002), knowledge and attitudes (78.2, 22.6-133.8; p = 0.006), medication adherence (-0.4, -0.8 to -0.1; p = 0.013), and depressive symptoms (-5.3, -7.8 to -2.7; p < 0.0001). All adjusted estimates account for age, sex assigned at birth, marital status, weeks since diagnosis, and weeks in treatment. INTERPRETATION: Individual culturally adapted psychoeducation added to routine care reduced recurrence risk and improved clinical outcomes in Pakistani adults with BD, and could optimise maintenance treatment in Pakistan and other low-resource settings. FUNDING: Canadian Institutes of Health Research.

papers.abstract_en: Obesity and osteoporosis are two major public health concerns. Dysregulation of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) lineage commitment has been closely linked to an imbalance between adipogenic and osteogenic differentiation, which leads to abnormal lipid accumulation and impaired bone homoeostasis. However, as the underlying mechanisms remain unclear, effective treatment options for these two tightly linked diseases are still lacking. Herein, integrin subunit β-like 1 (ITGBL1) is identified as a key regulator of the adipogenic and osteogenic lineage commitment of MSCs. ITGBL1 is downregulated in MSCs from mouse models of high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity and ovariectomy (OVX)-induced osteoporosis. ITGBL1 deficiency promotes the adipogenic differentiation of bone marrow-derived MSCs, adipose-derived MSCs and adipogenic precursor cells while impairing the osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow-derived MSCs and osteogenic precursor cells. Mechanistically, ITGBL1 promotes the NEDD4-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of PPARγ. ITGBL1 deficiency stabilizes PPARγ to activate adipogenic transcriptional programs. PPARγ further undergoes reciprocal transrepression with RUNX2 in specific cellular contexts, and these transcription factors transrepress and transactivate ITGBL1 in osteogenic and adipogenic lineage precursor cells, respectively. Thus, ITGBL1, PPARγ and RUNX2 constitute an interconnected regulatory network‌ that governs the lineage commitment of MSCs. Therapeutically, adeno-associated virus serotype 9-mediated ITGBL1 supplementation significantly alleviates obesity and/or osteoporosis in HFD-fed mice, OVX mice and systemic ITGBL1-deficient mice. Our findings reveal that ITGBL1 is crucial for maintaining the balance between the adipogenic and osteogenic differentiation of MSCs and has notable medicinal effects for the prevention and treatment of obesity and osteoporosis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bronchiectasis is a chronic, heterogeneous lung disease of rising prevalence; however, contemporary epidemiological data are lacking. Furthermore, paediatric prevalence and cystic fibrosis (CF)-related bronchiectasis prevalence are frequently absent from existing literature. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the prevalence of bronchiectasis in the United States? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This retrospective, observational study utilised data from the Optum® Clinformatics® Data Mart claims database to estimate the age- and sex-standardised prevalence of bronchiectasis in the US in people of all ages and paediatrics (aged <18 years). Prevalence was stratified by age, sex, ethnicity and insurance coverage. Individuals were required to have ≥1 day of enrolment during the index period (2018-2022); the index date was the latest day in this period with ≥365 days of prior continuous enrolment. RESULTS: In the overall population, 94,392 cases of bronchiectasis were identified (median age, 76 years). Five-year prevalence was 221.6 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 220.1-223.1) per 100,000 persons and increased with age. Prevalence was higher among females (274.6 per 100,000 persons), Asians (302.3 per 100,000 persons) and Medicare Advantage enrolees (528.6 per 100,000 persons). In total, 1.4% of the overall population had a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. Five-year prevalence in the paediatric population (including 465 cases; median age, 12 years) was 11.9 (95% CI: 10.8-13.1) per 100,000 persons. Paediatric prevalence was similar between sexes, higher in Caucasians and higher in those with non-CF-related bronchiectasis than CF-related bronchiectasis. INTERPRETATION: This current study reports that bronchiectasis prevalence continues to increase in the US compared with previous studies, with a consistently higher prevalence in females and Asians, and that a lower proportion of individuals have CF-related bronchiectasis compared with non-CF-related bronchiectasis.

papers.abstract_en: Phytohormone crosstalk is fundamental to plant development and adaptation. While the coordinated actions of different hormones are well recognized, the underlying molecular mechanisms in specific biological processes remain largely elusive. Here, we identified the WmERF113-WmERF115 module as a central hub that mediated jasmonic acid (JA)/abscisic acid (ABA)-gibberellins (GA) antagonism to regulate leaf senescence in Welwitschia, a desert plant with only two leaves that grow continuously over an exceptionally long lifespan. We revealed that the JA/ABA-inducible transcription factor (TF) WmERF113 directly activated senescence-associated genes (SAGs), promoting senescence and chlorophyll degradation, whereas the GA-responsive WmERF115 repressed the same targets to mitigate senescence. Notably, WmERF113 and WmERF115 physically interacted to form a heterodimer, mutually inhibiting each other's binding to target promoters. Furthermore, these two TFs acted as reciprocal trans-acting factors, repressing each other's expression through promoter cross-binding. This multiple-layer regulatory circuit ensured that leaf senescence of Welwitschia progressed in a temporally and spatially restricted manner. Our study provided an important conceptual framework in which phytohormone crosstalk was translated into TF antagonism for fine-tuning senescence, offering new insights into the adaptive strategies that enable plant survival in extreme environments.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To assess the global and country-level greenhouse gas emissions implications of external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) scale-up to 2050. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We conducted a country-level, scenario-based study across 181 countries to estimate EBRT-associated greenhouse gas emissions in 2022 and project emissions to 2050 under utilisation benchmarks of 50% and 64%, uniform schedules of 25, 15, and 5 fractions per course, and prespecified income-stratified Moderate and Ambitious hypofractionation pathways. Country-specific utilisation was examined as an access-constrained sensitivity scenario. RESULTS: Across all scenarios, global EBRT-associated emissions increased from 2022 to 2050. With 25-fraction delivery, emissions rose from 43.02 to 67.94 MtCO2e under the 50% utilisation and from 55.06 to 86.96 MtCO2e under the 64% utilisation. Under the 50% benchmark, 15- and 5-fraction schedules reduced 2050 emissions to 40.76 and 13.59 MtCO2e, respectively. Emissions shifted towards middle-income settings: the high-income share declined from 42.9% to 36.5%, while the 10 countries with the largest modelled EBRT-associated emissions still accounted for 64.5% of global emissions in 2022 and 60.6% in 2050. Compared with a uniform 25-fraction baseline, the Moderate pathway reduced global emissions by 23.3% in 2022 and 21.9% in 2050, while the Ambitious pathway reduced emissions by 36.5% and 34.7%, respectively. The largest absolute reductions occurred in high-income and upper-middle-income settings. CONCLUSION: Global EBRT-associated emissions are projected to rise substantially by 2050. Clinically appropriate hypofractionation offers a high-leverage mitigation opportunity, with priorities differing between decarbonising established high-volume systems and embedding low-carbon delivery during capacity expansion.

papers.abstract_en: Groundwater is a key resource for dry-season irrigation in central Myanmar, yet its mineral saturation characteristics and implications for agricultural infrastructure remain poorly understood. This study presents a hydrogeochemical assessment of groundwater from 17 government-operated irrigation wells in southern Tatkon Township, Nay Pyi Taw, Myanmar. Field measurements, laboratory analyses, and PHREEQC modelling were used to evaluate irrigation water quality and calcite saturation. Groundwater from most sampled wells is characterised by a Ca-Mg-HCO3 type, with hydrochemical composition mainly influenced by natural water-rock interactions, including probable carbonate weathering contributions. Most sampled wells show acidic to near-neutral conditions and are undersaturated with respect to calcite, with SIcalcite values ranging from - 2.06 to + 0.73 whereas one well shows localised calcite supersaturation. Sodium Adsorption Ratio (SAR) values ranged from 0.91 to 3.42, remaining well below the critical threshold of 10 and indicating low sodium hazard. Conventional salinity- and sodicity-based indices indicate that most sampled groundwater has generally acceptable conditions for maintaining soil infiltration and hydraulic functioning. However, calcite undersaturation, together with acidic conditions in several wells, suggests potential concerns for concrete linings and metal pumping infrastructure, while localised supersaturation may indicate a scaling tendency. These findings highlight that irrigation management within the investigated well network should consider both soil related suitability and the potential effects of groundwater chemistry on irrigation infrastructure.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Family caregivers provide essential support to older adults with disabilities from the community to nursing home settings. Yet little is known about how caregiving intensity and caregiver well-being differ across settings. METHODS: Using pooled 2021-2024 NHATS/NSOC data, we conducted repeated cross-sectional analyses of primary caregivers of US adults aged 71+ with disability residing in community, residential care, and nursing home settings. We compared caregiving experiences across settings. RESULTS: Overall, 60.4% of older adults had an identified caregiver, including 74.4% of nursing home residents, 63.8% of residential care residents, and 58.8% of community-dwelling adults. Caregivers of community-dwelling adults had the highest average caregiving hours (34.7 hours/week), compared with caregivers of older adults in residential care (14.4) and nursing homes (13.7). Depressive symptoms, anxiety, and financial difficulty were similar across settings. Emotional difficulty was more common among caregivers of residential care (46.7%) and nursing home residents (43.5%) than community caregivers (31.5%). Caregivers in the community were more likely to forgo social activities due to caregiving (26.8%) but were also more likely to report substantial perceived caregiving gains (score ≥6 on an 8-point scale; 72.0%). CONCLUSION: Caregiving persists in institutional settings, with responsibilities shifting rather than disappearing, underscoring the need for supports across settings.

papers.abstract_en: Motivated by the high prices of branded/patented pharmaceuticals in many parts of the world, this paper analyzes price regulations in a two-country (home and foreign) model where a single home firm serves both markets and its R&D investment determines product quality. We study two types of price regulations: direct price controls (PCs) and external reference pricing (ERP) under which the price that the firm is permitted to charge locally depends upon its price abroad. We show that although ERP undermines R&D incentives, its implementation can raise home welfare. However, home's optimal ERP policy is too restrictive from a joint welfare perspective. Furthermore, if the foreign market is subject to a PC, home prefers ERP to a PC due to strategic considerations that come into play due to the international price linkage created by ERP.

papers.abstract_en: Neutralizing antibodies act rapidly against SARS-CoV-2, but monoclonal antibodies are costly to manufacture and single-domain antibodies are cleared rapidly. Here we evaluated an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platform encoding the neutralizing nanobody VHH 72 and optimized the carrier by raising DSPC from 10 to 40 mol% and the citrate buffer from 25 to 300 mM. Relative to 10%PC-25mM, 40%PC-300mM produced larger particles (approximately 193 versus 75 nm), lower polydispersity, high encapsulation efficiency and better mRNA preservation in 50% serum (approximately 80% versus 43% at 24 h). Molecular dynamics simulations of the two lipid compositions gave structural descriptors consistent with tighter packing at 40 mol% DSPC, but did not address free energy or the citrate effect. In HEK293T cells, 40%PC-300mM increased VHH 72-eGFP-positive cells at 24, 48 and 72 h and cell-associated fusion protein at 72 h. In CD-1 mice, DiD-associated fluorescence declined more slowly in blood and was higher in liver through 72 h and spleen through 48 h; a luciferase reporter showed higher organ expression and a whole-body advantage through day 5. Serum VHH 72 peaked later and higher with 40%PC-300mM, and neutralizing activity persisted through day 7. In K18-hACE2 mice challenged intraperitoneally or intratracheally 1, 3 or 7 days after treatment, 40%PC-300mM gave the lowest blood and lung pseudovirus reporter signals at day 3 and was the only treatment significantly below PBS at day 7. These data support formulation optimization as a way to improve mRNA protection, reporter expression and the duration of functional VHH 72 exposure. Because the study used reporter constructs, a lipophilic dye, pseudovirus and mice, it does not establish intact-LNP biodistribution or protection against authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Aspiration is common in neonatal age, especially with a history of prematurity, and it can be silent until causing significant respiratory sequelae. The objective of this study is to evaluate the respiratory evolution of premature patients diagnosed with pulmonary aspiration during the first six months of life, using fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES). METHODS: Retrospective study of premature infants in whom FEES was performed over a period of 12 years. They were classified into 2 groups: aspiration vs non-aspiration. Respiratory events were studied in a 3-year follow-up in both groups. RESULTS: Sixty-two preterm infants younger than six months were included (39 with aspiration and 23 without aspiration). The mean gestational age was 28 weeks and the median age at FEES was 2.7 months. Approximately 60% of patients had associated comorbidities, with bronchopulmonary dysplasia being the most frequent. Thickened feeds were recommended in 82.1% of aspiration cases. During follow-up, hospital admissions due to respiratory causes occurred in 43.6% of the aspiration group and 52.2% of the non-aspiration group. The most common respiratory events were: upper respiratory tract infections (79.5%vs78.3%), bronchiolitis/bronchitis (76.9%vs69.6%), laryngitis (15.4%vs13%), brief resolved unexplained events (0% vs 13%), and pneumonia (30.8%vs26.1%). Although pneumonia appeared slightly earlier among infants with aspiration, no statistically significant differences were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Over a three-year follow-up period, preterm infants diagnosed with aspiration and receiving appropriate treatment exhibited respiratory morbidity comparable to thouse without aspiration. Long-term follow-up with lung function and imaging tests of these patients would be necessary to determine their subsequent evolution.

papers.title_zh: 来那度胺-地塞米松联合放疗治疗孤立性浆细胞瘤的长期结局：回顾性队列显示无进展生存改善，但无多发性骨髓瘤生存未见显著差异
papers.title_en: Long-Term Outcomes of Lenalidomide-Dexamethasone in Combination With Radiotherapy in Solitary Plasmacytoma.
papers.authors: Loap P, Laroze S, Bouscary D, Vignon M, Kirova Y
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiation Oncology, Institut Curie, Paris, France; Imaging, Innovative Radiotherapy and System Medicine, U…
papers.results: 中位随访6.31年；仅3例局部复发。来那度胺-地塞米松组无进展生存更长（HR 0.315；95%CI 0.128-0.775；p=0.012），10年无进展生存率71.8% vs 26.7%（单纯放疗）。联合治疗组6例进展者中3例（50.0%）进展为多发性骨髓瘤、3例（50.0%）为多发性浆细胞瘤。无多发性骨髓瘤生存两组差异无统计学意义（10年率86.6% vs 65.9%；p=0.19）。
papers.authors_conclusion: 来那度胺-地塞米松联合放疗与孤立性浆细胞瘤无进展生存的持续改善相关；这些长期结果支持对初诊即联合来那度胺-地塞米松加放疗进行前瞻性评估。
papers.ai_note: 两个主要终点中，无多发性骨髓瘤生存（MMFS）为阴性（p=0.19），结论主要建立在阳性的无进展生存上，属主要终点一半阴性时的选择性强调；未报告MMFS的HR及置信区间。回顾性非随机设计，分组依赖治疗年代与医师选择（2008年后PET/CT分期引入亦改变分期迁移），存在适应证混杂与时代效应；样本量小、进展事件少（联合组仅6例），PFS的HR置信区间宽；摘要未提供多因素校正结果。

pico.p: 2004-2025年连续收治的孤立性浆细胞瘤患者75例（均行骨髓评估、血清游离轻链检测及MRI，2008年末起常规PET/CT分期）
pico.ic: 放疗联合来那度胺-地塞米松（n=33）对比单纯放疗（n=42）

papers.reason: 为孤立性浆细胞瘤这一罕见浆细胞肿瘤提供长期随访的对照基线，提示全身治疗可能延缓进展但未证实降低进展为多发性骨髓瘤的风险，可作为前瞻性试验设计与终点选择的参考；与胸科日常手术/结节决策关联有限。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Radiotherapy achieves excellent local control in solitary plasmacytoma, but systemic progression remains a major limitation. We evaluated the long-term association between lenalidomide-dexamethasone combined with radiotherapy and disease outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database included 75 consecutive patients with solitary plasmacytoma treated between 2004 and 2025. All patients underwent bone marrow assessment, serum free light-chain testing, and magnetic resonance imaging, with PET/CT routinely incorporated into staging from late 2008 onward. Patients received radiotherapy alone (n=42) or radiotherapy combined with lenalidomide-dexamethasone (n=33). Primary endpoints were progression-free survival and multiple myeloma-free survival. Systemic progression-free survival, defined by progression to multiple myeloma, multiple plasmacytomas, or distant solitary plasmacytoma, was additionally evaluated. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 6.31 years. Only three local recurrences occurred. Lenalidomide-dexamethasone was associated with longer progression-free survival (HR, 0.315; 95% CI, 0.128-0.775; p=0.012), with 10-year rates of 71.8% versus 26.7% after radiotherapy alone. Among the six patients progressing after combined treatment, three (50.0%) developed multiple myeloma and three (50.0%) developed multiple plasmacytomas. Multiple myeloma-free survival did not differ significantly between groups (10-year rates, 86.6% vs 65.9%; p=0.19). CONCLUSION: Lenalidomide-dexamethasone combined with radiotherapy was associated with sustained improvement in progression-free survival in solitary plasmacytoma. These long-term findings support prospective evaluation of upfront lenalidomide-dexamethasone in combination with radiotherapy for solitary plasmacytoma.

papers.abstract_en: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. Comparative statistical analysis of organs across genetic backgrounds requires spatial, single-cell, atlas-scale data in replicates. Here we introduce atlas-scale transcriptome localization using aggregate signatures (ATLAS), a scalable tissue mapping method that learns transcriptional signatures from single-cell RNA sequencing data, encodes them in situ with tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes and decodes them to infer cell types and imputed transcriptomes. We validated ATLAS against direct MERFISH measurements of marker genes and through quantitative comparisons to four other technologies. We profiled 40 million cells across more than 400 coronal sections from central brains of five male and five female C57BL/6J mice and five male BTBR T+tf/J mice, an idiopathic autism model. Our analysis revealed more than 40 significant differences in cell-type distributions and identified 16 regional composition changes across male-female and B6-BTBR comparisons. ATLAS thus enables systematic comparative studies, facilitating organ-level structure-function analysis of disease models.

papers.abstract_en: Vγ9Vδ2 T cells mediate HLA-independent targeting of tumor cells, offering unique opportunities for cancer immunotherapy, yet their therapeutic efficacy remains limited. Here, using a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify UDP-galactose 4-epimerase (GALE) as a tumor-intrinsic checkpoint that restricts Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated killing. GALE is a key nucleotide-sugar metabolic enzyme that controls the interconversion of UDP-galactose and UDP-glucose, thereby supporting protein glycosylation and cell-surface glycan remodeling. Mechanistically, GALE promotes complex N-glycosylation of CD155 and CEACAM1, favoring their engagement with the inhibitory receptors TIGIT and TIM3, respectively, while limiting CD155 binding to the activating receptor CD226. GALE loss potentiates Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated tumor killing in multiple mouse models and colorectal cancer patient-derived organoids. Together, these findings reveal how nucleotide-sugar metabolism shapes tumor-immune communication through complex N-glycan remodeling and identify GALE and its downstream receptor-ligand interactions as potential therapeutic targets for enhancing Vγ9Vδ2 T cell antitumor activity.

papers.abstract_en: It is unclear whether human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) can be used as a nutrient source by Streptococcus pneumoniae. Here, we investigate whether and how S. pneumoniae metabolizes HMOs and whether these compounds inhibit pneumococcal adherence. We find that S. pneumoniae can metabolize several HMOs, except for 2'-fucosyllactose (2'FL). The process is regulated by the carbon catabolite repression system. Transcriptome analyses showed reduced expression of the lac operon I (lacABCD) in bacteria grown with two tested HMOs when compared to lactose (Lac). Genes for the Leloir pathway and exoglycosidases were upregulated. A genome-wide CRISPR interference screen showed that the lac operons I and II (lacEFG-2) are essential for metabolizing HMOs. Lac and non-metabolizable 2'FL were found to inhibit pneumococcal adherence to host cells in vitro. Importantly, 2'FL showed a stronger inhibitory effect compared to Lac in vivo. Further research is warranted to investigate whether the non-metabolizable 2'FL can be used to inhibit pneumococcal adherence.

papers.abstract_en: LUAD exhibits diversity in the mechanisms of angiogenesis and the tumor environment's responses to anti-VEGF therapy, while the tumor-cell-intrinsic mechanisms that prevent vascularization are not well understood. SCGB3A2 (secretoglobin 3A2; HIN-2/UGRP1) is a club/secretory marker of pulmonary adenocarcinoma without established angiogenic function. By using an unsupervised integration approach of two public LUAD single-cell RNA-seq cohorts, we described a SCGB3A2-high malignant epithelial state characterized by an angiogenesis-low phenotype as indicated by the low presence of VEGFA, hypoxic conditions, and a low epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), along with a secretory/anti-inflammatory program, which was confirmed in independent bulk cohorts (TCGA-LUAD, GSE72094) showing that SCGB3A2-high tumors experienced lower instances of angiogenesis, hypoxia, and scores related to EMT/invasion. Using spatial transcriptomics, we positioned SCGB3A2-high tumor cells next to endothelial cells and identified a spatially inferred VEGFA/B-FLT1 interaction pattern. In A549 and NCI-H1975 cells, conditioned medium from SCGB3A2-overexpressing cells contained higher levels of extracellular PGK2-immunoreactive signal and angiostatin and was associated with reduced HUVEC tube formation and VEGFR2 phosphorylation. Thus, SCGB3A2 is a marker for LUAD tumors characterized by low levels of angiogenesis, which is associated with an extracellular PGK2/angiostatin signal.

papers.abstract_en: Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) have emerged as a valuable tool for genetic risk prediction and stratification in human diseases. Over the past decade, extensive methodological efforts have focused on improving the predictive power of PRS, leading to the development of numerous methods for PRS construction. Benchmarking these various methods thus becomes an essential task that is crucial for guiding future PRS applications. While studies have benchmarked subsets of these methods on specific phenotypes and cohorts, the resulting evidence remains fragmented, with a lack of work that comprehensively assess the relative performance of the various PRS methods. We addressed this gap by constructing a PRS method benchmarking database, synthesizing published results in 2009-2025 and conducting spectral ranking inference with uncertainty quantification to rank 14 single ancestry summary statistics-based PRS methods that had sufficient benchmarking evidence to support reliable ranking. We constructed rankings using two complementary sources: original method-development studies and applications/benchmarking studies. While the highest-ranked methods (LDpred2 and AnnoPred) and the lowest-ranked method (C + T) were consistently identified from both sources, the relative ordering of most methods showed moderate variability. We further constructed phenotype-specific rankings, providing more detailed insights into the robustness and phenotype-specific strengths of individual methods. Collectively, the overall and phenotype-specific rankings of the PRS methods, along with the detailed model performance data curated from the literature, form a dynamic benchmarking database that can be continuously updated as new PRS methods and published benchmarking evidence emerge, providing a practical resource for future PRS method selection and application.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: We aimed to quantify the association between severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and the risk of incident diabetes. We also aimed to estimate the global burden of incident type 2 diabetes (T2D) attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies identified through PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and CENTRAL from inception to 29 January 2026. Adjusted relative risks (RRs) for incident T2D and type 1 diabetes (T1D) following SARS-CoV-2 infection were pooled using random-effects models. Population attributable fractions (PAFs) and attributable T2D cases were estimated by integrating pooled risk estimates with Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data on COVID-19 prevalence and T2D incidence. RESULTS: Fifteen cohort studies involving approximately 48.9 million participants were included. SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with an increased risk of incident T2D (13 studies; pooled RR, 1.25 [95% CI, 1.16-1.34]), although substantial heterogeneity was observed and the 95% prediction interval (PI) included the null (0.94-1.66). In subgroup analysis, the association was confined to mixed-variant studies (RR, 1.29 [95% CI, 1.23-1.36]; 95% PI, 1.09-1.54), whereas studies evaluating a single variant (Delta or Omicron) showed no excess risk (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.97-1.03]). The association with incident T1D did not reach conventional statistical significance (10 studies; pooled RR, 1.13 [95% CI, 0.99-1.30]). Globally, 24.53 million incident T2D cases occurred in 2023. The PAF attributable to COVID-19 of 1.12% (95% CI 0.90, 1.35), corresponding to 274,889 (95% CI 220,360, 331,698) incident T2D cases attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection. The largest attributable burdens were observed in India, the USA, and China. CONCLUSIONS: SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with a modest increase in pooled T2D risk. This association was primarily observed in mixed-variant studies, for which the 95% PI excluded the null. However, the overall pooled estimated was accompanied by substantial between-study heterogeneity, and its 95% PI crossing the null, indicating uncertainty in the association across populations and settings. At the population level, this excess risk translated into an estimated 275,000 incident T2D cases attributable to COVID-19 worldwide in 2023, highlighting the need for ongoing metabolic surveillance following infection. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Anti-Ro52/TRIM21 shows contradictory prognostic associations in interstitial lung disease (ILD), protective in some cohorts and adverse in others. We evaluated whether it acts as an independent predictor or a phenotypic marker and whether its effect is modified by disease subtype and myositis-specific antibodies. METHODS: We retrospectively identified 538 adults with radiologically confirmed interstitial lung disease (228 anti-Ro52-positive) from a 2010-2020 single-center cohort. Cox proportional-hazards models were sequentially adjusted for demographic, smoking, malignancy, and pulmonary-function covariates. Pre-specified effect modification by connective tissue disease (CTD) status and myositis-specific antibodies was assessed by likelihood-ratio interaction tests with false-discovery-rate correction. Robustness to missing data was supported by multiple imputation (m = 20) and a missing-not-at-random (MNAR) tipping-point analysis. RESULTS: Ro52 positivity was associated with younger age, CTD predominance, and lower complement levels. Pre-specified effect modification was suggested: anti-Ro52 trended toward lower mortality in CTD-ILD (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.49-1.07, P = 0.104) but did not independently increase mortality within the anti-MDA5-positive subgroup (HR 1.73, 95% CI 0.66-4.54). Instead, the adverse prognostic effect of anti-MDA5 was numerically greater among anti-Ro52-positive than Ro52-negative patients (MDA5 HR 10.57, 95% CI 3.60-31.03 vs. 2.56, 95% CI 0.97-6.74), although the formal interaction term did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.055). The fully adjusted (Model 6) HR was 0.72 (95% CI 0.52-0.99; P = 0.045); further adjustment for CTD status (Model 7) attenuated the association to non-significance (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.54-1.04, P = 0.091), and IPCW weighting and time-varying-age analyses were likewise non-significant; malignancy independently predicted mortality (HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.15-2.88; P = 0.012). CONCLUSION: Anti-Ro52 is a context-dependent phenotypic marker of immune-mediated ILD, not a universal prognostic biomarker. Its prognostic association is heterogeneous across ILD phenotypes: it is not independently protective in CTD-ILD (adjusted HR 0.73, P = 0.104), whereas the adverse prognostic effect of anti-MDA5 was numerically greater among anti-Ro52-positive than Ro52-negative patients (MDA5 HR 10.57 vs. 2.56), although this interaction did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.055); CTD-status adjustment similarly attenuated the Ro52 association (HR 0.75, P = 0.091). These findings support stratified prognostic models integrating Ro52 with autoantibody and disease-subtype context.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) is a promising technique for diagnosing infectious diseases. However, research on mcfDNA-based mNGS for diagnosing infections in liver transplantation (LT) recipients remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of plasma mcfDNA mNGS during the early post-LT period. METHODS: In this prospective diagnostic cohort study, adult LT recipients underwent plasma mcfDNA mNGS on postoperative days 7 and 14. The findings were compared with results of the blood cultures and other conventional microbiological tests at the species level. RESULTS: Among 193 LT recipients, mNGS positivity was observed in 14.5% on day 7 and 21.8% on day 14. The concordance between mNGS and blood culture for bacterial pathogens was modest on days 7 (35.0%) and 14 (14.3%) but increased substantially when other clinically relevant specimens were included (80.0% and 71.4%, respectively). mNGS identified additional pathogens not detected using blood culture in 59.3% and 74.2% of cases on days 7 and 14, respectively. Viral pathogens, including cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, and roseolovirus, were also detected. Among the 13 discordant cases (blood culture-positive and mNGS-negative), two (15.4%) were classified as contamination/colonization, five (38.5%) as weak positives, and six (46.2%) as not detected by mNGS. CONCLUSION: Plasma mcfDNA mNGS demonstrated substantial concordance with conventional microbiological testing when clinically relevant specimens were considered. mNGS may serve as a useful adjunct tool for early pathogen detection and clinical assessment of LT recipients.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To characterize the metabolic and inflammatory signatures distinguishing fatigued from non-fatigued HIV immunological non-responders (INRs) and to explore candidate biomarkers and potential mechanistic pathways underlying HIV-associated fatigue. METHODS: We performed untargeted metabolomics and cytokinomics on plasma obtained from 18 fatigued and 17 non-fatigued HIV-INRs. Mechanistic insights were explored via Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) networks and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. RESULTS: Compared to non-fatigued controls, the fatigued cohort showed significant up-regulation of 4-ketopimelic acid, cholesterol, and 1-hexadecyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine, with concurrent down-regulation of DL-arginine and D-pipecolic acid (P < 0.05). Immunologically, the fatigued group displayed elevated macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) but reduced interferon-induced protein 10 (IP-10/CXCL10) and interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels (P < 0.05). Functional enrichment analysis suggested the involvement of necroptosis, lipid metabolism, and atherosclerosis signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: Fatigue in HIV-INRs receiving long-term antiretroviral therapy was associated with distinct lipidomic and cytokinomic alterations. These results underscore the potential roles of dysregulated fatty acid metabolism, oxidative stress, and chronic low-grade inflammation in the pathophysiology of fatigue. Cholesterol and IL-18 emerged as candidate biomarkers associated with HIV-associated fatigue; however, their combined discriminatory performance was not statistically validated in this exploratory study and requires confirmation in larger, independent cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Oral dysbiosis has been associated with inflammatory processes in acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD). However, whether Aspergillus-associated or Candida-positive status is associated with distinct oral multi-omics profiles, and whether these profiles change following treatment, remains unclear. METHODS: In this prospective cohort study (August 2024 to July 2025), 18 AECOPD patients were enrolled and stratified into non-fungal exacerbators (n=6), Aspergillus-associated AECOPD (n=6), and Candida-positive AECOPD (n=6). Oral samples were collected before treatment and, where available, after treatment. The primary analyses compared pretreatment microbial and metabolic profiles across fungal-status groups, whereas longitudinal pre/post-treatment analyses were secondary and exploratory and were performed only in groups with sufficient paired samples. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups. At pretreatment, Aspergillus-associated AECOPD showed significantly reduced α diversity and distinct microbial community separation from non-fungal exacerbators (Bray-Curtis R = 0.378, P = 0.009), whereas Candida-positive AECOPD showed no significant global shift. At the genus level, exploratory LEfSe analysis identified distinct subgroup-associated candidate taxonomic signatures. PICRUSt2-based predicted functional profiles were broadly similar across groups. Metabolomic profiling showed the most pronounced baseline differences in the Aspergillus-associated group, with 11 upregulated and 90 downregulated metabolites versus the non-fungal group. Differential metabolites in this baseline comparison were predominantly mapped to sphingolipid metabolism, purine metabolism, one-carbon metabolism, and cAMP/cGMP signaling pathways. In secondary exploratory longitudinal analyses, metabolic shifts were observed in the non-fungal group (4 upregulated and 78 downregulated metabolites) and the Candida-positive group (14 upregulated and 8 downregulated metabolites). No formal longitudinal analysis was performed in the Aspergillus-associated group because only two post-treatment samples were available. O2PLS identified shared cross-omics variation distinguishing pretreatment Aspergillus-associated from non-fungal AECOPD, with several microbial and metabolite features contributing to the shared latent component. CONCLUSION: Compared with non-fungal and Candida-positive AECOPD, Aspergillus-associated AECOPD showed the most pronounced pretreatment oral microbial dysbiosis and metabolic alterations. These findings support the presence of a distinct oral microbial-metabolic phenotype associated with Aspergillus status and provide candidate signatures for future validation in larger longitudinal cohorts. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment and chronic pain have become major public health challenges, adversely affecting the lives of middle-aged and older adults. However, longitudinal evidence on pain characteristics and subsequent cognitive outcomes in Chinese populations remains limited. We examined whether baseline pain characteristics were associated with the risk of developing scale-identified cognitive impairment among middle-aged and older Chinese adults. METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study included 7,899 CHARLS participants aged 45 years and older who were free of scale-identified cognitive impairment at baseline in 2015 and had follow-up cognitive assessment data in 2020. Pain distribution and location were assessed by self-report. Cognitive function was measured using episodic memory and mental acuity tests, and scale-identified cognitive impairment was defined as a cognitive function score at least 1 SD below the wave-specific mean. Cox regression models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, sleep duration, and number of chronic diseases. RESULTS: Over an average follow-up period of 60.1 months, 21.2% of participants developed scale-identified incident cognitive impairment. Compared with the no-pain group, those experiencing multi-site pain exhibited a modestly higher risk of incident cognitive impairment (adjusted HR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.05 to 1.33). Subgroup analyses revealed that the risk remained significant among females (adjusted HR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.05 to 1.51) and individuals aged < 60 years (adjusted HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.44). Participants with headache-associated pain had a higher risk of scale-identified incident cognitive impairment (adjusted HR = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.15 to 1.53) compared with those without pain. CONCLUSIONS: Multi-site pain and headache-associated pain were associated with modestly elevated risks of scale-identified incident cognitive impairment. Considering the scale-identified cognitive outcomes and self-reported pain assessment, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Future studies with more detailed pain measures and longer follow-up are warranted.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Diagnosis of asthma and/or COPD is challenging due to overlapping clinical and physiological characteristics; however, due to varying treatment recommendations, determining the correct diagnosis is vital to clinical care. Hyperpolarised xenon-129 ventilation (129Xe)-magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides high spatial resolution three-dimensional images of gas distribution within the lungs. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have successfully classified pulmonary pathologies via medical images, but due to their black-box nature, clinical application is challenging. Here, we aim to develop an explainable AI framework to classify patients with asthma and/or COPD using 129Xe-MRI alone. METHODS: 129Xe-MRI from 207 patients with asthma and/or COPD were classified using a vision transformer (ViT) and a convolutional neural network (CNN). Regional visualisations of areas of importance (AOIs) associated with each diagnosis were generated. Regional patterns were investigated to develop a shape-based metric which quantified asthma-like and COPD-like features. RESULTS: The ViT accurately classified asthma and/or COPD patients in 83% (n=25/30) of cases (area under the curve (AUC) 0.86, F1 score 0.82), outperforming the CNN (AUC 0.71, F1 score 0.62). Patients with asthma had more diffuse, elongated AOIs associated with disease grouping while patients with COPD had more focal, spherical AOIs. The proposed sphericity score weakly correlated with conventional lung function metrics in clinically understandable ways. When applied to patients with overlapping features of asthma and COPD (asthma+COPD), the classification framework informed the prevalence and regional distribution of asthma-like and COPD-like features. CONCLUSION: Explainable AI classification of 129Xe-MRI could facilitate diagnosis of patients with asthma and/or COPD, including determining the prevalence of asthma-like or COPD-like features in patients with asthma+COPD, potentially informing management and treatment.

papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT: PURPOSE: Nasogastric tube (NGT) usage is common among inpatients. However, there is a lack of a convenient and objective tool for assessing a patient's swallowing function for NGT removal. The feasibility of using submental ultrasound for making decisions regarding NGT removal remains unclear. ABSTRACT: MATERIALS AND METHODS: This pilot study included patients with NGTs who underwent submental ultrasound examination for NGT removal from March 2023 to December 2025. Patients were divided into derivation and validation cohorts by different examiners. We first measured the resting mandible-hyoid distance and shortest distance when swallowing and then calculated the maximum hyoid bone displacement. ABSTRACT: RESULTS: In the derivation cohort, the maximum displacement was shorter in the NGT group (n = 31) than in the control group (n = 27) (1.26 vs. 1.83 cm, p ≤ 0.001), and the displacement was shorter in the "NGT not removed" subgroup (NG-NR, n = 21) than in the "NGT removed" subgroup (NG-R, n = 10) (1.09 vs. 1.63 cm, p = 0.006). In the validation cohort, the displacement was shorter in the NG-NR subgroup (n = 18) than in the NG-R subgroup (n = 6) (1.36 vs. 1.89 cm, p ≤ 0.001). In the derivation cohort, the displacement showed an AUROC of 0.805 for distinguishing between the NG-NR and NG-R subgroups. A cut-off value of 1.32 cm yielded a sensitivity of 80.0% and a specificity of 81.0%. In the validation cohort, the AUROC was 0.836. In the age- and sex-matched validation cohort, the AUROC was 0.831. The interrater consistency was good. ABSTRACT: CONCLUSION: Given its good discriminatory performance with regard to NG-R patient identification, interrater consistency, and convenience, submental ultrasound might be an effective screening tool for identifying suitable postacute NGT patients to start swallowing training before NGT removal.

papers.abstract_en: Digital cytology, telecytology, and artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping cytopathology by expanding access to primary diagnosis, remote rapid on-site evaluation, consultation, quality assurance, education, archiving, and research. This review summarizes the technological basis of digital cytology, its current clinical and educational applications, implementation strategies, telecytology platforms, and emerging AI tools in gynecologic and non-gynecologic cytology. Compared with surgical pathology, digital cytology faces greater technical challenges because cytologic specimens often contain three-dimensional cell clusters, variable thickness, and overlapping cells, which increase demands on focusing, scanning time, image storage, and infrastructure. Recent advances in z-stacking, extended depth of focus, and whole-slide imaging have improved digital visualization, while updated professional guidance has supported broader validation of digital cytology for primary diagnosis and rapid on-site evaluation. Telecytology has shown high diagnostic concordance and has improved access to expert assessment, particularly for rapid on-site evaluation in resource-limited or remote settings. AI applications have shown promising performance in screening, classification, and quality control, especially in cervical cytology, with expanding use in non-gynecologic specimens. However, implementation remains constrained by technical complexity, variable image quality, regulatory and medicolegal concerns, infrastructure requirements, cost, and the need for robust validation and training. Overall, digital cytology and AI are guiding the transition into a Cytopathology 2.0 era characterized by greater connectivity, scalability, and data‑driven practice, although widespread adoption will depend on further standardization, robust validation, and smooth integration into everyday workflows.

papers.abstract_en: Bacterial invasion and genotoxicity are key contributors to infectious disease progression and carcinogenesis. Yet current methods do not quantify these processes systematically and at single-cell resolution, limiting our ability to explore how interplay of virulence factors and drug effects shape pathogenicity. Here, we present MALVINA, a high-throughput deep-learning workflow integrating host-pathogen co-culture and high-content imaging to jointly measure bacterial invasion and host DNA damage. Applied to Escherichia coli isolates and human colorectal epithelial cells, we demonstrate MALVINA's versatility by deciphering (1) strains with elevated invasive or genotoxic potential, (2) interbacterial modulation of virulence, (3) pro-virulent drug effects, (4) virulence-targeting drugs, and (5) bacterial potentiation of drug toxicity. MALVINA revealed strain-specific virulence profiles and colibactin-dependent suppression of competitors' invasion coupled with enhanced genotoxicity. It also enabled identification of drug-induced modulation of bacterial invasion and genotoxicity, offering a new perspective for virulence-aware drug profiling. Overall, MALVINA offers an adaptable framework for dissecting pathogen-host-drug interactions.

papers.abstract_en: Gastrointestinal fistulas (GFs) represent one of the main causes of morbidity and mortality. While endoscopic techniques provide a minimally invasive approach to GF repair, offering advantages over conventional surgical approaches, the integration of endoscopic delivery with hydrogel sealants in user-friendly and easy processes approaches remains a great challenge. Here we develop a thermoresponsive positively charged poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM)/Ga3+ (PGaIII) hydrogel sealant, formed by slug-inspired biomimetic self-assembly. The PGaIII integrated injectability and single-step-formed Janus-type adhesion to tissues, simultaneously featuring excellent biocompatibility, water/acid resistance, active shrinkage and antibacterial properties, enabling its effective ready-to-use biological sealant for endoscopic repair of GFs and prevention of postoperative adhesions. To validate the efficacy of PGaIII in treating GFs, we demonstrate its effectiveness in repairing GFs and its convenience in non-invasive endoscopic surgery in living Sprague-Dawley rat and Bama miniature pig models. The proposed PGaIII holds potential for the repair of fistulas in other organs in vivo, thereby promoting the establishment of safer and more effective clinical treatment options for related diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA) is a developmental disorder associated with chromosome segregation defects. Mutations in the centrosomal protein Cep57 cause MVA2 syndrome, yet the molecular basis of Cep57 function has remained unclear. Here, using MINFLUX nanoscopy, structural biology, biochemical approaches, and analyses of patient-derived cells, we show how Cep57 organizes the inner pericentriolar material (PCM) to support centriole biogenesis. We show that Cep57 acts as a molecular bridge between centriolar microtubules and the PCM through two architecturally distinct interactions. Its oligomeric C-terminus anchors to centriolar microtubules, whereas its dimeric N-terminus engages Cep63 through a conserved bundle-like interaction, thereby linking the Cep63-Cep152 platform to the centriole and recruiting Plk4 and other components required for procentriole formation. Analysis of primary T lymphocytes from MVA2 patients carrying the Cep63-binding-defective CEP57∆exon 3 mutation reveals a predominant centriole-duplication defect accompanied by minor centriole amplification, likely resulting from disorganized PCM-induced premature centriole disengagement. Our findings show Cep57 as a central architectural organizer that couples centriolar microtubules to the molecular machinery driving centriole biogenesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding centrosome dysfunction and aneuploidy-associated diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Conventional ex vivo chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy is limited by cumbersome manufacturing workflows, prohibitive costs and various treatment-related risks. In vivo CAR-T technology directly generates engineered cells within patients, conferring distinct advantages in operational simplicity, biosafety and clinical accessibility. This review systematically evaluates existing delivery platforms and classifies in vivo CAR-T into two core paradigms: persistent engineering and transient reprogramming, each featuring distinct properties tailored to different clinical indications. It further summarizes preclinical advances and clinical data covering hematological malignancies, solid tumors, autoimmune disorders and organ fibrosis, in which numerous investigational candidates have exhibited encouraging efficacy. Ultimately, five translational barriers summarized as the 5S challenges (specificity, stability, safety, suppression and scalability) and their matched optimization tactics are comprehensively discussed. This review provides a clinician-oriented decision matrix that links carriers selection to disease biology, and a 5S optimization framework to guide next-generation vector design. Collectively, these insights establish a translational roadmap for customizing in vivo CAR-T design to specific clinical indications and take a critical step toward realizing the full therapeutic potential of this disruptive modality.

papers.abstract_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe respiratory illness across the lifespan, particularly in infants and older adults. Nonetheless, effective antiviral therapies remain limited. Here, we performed a clinically guided, medium-throughput screening of approved drugs used in pediatric populations and identified sparfloxacin (SPFX), a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, as a mechanistically informative antiviral scaffold. SPFX showed antiviral activity against genetically distinct RSV clinical isolates in vitro, and suppressed RSV infection in a mechanistic mouse model in vivo. Mechanistically, our findings support a host-virus dual-target framework in which SPFX suppresses RSV replication through activity consistent with modulation of viral RNA polymerase function together with a pro-viral HSP70-associated host pathway. Using primary human pediatric airway epithelial cells, we identified SPFX-responsive host factors and observed suppression of HSP70 expression independent of infection. Together, these findings establish SPFX as a mechanistically informative antiviral scaffold and support a host-virus dual-target framework for future RSV therapeutic development.

papers.abstract_en: Metabolomics has demonstrated immense potential in elucidating mechanisms of action and off-target effects of known drugs. Here, we propose that metabolomic screening of cellular response to treatment with drug-like compounds can uncover clinically relevant inhibitors - driven by the extensive catalog of metabolic pathways implicated in human diseases. We developed a high-throughput LC-MS metabolomics pipeline paired with a computational Graph Neural Network for target deconvolution, and applied it to screen a library of 1,020 drug-like compounds in cultured cells in vitro. The screen revealed four drug-like compounds targeting key disease pathways, including inhibitors of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and an inducer of glutathione metabolism; validated via comprehensive metabolic assessments and growth rescue experiments. In a muscle atrophy model, driven by redox imbalance, the glutathione metabolism inducer reversed atrophy markers and restored protein content. Our scalable pipeline can be readily expanded to screen thousands of compounds, paving the way for the discovery of clinically relevant metabolic inhibitors.

papers.abstract_en: Repeated cocaine exposure during adolescence disrupts physiological brain maturation, inducing persistent neuroplastic adaptations that evolve throughout withdrawal. Because stressful experiences are among the most powerful triggers of relapse during abstinence, uncovering how cocaine withdrawal affects the neurobiological mechanisms of stress adaptation and emotional responses remains a critical challenge in addiction research. Here, we investigated whether prolonged withdrawal from adolescent cocaine exposure alters hippocampal neuroimmune responses to a subsequent stressful challenge. Male adolescent rats received cocaine (5mg/kg, s.c.) for 15 consecutive days followed by a 14-day withdrawal period. At the end of withdrawal, animals were exposed to acute restraint stress (ARS) and assessed for anxiety-like behavior. Our findings demonstrate that prolonged withdrawal from adolescent cocaine exposure impairs emotional adaptation to acute stress, accompanied by persistent neuroimmune dysregulation across both central and peripheral compartments. Within the hippocampus, a key limbic hub integrating contextual drug-associated memories, emotional processes and stress adaptation, cocaine withdrawal altered microglial homeostasis while reshaping stress-responsive neuro-glial communication pathways in a region-specific manner, particularly the CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis within the ventral subregion. Stress exposure revealed distinct microglial and synaptic, structural and molecular, adaptations in cocaine-withdrawn rats, characterized by the recruitment of a surveillance-like microglial phenotype and an altered pattern of neuron-microglia communication. These central alterations were accompanied by peripheral lymphopenia and a blunted lymphocyte response to the challenge. Together, these findings support the existence of a latent neuroimmune vulnerability induced by cocaine withdrawal that becomes apparent under challenging conditions potentially driving maladaptive stress processing.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Traditional influenza surveillance systems rely on sentinel hospitals and often experience a 1- to 2-week reporting lag, limiting timely public health response. Social media platforms provide real-time data streams, but extracting reliable epidemiological signals remains challenging due to substantial linguistic noise. Although large language models (LLMs) improve semantic extraction, their computational cost limits routine deployment in resource-constrained public health settings. OBJECTIVE: This study proposes and evaluates a hybrid framework that distills knowledge from an LLM (DeepSeek) into a lightweight bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT)-based classifier for real-time influenza surveillance using Weibo data from Guangdong Province, China, during the 2025 influenza season. The study further assesses the temporal alignment between the derived signal and official influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data. METHODS: A total of 389,959 Weibo posts from epidemiological weeks 7 to 50 (February 10 to December 14, 2025) were collected using a domain-specific keyword strategy. After multistage filtering, 99,158 posts were retained for analysis. A DeepSeek-Chat model was used to generate pseudo-labels for 2500 posts via zero-shot prompting, which were evaluated against expert annotations (Cohen κ=0.846) and used to fine-tune a Chinese-RoBERTa-WWM-ext classifier (a robustly optimized BERT pretraining approach). A chronological train-validation-test split was applied to reduce temporal leakage. The trained model was used to construct a weekly Weibo Flu Index. This index was compared with keyword-based and Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) + logistic regression baselines using time-lag Pearson correlation (0-5 wk) against official ILI% data. Savitzky-Golay smoothing and second-derivative analysis were applied to identify epidemic inflection points and peak timing. RESULTS: The classifier achieved an accuracy of 85.1% and an F1-score of 0.800 on a chronologically held-out test set, identifying 29,779 posts (30.0%) as ILI self-reports among 99,158 posts. The BERT-derived index showed the strongest correlation with official ILI% at lag 0 (r=0.523, 95% CI 0.268-0.710; R²=0.274) and lag 1 (r=0.446, 95% CI 0.169-0.658), compared with the keyword baseline (lag 0: r=0.481, R²=0.231) and TF-IDF baseline (lag 0: r=0.185, R²=0.034). Inflection analysis indicated that the Weibo-derived signal preceded both the epidemic rise (week 44 vs week 45) and peak (week 48 vs week 49) in official ILI data, corresponding to an approximate 1-week lead at both transition points. CONCLUSIONS: The results suggest that a DeepSeek-augmented lightweight BERT classifier can extract meaningful influenza-related signals from noisy Chinese social media data and produce a surveillance index that shows an approximate 1-week lead relative to official ILI reporting, with improved performance over keyword-based and TF-IDF approaches. This framework provides a proof-of-concept for cost-effective real-time influenza nowcasting using social media data.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Falls are an important public health problem among community-dwelling older adults. Patient-reported fall experiences are important for community fall-risk screening, but how these experiences become screening data remains poorly understood. METHODS: We conducted a multiperspective qualitative study in community health centres and surrounding communities in Xi'an, China. Community-dwelling older adults, family caregivers and primary healthcare workers were recruited using purposive and maximum-variation sampling. Semi-structured interviews were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis and cross-group comparison. RESULTS: A total of 47 participants were interviewed, including 23 community-dwelling older adults, 11 family caregivers and 13 primary healthcare workers. We identified a 6-link process through which fall experiences became patient-reported data: renaming, recalling, weighing before expression, reprocessing within the family, community inquiry and data completion and reshaping through feedback. These links were explained by three themes and nine subthemes. Fall experiences were filtered through everyday definitions, normalisation of near-falls and ageing and memory reconstruction based on life anchors and consequences. Reporting willingness was negotiated through autonomy, identity, family relationships, fear of troubling others and service expectations. Once information entered community screening, oral accounts were summarised in structured records, interpreted through professional judgement and further reshaped by feedback from services. CONCLUSION: Patient-reported fall data are shaped by more than recall alone. They are also influenced by interpretation, family interaction, screening practices, documentation and feedback. Screening may be improved through understandable questions, documentation of near-falls and uncertainty and clearer links between reported information and follow-up services.

papers.abstract_en: Rare earth elements (REEs) are emerging contaminants, yet their organ-specific accumulation and short-term redistribution in marine bivalves remain poorly understood. We quantified Sc, Y, and 14 lanthanides by ICP-MS in six soft tissues, shell, and crystalline style of the Black Sea scallop Flexopecten glaber ponticus collected from a Crimean shellfish farm in May and June 2023. REE accumulation was strongly tissue-specific. In June, the crystalline style had the highest ΣREE concentration (including Sc; median 7.81 mg kg-1 dw), whereas adductor muscle and shell had the lowest values (1.02 and 1.07 mg kg-1 dw, respectively). Mixed-effects models detected tissue effects for 15 of 16 elements and significant Month × Tissue interactions for Sc, Y, Nd, Gd and Yb. Sc increased 3.28-fold in visceral mass and 4.33-fold in foot, whereas Y decreased by 55-88% across visceral mass, digestive gland, gonads, and adductor muscle. Most local-sediment-normalized REE/Yb ratios were below unity, indicating relative HREE enrichment. Positive Eu anomalies were widespread, while recurrent odd-numbered peaks in many May profiles were more consistent with biological attenuation of the natural Oddo-Harkins pattern than with discrete environmental anomalies. Y-Ho mixture regression resolved three origin-constrained slopes (11.856, 36.672, and 60.614), with 30 of 32 June tissue observations assigned to the intermediate component. A two-endpoint burden-based kinetic model provided exploratory, model-conditional coefficients for REE input, outflow, and redistribution. The dissolved-and-dietary formulation was the most parsimonious, whereas carrier-proxy models improved descriptive fit (best R2 = 0.957). For this Crimean population, tissue choice, feeding/depuration status and reproductive stage should be standardized for REE biomonitoring. Digestive tissues and the crystalline style provide responsive but potentially particle-influenced signals, adductor muscle a comparatively conservative soft-tissue matrix, and shell a longer-term biomineralized record.
