papers.abstract_en: Groundwater pollution control commonly prioritizes contaminants and locations according to observed concentrations or associated risks, implicitly assuming that high risk corresponds to high mitigation potential. However, this assumption may not hold where groundwater quality is jointly controlled by anthropogenic inputs and natural geochemical backgrounds. This study developed a natural-background-constrained framework to distinguish current groundwater risk from achievable risk reduction and applied it to 121 monitoring wells in a 1.54 km2 chemical industrial park in eastern China. Individual and mixture ecological risks were integrated with deterministic and probabilistic human health risks across multiple receptor groups into an environmental health risk index (EHRI). Idealized contaminant-removal scenarios were first used to identify dominant risk contributors, followed by natural background levels (NBLs)-constrained scenarios to quantify potential risk reduction. The two scenarios revealed a marked decoupling between risk contribution and achievable risk reduction. As was the dominant contributor to baseline EHRI, but reducing it to its NBL produced almost no EHRI decrease because its natural background level approached or exceeded the health-risk-based concentration threshold. In contrast, Cl-, NH4+, and Na+ yielded substantially greater reductions, resulting in a control priority of Cl->NH4+>Na+>As. Spatial EHRI reduction further identified zones with the greatest risk-reduction potential, while residual risk was used to prioritize post-control monitoring. The proposed monitoring scheme would reduce annual sampling events by 14.7% while maintaining more frequent sampling at high-priority locations. These findings provide insights into groundwater pollution prioritization by distinguishing controllable from persistent background risk.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults aged ≥18 years living with HIV and to provide evidence supporting influenza vaccination in this population in China. METHODS: This single-center, open-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three-arm clinical study. For the present comparative analysis, 472 vaccinated participants were planned, including 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2). Participants in both groups received one dose of IIV3 (0.5 mL) on Day 0. Blood samples were collected before and 28 days after vaccination for hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody testing against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains. Immunogenicity endpoints included seroconversion rate, seroprotection rate, geometric mean titer (GMT), and geometric mean increase (GMI). Safety was assessed by monitoring solicited and unsolicited adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during 6 months of follow-up. An unvaccinated cohort of adults living with HIV from the original trial was included only for an exploratory, descriptive analysis of influenza-like illness (ILI), without assessment of vaccine efficacy. RESULTS: A total of 489 participants were enrolled, including 237 in Group 1 and 252 in Group 2. At 28 days post-vaccination, seroconversion rates did not differ significantly between Group 1 and Group 2 for A(H1N1) (91.00% vs. 86.69%, P > 0.05), but significantly lower for A(H3N2) (49.50% vs. 89.52%) and B/Victoria (40.00% vs. 64.52%) (both P < 0.001). Seroprotection rates were also lower in Group 1 than in Group 2 for A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria (94.00% vs. 97.98%, 63.50% vs. 97.18%, and 40.50% vs. 68.55%, respectively). Post-vaccination GMTs were significantly lower in Group 1 for all three strains (all P < 0.001). GMI was higher for A(H1N1) but lower for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in Group 1 than in Group 2 (all P < 0.001). Multivariable analyses showed that HIV infection remained independently associated with several measures of vaccine-induced immune responses after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, particularly for A(H3N2). IIV3 was generally safe and well tolerated. Most AEs were mild in severity, and no Grade 4 adverse reactions or vaccine-related SAEs were reported. During the period from 29 days to 6 months after vaccination, few influenza-like illness events were reported among vaccinated and unvaccinated participants living with HIV; these findings were descriptive and were not used to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza. CONCLUSION: Adults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses following IIV3 vaccination, although the magnitude of response varied across influenza strains. A(H1N1) seroconversion was high in adults living with HIV, whereas responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria were generally lower than those in HIV-uninfected adults. HIV infection remained associated with reduced vaccine-induced immune responses for several strain-specific outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with associations particularly evident for A(H3N2). IIV3 was safe and well tolerated, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in adults living with HIV. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dry eye disease (DED) is a common multifactorial ocular surface disorder characterized by tear film instability, inflammation, and visual impairment, with rising global prevalence affecting quality of life. While inflammation is central to DED pathophysiology, the role of systemic metabolic dysregulation in modulating local ocular surface inflammation remains unclear. This study investigates the correlation between systemic branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) metabolism and tear inflammatory markers as well as visual-related quality of life (VR-QOL) in DED patients. METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 111 DED patients and 64 healthy controls from a single center (2022-2024). In the pilot phase, tear samples from 26 DED and 22 controls underwent untargeted metabolomics using UPLC-MS to identify differential metabolites and pathways. In the serum-based sequential exploratory phase, serum BCAA levels (leucine, valine, ILE) were measured in 85 DED patients (stratified by severity) and 42 controls. Tear inflammatory factors (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, hs-CRP, TNF-α) were quantified by ELISA/immunofluorescence. Pearson correlation analyzed associations between serum BCAAs and ocular surface sign parameters (Schirmer's test, corneal staining), and inflammatory markers. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the apparent discriminative ability of serum BCAAs for suboptimal visual quality of life in patients with dry eye disease (DED). RESULTS: Untargeted metabolomics revealed 15 significantly altered tear metabolites in DED (8 upregulated, 7 downregulated). Enrichment analysis revealed a suggestive trend toward enrichment of the BCAA biosynthesis pathway (Raw P = 0.016; after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, FDR Q = 0.058, which did not meet the significance threshold of Q < 0.05.). In this study, pathways with raw P < 0.05 but corrected Q ≥ 0.05 were defined as exhibiting a "suggestive enrichment trend" and were not considered as definitive conclusions, warranting further targeted validation. Serum levels of leucine, valine, and ILE were significantly elevated in both mild-to-moderate and severe DED groups versus controls (all P<0.05), but did not differ by severity. Positive correlations were found between each BCAA and specific tear inflammatory factors (IL-1β, hs-CRP, TNF-α; r=0.35-0.66, all P<0.05), while no significant associations emerged with IL-6, IL-8, or clinical signs. ROC analysis revealed notable associations between serum BCAAs and poor VR-QOL, with AUCs of 0.916 (leucine), 0.837 (valine), and 0.886 (ILE). These exploratory findings suggest a potential link between BCAA levels and vision-related quality of life, but do not establish clinical utility as biomarkers. CONCLUSIONS: Untargeted tear metabolomics in a small cohort revealed BCAA-related metabolic alterations in DED. Sequential exploratory analysis of an independent large-sample serum cohort further demonstrated that elevated serum Leu, Val, and ILE, which correlated positively with tear IL-1β, hs-CRP, and TNF-α at the population level. These findings provide exploratory evidence linking serum BCAAs to DED. However, given the use of two distinct matrices without paired sampling and the control group sample size n = 42 during the serum association exploratory phase being modestly lower than the predetermined goal-potentially compromising the statistical power of some tests-the results only support population-level cross-biofluid associations and do not confirm individual-level coupling.

papers.abstract_en: The success of germline-targeting vaccines and rational antibody design depends on quantifying the population-level frequencies of specific antibody features, such as CDR lengths, sequence motifs, germline usage or preferred chain pairings, across the natural human repertoire. The maturation of high-throughput sequencing has generated large database repertoires containing billions of sequences, allowing researchers to assess naïve B-cell precursor frequencies and evaluate biologically plausible chain combinations. However, leveraging this scale of data remains a significant bottleneck, as current databases trap scientists between computationally demanding bulk downloads, restrictive, single-purpose web interfaces or outdated datasets. To address this gap, we introduce ABHunter, an automatically updated, open-access framework designed to explore and filter the healthy-human subset of the Observed Antibody Space (OAS) database, which currently stands at ~1.86-billion-sequence as of January 2026. Accessible via any web browser, the platform executes searches with median times ranging from 3.7 seconds for simple gene usage profiles to 20.8 seconds for complex paratope motifs, with full sequence retrieval completed in 118 seconds for 1 million hits. The interface allows users to quantify antibody feature frequencies to assess the natural abundance of targeted B-cells across various isotypes (e.g., utilizing IgM for precursor B-cell analysis), as well as map native repertoire contexts to scaffold isolated features. Additionally, it predicts biologically plausible inter-chain pairings for therapeutic design by using a statistical co-occurrence model that extrapolates pairing probabilities from the limited natively paired subset comprising 0.03% of the data across six donors. Furthermore, every search generates a comprehensive statistical landscape, detailing underlying complementarity-determining regions length distributions, amino acid compositions, and gene coupling patterns. For custom analysis and integration into bioinformatic pipelines, the optimized data structure reduces the storage footprint to 106 GB, allowing the entire tool to run locally on a standard laptop. ABHunter eliminates the compromise between accessibility and flexibility, transforming large-scale sequencing data into a universally accessible resource for next-generation therapeutic discovery. The platform is freely available at abhunter.org.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tezepelumab is a monoclonal antibody that targets thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP). It reduces airway hyperresponsiveness, eosinophilia, mucus plugging, and asthma exacerbations, which are commonly caused by viral infections. Although clinical TSLP blockade attenuates virus-induced IL-33 and T2 cytokines in human bronchial epithelial cells (HBECs), the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. AIM: The aim of this study was to identify transcriptomic changes modulated by tezepelumab in HBECs and determine their downstream remodelling-related effects on bronchial smooth muscle cells (BSMCs). METHODS: HBECs from patients with uncontrolled asthma before and after 12 weeks of tezepelumab (n = 13) or placebo (n = 13) were expanded in vitro as submerged monocultures and subsequently exposed to poly(I:C). Validation analyses showed variable responses across the cohort, with attenuation observed primarily in patients with higher baseline inflammatory responses. CONCLUSION: Clinical TSLP blockade by tezepelumab was associated with altered epithelial transcriptional responses and reduced TGF-β2 gene expression in BSMCs exposed to epithelial conditioned media. papers.abstract_en: Tuberculosis, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a leading cause of infectious mortality worldwide, a burden compounded by rising drug resistance. While mitochondria were long dismissed as mere powerhouses, they now function as hubs that integrate immune metabolism, innate immune signaling, and cell-death decisions. During infection, M.tb severely disrupts these hubs through organelle swelling, cristae remodeling, mitochondrial DNA release, and rewired oxidative phosphorylation. Despite this disruption, the field remains divided over whether mitophagy, the terminal tier of quality control, protects the host or serves the pathogen. The answer depends on the pathway engaged. Here, we synthesize evidence that M.tb engages a multilevel mitochondrial quality control network spanning chaperones and proteases, the integrated stress response, fusion and fission dynamics, and mitophagy. We propose that distinct mitophagy pathways yield mechanistically distinct, context-dependent outcomes during mycobacterial infection. Notably, the PINK1 and Parkin axis mediates both protective antibacterial xenophagy and pathogen-exploited mitophagy. Beyond this axis, BNIP3, NIX, and FUNDC1 can limit or promote bacterial survival, depending on pathway identity, infection stage, and host-cell metabolic state. This framework offers a way to interpret effects that appear to conflict, whether they protect the host or favor the pathogen, traces the outcome to which pathway is engaged, the context of infection, and the state of the host cell, and identifies specific MQC nodes, including mitochondrial reactive oxygen species thresholds and the PINK1-Parkin axis, as candidate targets for host-directed therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Allergic asthma is a heterogeneous inflammatory airway disorder driven by dysregulated immune responses and epithelial-immune crosstalk. Dihydroartemisinin (DHA), an active derivative of artemisinin, exhibits broad anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties; however, its mechanistic role in allergic asthma remains incompletely defined. METHODS: Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways of DHA in asthma. These predictions were validated in a house dust mite (HDM) induced murine asthma model and HDM stimulated human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cells using histopathology, flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, ELISA, and molecular docking. RESULTS: Network analysis identified nine hub targets and highlighted the PI3K-AKT pathway as a central regulatory axis. In vivo, DHA markedly attenuated airway inflammation, reduced eosinophil and neutrophil infiltration, and decreased Th2 cytokine production. In HDM-stimulated HBE cells, DHA suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and downregulated EGFR, MMP9, and PTGS2. Mechanistically, DHA inhibited activation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling cascade both in vitro and in vivo, consistent with molecular docking predictions demonstrating stable binding of DHA to PI3K related targets. CONCLUSIONS: DHA alleviates allergic airway inflammation predominantly through suppression of the PI3K-AKT signaling axis, thereby modulating epithelial inflammatory responses and type 2 immunity. These findings provide mechanistic insight into DHA-mediated immunoregulation and support its potential repositioning as a therapeutic candidate for allergic asthma.

papers.abstract_en: House dust mites (HDM) produce an unparalleled diversity of indoor allergens, yet their allergen composition has been inferred mostly from transcriptomes rather than proteins. METHODS: The homologous allergen proteins were identified and phylogenetically analyzed in HDM, stored-product, parasitic, herbivorous, and soil-living mites. Using high-sensitivity mass spectrometry, we generated a comprehensive protein-level allergome for Dermatophagoides farinae and Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus, identifying ~191 putative homologous allergens, including variants and proteome sequences of undetermined genomic origin, assigned to 40 of the 44 currently recognized HDM allergen groups and 2 groups of Tyrophagus putrescentiae allergens (Tyr p 35 and Tyr p 36). Blo t 12 was not detected, and Blo t 19 and Der f 17 were excluded from analyses; Blo t 41 was suggested as Gr_23. The set of allergen groups is conserved between HDM species, but the number of variants and abundance differ markedly between species, as well as protein fractions from mite bodies and feces. In the feces proteome, the most abundant allergen groups in D. farinae were cysteine protease (Gr_1), NPC2 family proteins (Gr_2), and C2 domain-containing protein (Gr_36), which were less abundant in D. pteronyssinus. Although trypsins (Gr_3/6/9) had the same intensity as in D. farinae, they formed the allergen spectrum of D. pteronyssinus feces. Body and fecal proteome profiles were not significantly correlated (Spearman correlation), suggesting that mite bodies and feces are not interchangeable allergen sources. This may be relevant for commercial vaccines and diagnostic sets, which are based on mixtures of feces and bodies, so that their allergen profile depends on the proportion of these components.

papers.abstract_en: Astragali Radix (AR) and Curcumae Rhizoma (CR) herb pair (AC) is a traditional anti-psoriatic formula, but its active constituents and mechanisms remain poorly defined. In imiquimod-induced psoriatic mice, the 3:1 AC ratio optimally alleviated skin lesions and downregulated TNF-α and IL-17 A. Using a fraction-knockout approach combined with chemical profiling, we identified AR-III and CR-II as core bioactive fractions and characterized calycosin (Cal), astragaloside IV (Ast IV), and zederone (Zed) as principal active compounds. Network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted their high affinity for the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α axis. In vivo, the three monomers ameliorated psoriasis-like manifestations in a dose-dependent manner, and Zed + Cal outperformed Zed + Ast IV. In IL-17 A-stimulated HaCaT cells, Zed + Cal synergistically suppressed hyperproliferation (CI < 1), reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, and restored intracellular ATP content. Pharmacological inhibition and siRNA-mediated knockdown abolished these effects in vitro; a cellular thermal shift assay confirmed direct binding of both monomers to AMPK; and in vivo co-administration of the AMPK inhibitor dorsomorphin largely reversed the anti-psoriatic efficacy of Zed + Cal. Together, these findings indicate that AMPK is a key mediator of the protective effects of Zed + Cal in vitro and of its anti-psoriatic efficacy in vivo. Zed + Cal achieved efficacy comparable to methotrexate in the IMQ model while restoring cellular ATP levels. This work identifies the core bioactive constituents of the AC herb pair. It characterizes an AMPK-associated anti-inflammatory pathway in keratinocyte models, providing a novel multi-component candidate for psoriasis research.

papers.abstract_en: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by microbial infection that can lead to periodontal tissue damage and alveolar bone resorption. Macrophages contribute to the regulation of periodontal inflammation and local tissue homeostasis, but the role of integrin α9β1 in these processes remains unclear. Here, we combined analysis of human gingival single-cell transcriptomic data, a mouse model of myeloid cell-specific conditional Itga9 deletion, in vitro experiments with bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs), and conditioned-medium experiments in gingival fibroblasts to investigate how α9β1 affects the immune microenvironment and bone destruction in periodontitis. ITGA9 was highly expressed in human gingival macrophages and was further upregulated in periodontitis. Itga9 deletion altered the basal transcriptional state of BMMs and their response to Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg), with reduced TNF production, downregulation of inflammation-related gene sets, and lower AKT and S6 phosphorylation following Pg stimulation. In vivo, myeloid Itga9 deletion reduced periodontal tissue damage and alveolar bone loss and was accompanied by changes in local immune cell composition and fibroblast-associated communication networks. Gene sets related to skeletal development, ossification, and extracellular matrix (ECM)-receptor interactions were positively enriched in fibroblasts. Further in vitro experiments showed that conditioned medium from Pg-stimulated KO BMMs was less inhibitory to gingival fibroblast mineralization than that from Pg-stimulated Het BMMs, as reflected by higher expression of mineralization-related genes, greater alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, and increased mineralized nodule formation. These findings suggest that myeloid integrin α9β1 contributes to the regulation of immune and stromal cell functions in periodontitis and that targeting this receptor may help reduce inflammation-associated bone destruction and support the mineralization potential of gingival fibroblasts.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Given the shared modes of transmission, HIV, HBV, and HCV confer a high risk of co-infection, particularly among key populations. Currently, clinical screening for these viruses still relies predominantly on serological assays, which fail to detect a substantial proportion of infections, including occult HBV infection (OBI, defined as HBsAg-negative but HBV DNA-positive) and current HCV infection. HIV/HBV/HCV multiplex nucleic acid testing (NAT) has been widely adopted in blood screening due to its superior sensitivity, specificity, and shorter window period. However, this highly effective screening assay has not yet been translated into routine clinical screening for high-risk populations. METHODS: To evaluate its clinical performance and feasibility, we conducted a cross-sectional study enrolling 802 people who use drugs (PWUD) and 400 men who have sex with men (MSM) in China. All participants underwent parallel serological screening and HIV/HBV/HCV multiplex NAT, with final infection status confirmed by supplementary testing, epidemiological history, and clinical symptoms. RESULTS: Upfront HIV/HBV/HCV multiplex NAT identified 12 additional OBI cases (incremental yield 12/1,202) that were missed by HBsAg-only screening and HBsAg-triggered reflex testing. HCV RNA testing distinguished current from non-current HCV infection, but this benefit was not specific to the multiplex strategy. Acceptance of multiplex NAT and post-diagnosis treatment was high among participants. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that HIV/HBV/HCV multiplex NAT could detect clinically relevant infections undetectable by serology in key populations, suggesting potential clinical benefits. However, further prospective implementation studies and cost-effectiveness analyses are warranted before routine integration into clinical practice.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Fusobacterium nucleatum, an oral-associated bacterium implicated in several extraoral diseases, has recently been proposed as a potential contributor to endometriosis through microbial translocation, inflammation, and fibrosis. However, the consistency and clinical significance of this association remain uncertain. This systematic review evaluated the human and experimental evidence linking F. nucleatum with endometriosis and assessed the plausibility of a proposed oral microbe-host axis. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through August 31, 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Human and animal studies reporting F. nucleatum or historically related F. nucleatum-complex taxa in relation to endometriosis were included. Risk of bias was assessed using a prespecified adapted ROBINS-I framework for human observational studies and SYRCLE for animal studies. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in anatomical compartments, detection methods, and outcomes, meta-analysis was not appropriate and findings were synthesized qualitatively. RESULTS: Four human studies encompassing 384 participants at the study level were included, although analysis-specific denominators varied. Direct tissue evidence came from two studies and was conflicting: Muraoka et al. reported Fusobacterium positivity in 64.3% of endometrial samples from women with endometriosis versus 7.1% of controls in a 42-versus-42 tissue subset, whereas Graciano-España et al. found no significant case-control difference in F. nucleatum abundance among 55 cases and 37 controls. Indirect microbiome studies reported oral Fusobacterium enrichment in moderate/severe endometriosis and vaginal F. animalis depletion in chronic pelvic pain with endometriosis. All human studies were judged at serious overall risk of bias, and certainty of evidence was very low. Experimental evidence suggesting TGF-β-mediated lesion growth and fibrosis derived principally from one translational study and lacked independent replication. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports biological plausibility but not a consistent or causal association between F. nucleatum and endometriosis. Direct tissue evidence is limited to two conflicting studies, while non-tissue microbiome findings are indirect. Standardized contamination-controlled sampling, paired anatomical-site sampling, strain-level analyses, and longitudinal studies are required before microbial translocation, temporality, causality, or antimicrobial treatment can be established. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261337885.

papers.abstract_en: Leptospirosis is a neglected global zoonosis caused by pathogenic Leptospira, which rely on a vast repertoire of outer membrane proteins (OMPs) to mediate tissue colonization and immune evasion. Despite being usually associated with regulation of gene expression of iron transport system proteins, FecR domain-containing proteins seem to possess a multifunctional role for Leptospira. This study characterizes two FecR proteins from L. interrogans serovar Copenhageni, LIC_10902 and LIC_20185, previously predicted as hypothetical proteins. Target proteins were analysed in silico for cloning parameters obtention and structural analysis. Target protein genes were amplified from L. interrogans sv. Copenhageni genome, cloned in the pAE vector and recombinant proteins were produced in Escherichia coli BL21 Star (DE3) pLysS. Recombinant protein purification was achieved by metal affinity chromatography and purified recombinant proteins were structurally characterized by circular dichroism (CD), and their immunogenicity and role in host-pathogen interactions were evaluated by ELISA. Analysis shows these proteins are conserved among pathogenic species and suggested that both contain a β-sheet-rich FecR domain. Purified recombinant proteins were produced in Escherichia coli. In vitro, rLIC_20185 bound elastin and E-cadherin, while both proteins interacted with plasminogen (PLG), vitronectin (VT), and complement components C4b, C7, C8, and C9. Experiments with LIC_10902 fragments indicated that the FecR domain mediates C8, C9, and PLG binding. Furthermore, both proteins inhibited in vitro C9 polymerization, and their interaction with PLG enabled its activation into plasmin (PLA). Although production in non-pathogenic L. biflexa serovar Patoc (LbP) did not increase resistance to normal human serum (NHS), our results collectively suggest that both proteins could mediate pathogen-host interactions and potentially contribute to tissue adhesion and immune evasion.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Acinetobacter baumannii is a major cause of healthcare-associated infections owing to its ability to acquire multidrug resistance and express multiple virulence determinants that facilitate persistence in both clinical and hospital environments. However, comparative studies evaluating the phenotypic expression of virulence factors alongside their genomic determinants in paired clinical and patient-environmental isolates remain limited. This study investigated the phenotypic virulence characteristics and corresponding genomic distribution of virulence-associated genes among multidrug-resistant (MDR) A. baumannii isolated from clinical specimens and patient environmental surroundings. METHODS: A total of 110 non-duplicate MDR A. baumannii isolates, comprising 55 clinical and 55 corresponding patient-environmental isolates, were included. Biofilm formation, haemolytic activity, proteolytic activity, and siderophore production were evaluated using standard phenotypic assays. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on all isolates using the Illumina MiSeq platform, followed by genome assembly, annotation, and identification of virulence-associated genes using the Virulence Factor Database (VFDB). Comparative analyses were performed between clinical and environmental isolates. RESULTS: Clinical isolates demonstrated significantly higher frequencies of strong biofilm formation (34/55, 61.8% vs. 6/55, 10.9%), haemolytic activity (29/55, 52.7% vs. 13/55, 23.6%), and siderophore production (31/55, 56.4% vs. 17/55, 30.9%) than environmental isolates (P < 0.05), whereas proteolytic activity was comparable between the two groups (36/55, 65.5% vs. 33/55, 60.0%). Whole-genome sequencing revealed a high prevalence of virulence-associated genes involved in biofilm formation, haemolysis, proteolysis, and iron acquisition among phenotypically positive isolates. Several virulence-associated genes were also detected in a subset of phenotypically negative isolates, indicating a phenotype-genotype discordance and suggesting that gene carriage alone does not necessarily predict phenotypic expression. DISCUSSION: Clinical MDR A. baumannii isolates exhibited greater virulence than corresponding patient-environmental isolates; however, environmental isolates retained multiple virulence-associated genes, highlighting their potential role as reservoirs for persistence and transmission within healthcare settings. Integrating phenotypic virulence assays with whole-genome sequencing provides a comprehensive understanding of the virulence potential of MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of continuous environmental surveillance and infection prevention strategies to limit the dissemination of highly virulent strains.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Persistent isolated elevation of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) often poses a diagnostic challenge. Macro-AST, though underrecognized, is a benign cause that may avoid unnecessary investigations. AIM: To characterize the clinical and laboratory features of macro-AST in Chinese adults and to describe our experience with the PEG precipitation method in identifying this condition. METHODS: Clinical data from patients presenting with persistent isolated AST elevation at Beijing Ditan Hospital, Capital Medical University, between February and August 2025 were analyzed. All patients underwent comprehensive laboratory tests (including routine biochemistry, muscle enzymes and autoantibodies), imaging studies (abdominal ultrasound and transient elastography), and liver biopsy. After excluding other definitive diseases, macro-AST was confirmed using the PEG precipitation method. Sera from one healthy control and one disease control (with chronic active hepatitis B) were also collected. RESULTS: Three patients (2 female, 1 male) were confirmed with macro-AST. Immunological evaluation revealed heterogeneous serological features among the three patients, including positive autoantibodies and variably elevated immunoglobulin levels in a subset of cases. The persistent isolated AST elevation was not adequately explained by any histological finding. Following PEG precipitation, the AST recovery rate was considerably lower in macro-AST patients (mean 9.71% ± 6.29%; individual values: 2.02%, 17.42%, and 9.68%) than in the healthy control (88.10%) and the disease control with chronic active hepatitis B (59.63%), while PPA% was markedly higher in macro-AST patients (mean 90.29% ± 6.28%; individual values: 97.97%, 82.58%, and 90.32%) than in the healthy control (11.90%) and the disease control (40.37%). CONCLUSION: Macro-AST should be considered in cases of persistent isolated AST elevation with unremarkable workup. Testing for macro-AST by PEG precipitation should be considered before proceeding to invasive procedures such as liver biopsy. In this study, the PEG precipitation method proved to be a practical adjunctive tool for identifying macro-AST, although its reliability and diagnostic accuracy in a wider population remain to be confirmed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nontyphoidal Salmonella can cause bloodstream infection in vulnerable hosts, yet the bacterial differences that remain when paired stool and blood isolates are already near-clonal are not well defined. Core-genome SNP analysis is useful for assessing relatedness, but may overlook small circular accessory elements that are difficult to resolve using standard assembly workflows. This study investigated whether a clinically linked same-host stool-blood Salmonella pair contained validated small Col-like accessory elements not apparent from core SNP analysis alone. METHODS: We analyzed a temporally adjacent same-host stool-blood Salmonella index pair, FB1-XY1, together with two short-interval stool-stool comparator pairs. The analysis integrated strict reads-backed core SNP filtering, accessory-element analysis, Illumina and ONT read-level support, PCR/Sanger/qPCR validation and public-genome background screening. RESULTS: Strict reads-backed filtering retained only four core SNPs in the FB1-XY1 pair, whereas both stool-stool comparator pairs had no retained strict core SNPs. Despite this minimal core-genome divergence, the blood isolate XY1 carried two validated small Col-like accessory elements. The first was an assembly-resolved 13.8-kb ColRNAI-like plasmid containing ColRNAI-like replicon hits and duplicated cka/colicin K-like annotations, with a Proteinase K-sensitive inhibitory phenotype. The second was a 5,241-bp Col156-like circular element, contig_40, which was not represented as a near-full-length replicon in the final XY1 closed-assembly output but was supported by full-length XY1 Illumina and ONT read coverage, 116 ONT junction-spanning reads, PCR, Sanger sequencing, multi-colony screening and qPCR. FB1 Illumina reads showed no corresponding support for contig_40. In a screened public Salmonella background of 16,456 genomes, strict full-length hits were rare for both elements: 2 hits for the 13.8-kb plasmid and 15 hits for contig_40. papers.abstract_en: Transmembrane serine protease 4 (TMPRSS4) is associated with poor prognosis in multiple cancers, including non-small cell lung, pancreatic, and colorectal cancers. We previously showed that TMPRSS4 promotes cancer stem-like properties in prostate cancer in a manner dependent on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) transcription factors. Here, we identified a novel TMPRSS4-EMT transcription factor-KRAS axis that drives cancer stem-like features and tumorigenesis in colon and lung cancers. TMPRSS4 knockdown suppressed tumor growth and cancer stem-like properties, accompanied by reduced KRAS expression and decreased phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and AKT, consistent with transcriptomic analysis showing activation of RAS, MAPK, and PI3K-AKT signaling pathways by TMPRSS4. Mechanistically, the EMT-inducing transcription factors SLUG and TWIST1 were required for TMPRSS4-mediated KRAS upregulation. These factors enhanced KRAS transcription through the E-box element within the intron 1 regulatory region of KRAS and increased KRAS expression post-transcriptionally via repression of KRAS-targeting miR-200c. Clinically, TMPRSS4 expression positively correlated with KRAS expression, and co-expression of TMPRSS4 and KRAS was associated with poor survival across multiple cancers. Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized TMPRSS4-SLUG/TWIST1-KRAS pathway that promotes tumor progression, highlighting the TMPRSS4-KRAS axis as a potential therapeutic target for cancers driven by KRAS mutation and/or elevation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Maternal and Perinatal Quality Care Collaboratives (M/PQCs) are voluntary state-based initiatives that leverage shared data systems, evidence-based toolkits, and quality improvement science to reduce preventable maternal and infant harm. METHODS: A scoping review of academic and grey literature was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and registered in Open Science Framework. Seven databases were searched for U.S.-based M/PQC studies published between January 2000 - November 2024, analyzed in 2025. Two independent reviewers screened 456 deduplicated records; 31 met eligibility criteria. Quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by implementation theme and intervention topic. RESULTS: Thirty-one studies spanning 16 states and one national analysis were included. Five themes were identified across two domains. Implementation approaches included: (A) building statewide governance infrastructure; (B) translating evidence into practice through standardized toolkits; and (C) strengthening communication, teamwork, and process outcomes. Impacts included: (D) demonstrated reductions in maternal and birth morbidity, including 45-95% reductions in early elective deliveries, 76-87% improvements in timely hypertension treatment, and national-level reductions in eclampsia and intensive care unit admissions; and (E) expansion of the collaborative mission toward contraceptive access, opioid use disorder care, and racial health equity. DISCUSSION: M/PQCs function as a form of primary and secondary prevention, institutionalizing evidence-based protocols before obstetric emergencies occur. M/PQCs' evolution from clinical safety bundles toward equity, access, and social determinants signals an expanding mandate. Future initiatives should prioritize disaggregated outcome reporting, health equity frameworks, and inclusion of community birth and outpatient settings to ensure M/PQC gains are equitably distributed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Value-based payment (VBP) schemes have emerged as alternatives or complements to traditional payment models, to realign financial incentives toward quality, efficiency, and patient-centered outcomes. Despite their rapid expansion, no recent review synthesizes both design features and reported impacts. OBJECTIVE: To provide an overview of recent VBP schemes, highlighting policy objectives, design parameters, and reported impacts, without focusing on specific countries or care settings. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following JBI methodology. Searches in Medline (via PubMed) and Web of Science identified English-language peer-reviewed articles, systematic or scoping reviews published between January 2015 and July 2024. The review focused on large-scale VBP schemes implemented after 2010 or active between 2010 and 2024. Studies were included if they described a VBP scheme and/or evaluated its impact using quantitative evaluation methods. Gray literature supplemented information on identified models. RESULTS: We identified 61 VBP schemes across 15 countries: 38 pay-for-performance, 18 bundled payment, and 5 shared savings. Common objectives included improving cost efficiency (40%) and care coordination (38%). One-third targeted multiple care settings, and about half focused on multiple conditions. Among the 41 VBP schemes that underwent impact evaluation, positive effects were most frequently observed for clinical process (n = 14), followed by efficiency (n = 11), patient outcomes (n = 11). CONCLUSION: Although VBP schemes hold considerable promise, the ability of these programs to deliver desired outcomes depends heavily on their specific design and the context in which they are implemented. Continuous evaluation and iterative refinement are essential to ensure these programs achieve measurable improvements in quality, efficiency, and patient experience.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Slovakia adopted a comprehensive hospital network reform in 2021 (Act 540/2021 Coll.) under its Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP), motivated by a fragmented network of small, low-volume hospitals and limited transparency on services, quality and waiting times. REFORM CONTENT: The reform reorganises hospitals into five statutory levels, each defined by a portfolio of medical programmes, maximum waiting times, minimum case volumes and quality indicators. This paper provides a policy and regulatory overview of the reform's design, its content and the trajectory of its implementation. EXPECTED RESULTS: The reform aims to concentrate complex care, improve clinical outcomes, reduce variation, shorten waiting times and improve efficiency. Although the legislative architecture was largely in place by end-2023, core operational pillars are still unfinished: the quality-indicator decree was only adopted in mid-2025, with first availability for categorisation in 2027; staffing-norm legislation has yet to enter the legislative process; minimum-volume thresholds have been repeatedly revised downward; and no provider has so far been excluded from the network on volume grounds. POLICY IMPLICATIONS: The roll-out has been affected by political interference, repeated amendments, delays and politically driven re-categorisations, illustrating the gap between a legalistic design and its political execution. Policy implications stress the importance of aligned payment systems, sustained stakeholder engagement and systematic evaluation against the reform's stated objectives. Outcomes for efficiency, waiting times and treatable mortality will be the subject of future quantitative research as administrative data become available.

papers.abstract_en: Protein kinase data originate from sources with different identifiers, definitions, and evidence models. KinomeX (https://kinomex.dokhlab.org) is an online platform that aligns the human protein kinase list from KinHub with reviewed entries from UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot and links each record to source-specific evidence. Missing records are marked as unavailable. We developed the Pharmaceutical Development Interest Score (PDIS), which combines citation, clinical-trial, structural, and chemical data with adjustable component weights. These rankings are consistent across numerous weightings (median Spearman ρ = 0.955) and better reflect Pharos target development levels than citation counts alone. Examples highlight 93 under-cited but structurally and chemically accessible kinases and 47 CNS-specific kinases, with evidence on structure, chemistry, and variants. KinomeX enables evidence review and hypothesis formation, using PDIS to indicate documented development efforts rather than biological significance.

CONCLUSIONS: The increase in suspected cases reflects enhanced surveillance, awareness, and broader testing rather than a proportional rise in confirmed infections. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pneumococcal conjugate (PCV) and polysaccharide (PPSV) vaccines have reduced invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in Australia. Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models with five-fold cross-validation classified IPD due to PPSV23-type serotypes. Vaccinated individuals showed lower vaccine-type proportions than non- or partially vaccinated cases across age groups. Vaccine-type proportions were highest for pneumonia and in the Northern Territory, with greatest residual burden among older adults and Indigenous Australians. Machine-learning models classifying PPSV23-type IPD (accuracy ≈92%) identified vaccination-related variables, clinical presentation, and year of infection as key predictors; excluding these variables reduced AUC from 0.97-0.98 to 0.69. papers.abstract_en: Scholars and practitioners of global health humanitarianism have increasingly reflected on acceptable visual representation in global health, employing a range of terms such as biases, tropes and stereotypes, with a focus on "white saviourism" and "suffering subjects". We introduce the term global health iconography to advance this discussion, arguing that global health has historically reproduced four main kinds of highly-controlled image types (the icons) mapped around two binary oppositions: gazing vs intervening, referring to observing a photographic subject with or without intervention taking place; and suffering vs empowerment, referring to the implied state of the photography subject. We drew on interviews with 29 photographers (conducted December 2023 - May 2024) and analysis of images pulled from 50 global health organizations' websites to understand how photographers approached the creation of stereotypical images requested by their employers, and the mundane arrangements needed for assembling such images in communities. We find that institutionalized global health photography is a collective system of icon production in which pre-defined symbolic forms are repeated and normalized, while alternative representations get discarded as photographers are pressured to create images aligning with a recognizable visual canon. The paper argues that global health visual culture has been moving from an iconography of gazing at suffering to gazing at empowerment, mediated by public criticism and arcs of redemption resulting in iterative paradigm shifts. We conclude that decolonizing the global health visual culture requires a form of iconoclasm and not merely offering supposedly better icons as well as wrestling with the uneasy rise of generative AI imagery.

papers.abstract_en: STUDY OBJECTIVES: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is characterised by episodic complete or partial upper airway collapse during sleep. Diagnostic methods such as polysomnography (PSG) are resource-intensive and of limited utility for characterising upper-airway collapse to guide surgery. The expanding use of domiciliary sleep assessments presents an opportunity to improve access to OSA diagnosis. This review aims to evaluate the accuracy, clinical utility and limitations of domiciliary sleep assessment to diagnose OSA and localise airway collapse. METHOD: A scoping review was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library. Articles published between January 1, 2015, and September 1, 2025, were included. Domiciliary sleep assessment showed a sensitivity and specificity for moderate-to-severe OSA exceeding 90% in several studies of selected high pre-test probability cohorts. However, performance to detect mild OSA remains suboptimal. In contrast, entropy-based audio analysis and mandibular positioners show promise in obstructive site localisation and treatment selection. Domiciliary sleep assessments are limited by night-to-night variability and inadequate airway flow phenotyping. CONCLUSIONS: Domiciliary sleep assessment has clinically useful accuracy to diagnose moderate-to-severe OSA. Enhanced integration of upper airway flow characteristics represents a key area of development, with the potential to improve patient selection for targeted surgical interventions.

papers.abstract_en: Asthma is heterogeneous and frequently accompanied by depression, affecting disease mechanisms and management. Both asthma and depression have been associated with inflammation and microbiota alterations, but their combined impact on microbial compositions remains unclear. Our exploratory study analyzed lung and gut microbiota in patients with asthma and depression to identify associations between microbiota composition and disease markers. This cross-sectional study included 20 healthy controls, 20 patients with asthma, and 20 patients with asthma and comorbid depression. Participants underwent clinical characterization and assessment of asthma control, depression, anxiety, and perceived stress. Induced sputum and fecal samples were collected for microbiota analysis, and inflammatory cytokines were measured in serum and sputum. Microbial profiling was performed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Lung function and FeNO levels were comparable between all groups. Asthma control scores were lower, and psychological scores were significantly higher in patients with asthma and comorbid depression compared with asthma alone and controls. Despite similar alpha and beta diversity across groups, sputum and fecal microbiota, particularly of healthy controls and comorbid patients, significantly differed in genus-level taxonomic composition. Correlation analyses demonstrated associations between clinical and psychological parameters and microbial profiles, including a consistent negative correlation between psychological scores and Neisseria abundance in both sputum and fecal samples. Asthma with comorbid depression is associated with distinct alterations in respiratory and gut microbiota, including reduced Neisseria perflava abundance correlating with psychological symptom severity.IMPORTANCEAsthma and depression frequently coexist, yet the potential contribution of microbial alterations to this comorbidity remains poorly understood. Because both respiratory and gut microbiota have been implicated in immune regulation and disease pathophysiology, characterizing microbiota patterns associated with asthma and depression may provide new insights into the biological links between these conditions. In this exploratory study, we investigated respiratory and gut microbiota in individuals with asthma, with and without comorbid depression, and healthy controls. Genus-level community composition differed between groups, particularly between controls and patients with asthma and depression. Notably, reduced abundance of Neisseria perflava in sputum and fecal samples was consistently associated with greater psychological symptom severity. These findings suggest that asthma accompanied by depression is associated with distinct alterations in microbial communities at multiple body sites. Further studies are warranted to determine whether such microbiota-psychological associations contribute to disease mechanisms or may serve as biomarkers of asthma-depression comorbidity.

papers.abstract_en: China's 2016 long-term care insurance (LTCI) pilots represent one of the world's largest social-care policy experiments. Using the five waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) from 2011 to 2020, we examine how access to LTCI affects the physical and mental health of informal caregivers. We distinguish between spousal caregivers and adult-child caregivers. The latter provide nearly half of all informal care yet have received little attention in the literature. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that LTCI reduces physical pain for both groups of caregivers, although its effects on their mental health are limited. Our findings highlight the uneven health benefits of social-care reform and underscore the need for policies that provide stronger mental health support for caregivers in ageing societies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Rett syndrome is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder associated with functional impairments that emerge in early childhood and persist throughout life. Despite improved understanding of its genetic basis and natural history, therapeutic options remain limited, and care frameworks across Europe are highly variable. This study aimed to characterize the lived experiences, unmet needs, and evolving challenges faced by individuals with Rett syndrome and their caregivers across multiple European countries. RESULTS: Sixty caregivers across eight countries completed five-day diaries, and thirty participated in in-depth interviews. The sample represented children (36%), adolescents (42%), and adults (22%) with Rett syndrome; 97% were female. Difficulty using hands (reported by 88% of caregivers) and difficulty communicating (78%) were the most frequently observed symptoms. Daily activities were heavily affected, with symptoms impacting 59% of activities for children, 61% for adolescents, and 38% for adults. Some comorbidities increased with age, including scoliosis (45% in children vs. 92% in adults) and pneumonia (54% in adults). Care demands were substantial, with caregivers of adults spending an average of 41 hours per week providing emotional support alone, along with high time requirements for feeding (20 hours), washing and bathing (8 hours), and administering medication (5 hours). CONCLUSIONS: Caregiver experiences across Europe reveal a consistent pattern of unmet needs, high symptom burden, and fragmented, poorly coordinated care for individuals with Rett syndrome. The changing needs across the lifespan underscore the importance of anticipatory, multidisciplinary care models and improved transition pathways into adulthood. As participants were recruited through patient advocacy groups, the study population may represent a comparatively informed and healthcare-engaged subgroup of caregivers, highlighting that unmet needs and care challenges across the broader RTT caregiver community may be even greater among families with less access to advocacy networks and specialized support resources. These findings highlight the need for system-level changes and the development of comprehensive, standardized care frameworks for Rett syndrome across Europe.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Affect is dynamic. During addiction recovery, it may be laden with experiences like pain or craving, which may combine to heighten risk for substance use. Multidimensional affect-laden experiences can be identified using a novel application of latent class analysis (LCA) applied to intensive longitudinal data. Identifying momentary affect-laden classes may enable detection of risk for substance use in adults in early addiction recovery. METHODS: Participants were adults (n = 185; M = 43.6, SD = 10.7; 40% female) who recently completed substance use disorder treatment. Every day for two weeks, they received five ecological momentary assessments of high- and low-arousal positive affect (PA) and negative affect (NA), boredom, tired, alert, pain, and craving. LCA was applied to these nine indicators of momentary affect. Same-moment self-efficacy for remaining abstinent and using substances by the next prompt were modeled as a function of momentary affect-laden classes. RESULTS: Six momentary affect-laden classes were identified: Activated Positive Affect (32% of all moments); Activated Negative Affect (13%); Low Energy (8%); Calm Positive Affect (26%); Pain, Craving, and Positive Affect (13%); and Pain, Craving, and Negative Affect (8%). Moments characterized by Pain and Craving had the poorest substance use outcomes. Low Energy moments were among the best in terms of self-efficacy and reduced risk for substance use. Activated Positive Affect moments were among the lowest risk for substance use, even compared to Calm Positive Affect moments. CONCLUSIONS: Findings provide insight into detecting poor self-efficacy and subsequent substance use based on multidimensional affect-laden states during early recovery.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The dual use of traditional cigarettes and e-cigarettes is common among adolescents. Dual use is likely more harmful than smoking traditional cigarettes or using e-cigarettes alone. However, few studies have explored the behavioral and psychological factors associated with this pattern of tobacco use among Chinese adolescents. METHODS: We surveyed high school students in all 31 provincial-level administrative divisions (PLADs) in mainland China. Tobacco use was categorized as current dual use, exclusive traditional cigarette use, exclusive e-cigarette use, and non-use. We collected 11 behavioral and psychological variables potentially associated with current tobacco use, including physical activity, screen time, sleep duration, diet, alcohol use, fighting, social self-control, self-esteem, self-efficacy, stress, and depression. Multinomial logistic regression adjusted for PLAD fixed effects was employed to analyze the associations. RESULTS: The weighted sample included 15,000 students with an equal distribution of sex and a median age of 17 years (IQR: 16-18). About 6.9% (95% confidence interval: 6.5%-7.3%) reported current dual use. Several behavioral and psychological factors, including excessive screen time (OR = 0.70, 95% CI = 0.61-0.80; appropriate screen time as the reference group), unhealthy dietary habits (OR = 1.34, 95% CI = 1.15-1.56; healthy diet as the reference group), alcohol use (occasional: OR = 5.53, 95% CI = 4.27-7.17; habitual: OR = 12.71, 95% CI = 9.24-17.47; never use as the reference group), fighting (occasionally: OR = 1.69, 95% CI = 1.41-2.03; habitual: OR = 1.83, 95% CI = 1.18-2.82; never fight as the reference group), strong social self-control (OR = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.57-0.82; moderate as the reference group), strong self-esteem (OR = 1.62, 95% CI = 1.36-1.94; moderate as the reference group), self-efficacy (strong: OR = 1.61, 95% CI = 1.38-1.88; weak: OR = 0.78, 95% CI = 0.62-0.97; moderate as the reference group), and strong stress (OR = 0.78, 95% CI = 0.64-0.95; moderate as the reference group), were found to be associated with the current dual use. Some of the above factors were also associated with the current exclusive use of traditional cigarettes or e-cigarettes. CONCLUSIONS: This study reports on the phenomenon of current dual use and its behavioral and psychological associated factors among high school students in China. Families and schools should pay attention to adolescents' health risk behaviors and psychological health, as these factors were found to be associated with tobacco use. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To identify dietary patterns among adult childhood cancer survivors (CCSs), examine their determinants, and assess whether they differ according to cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk profiles. METHODS: CCSs from the Swiss Childhood Cancer Survivor Study diagnosed before age 21 years (1976-2005), surviving ≥ 5 years and aged ≥ 18 years in 2017, completed a food frequency questionnaire (SCCSS-Nutrition). Factor and hierarchical cluster analyses of 52 food groups identified dietary patterns. We categorised CCSs as having CVD, CVD risk factors (obesity, hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol), or being CVD risk-free. Multinomial logistic regression assessed associations between dietary patterns and CVD risk profiles. RESULTS: Among 802 CCSs (median age: 35 years; IQR: 29-41; 50% male), we identified five dietary patterns: Mediterranean-inspired diet (22%), Western indulgence diet (38%), Western sweet & fatty diet (26%), restrained indulgence diet (9%), plant-based & alcohol-rich diet (6%). Male sex, younger age, German-speaking region, smoking, and living with others were associated with Western indulgence, Western sweet & fatty, and restrained indulgence diets. Higher Swiss socioeconomic position (Swiss-SEP) and education, and not having children, were associated with the plant-based & alcohol-rich diet, higher Swiss-SEP was also associated with the Western indulgence diet. No associations were observed between dietary patterns and CVD risk profiles. CONCLUSIONS: Dietary patterns among adult CCSs were socially patterned and differed according to sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics, but were not associated with CVD risk profiles. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Dietary counselling and broader lifestyle support should be considered as part of long-term survivorship care for CCSs.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is one of the common malignant tumors. TATA protein-associated factor 9B (TAF9B) is essential for regulating RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription, and this regulation at the transcriptional level, which is closely related to the carcinogenesis of various tumors, represents a complex process. This study aimed to investigate the expression of TAF9B in ESCC and its potential effect on patient prognosis. Real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction analysis showed that the expression level of TAF9B was significantly upregulated in ESCC tissues (P = 0.0039). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated that patients with low TAF9B expression exhibited better overall survival than those with high TAF9B expression (P = 0.01). This study indicated that TAF9B is highly expressed in ESCC and may have prognostic relevance for ESCC patients. Further studies revealed that TAF9B knockdown could inhibit the proliferation of ESCC cells both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome sequencing analysis and validation experiments confirmed that a disintegrin and metalloproteinase 17 (ADAM17) acts as a downstream target gene regulated by TAF9B. Our study demonstrated that TAF9B promotes TATA binding protein occupancy at the ADAM17 promoter and upregulates ADAM17 expression. This process further activates the TNF-α/NF-κB signaling pathway and suppresses apoptosis in ESCC cells. Collectively, TAF9B acts as a novel oncogenic factor in ESCC and promotes tumor progression.

papers.abstract_en: Phosphorylation of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) regulates many biomolecular interactions, yet its quantitative effects on binding of highly charged IDPs to nucleic acids remain unclear. Here, we show that multi-site phosphorylation of the disordered arginine/serine-rich (RS) domain of the splicing factor SRSF1 functions as an electrostatic rheostat controlling RNA binding. Using enzymatic phosphorylation, phosphomimetic variants, chemically synthesized phosphopeptides, and single-molecule Förster resonance energy transfer measurements, we identify the RS domain as a strong driver of protein-RNA association. Progressive phosphorylation gradually weakens this interaction, and extensive phosphorylation abolishes detectable RNA binding. Notably, the binding free energy varies linearly with RS domain net charge, independent of whether the charge arises from phosphorylation or acidic phosphomimetic substitutions. Together, our findings establish a quantitative framework for how phosphorylation tunes interactions between charged IDPs and nucleic acids, and rationalize why two acidic amino acid residues are needed to mimic the effect of a single phosphorylation event.

papers.abstract_en: The nanomedicine field has seen a paradigm shift towards multifunctional drug designs to maximise drug efficacy. Assembly of functionalised oligonucleotide (ODN) modules onto an albumin scaffold is an attractive solution offering a technological advancement in albumin-based drug delivery we apply in this work for a T-Cell Engager (TCE) and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (ICI) immuno-oncology combination. The "plug-and-play" modular approach was used to incorporate an anti-programmed cell death protein ligand 1 (anti-PD-L1) nanobody-ODN module onto a bispecific anti-EGFR x anti-CD3 scFv-albumin TCE fusion. Cys34 ODN site-specific conjugation on albumin allowed subsequent base-driven annealing of the complementary anti-PD-L1 nanobody-ODN module offering an easy and versatile alternative to established protein engineering approaches. The biomolecular components elements demonstrated effective binding of cellular targets in vitro, efficient PD-1/PD-L1 axis blockade and enhanced T-cell mediated cancer cell killing compared to single or separate combined treatments. Modular assembly on an albumin scaffold engineered with high neonatal Fc receptor affinity increased the circulatory half-life in humanised FcRn/albumin mice from 18.8 h to 26.6 h compared to wild type albumin sequences. This biomolecular assembly reflects the transition in the field towards multifunctional platforms exemplified in this work with an ICI and TCE combination promoting application for a range of functionalities and drug class combinations and offering programable half-life through inclusion of albumin sequences with different FcRn affinities.

papers.abstract_en: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) constitutes the leading cause of chronic low back pain. Oxidative stress and ferroptosis act as critical pathological drivers of IVDD progression. Nevertheless, the cellular heterogeneity of nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs), endogenous repair homeostasis, and the regulatory network linking mechanical signals to ferroptosis remain poorly defined. In the present study, single-cell RNA sequencing was adopted to dissect the dynamic features of human NPC subpopulations, verifying that progressive depletion of progenitor NPCs (P-NPCs) serves as the core trigger for disrupted repair homeostasis during IVDD development. Combined with clinical specimen validation, multi-omics profiling and in vitro cellular models, we demonstrated that aberrant mechanical stress activates the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 and triggers Ca²⁺ influx. This event downregulates the transcription of GPX4, the master effector against ferroptosis; simultaneously, it upregulates the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM21 to accelerate GPX4 ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation. These two coordinated pathways aggravate oxidative stress, iron overload and lipid peroxidation in NPCs, accompanied by typical mitochondrial morphological damage. Ferroptotic NPCs further shape a pathological microenvironment that suppresses P-NPC viability and triggers P-NPC apoptosis, thereby establishing a cascading and self-amplifying degenerative loop. Both in vitro treatment with a PIEZO1 inhibitor and in vivo mechanical loading assays using nucleus pulposus-specific PIEZO1 knockout mice validated that PIEZO1 blockade restores GPX4 activity, rebalances redox homeostasis and robustly retards IVDD progression.

papers.abstract_en: Delivering mRNA to the lungs promises treatment of genetic, infectious and non-communicable lung diseases. Yet, conventional lipid nanoparticle formulations lack the stability needed to endure the harsh mechanical stress during nebulization. Additionally, once deposited in the respiratory tract, gene delivery systems may first have to overcome the mucus barrier, before actually transfecting the target cells. To overcome these challenges, we utilize lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles (LPH), merging the stability of pharmaceutical polymers with the transfection efficiency of cationic and ionizable lipids. LPH are produced in a robust microfluidic process, accomplish near-complete encapsulation efficiency, even after nebulization, and confer high transfection efficiency in A549 cells. To provide colloidal stability after aerosolization, we developed a coating strategy with hyaluronic acid (HA) and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA), ensuring ideal nebulization stability by steric shielding. This formulation showed good transfection efficiency of air-liquid interface grown Calu-3 cells, producing and covered by mucus. The potential of LPH to deliver mRNA to mammalian cells was first shown in primary human lung fibroblasts in vitro and could also be confirmed after intratracheal administration to mice in vivo. Together, these findings validate LPH as a versatile and aerosolizable mRNA delivery platform, overcoming the key technological and biological barriers in pulmonary gene delivery.

papers.abstract_en: After spinal cord injury, clinical management aims to support tissue perfusion, but current methods rely on the indirect control of arterial blood pressure without direct measurement of the local blood flow. This limits the ability to tailor drug delivery to the injured tissue. Here, we show that spinal cord blood flow can be regulated using a closed-loop controller that adjusts vasopressor infusion on the basis of real-time ultrasound flow measurement. We characterize the dynamic relationship between drug infusion, arterial pressure and spinal cord blood flow, and we use these data to design a feedback controller that targets a predefined flow level. We validate the system in simulations, implement the controller in real time in rodents and translate it to pigs. We show that the controller reduced blood flow deviations and variability compared with constant dosing and supported functional recovery in a rodent survival model. These results show a closed-loop spinal cord perfusion control strategy that leverages clinically available measurements and pharmacological interventions, supporting its translation to clinical settings for the management of acute spinal cord injury.

papers.abstract_en: Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2) is a mast-cell-enriched receptor that mediates immunoglobulin E-independent activation by structurally diverse neuropeptides, host-defense peptides, microbial products, and selected cationic drugs. Its biology links tissue stress and neuroimmune signaling to degranulation, vascular responses, pruritus, barrier dysfunction, and inflammatory amplification, but the extent to which individual diseases depend on this pathway remains uncertain. The strongest clinical rationale begins with non-IgE-mediated immediate drug hypersensitivity, for which MRGPRX2 provides a direct mechanistic framework, although rocuronium illustrates the need to distinguish human MRGPRX2 pharmacology from murine Mrgprb2 and from IgE-mediated perioperative allergy. In atopic dermatitis, preclinical and human skin data support a potential amplifier role in type 2 inflammation and itch, but a randomized phase 2b study of EVO756 did not demonstrate efficacy in an unselected population. In chronic urticaria, challenge, biomarker, and genetic studies suggest an MRGPRX2-responsive subgroup within a heterogeneous disease, whereas a randomized phase 2b study of EVO756 in unselected chronic spontaneous urticaria was also negative despite earlier pharmacodynamic activity. Ulcerative colitis provides additional human tissue evidence for an MRGPRX2-associated mast-cell circuit, although murine Mrgprb2 studies show context-dependent protective and pathogenic effects. Emerging evidence in chronic prurigo, allergic contact dermatitis, asthma, mastocytosis, rheumatoid arthritis, synovial inflammation, and neurogenic inflammation is also considered, with explicit separation of human observations from mouse-model evidence. We integrate these findings with receptor pharmacology and early clinical development, emphasizing evidence hierarchy, validated biomarker needs, patient selection, tissue target engagement, safety, and trial design. Current data support MRGPRX2 as an investigational endotype-defining pathway rather than a universal driver of allergic or immune-mediated disease.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is closely linked to chronic inflammation, but the transcriptional mechanisms connecting epithelial inflammatory remodeling with malignant transformation remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We integrated secondary analysis of published single-cell epithelial transition-state data, virtual SP1 perturbation, TCGA analyses, xCell immune infiltration analysis, TIDE-based exploratory immunotherapy prediction, Co-IP/MS, and a 4NQO-induced mouse model to investigate SP1-associated network remodeling during ESCC carcinogenesis. RESULTS: SP1 regulatory importance increased across pairwise epithelial state comparisons. In adjacent normal epithelial cells, virtual SP1 overexpression affected genes linked to inflammatory response, NF-κB-related signaling, epithelial stress remodeling, and proliferation. SP1 expression correlated with immune infiltration features and immune checkpoint gene expression, and TIDE analysis suggested an association with predicted immunotherapy-related features. SP1-binding partners were enriched in RNA metabolism, RNA splicing, and nuclear protein-complex annotations, suggesting potential non-canonical regulatory associations that require further experimental validation. CONCLUSIONS: SP1 may represent a progressively enhanced transcriptional hub during inflammation-associated ESCC carcinogenesis, with state-dependent network remodeling spanning epithelial inflammatory stress, malignant transformation, and tumor immune features.

papers.abstract_en: During mitotic growth, Saccharomyces cerevisiae cells age by dividing asymmetrically, producing young daughter cells while retaining age-associated damage in the mother cell, which will eventually become senescent. Gametogenesis naturally and fully resets precursor cell lifespan, even for replicatively aged cells. However, the mechanisms responsible for gametogenic rejuvenation have remained mysterious. This is partly due to the existing methods to quantify lifespan resetting in this context, which are limited to low-throughput and labor-intensive approaches. Here, we introduce a high-throughput assay that allows systematic characterization of factors required for gametogenic rejuvenation. With this approach, we show that we can sensitively measure a wide range of gamete replicative lifespans that are consistent with established mutants. Excitingly, we also discover that Atg39 and Atg40, receptors involved in selective autophagy of the ER, are molecular determinants of gametogenic rejuvenation. This technique will enable systematic identification of the molecular factors that drive gametogenic rejuvenation.

papers.title_zh: 1999-2023年美国误吸相关呼吸衰竭死亡率呈上升趋势：基于多死因数据库的描述性分析
papers.title_en: Mortality trends of aspiration-associated respiratory failure in the united states : a multiple cause of death analysis.
papers.authors: Alam T, Alokozay E, Kamal S, Areesha F, Rashid MI, Abufatima IO, Nisa NU, Azhar MJ et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Dow University of Health Sciences, Karachi, Pakistan.
papers.results: 1999-2023年共识别372,764例误吸相关呼吸衰竭死亡；年龄标化死亡率由4.27/10万升至10.17/10万（AAPC 3.98%；p<0.001）；男性平均AAMR高于女性（8.94 vs 4.72/10万）；≥65岁成人粗死亡率最高（27.79/10万）；非西班牙裔非洲裔（7.10）与美洲印第安/阿拉斯加原住民（6.61）平均AAMR最高；都市地区AAMR略高于非都市地区（5.99 vs 5.40）
papers.authors_conclusion: 误吸相关呼吸衰竭死亡在1999-2023年显著增加，并存在显著的人口学与地理差异；这些发现支持改善吞咽障碍预防、监测及有针对性的公共卫生干预。
papers.ai_note: 本研究为纯描述性多死因编码分析，无个体层面临床资料，无法区分误吸为根本死因还是伴随/contributing 死因，亦无法校正合并症与编码习惯变迁（ICD版本/死因填报告知度提高）对趋势的贡献，故AAMR上升可能部分反映编码与识别敏感性变化而非真实发病增加；仅报告AAPC与均值AAMR，未给出分层率的置信区间与组间比较统计检验，组间差异（如都市vs非都市5.99 vs 5.40）未做显著性检验；摘要未报告Joinpoint分段的具体拐点年份与各段APC；结论建议的“吞咽障碍预防”等干预措施属外推，未在本研究数据中验证。

pico.p: 1999-2023年美国≥25岁成人中，死亡证明上以误吸（Aspiration）与呼吸衰竭为根本或 contributing 死因者，共372,764例死亡
pico.ic: 无干预暴露比较；按年份、性别、年龄（≥65岁）、种族/族裔（非西班牙裔非洲裔、美洲印第安/阿拉斯加原住民等）及都市/非都市地区分层比较死亡率

papers.reason: 为非肿瘤性呼吸系统疾病的死亡趋势与人群差异提供全国性基线数据，可为误吸/吞咽障碍相关呼吸衰竭的监测研究、公共卫生资源配置及围手术期误吸风险背景估计提供参照，但与胸外科肿瘤诊疗决策的直接关联有限。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Aspiration-associated respiratory failure is an important but under-recognized cause of morbidity and mortality among U.S. adults. Despite its clinical significance, national epidemiologic patterns and demographic disparities remain poorly characterized. METHODS: Mortality data from the CDC WONDER Database (1999-2023) were extracted for adults aged ≥ 25 years in the U.S. with Aspiration and Respiratory Failure listed as underlying or contributing causes of death. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate the Annual Percent Change (APC) and Annual Average Percentage Change (AAPC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Between 1999 and 2023, 372,764 deaths involving aspiration-associated respiratory failure were identified among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years. The age-adjusted mortality rate increased from 4.27 to 10.17 per 100,000 population (AAPC: 3.98%; p < 0.001). Males had higher mean AAMRs than females (8.94 vs. 4.72 per 100,000). Adults aged ≥ 65 years had the highest crude mortality rate (27.79 per 100,000). Non-Hispanic African Americans (7.10) and American Indian/Alaska Native populations (6.61) had the highest mean AAMRs, while metropolitan areas had slightly higher AAMRs than non-metropolitan areas (5.99 vs. 5.40). CONCLUSION: Mortality involving aspiration-associated respiratory failure increased significantly from 1999 to 2023, with substantial demographic and geographic disparities. These findings support improved dysphagia prevention, surveillance, and targeted public health interventions.

papers.title_zh: SHP2在癌症中的作用及靶向治疗挑战：从肿瘤生物学到变构抑制剂的综述
papers.title_en: SHP2 in Cancer: From Tumor Biology to Therapeutic Targeting.
papers.authors: Jama M, Overduin M, Barakat KH
papers.affiliation_highlight: Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, University of Alberta, Edmonton, Canada.
papers.authors_conclusion: SHP2是癌症治疗有吸引力的靶点，但SHP2的复杂作用、单药疗效及SHP2突变体情境仍带来挑战；当前变构抑制剂缺乏明确的选择性靶向高活性SHP2的作用模式，需更深入理解SHP2调控机制及其与肿瘤微环境的相互作用以优化SHP2靶向治疗。
papers.ai_note: 本文为叙述性综述，无原始研究设计、定量结果或临床终点数据；摘要以机制与治疗前景为主，无法据此评估疗效与安全性结论的证据强度。

pico.p: 多种恶性肿瘤（综述，无原始样本量）
pico.ic: SHP2变构抑制剂单药或联合EGFR/PD-1/KRAS/MEK抑制剂；对照未系统报告

papers.reason: 提供SHP2作为泛癌种信号节点及变构抑制剂联合策略的背景框架，对胸部肿瘤靶向治疗选题与联合方案设计有间接参考价值，但不直接改变胸科临床判断。
papers.abstract_en: SHP2 is a tyrosine phosphatase that mediates intracellular signaling downstream of transmembrane receptors regulated by a pair of src homology 2 (SH2) domains. Its overexpression and mutation are pivotal in driving tumor progression by influencing various cancer's fundamental characteristics, such as metastasis, DNA repair, angiogenesis, immunosuppression, and telomere extension. SHP2 acts as a convergent node of oncogenic signaling pathways including MAPK, PI3K-AKT, VEGF, JAK-STAT making it an attractive target for cancer therapeutics. Preclinical studies demonstrate that SHP2 allosteric inhibitors in combination with EGFR, PD-1, KRAS, or MEK inhibitors, show potent antitumour activity and effectively overcome adaptive resistance beyond conventional therapies. Multiple SHP2 allosteric inhibitors are currently in clinical trials to assess their effectiveness, safety, and tolerability in treating various malignancies. Despite these advancements, SHP2's complex role presents challenges for the efficacy of SHP2 monotherapy and in the context of SHP2 mutants. Current allosteric inhibitors lack a well-defined mode of action for selectively targeting hyperactive SHP2 in malignancies. Moreover, a deeper understanding of SHP2's regulatory mechanisms and its interactions within the tumor microenvironment is needed to optimize SHP2-directed therapies. This review highlights these challenges, with a focus on SHP2 regulation, disease-associated mutants, its role in cancer cells and the tumor microenvironment, current and future therapeutic prospects.
